Introduction

介绍

How Learning Works

学习是如何运作的

L ife depends on learning. We spend decades in school, acquiring an education. We want to be good at our jobs, not just for the perks that come from being one of the best, but for the pride that comes from mastering a craft. Even the things we do for fun, we enjoy to a large extent because we feel we’re capable of getting better at them.

生命离不开学习。我们花费数十年时间在学校接受教育。我们渴望在工作中表现出色，不仅是为了获得成为佼佼者所带来的优待，更是为了精通技艺后获得的成就感。即使是娱乐消遣，我们之所以乐在其中，很大程度上是因为我们觉得自己有能力做得更好。

Yet learning is often mysterious. Sometimes it comes effortlessly, as when we quickly find our way around a new neighborhood or pick up the routine at a new job. In other cases, it’s a slog. We may spend hours in the library, with little to show for it on the final exam. We may want to switch companies, industries, or even professions, but not feel qualified to make the leap. We can spend decades driving a car, typing on a computer, or hitting a tennis serve without reliably getting better at any of them. Improvement is inconsistent, if it comes at all.

然而，学习往往充满神秘。有时它毫不费力，比如我们很快就能熟悉新街区，或者迅速适应新工作的流程。但在其他情况下，学习却异常艰辛。我们可能在图书馆里花费数小时，最终考试却一无所获。我们可能想要更换公司、行业，甚至职业，但却觉得自己没有能力做出改变。我们可能花费数十年时间开车、打字或练习网球发球，却无法在这些方面取得显著进步。进步并不稳定，甚至根本不会到来。

Whether your aim is eventual mastery or just to get a little bit better, it helps to understand how learning works. Simple principles can explain why progress comes easily in some situations, and can be frustratingly absent in others. To begin, let’s look at an unlikely story of world-class skill development—how Tetris players suddenly became much better at the game, three decades after it first became popular.

无论你的目标是最终精通还是仅仅想略有进步，了解学习的原理都至关重要。一些简单的原则可以解释为什么在某些情况下进步轻而易举，而在另一些情况下却令人沮丧地停滞不前。首先，让我们来看一个世界级技能提升的非凡故事——俄罗斯方块玩家在游戏流行三十年后，如何突然间技艺突飞猛进。

The Tetris Enigma

俄罗斯方块之谜

As he does most days, Joseph Saelee fired up a game of Tetris on February 15, 2020. Immediately, the iconic, four-square multicolored bricks begin falling at a rate of roughly one every second. Despite a pace that would make most arcade buffs sweat, Saelee is barely paying attention. Instead, he’s chatting with the handful of followers who have come to watch him play live on the online streaming platform Twitch. The conversation slows as he reaches level 19. Saelee must now find and maneuver each brick into the best possible spot in the two-thirds of a second it takes for them to reach the bottom. Before it lands, he is already glancing at the display indicating the next piece—the only reprieve from the otherwise completely unpredictable sequence of shapes. After nine levels at this blistering pace, the speed doubles once more. The bricks barely blink into existence before they are already at the bottom of the screen. As he completes this stage, the level counter glitches, changing from displaying “29” to “00”—a clear sign that the game designers thought nobody would make it this far. Seemingly in a trance, Saelee jiggles his fingers to tap the buttons on his controller more than ten times per second. He is able to perfectly place each brick, clearing space fast enough to prevent new ones from overwhelming the screen. After a few minutes, he makes his first mistake—a single misplaced brick stands tall above the otherwise neatly arranged rows. In the blink of an eye, it is all over, a deluge of squares filling the screen. Despite this, Saelee is smiling. Defeat may have been inevitable, but Saelee had managed to reach level 34, a feat that had never been accomplished in the thirty-year history of one of the most popular video games of all time. Saelee was just eighteen years old.

2020年2月15日，约瑟夫·萨利像往常一样打开了俄罗斯方块游戏。标志性的四方彩色方块立刻开始以大约每秒一个的速度落下。尽管这样的速度足以让大多数街机游戏爱好者汗流浃背，但萨利却几乎没怎么注意。他正和几个在Twitch直播平台上观看他游戏的粉丝聊天。当他到达第19关时，聊天节奏慢了下来。萨利必须在方块落地前三分之二秒的时间里，找到并移动每个方块到最佳位置。在方块落地之前，他已经瞥了一眼屏幕上显示的下一个方块——这是游戏中唯一能让他暂时摆脱完全不可预测的方块排列的线索。以这种惊人的速度通关九关后，速度再次翻倍。方块几乎是瞬间出现，就已经落到了屏幕底部。当他完成这一关时，关卡计数器出现了故障，从“29”变成了“00”——这显然表明游戏设计师认为没人能走到这一步。萨利仿佛着了魔一般，手指飞快地敲击着手柄上的按钮，速度超过每秒十次。他能完美地放置每一块砖，迅速清理出空间，防止新的砖块铺满屏幕。几分钟后，他犯了第一个错误——一块放错位置的砖块高高耸立在原本整齐排列的砖块之上。转眼间，一切结束了，屏幕上瞬间被大量的方块填满。尽管如此，萨利脸上依然带着笑容。失败或许在所难免，但萨利成功到达了第34关，这在有史以来最受欢迎的电子游戏之一的三十年历史中，从未有人达到过。萨利当时只有十八岁。

Joseph Saelee is obviously skilled at Tetris . But what is more remarkable is how much better he is than the first generation of players who were obsessed with the game. Playing on level 29 was long thought impossible. Bricks dropped so fast that simply holding left or right, a player couldn’t move them all the way to the edge of the screen before they became locked in place at the bottom. Since a complete, horizontal row of blocks is needed for them to disappear in the satisfying Tetris click, fans regarded the level unplayable, nicknaming it the “killscreen.” Another feat, achieving a maximum score of 999,999 points in a single session, was long sought by early players. But the first documented “max-out” didn’t occur until two decades after the game’s release, when Harry Hong reached the top score. In contrast, over the span of a single tournament in 2020, Saelee maxed out twelve separate times. Nor is Saelee unique in his Tetris proficiency. During the same tournament, forty different players reached the maximum possible score. How does a game, long past its prime, produce much better players?

约瑟夫·萨利显然是一位俄罗斯方块高手。但更令人惊叹的是，他的水平远超那些痴迷于这款游戏的第一代玩家。长期以来，人们认为通关第29关是不可能的。方块下落速度极快，玩家仅仅按住左或右方向键，根本无法将它们移动到屏幕边缘，它们就会在底部卡住不动。由于需要一整行水平方块才能消除，发出令人满意的“俄罗斯方块”咔哒声，因此玩家们认为这一关根本无法通关，并将其戏称为“死亡屏幕”。另一个早期玩家梦寐以求的壮举是单局游戏获得999,999分的最高分。但有记录的第一个“满分”直到游戏发行二十年后才出现，由哈里·洪创下。相比之下，萨利在2020年的一次锦标赛中就十二次达到了满分。当然，萨利的俄罗斯方块高超水平并非个例。在同一场比赛中，有四十名不同的选手达到了最高分。一款早已过了鼎盛时期的游戏，为何还能涌现出如此优秀的玩家？

Tetris , Then and Now

俄罗斯方块，过去与现在

Tetris feels dated today, so it’s easy to forget the sensation it caused when it debuted. Invented by Russian computer scientist Alexey Pajitnov in 1984, the game spread via floppy disc through the twilight years of the Soviet Union. Pajitnov, like many an office employee after him, was hooked by his own creation, playing Tetris instead of working. Vladimir Pokhilko, a psychologist and friend of Pajitnov, thought the game was so enticing it could be used to study addiction. Eventually he had to destroy all his copies when it became clear that his research staff weren’t getting any work done. After it was stumbled upon by software broker Robert Stein during a trip to Hungary, the game set off a ferocious battle for distribution rights in the West. Eventually Nintendo emerged victorious, creating the definitive edition for its Nintendo Entertainment System (NES), selling millions of copies and creating a generation of devoted fans.

如今，俄罗斯方块游戏似乎已经过时，人们很容易忘记它初次问世时引起的轰动。这款游戏由俄罗斯计算机科学家阿列克谢·帕基特诺夫于1984年发明，并在苏联解体前的最后几年通过软盘传播开来。帕基特诺夫和许多后来的上班族一样，沉迷于自己的发明，玩俄罗斯方块玩到无法工作。帕基特诺夫的朋友、心理学家弗拉基米尔·波希尔科认为这款游戏极具吸引力，甚至可以用来研究成瘾。最终，当他发现研究人员根本无法完成任何工作时，他不得不销毁所有游戏拷贝。软件经纪人罗伯特·斯坦在匈牙利旅行时偶然发现了这款游戏，随后在西方引发了一场激烈的发行权争夺战。最终，任天堂胜出，为其任天堂娱乐系统（NES）打造了终极版，销量数百万份，并培养了一代忠实粉丝。

While for most players, Tetris was just an amusing pastime, others became obsessed. Ben Mullen, an early record holder, kept detailed statistics on his play to try to find hidden patterns to optimize his performance. “I found out that, actually, exactly one half hour after you have some coffee, you play the best Tetris ,” he reports. Harry Hong played so much he had to place a shirt between his thumb and the controller to keep from getting blisters. Others played until they began to hallucinate falling blocks, in what would later be called the “ Tetris effect.” But devoted as they were, none came close to the performance effortlessly displayed by modern players like Saelee.

对大多数玩家来说，俄罗斯方块只是一种有趣的消遣，但也有一些人沉迷其中。早期纪录保持者本·穆伦（Ben Mullen）详细记录了自己的游戏数据，试图从中找出隐藏的规律来优化自己的发挥。“我发现，实际上，喝完咖啡半小时后，你的俄罗斯方块水平会达到最佳状态，”他说道。哈里·洪（Harry Hong）玩得太多，以至于不得不在拇指和手柄之间垫一件衬衫，以免磨出水泡。还有一些人玩到出现幻觉，看到方块不断下落，这种现象后来被称为“俄罗斯方块效应”。但即便他们如此投入，也无法与像萨利（Saelee）这样的现代玩家轻松展现的水平相提并论。

Resolving the Enigma

解开谜团

A clue to understanding the stark change in proficiency comes from observing how players made their achievements known. In the earliest days, official records were managed by Twin Galaxies, a video game record database. Players submitted their high scores, along with some form of verification. If deemed legitimate, referees would post the scores to a central leaderboard on their website. But the process was cumbersome. Players might fail to sufficiently document an attempt, resulting in a record that was ultimately unsubmittable. This was the fate of Jonas Neubauer and Thor Aackerlund, who had claimed to have reached a max-out before Harry Hong, but couldn’t prove it. But for years, there was no other option. If you wanted to be seen as the best, you had to go through Twin Galaxies.

要理解玩家水平的巨大变化，关键在于观察他们如何展示自己的成就。早期，官方记录由Twin Galaxies——一个电子游戏记录数据库——管理。玩家提交自己的最高分，并附上某种形式的验证信息。如果审核通过，裁判会将分数发布到其网站的中央排行榜上。但这个过程十分繁琐。玩家可能无法充分记录某次尝试，导致最终无法提交记录。Jonas Neubauer和Thor Aackerlund就遭遇了这种情况，他们声称自己在Harry Hong之前达到了最高分，但却无法证明。但多年来，别无他法。如果你想被视为最强者，就必须通过Twin Galaxies。

This started to change after YouTube. Freely uploading videos, players could share their world records directly, rather than going through an intermediary. While this made it easier to submit a new top score, it had an important side effect: if you posted a video of a world record performance, everyone could see how you did it. Before that, Twin Galaxies had only posted the top score, not the evidence itself used to verify it. Players could now not only marvel at the skill of elite Tetris players, but see how they did it.

YouTube出现后，情况开始发生变化。玩家可以自由上传视频，直接分享他们的世界纪录，无需通过中间平台。这虽然让提交新的最高分变得更加容易，但也带来了一个重要的副作用：如果你发布了一段世界纪录的视频，所有人都能看到你是如何做到的。在此之前，Twin Galaxies只会发布最高分，而不会发布用于验证该分数的证据。现在，玩家不仅可以惊叹于俄罗斯方块高手的精湛技艺，还能看到他们是如何做到的。

While early YouTube provided greater transparency, the informal nature of the records also created temptations to cheat. Older games like Tetris could be run on an emulator, a piece of software that allows you to play console games on a personal computer. This specialized software lets players slow down the gameplay or rewind to undo mistakes. While careful sleuthing can often spot telltale signs of a fraudulent record, genuine players started investing in ways to authenticate their performance. Recording not just the screen but also video of the players’ hands became common. Livestreaming further increased authenticity, as the best players could be watched playing the game in real time, making cheating nearly impossible.

早期的YouTube虽然提高了透明度，但记录的非正式性也滋生了作弊的诱惑。像俄罗斯方块这样的老游戏可以在模拟器上运行，模拟器是一种可以让玩家在个人电脑上玩主机游戏的软件。这种专用软件可以让玩家减慢游戏速度或倒带回放来纠正错误。虽然仔细的调查通常可以发现作弊记录的蛛丝马迹，但真正的玩家开始投入资源来验证自己的表现。录制屏幕视频，甚至录制玩家的手部动作，都变得司空见惯。直播进一步提高了真实性，因为顶尖玩家可以实时观看游戏，作弊几乎成为不可能。

Observing hand movements, innovations in button pressing could be widely replicated. A method known as hypertapping, where players vibrate their thumb to hit the direction buttons more than ten times per second, was key to breaking through the level 29 barrier. Thor Aackerlund, the best player of the early era, had invented the technique. But as few could witness and emulate his approach, it remained unused for nearly two decades. Livestreaming also created an incentive for commentary. Great players, pushed to communicate with an audience, shared their thinking behind the game in real time. Discussion ran in both directions, as top players not only shared their strategies, but viewers could immediately scrutinize potential mistakes. While an earlier era of game masters might have jealously coveted a secret strategy that gave them an edge, modern competitors were forced to be radically transparent, with every button press exposed for all the world to see.

通过观察手部动作，按键技巧的创新得以广泛复制。一种被称为“超速敲击”的技巧，即玩家通过震动拇指以每秒超过十次的频率点击方向键，是突破29级瓶颈的关键。早期最优秀的玩家托尔·阿克伦德发明了这项技巧。但由于很少有人能够亲眼目睹并模仿他的方法，这项技巧在近二十年的时间里都未被广泛应用。直播也促进了解说。优秀的玩家在与观众交流的推动下，实时分享了他们游戏背后的思考。讨论是双向的，顶尖玩家不仅分享他们的策略，观众也能立即审视潜在的错误。虽然早期的游戏大师们可能会对那些能让他们占尽优势的秘密策略垂涎三尺，但现代的竞争者却被迫做到完全透明，每一次按键都暴露在全世界的视野之下。

Online forums greatly expanded the network of potential players to learn from. In the 1990s, your resources for improvement were limited to your circle of friends. If you happened to know a very good Tetris player, you might learn a few tricks. But if you didn’t, some of the subtler aspects of the game might be invisible to you, despite years of experience. Harry Hong revealed in a 2010 documentary that his preferred strategy was building his blocks on the right, leaving a gap on the left side of the screen. This strategy is considered inferior today. A quirk in the game’s rotation algorithm makes the all-important bar-shaped block easier to rotate and shift to the opposite side. Dana Wilcox, another former top player, wasn’t even aware that you could rotate the pieces in both directions. Such a gap in knowledge meant she couldn’t execute a few tricky maneuvers, such as a “T spin,” where the T-shaped block is twisted at the last possible moment to hook into an otherwise unreachable position. Today a new player can easily find the best strategies, even if they take considerable practice to master.

在线论坛极大地拓展了潜在玩家的学习渠道。在20世纪90年代，提升游戏水平的资源仅限于你的朋友圈。如果你碰巧认识一位俄罗斯方块高手，或许能学到一些技巧。但如果你不认识，即使拥有多年的经验，游戏中一些更微妙的技巧也可能对你来说是难以察觉的。哈里·洪在2010年的一部纪录片中透露，他最喜欢的策略是在屏幕右侧放置方块，在左侧留出空位。如今，这种策略被认为不够好。游戏旋转算法的一个漏洞使得至关重要的条形方块更容易旋转并移动到屏幕的另一侧。另一位曾经的顶尖玩家达娜·威尔科克斯甚至不知道方块可以双向旋转。这种知识上的缺失意味着她无法完成一些高难度的操作，例如“T形旋转”，即在最后一刻扭转T形方块，使其钩住原本无法到达的位置。如今，即使是新手玩家也能轻松找到最佳策略，尽管掌握这些策略需要大量的练习。

Tetris players are better today because their environment enables it. Video hosting allows detailed demonstrations of the best play to be broadcast widely. Online forums transform informal conversations into permanent reservoirs of knowledge. Livestreaming encourages extensive practice, including near-instantaneous feedback from an audience increasingly knowledgeable about the top techniques. Ultimately, the story of Tetris is not about any individual, although players such as Joseph Saelee certainly merit distinction. Instead, it’s a story about the game itself, and how the way it was played accelerated progress.

如今俄罗斯方块玩家水平更高，得益于他们所处的环境。视频托管平台使得最佳操作的详细演示得以广泛传播。在线论坛将非正式的交流转化为永久的知识宝库。直播鼓励玩家进行大量的练习，并能从日益精通顶尖技巧的观众那里获得近乎即时的反馈。归根结底，俄罗斯方块的故事并非关于任何个人，尽管像约瑟夫·萨利这样的玩家无疑值得称道。相反，它讲述的是游戏本身的故事，以及游戏玩法如何加速了游戏的发展。

The Three Factors for Getting Better at Anything

提升任何技能的三大要素

As the story of Tetris illustrates, improvement depends on more than just talent or tenacity. There are three factors that determine how much we learn:

正如俄罗斯方块的故事所展现的那样，进步不仅仅取决于天赋或毅力。有三个因素决定了我们能学到多少：

  1. See. Most of what we know comes from other people. The ease of learning from others determines, to a large extent, how quickly we can improve.
    你看，我们所知的大部分都来自他人。向他人学习的难易程度，在很大程度上决定了我们进步的速度。
  2. Do. Mastery requires practice. But not just any practice will do. Our brains are fantastic effort-saving machines, which can be both a tremendous advantage and a curse.
    去做吧。精通需要练习。但并非任何练习都有效。我们的大脑是绝佳的省力机器，这既是巨大的优势，也是一大弊端。
  3. Feedback. Progress requires iterative adjustment. Not just the red stroke of a teacher’s pen, but contact with the reality we’re trying to influence.
    反馈。进步需要不断迭代调整。这不仅仅是老师用红笔划一下，而是要与我们试图影响的现实进行接触。

When we’re able to learn from the example of other people, practice extensively ourselves, and get reliable feedback, rapid progress results. Yet, when one or all of these factors are inhibited, improvement often becomes impossible.

当我们能够从他人的例子中学习、进行大量的自我练习并获得可靠的反馈时，就能快速取得进步。然而，当这些因素中的一个或多个受到阻碍时，进步往往就变得不可能了。

More often, we find ourselves in a situation between the extremes that maximize learnability or prevent it entirely. Instead, there are both obstacles and opportunities, ways we can accelerate progress by finding the right environments, mentors, practice regimens, and projects to work on. The difficulty is often in knowing exactly what to look for.

更多时候，我们发现自己处于两种极端情况之间：要么最大限度地提高学习效率，要么完全阻碍学习。实际上，既存在障碍也存在机遇，我们可以通过找到合适的学习环境、导师、练习方法和项目来加速进步。难点往往在于我们究竟应该寻找什么。

See: The Power of Examples

参见：《榜样的力量》

We learn best through other people. Our ability to learn from each other greatly exceeds our ability to solve problems on our own. Tetris performance accelerated once the methods for high-level play became widely accessible. “The secret of our species’ success lies not in our raw, innate intelligence or in any specialized mental abilities,” writes Harvard anthropologist Joseph Henrich. Instead, he argues it’s the ability to learn easily from the innovations of others that makes us uniquely capable as a species.

我们通过与他人交流学习效果最佳。我们彼此学习的能力远远超过我们独立解决问题的能力。俄罗斯方块游戏的高手技巧普及之后，其游戏水平也随之突飞猛进。哈佛大学人类学家约瑟夫·亨里奇写道：“我们物种成功的秘诀不在于我们原始的、与生俱来的智力，也不在于任何特殊的心理能力。”相反，他认为，正是我们能够轻松地从他人的创新中学习，才使我们作为物种拥有独一无二的能力。

In some cases, intelligent animals can beat us in displays of problem-solving ability. Researchers have shown that crows can solve the problem of getting food out of a narrow bottle by fashioning a hook with a metal wire. Yet if a modified version of the same task is given to five-year-olds, fewer than a tenth figure out the trick. But if our problem-solving capacities are only modestly greater than some of our animal cousins, our imitative abilities are second to none. In an experiment, researchers compared two-and-a-half-year-old children to chimpanzees and orangutans on a battery of cognitive tests. Contrary to our species’ presumed superiority, the researchers found that children and apes performed similarly on puzzles involving spatial, quantitative and causal reasoning, with the chimps even edging out the children on some tasks. The clear exception was in social learning, where the toddlers were easily able to solve a problem when given a demonstration, but virtually none of the apes could. Young children may not compare favorably to crows and chimps in raw problem-solving ability, but they regularly learn to read, write, talk, add, multiply, draw, sing, and use a television remote—something no other animal can even attempt. The cliché of mindless learning, “monkey see, monkey do,” has it exactly backward. Imitation is the foundation for human ingenuity.

在某些情况下，聪明的动物在解决问题的能力上甚至胜过我们。研究人员发现，乌鸦能用金属丝制作钩子，从狭窄的瓶子里取出食物。然而，如果把同样的任务稍作修改，交给五岁的孩子，只有不到十分之一的孩子能掌握诀窍。尽管我们的解决问题能力只比一些动物近亲略胜一筹，但我们的模仿能力却无人能及。在一项实验中，研究人员让两岁半的儿童与黑猩猩和猩猩进行一系列认知测试。与人们普遍认为的人类优越性相反，研究人员发现，儿童和猿类在涉及空间、数量和因果推理的谜题上表现相似，黑猩猩甚至在某些任务上略胜一筹。唯一的例外是社交学习，幼儿在得到示范后能够轻松解决问题，而几乎所有猿类都做不到。幼儿在解决问题的能力上或许无法与乌鸦和黑猩猩相提并论，但他们却能学会阅读、写作、说话、加法、乘法、绘画、唱歌，甚至还能使用电视遥控器——这些都是其他动物想都不敢想的。那种“有样学样”的陈词滥调恰恰颠倒了事实。模仿才是人类创造力的基石。

Yet the ability to learn from others has its drawbacks. When we lack access to people we can learn from, we struggle to make progress. The early devotees of Tetris were essentially isolated from one another. They played alone, or with a handful of close friends. Techniques for best play couldn’t be transmitted, so each person had to evolve their own methods. In rare cases, such as with the video game prodigy Thor Aackerlund, this could go quite far. But in most cases, the result was play far below human potential. New technologies such as video uploading, livestreaming, and online forums greatly accelerated the dissemination of best practices. Even if Tetris is no longer the most popular game in the world, today’s generation of players is far more interconnected.

然而，向他人学习的能力也有其弊端。当我们缺乏可以学习的对象时，进步就会举步维艰。早期的俄罗斯方块爱好者基本上是彼此隔绝的。他们要么独自游戏，要么只和少数几个亲密的朋友一起玩。最佳玩法技巧无法传播，所以每个人都必须摸索出自己的方法。在极少数情况下，例如电子游戏神童托尔·阿克伦德，这种方法或许能取得相当大的成就。但在大多数情况下，其结果远低于人类的潜能。视频上传、直播和在线论坛等新技术极大地加速了最佳实践的传播。即使俄罗斯方块不再是世界上最受欢迎的游戏，但如今的玩家群体之间的联系也更加紧密。

Figure 1

图 1

More connections between players means more chances for innovations to spread. Members of the network on the right have more opportunities to learn from peers than those on the left.

玩家之间联系越紧密，创新传播的机会就越多。右侧网络中的成员比左侧网络中的成员有更多机会向同行学习。

The quality of examples we learn from also matters greatly. The transition to scientific chemistry from its origins in alchemical practice serves as a useful illustration. Early alchemists may have been wrong about the possibility of turning base metals into gold, but they did possess some reliable chemical knowledge. Many alchemists worked to develop a theory of matter and others even conducted controlled experiments. Yet they chose to deliberately obfuscate their findings out of a desire to keep esoteric techniques out of less experienced hands. As historian and chemist Lawrence Principe writes, “Alchemy’s primary sources present a forbidding tangle of intentional secrecy, bizarre language, obscure ideas, and strange imagery. The alchemists did not make it easy for others to understand what they were doing.” Alchemists used code names, or Decknamen , to conceal the identity of certain substances. They wrapped recipes inside fantastical allegories that had to be deciphered to be understood. They omitted, swapped, or added unnecessary steps to confuse unskilled readers. While this certainly had the intended effect of limiting knowledge to a privileged few, it also prevented the accumulation of reliable knowledge. Would-be alchemists had to repeat predecessor’s experiments dozens of times. A failed attempt didn’t prove the recipe was incorrect, as it was always possible that it hadn’t been properly decoded. Even a brilliant thinker such as Isaac Newton spent much of his life chasing down alchemical lore without realizing it was a dead end. In contrast, Robert Boyle’s experiments with his air pump—which led to the formulation of Boyle’s Law still taught in chemistry classes today—were meticulously documented, with dozens of illustrations of his experimental setup and the measurements he obtained. Confusing explanations and omitted steps in a process aren’t limited to alchemical texts. We often struggle to learn when materials are poorly designed and force us to do more work than is necessary to understand a concept or master a procedure.

我们所学习的实例的质量也至关重要。从炼金术实践到科学化学的过渡就是一个很好的例证。早期的炼金术士或许错误地认为贱金属可以变成黄金，但他们确实掌握了一些可靠的化学知识。许多炼金术士致力于发展物质理论，甚至有人进行了对照实验。然而，出于防止经验不足的人接触深奥技艺的考虑，他们选择刻意隐瞒自己的发现。正如历史学家兼化学家劳伦斯·普林西比所写：“炼金术的原始文献呈现出一幅令人望而生畏的迷雾，其中充斥着刻意的保密、怪异的语言、晦涩的思想和奇异的意象。炼金术士并没有让其他人轻易理解他们的所作所为。”炼金术士使用代号，或称“代号”（Decknamen），来隐藏某些物质的身份。他们将配方包裹在奇幻的寓言故事中，需要破译才能理解。他们省略、替换或添加不必要的步骤，以迷惑缺乏经验的读者。虽然这确实达到了将知识限制在少数特权阶层的预期效果，但也阻碍了可靠知识的积累。那些渴望成为炼金术士的人不得不重复前人的实验数十次。一次失败的尝试并不能证明配方是错误的，因为配方总有可能没有被正确解读。即使是像艾萨克·牛顿这样杰出的思想家，也曾花费大量时间追寻炼金术的知识，却没意识到这是一条死路。相比之下，罗伯特·波义耳用气泵进行的实验——最终形成了至今仍在化学课堂上教授的波义耳定律——被一丝不苟地记录下来，并附有数十幅实验装置和测量数据的插图。令人困惑的解释和步骤的省略并非炼金术文献所独有。当学习材料设计糟糕，迫使我们付出超出理解概念或掌握操作步骤所需的努力时，我们常常会感到学习困难。

Knowledge is not evenly distributed. Despite the promise of the internet age, the majority of the world’s knowledge isn’t written down and freely available. Instead, it’s locked away in the minds of experts, many of whom would struggle to articulate what they know. Knowledge is often not inside the head of any individual at all, but embodied in practices spread over groups. In a 1980 documentary, economist Milton Friedman, channeling an earlier essay by Leonard Read, used the example of a wooden pencil. “There’s not a single person in the world who could make this pencil. Remarkable statement? Not at all.” Friedman goes on to explain that the wood chopped down requires saws, which requires steel, which requires iron ore. The rubber, paint, glue, and graphite all involve enormously complicated supply chains to manufacture. The knowledge of building something as simple as a pencil isn’t held by any individual, but groups who work together toward a common purpose. As our science and technology develop further, individual achievements may become increasingly rare as distributed groups become necessary to bring together all the knowledge required to solve hard problems. New advances in artificial intelligence may accelerate this trend, as the world of book knowledge becomes increasingly accessible, but the tacit understanding of unspoken practice remains within cloistered communities of experts. Access to the environments where knowledge resides is often a bigger hurdle to mastery than learning itself.

知识并非均匀分布。尽管互联网时代前景广阔，但世界上绝大多数的知识并未被记录下来并免费获取。相反，它们被锁在专家的头脑中，而许多专家甚至难以清晰地表达自己的知识。知识往往并非存在于任何个人的头脑中，而是体现在群体实践中。在1980年的一部纪录片中，经济学家米尔顿·弗里德曼引用伦纳德·里德的一篇早期文章，以木制铅笔为例。“世界上没有一个人能做出这支铅笔。这说法令人惊讶吗？一点也不。”弗里德曼接着解释说，砍伐木材需要锯子，锯子需要钢材，钢材需要铁矿石。橡胶、油漆、胶水和石墨的生产都需要极其复杂的供应链。制造像铅笔这样简单的东西的知识并非掌握在某个人手中，而是掌握在为了共同目标而共同努力的群体手中。随着科技的不断进步，个人成就或许会变得越来越稀少，因为解决难题需要分散的团队协作，汇集所有必要的知识。人工智能的最新进展可能会加速这一趋势，因为书本知识变得越来越容易获取，但那些不成文的实践经验仍然局限于封闭的专家群体中。获取知识所蕴含的环境，往往比学习本身更能阻碍人们掌握知识。

Do: The Necessity of Practice

实践的必要性

Being able to learn from others is only the first step. Skill requires practice, not just observation. Practice plays a number of important roles in learning. The first is that repeated practice reduces the mental effort to perform tasks. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), researchers observed the brain activity of Tetris players as they gained experience with the game. Contrary to the expectation that using more of your brain equals greater performance, players’ neuronal activity decreased as they played more. This broadly supports the idea that, through repeated play, the players had become more efficient in using their nervous system. If you’ve driven a car for years, you have probably noticed something similar. What was previously an effortful task that required your full attention now can be done unthinkingly. Your mind wanders elsewhere while your hands and feet go through the motions. The ability to automate component skills is a key factor in the performance of many complex tasks, and is one of the reasons why we can’t simply perform at an expert level merely from watching someone else do it.

能够向他人学习仅仅是第一步。技能的习得需要练习，而不仅仅是观察。练习在学习过程中扮演着诸多重要角色。首先，反复练习可以降低完成任务所需的脑力消耗。研究人员利用功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）观察了俄罗斯方块玩家在游戏经验积累过程中的大脑活动。与人们通常认为大脑活动越多表现越好的预期相反，玩家的神经元活动随着游戏时间的增加而降低。这有力地支持了这样一种观点：通过反复练习，玩家的神经系统使用效率得到了提升。如果你开车多年，你可能也注意到了类似的现象。以前需要全神贯注、费力才能完成的任务，现在可以毫不费力地完成。你的思绪会飘向别处，而你的手脚则自动完成操作。自动化执行各项技能是完成许多复杂任务的关键因素，这也是为什么我们不能仅仅通过观看他人操作就达到专家水平的原因之一。

Another reason for practice is the importance of memory retrieval. Watching someone perform a skill is often necessary to figure out how to do it. But if the answer is always available when we practice for ourselves, we may not remember it deeply. If you’re old enough to remember an era before cell phones, you probably memorized a few dozen phone numbers you called regularly. Today, despite seeing the number every time you hit the dial button, you may struggle to recall a single phone number other than your own. The difference is that, before contacts were saved directly on our phones, every call forced you to retrieve the number from memory. Retrieval beats review for strengthening your memory.

练习的另一个原因是记忆提取的重要性。观看别人演示一项技能通常是学习其方法的必要步骤。但如果我们自己练习时答案总是唾手可得，我们就可能无法将其牢记于心。如果你年纪足够大，还记得手机出现之前的时代，你可能记住了几十个经常拨打的电话号码。如今，尽管每次拨号时都能看到号码，但除了自己的号码之外，你可能很难想起其他任何电话号码。区别在于，在联系人直接保存到手机之前，每次通话都迫使你从记忆中提取号码。提取比复习更能强化记忆。

Finally, while we’re fantastic imitators, many parts of a skill cannot be emulated. How the arm moves in a tennis serve or how the wrist flicks in a brushstroke can certainly be observed. But everyone’s musculature is unique, so these observations are only approximations of how you must perform the skill yourself. Perceptual skills like discriminating patterns in an X-ray or predicting the path of a golf ball rolling down a green have large tacit components that can’t be easily communicated, even with a patient teacher. Hands-on practice is essential to master the aspects of skills that can’t be taught in a book.

最后，虽然我们都是出色的模仿者，但许多技能的要素是无法完全复制的。网球发球时手臂的运动方式，或者画笔挥动手腕的动作，当然都可以观察。但每个人的肌肉结构都是独一无二的，因此这些观察只能近似地告诉你如何才能真正掌握这项技能。像辨别X光片中的图案或预测高尔夫球在果岭上的滚动轨迹这类感知技能，包含大量难以言喻的隐性成分，即使是耐心细致的老师也难以传授。实践操作对于掌握那些无法从书本中学习到的技能至关重要。

The necessity of action in learning creates its own obstacles. It’s more effortful to actively practice than to passively watch a video, so it’s easy to lean toward consumption rather than action. Access to the real environment for performing the skill may be limited. It’s hard to get good as a pilot without a plane or as a filmmaker without a camera. Finally, the balance between learning from others and doing it for yourself can be tricky to find with complex skills. Too little support, and learning is frustrating trial and error. Yet too much can be harmful too, as when seeing a pattern preempts our ability to retrieve it. We don’t always make this choice correctly. Researchers have found that low-ability students benefit from more structured environments, so they can learn problem-solving patterns they don’t yet have in memory, while high-ability students benefit more from less structured environments, where they can get more realistic practice and are forced to retrieve knowledge they already possess. Yet students prefer the method of learning that works worse for them! An explanation for this perverse tendency is that learning is effortful and we try to conserve effort. Low-ability students find the demands made by the structured approach taxing, and so opt for the flexibility to avoid meeting a rigorous standard. In contrast, high-ability students find the added structure easier and so prefer following the recipe rather than generating the right answer on their own. Fine-tuning the difficulty matters greatly for learning, and we don’t always get it right.

学习中行动的必要性本身就构成了障碍。主动练习比被动观看视频更费力，因此人们很容易倾向于被动接受而非主动行动。练习技能所需的真实环境也可能受到限制。没有飞机就很难成为一名优秀的飞行员，没有摄像机就很难成为一名优秀的电影制作人。最后，对于复杂的技能而言，在向他人学习和自主学习之间找到平衡点可能很棘手。支持太少，学习就会变成令人沮丧的反复试错。然而，支持过多也可能有害，因为看到某种模式会让我们无法提取它。我们并非总能做出正确的选择。研究人员发现，能力较弱的学生更能从结构化环境中获益，这样他们就能学习到记忆中尚未掌握的问题解决模式；而能力较强的学生则更能从结构化程度较低的环境中获益，在这种环境中，他们可以获得更真实的练习，并被迫提取他们已经掌握的知识。然而，学生们却更倾向于选择对他们效果最差的学习方法！这种反常倾向的一种解释是，学习需要付出努力，而我们总是试图节省精力。能力较弱的学生觉得结构化教学方法的要求过高，因此他们倾向于选择灵活的方式来避免达到严格的标准。相反，能力较强的学生则觉得结构化教学更容易，因此他们更喜欢按部就班地完成任务，而不是独立思考得出正确答案。难度的精准把控对学习至关重要，而我们并非总能做到这一点。

Feedback: Adapting with Experience

反馈：从经验中适应

Repeated practice isn’t enough. Without feedback, improvement is often impossible. As early as 1931, psychologist Edward Thorndike had subjects practice drawing lines of a particular length. Despite performing the skill three thousand times (in what must have been a riveting experiment), subjects failed to make any progress. The expert of expertise, psychologist Anders Ericsson, developed the concept of deliberate practice to explain how elite performers in music, chess, athletics, and medicine were able to reach peak levels. The presence of immediate feedback was central to this conception. Just as high-quality, immediate feedback underlies the progressively deepening skill of elite athletes and musicians, its absence can also explain deteriorating performance. In a systematic review, researchers found that the quality of medical care tended to decline as doctors spent more time on the job. Patient outcomes only depend partly on doctor’s interventions, and the difference between best practices and outdated techniques is often only possible to spot in carefully controlled trials. This spotty feedback means it can be difficult to engage in the kind of deliberate practice Ericsson argued is central to continuing mastery.

反复练习并不足以取得进步。没有反馈，进步往往无从谈起。早在1931年，心理学家爱德华·桑代克就让受试者练习画特定长度的线条。尽管他们练习了三千次（这无疑是一项引人入胜的实验），受试者却毫无进展。心理学家安德斯·埃里克森作为该领域的专家，提出了刻意练习的概念，用以解释音乐、国际象棋、体育和医学等领域的精英如何达到巅峰水平。即时反馈是这一概念的核心。正如高质量的即时反馈是精英运动员和音乐家技能不断提升的基础一样，缺乏反馈也会导致他们的表现下滑。在一项系统性综述中，研究人员发现，随着医生工作时间的延长，医疗质量往往会下降。患者的治疗结果仅部分取决于医生的干预，而最佳实践与过时技术之间的差异通常只有在精心控制的试验中才能显现出来。这种零散的反馈意味着很难进行埃里克森所说的对持续精进至关重要的刻意练习。

We can accelerate our progress by creating better systems for feedback. During the Vietnam War, both the Navy and Air Force were losing a fighter plane for every two enemy planes taken down. To improve this, the Navy created the Navy Fighter Weapons School, also known as the Top Gun program. This involved simulated sorties where trainees flew against the best possible pilots. After each encounter, their performance was reviewed in depth, with each decision discussed in an after-action report. The result was that while the Air Force’s success in taking down enemy fighters continued to be two-to-one, the Navy jumped up to twelve-to-one, a sixfold improvement. Ericsson reported an experiment run with foreign exchange traders in a European bank that experienced similar performance improvements from the competitive simulations with after-action feedback. Being able to design more valid, informative feedback into your improvement efforts can be the difference between progress and stagnation.

我们可以通过建立更完善的反馈系统来加速进步。在越南战争期间，海军和空军每击落两架敌机，自身就会损失一架战斗机。为了改善这一状况，海军创建了海军战斗机武器学校，也就是著名的“壮志凌云”计划。该计划包括模拟飞行任务，让受训人员与最优秀的飞行员进行对抗。每次交锋后，他们的表现都会被深入分析，每个决策都会在事后报告中进行讨论。结果是，尽管空军击落敌机的成功率仍然是二比一，但海军的这一比例跃升至十二比一，提高了六倍。爱立信公司报告称，他们在欧洲一家银行的外汇交易员中进行了一项实验，结果显示，通过事后反馈的竞争性模拟，他们的绩效也得到了类似的提升。能够在改进工作中设计出更有效、更有价值的反馈机制，是进步与停滞的关键所在。

Why Learning Still Matters

为什么学习仍然重要

Separate from the worry about whether improvement is possible is the worry that learning may soon be obsolete. As I write this, sophisticated computer programs can now write poems, explain quantum mechanics, and illustrate pictures in any artistic style, on demand. Assuming such technological progress continues, what will be the point of mastering skills that can be performed effortlessly through silicon chips? But the rise of technological change is just as likely to create a demand for new learning as it is to undermine old abilities. The invention of paper was decried by Socrates for degrading the faculty of memory, but the outcome was an explosion of knowledge that no individual could hope to memorize in a single lifetime. Information technology has rendered some jobs nearly obsolete, even as it has invented new ones that did not exist before. In a paper authored by Massachusetts Institute of Technology economist David Autor and colleagues, the researchers found that roughly 60 percent of the jobs people had in 2018 didn’t exist in 1940. While technology may have reduced the demand for typists and telephone operators, it also created an explosion of software developers and business analysts. A reasonable extrapolation of past technological trends would suggest that advances in artificial intelligence will result in greater demands for learning, not less. Predictions are hard, especially about the future. * And so I will avoid speculating on which exact skills and knowledge will end up as essential for future generations. However, insights into the process of learning, and how we can make it more successful, are likely to become more relevant, not less.

除了担忧是否有可能进步之外，还有人担心学习很快就会过时。就在我写这篇文章的时候，复杂的计算机程序已经可以按需创作诗歌、解释量子力学，并以任何艺术风格绘制插图。假设这种技术进步持续下去，那么掌握那些可以通过硅芯片轻松完成的技能还有什么意义呢？但是，技术变革的兴起既有可能催生对新学习的需求，也有可能削弱旧有的能力。纸张的发明曾被苏格拉底斥为削弱记忆力，但其结果是知识的爆炸式增长，任何人都不可能在一生中全部记住。信息技术使一些工作几乎过时，同时也创造了以前不存在的新工作。麻省理工学院经济学家大卫·奥特及其同事在一篇论文中发现，2018年人们从事的工作中，约有60%在1940年并不存在。虽然科技发展可能减少了对打字员和电话接线员的需求，但也催生了软件开发人员和商业分析师的激增。根据以往的技术发展趋势合理推断，人工智能的进步将导致对学习的需求增加，而不是减少。预测很难，尤其是对未来的预测。* 因此，我不会妄加揣测哪些技能和知识最终将成为未来几代人的必备技能。然而，对学习过程的洞察，以及如何提高学习效率，很可能会变得更加重要，而不是不那么重要。

A Curious Quest

一次奇妙的探索

I’ve long been fascinated by learning. In 2019, I published my book Ultralearning , diving into the strange world of obsessive autodidacts, and drawing upon some of my own experiences learning languages, programming, and art. But curiosity is a strange drive. Unlike hunger or thirst, curiosity is stoked, not sated, when we learn more. And so, despite spending years both striving to learn new skills, and trying to make sense of the academic research behind skill development, I ended up embarking on a new quest to try to resolve questions my previous efforts left unanswered. A couple hundred books and several hundred academic papers later, I’ve found satisfying explanations for some of my earlier puzzles. But, in keeping with all quests of curiosity, new questions have multiplied in their place. This book is, in many ways, an effort to make sense of what I’ve found.

我一直对学习充满热情。2019年，我出版了《超速学习》一书，深入探索了痴迷自学者的奇妙世界，并借鉴了我自己学习语言、编程和艺术的一些经验。但好奇心是一种奇特的驱动力。与饥饿或口渴不同，当我们学习更多时，好奇心只会更加强烈，而不会得到满足。因此，尽管我多年来一直努力学习新技能，并试图理解技能发展背后的学术研究，最终我还是踏上了新的征程，试图解答我之前努力未能解答的问题。在阅读了数百本书和数百篇学术论文之后，我终于找到了一些早期谜题的令人满意的解释。但是，正如所有好奇心探索一样，新的问题也随之而来。这本书在很多方面都是为了理解我所发现的一切。

I wrote this book with two audiences in mind. First, I wanted to write from the learner’s perspective. If you want to get better at anything, how should you do it? What kinds of examples should you seek? What kind of practice works best? What influences whether you’ll attain mastery or plateau early on? Secondarily, I wanted to examine how teachers, coaches, parents, and those responsible for shaping learning within an organization can cultivate improvement. Since the birth of my two curious learners, I’ve become keenly interested in what I can do as a father to guide them in becoming the best they can be. Good teachers are precious, and the science underlying successfully fostering skill development is not widely known. Above all, I wrote this book for people like me—those interested in getting better, but not always sure the best way to proceed.

我写这本书时考虑到了两个读者群体。首先，我想从学习者的角度出发。如果你想在任何方面有所进步，应该怎么做？应该寻找什么样的例子？哪种练习方法最有效？什么因素会影响你最终能否精通，还是会很快停滞不前？其次，我想探讨教师、教练、家长以及组织内负责塑造学习的人员如何才能促进进步。自从我的两个求知欲旺盛的孩子出生以来，我便开始认真思考，作为父亲，我能做些什么来引导他们发挥出最大的潜能。优秀的教师弥足珍贵，而成功培养技能背后的科学原理却鲜为人知。最重要的是，我写这本书是为了像我一样的人——那些渴望进步，却又常常不知如何迈向成功之路的人。

What to Expect from This Book

本书内容简介

Over the next twelve chapters, we’ll dive deeper into the three themes of seeing, doing, and feedback. Improvement may not always come easily, but we can all think more intelligently about how we learn. Each chapter is expressed as a simple maxim. My hope is that long after the details of the research explored in each chapter have faded, these rules of thumb will serve as both a reminder and a useful—if imperfect—summary of the key principles.

接下来的十二章，我们将深入探讨“观察”、“实践”和“反馈”这三个主题。进步或许并非一帆风顺，但我们都可以更明智地思考学习方式。每一章都以一句简洁的格言概括。我希望，即便每章探讨的研究细节逐渐淡去，这些经验法则仍能起到提醒作用，并作为对关键原则的实用（即便并不完美）总结。

Maxims one through four are about the power of examples:

第一至第四条箴言都强调了例子的力量：

  1. Problem Solving Is Search. We’ll begin with a mathematical mystery that lasted for over three centuries, and the groundbreaking theory of problem solving that can help us understand its resolution. We’ll explore the difference between routine and creative thinking, and how what we learn from others greatly shapes the complexity of problems we can solve.
    解决问题就是探索。我们将从一个持续了三个多世纪的数学谜题入手，探讨有助于我们理解其解法的开创性问题解决理论。我们将探索常规思维和创造性思维之间的区别，以及我们从他人身上学到的东西如何极大地影响我们能够解决的问题的复杂性。
  2. Creativity Begins with Copying. Next, we’ll dive into artistic training during the Renaissance. Imitation—far from being opposed to creativity—is the seed for original work. We’ll explore the mind’s bottleneck, and how the best strategies for acquiring knowledge often differ from the processes used to generate new ideas.
    创造力始于模仿。接下来，我们将深入探讨文艺复兴时期的艺术训练。模仿——远非与创造力对立——而是原创作品的种子。我们将探索思维的瓶颈，以及获取知识的最佳策略为何往往与产生新想法的过程有所不同。
  3. Success Is the Best Teacher. Sophisticated skills depend on having the proper foundation. When the building blocks are missing, learning is slow and frustrating. Experiencing genuine successes early in the learning process can make motivation self-reinforcing.
    成功是最好的老师。精湛的技能离不开扎实的基础。如果缺少必要的基础，学习就会缓慢而令人沮丧。在学习初期体验到真正的成功，能够使学习动力自我强化。
  4. Knowledge Becomes Invisible with Experience. Finally, we’ll explore the curse of knowledge, or how expertise leads to a receding awareness of the basis of our own proficiency. Expert intuition, while powerful, often makes it more difficult to acquire complex skills, as capable performers lose the ability to explain how they do it. To remedy this difficulty, we’ll explore a family of tools to extract the knowledge experts take for granted.
    经验使知识变得隐形。最后，我们将探讨知识的诅咒，即专业技能如何导致我们对自身能力基础的认知逐渐减弱。专家的直觉虽然强大，但往往会使掌握复杂技能变得更加困难，因为能力出众的人会逐渐失去解释自己如何做到的能力。为了解决这一难题，我们将探索一系列工具，以提取专家习以为常的知识。

Maxims five through eight deal with improving our practice:

第五至第八条箴言旨在改进我们的实践：

  1. The Difficulty Sweet Spot. Progress depends on finding a delicate balance between making practice too hard or too easy. We’ll explore research showing when difficulties can be desirable . . . as well as when they are not. We’ll look at the writer’s paradox—or, why the best writers seem to suffer from the most writer’s block. We’ll examine several tools for fine-tuning the difficulty level of your improvement efforts, from progressive problem solving to constructing a practice loop.
    难度的最佳平衡点。进步取决于在练习难度上找到一个微妙的平衡点，既不能太难，也不能太容易。我们将探讨相关研究，了解何时需要增加难度……以及何时需要增加难度。我们将探究写作悖论——或者说，为什么最优秀的作家似乎最容易遇到写作瓶颈。我们将研究几种微调练习难度的工具，从渐进式问题解决到构建练习循环。
  2. The Mind Is Not a Muscle. What improves when we practice a skill? Despite its enduring appeal as an analogy, the metaphor that the mind is like a muscle is highly flawed, as shown by over a century of research. Research on the transfer of learning will help us understand when strengthening one ability will lead to improved performance in another.
    大脑并非肌肉。练习一项技能究竟能提升什么？尽管“大脑如同肌肉”这一比喻经久不衰，但一个多世纪的研究表明，这种比喻存在诸多缺陷。学习迁移的研究将有助于我们理解，强化一项能力何时能够提升另一项能力。
  3. Variability Over Repetition. Next, we’ll dig into the development of improvisational abilities among jazz musicians. How do players create complex performances without repeating themselves? In answering this question, we’ll explore the science showing how practice variability can lead to more flexible skills.
    变化胜于重复。接下来，我们将深入探讨爵士乐手即兴演奏能力的培养。乐手们如何在不重复自身的情况下创作出复杂的演奏？为了解答这个问题，我们将探索相关的科学研究，这些研究表明，练习方式的变化能够带来更灵活的技能。
  4. Quality Comes from Quantity. Genius is prolific. In this chapter, I’ll explore research showing how, to a surprising extent, creativity simply is productivity. Those who produce the best work are almost invariably those who produce the most work. We’ll look at the implications of this for your own efforts to make an impact.
    质量源于数量。天才往往高产。在本章中，我将探讨一些研究，这些研究表明，在很大程度上，创造力其实就是生产力。那些创作出最优秀作品的人，几乎无一例外都是创作最多作品的人。我们将探讨这对于你如何努力产生影响有何启示。

Maxims nine through twelve revolve around the role of feedback:

第九条至第十二条准则都围绕反馈的作用展开：

  1. Experience Doesn’t Reliably Ensure Expertise. Practice doesn’t make perfect. Indeed, without the right kind of feedback, practice often doesn’t even make us very good. In this chapter, we’ll look at learning in environments of uncertainty. We’ll compare poker players, who manage to master a complex game despite wild swings of luck, with the more typical case where decades of professional experience lead to mediocre predictions. Drawing on these differences, I’ll offer suggestions on how we might tame unfriendly learning environments.
    经验并不能可靠地确保精通。练习并不能造就完美。事实上，如果没有正确的反馈，练习往往甚至无法让我们变得非常优秀。在本章中，我们将探讨如何在不确定的环境中学习。我们将对比那些尽管运气起伏不定却能精通复杂游戏的扑克玩家，与那些拥有数十年职业经验却预测能力平庸的普通人。基于这些差异，我将提出一些建议，帮助我们更好地应对不利的学习环境。
  2. Practice Must Meet Reality. In this chapter, we’ll explore the reckoning from the worst aviation disaster in history. What we learn in a classroom has a complex relationship to what is practiced in the field. True proficiency requires contact with the physical and social settings where a skill will be used.
    实践必须与现实相符。本章我们将探讨历史上最严重的航空灾难所带来的反思。课堂所学与实际操作之间存在着复杂的关系。真正的熟练掌握需要与技能应用的实际环境（包括物理环境和社会环境）进行接触。
  3. Improvement Is Not a Straight Line. Getting better often first requires getting worse. In many subjects, we come equipped with intuitions that bear little resemblance to proven scientific theories. As we progress, improvement comes to depend on rooting out misconceptions, inefficiencies, and mistakes.
    进步并非一帆风顺。往往进步的第一步是经历退步。在许多领域，我们凭借直觉形成的观点与已被证实的科学理论相去甚远。随着学习的深入，进步最终取决于我们能否根除误解、低效做法和错误。
  4. Fears Fade with Exposure. Finally, I’ll shift from learning skills to the anxieties that often surround them. We’ll look at the surprising effectiveness of exposure therapy in overcoming fear, and why many of the intuitive strategies we develop to cope with our anxieties backfire. Courage, not just cleverness, is essential for mastery.
    恐惧会随着暴露疗法而消退。最后，我将从学习技能转向探讨伴随这些技能而来的焦虑。我们将探讨暴露疗法在克服恐惧方面令人惊讶的有效性，以及为什么我们许多用来应对焦虑的直觉策略会适得其反。勇气，而不仅仅是聪明才智，才是掌握技能的关键。

Finally, in the conclusion, I’ll step back from the research and discuss how you can integrate these ideas in your own practice. Whether you’re studying for an exam, needing to learn a new skill at work, or just want to get better at something you’re interested in, I hope these suggestions will provide a starting point for thinking about how you might do it better.

最后，在结论部分，我将跳出研究本身，探讨如何将这些理念融入到你的实践中。无论你是在备考、需要在工作中学习新技能，还是仅仅想在自己感兴趣的领域有所建树，我都希望这些建议能为你思考如何做得更好提供一个起点。

To start, let’s look at the science of problem solving, by looking at the story of a puzzle that took over three hundred and fifty years to resolve.

首先，让我们通过一个耗时三百五十年才得以解决的谜题的故事，来了解解决问题的科学。

Learning from Others

Chapter 1

第一章

Problem Solving Is Search

问题解决即搜索

Whenever one cannot go from the given situation to the desired situation simply by action, then there has to be recourse to thinking.

当一个人无法仅通过行动从现状过渡到理想状态时，就必须诉诸思考。

—Psychologist Karl Duncker

——心理学家卡尔·邓克

  • How do people solve hard problems?
    人们如何解决难题？
  • Are there generic methods that work on all kinds of problems?
    是否存在适用于所有类型问题的通用方法？
  • How do we solve problems that no one has ever solved before?
    我们如何解决以前从未有人解决过的问题？

I have a truly marvelous proof of this, which this margin is too narrow to contain.” In that one sentence, Pierre de Fermat created a mystery that would perplex mathematicians for over three centuries. It stumped the great Leonhard Euler. Almost a century after the enigmatic mathematician’s death, Euler begged a friend to rummage around his old house, hoping some scrap of a proof remained. It fooled the mathematicians Augustin Cauchy and Gabriel Lamé, who briefly claimed to have discovered a proof, before a fatal flaw in their logic was uncovered. German industrialist Paul Wolfskehl put up a prize of one hundred thousand marks to anyone who could resolve the riddle. Yet despite their best efforts, the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem remained a mystery.

“我有一个非常精妙的证明，可惜这页空白太窄，写不下。” 费马的这句话，就为数学家们留下了一个长达三个多世纪的谜团。就连伟大的莱昂哈德·欧拉也束手无策。在费马去世近一个世纪后，欧拉恳求一位朋友在他以前的房子里翻找，希望能找到一些证明的蛛丝马迹。数学家奥古斯丁·柯西和加布里埃尔·拉梅也曾一度声称发现了证明，但最终他们的逻辑漏洞被揭穿。德国实业家保罗·沃尔夫斯克尔悬赏十万马克，奖励任何能够解开这个谜题的人。然而，尽管费马大定理的证明始终是个谜。

Fermat’s claim is easy to understand, even if it isn’t easy to prove. Pythagoras tells us that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is the sum of the square of the lengths of the other two sides: a 2 + b 2 = c 2 . If you play around with it, you can find whole numbers that fit the equation. The numbers 3, 4, and 5 do the trick (9 + 16 = 25); so do 5, 12, and 13 (25 + 144 = 169). In fact, there are an infinite number of these Pythagorean triples, so called because the ancient Greek himself showed they were limitless. But what if you changed the equation, adding cubes instead of squares? Could you find any three whole numbers that fit the pattern? Fermat said you couldn’t. In fact, he argued, if you took any exponent higher than two, you would always fail. Stated mathematically, Fermat argued the equation a n + b n = c n had no whole number solutions for n greater than two.

费马的论断很容易理解，即使证明起来并不容易。毕达哥拉斯告诉我们，在直角三角形中，斜边的平方等于另外两直角边的平方之和：a + b = c。如果你仔细推敲，就能找到符合这个等式的整数。例如，3、4 和 5 满足条件（9 + 16 = 25）；5、12 和 13 也满足条件（25 + 144 = 169）。事实上，毕达哥拉斯三元组有无穷多个，之所以称之为“毕达哥拉斯三元组”，是因为古希腊人毕达哥拉斯本人证明了它们的无穷无尽。但是，如果你改变等式，用立方代替平方呢？你能找到任意三个符合这个规律的整数吗？费马说你找不到。事实上，他认为，如果指数大于2，则方程总是会失败。用数学术语来说，费马论证了方程a<sub>n</sub> + b<sub>n</sub> = c<sub>n</sub>对于大于2的n没有整数解。

Figure 2

图 2

Two squares can be added up to make another square: 3 2 + 4 2 = 5 2 . But two cubes will never make a perfect cube. Here, for instance, 6 3 + 8 3 = 9 3 –1.

两个正方形可以相加得到另一个正方形：3 2 + 4 2 = 5 2 。但是两个立方体永远不可能相加得到一个完全立方数。例如，6 3 + 8 3 = 9 3 –1。

Andrew Wiles first heard of the enigma of Fermat’s Last Theorem when he was ten years old. “It looked so simple yet all the great mathematicians in history couldn’t solve it,” he reflected upon his first encounter. “I knew from that moment I would never let it go.” Wiles went to school, graduated from Cambridge University, and specialized in a branch of mathematics known as elliptic curves. Fermat’s final puzzle never strayed far from Wiles’s thoughts as he established his career. Still, having bested mathematicians for centuries, he could see no path forward to finding a proof.

安德鲁·怀尔斯十岁时第一次听说了费马大定理的谜题。“它看起来如此简单，但历史上所有伟大的数学家都无法解开它，”他回忆起第一次接触时说道，“从那一刻起，我就知道我永远不会放弃它。”怀尔斯上学后毕业于剑桥大学，专攻椭圆曲线这一数学分支。在他建立职业生涯的过程中，费马的最后一个难题始终萦绕在他的脑海中。然而，尽管几个世纪以来数学家们都束手无策，他仍然找不到证明它的方法。

This changed in 1984. Mathematician Gerhard Frey suggested an unexpected link between Fermat’s Last Theorem and a famous conjecture made by a duo in Japan. Yutaka Taniyama and Goro Shimura had argued that two seemingly distant branches of the mathematical tree were actually twisted together. Every modular form, they argued, had a counterpart in an elliptic curve. The conjecture had been a workhorse for mathematicians, with many papers tentatively assuming it for their conclusion. Still, it was no more than a suspicion. Frey’s contribution was an even more surprising connection: if the Taniyama-Shimura conjecture was true, so was Fermat’s Last Theorem. Wiles, already a specialist in elliptic curves, had finally found a path to realizing his childhood dream. All he had to do was prove Taniyama and Shimura’s hunch was correct.

1984年，情况发生了改变。数学家格哈德·弗雷提出了费马大定理与日本两位数学家提出的一个著名猜想之间出人意料的联系。谷山丰和志村五郎认为，数学树上两个看似毫不相干的分支实际上是相互交织的。他们指出，每一个模形式在椭圆曲线中都有对应的形式。这个猜想一直是数学家们的常用工具，许多论文都曾尝试将其作为结论。然而，它始终只是一种猜想。弗雷的贡献则揭示了一个更加令人惊讶的联系：如果谷山-志村猜想成立，那么费马大定理也成立。怀尔斯，这位椭圆曲线专家，终于找到了实现儿时梦想的途径。他所要做的就是证明谷山和志村的猜想是正确的。

Wiles chose to work in total secrecy. Having accumulated some publishable work, he decided to drip it out in a series of papers, creating the impression he was still actively working on old projects. He stopped going to conferences and cut his teaching duties to the bone. Every moment he wasn’t at work or with family, he was working on the proof. Adopting a risky strategy, he was isolating himself from the help of colleagues. He claimed the solitude increased his focus. Still, it probably didn’t escape his notice that if he worked on the problem alone, he wouldn’t have to compete for glory if he uncovered the proof.

威尔斯选择完全秘密地进行研究。他积累了一些可以发表的成果后，决定分批发表，以一系列论文的形式呈现，给人一种他仍在积极研究旧项目的假象。他不再参加学术会议，并将教学任务缩减到最低限度。除了工作和陪伴家人之外，他的每一分每一秒都在研究证明。他采取了一种冒险的策略，将自己与同事隔绝开来。他声称这种独处能让他更加专注。然而，他或许也意识到，如果他独自研究这个问题，一旦他发现了证明，就无需与他人争夺荣誉。

Wiles’s first eighteen months were spent at the library, learning every piece of mathematics related to modular forms and elliptic curves. An adventurer wandering into an uncharted jungle, he needed to equip his toolkit for any possibility. After mastering the essentials, he explored the math on his own, looking for patterns that might suggest a path to a proof. After two years of solitary work, he made his first breakthrough. He found a way to demonstrate that the first element of each modular form was linked to the first element of every elliptic curve. Now he had only an infinity of elements left to go.

怀尔斯最初的十八个月都泡在图书馆里，学习所有与模形式和椭圆曲线相关的数学知识。他就像一个探险家，踏入一片未知的丛林，必须为任何可能的情况做好准备。掌握了基础知识后，他开始独自探索数学，寻找可能指向证明的规律。经过两年的独自钻研，他取得了第一个突破。他找到了一种方法，证明每个模形式的第一个元素都与每个椭圆曲线的第一个元素相关联。现在，他只剩下无穷多个元素需要证明了。

Hitting an impasse, he probed his colleagues for help, careful not to reveal the nature of his project. Maybe they knew of some yet-unpublished mathematics that escaped Wiles’s notice? His old advisor, John Coates, mentioned work done by one of his students, Matheus Flach, extending the technique of another mathematician, Victor Kolyvagin. “It seemed to be exactly what I needed,” Wiles recalled, “although I knew I would still have to further develop this Kolyvagin-Flach method.” Wiles was close, but “it involved a lot of sophisticated machinery that I wasn’t really familiar with. There was a lot of hard algebra which required me to learn a lot of new mathematics.” Wiles finally decided to break his silence. Confiding in his friend and fellow mathematician Nick Katz, he got the pointers to finish his proof. After seven years of effort, Wiles succeeded where no mathematician had in over three centuries. “It was the most important moment of my working life,” Wiles reflected in a BBC documentary made about his triumph, “Nothing I ever do again will mean as much.”

陷入僵局后，他向同事寻求帮助，小心翼翼地不透露自己项目的性质。或许他们知道一些尚未发表、威尔斯尚未注意到的数学成果？他的老导师约翰·科茨提到了他的学生马修斯·弗拉赫的工作，弗拉赫扩展了另一位数学家维克托·科利瓦金的技术。“这似乎正是我需要的，”威尔斯回忆道，“尽管我知道我仍然需要进一步发展科利瓦金-弗拉赫方法。”威尔斯已经接近成功，但“它涉及许多我并不熟悉的复杂机制。其中有很多艰深的代数知识，需要我学习大量的新数学。”威尔斯最终决定打破沉默。他向朋友兼数学家尼克·卡茨倾诉，卡茨给了他完成证明的指导。经过七年的努力，威尔斯取得了三百多年来数学家都未能取得的成就。 “那是我职业生涯中最重要的一刻，”威尔斯在BBC为他拍摄的一部纪录片中回忆道，“我以后所做的任何事情都不会有那么大的意义。”

How People Solve Hard Problems

人们如何解决难题

Few challenges are as tricky as Fermat’s Last Theorem. Yet Wiles’s story reveals much about the thinking behind solving hard problems. In 1972, the cognitive scientists Herbert Simon and Allen Newell published a landmark book, Human Problem Solving , investigating those mental processes. In their research, they asked participants to share what they were thinking about as they solved problems. Comparing their performance to a model, the duo made rigorous observations about how people work through tricky puzzles. Their discoveries kicked off decades of research and have been applied in domains as diverse as chess, writing, science, mathematics, and medicine.

很少有难题能像费马大定理那样棘手。然而，怀尔斯的故事却揭示了解决难题背后的思维模式。1972年，认知科学家赫伯特·西蒙和艾伦·纽厄尔出版了里程碑式的著作《人类问题解决》，深入探讨了这些心理过程。在他们的研究中，他们要求参与者分享他们在解决问题时的思考过程。通过将他们的表现与一个模型进行比较，两人对人们如何解决棘手难题进行了严谨的观察。他们的发现开启了数十年的研究，并被应用于国际象棋、写作、科学、数学和医学等众多领域。

Central to Simon and Newell’s theory was the idea that problem solving is a search through a problem space. A problem space is like a maze: You know where you are now and you can tell whether or not you’ve reached the destination. Along the way, however, you’re constrained by walls that limit how you can move. What makes a maze difficult is that you can’t just walk straight to the finish, but need to search to find the twisted path that reaches the exit.

西蒙和纽厄尔理论的核心思想是，解决问题的过程就是在问题空间中进行搜索。问题空间就像一个迷宫：你知道自己现在在哪里，也能判断是否到达了目的地。然而，在前进的过程中，你会受到限制，被墙壁束缚，无法自由移动。迷宫的难点在于，你不能直接走到终点，而是需要不断搜索，才能找到通往出口的曲折路径。

In a maze, the problem space is a physical one. But problem spaces are typically abstract. Consider trying to solve a Rubik’s Cube. The starting position is the scrambled cube. The finished position has only one color on each side. The moves you can make are the twists and turns of the cube. The problem space here isn’t a literal space, but a space of configurations. Each spin changes the state of the problem into an adjacent one. The goal, as with the maze, is to navigate this abstract space and get from the start to the finish.

在迷宫中，问题空间是实际存在的物理空间。但问题空间通常是抽象的。以解魔方为例。初始状态是打乱的魔方。最终状态是每个面都只有一种颜色。你可以做的就是转动魔方。这里的问题空间并非一个实际存在的物理空间，而是一个由各种状态构成的空间。每次转动魔方都会改变问题的状态，使其变为相邻的状态。与迷宫一样，目标是在这个抽象空间中穿行，最终从起点到达终点。

Proving Fermat’s Last Theorem was also a search through a problem space. In Wiles’s case, he had to pick a starting point of previously proven mathematical theorems. His end goal was to write the statement that a n + b n = c n had no solutions for n greater than two. What made the task difficult was the requirement that each move in the problem space be a valid deduction from previous results. The constraints of logic worked like the walls of the maze preventing Wiles from writing down whatever he’d like. Wiles had to chart a path through the twisted corridors of mathematics to a statement confirming Fermat was right.

证明费马大定理也是一次在问题空间中的探索。对怀尔斯而言，他必须从已证明的数学定理中选择一个起点。他的最终目标是写出这样的命题：当 n 大于 2 时，方程组 a n + b n = c n 无解。这项任务的难点在于，问题空间中的每一步都必须是对先前结果的有效推导。逻辑的约束就像迷宫的墙壁，阻止怀尔斯随意写下任何内容。怀尔斯必须沿着数学曲折的路径，最终找到一条证实费马大定理正确的命题。

Once you get used to seeing them, it’s easy to spot problem spaces everywhere. Scientists search through a problem space to discover new laws. The starting point is a confusing set of data. The ending point is a theory that explains the data. Solving a problem involves searching through both a space of hypotheses that might explain the data and a space of possible experiments that can test the theory. An architect designing a building is searching a problem space of possible designs, looking for one that fits the constraints of cost, space, and building codes, while trying to optimize its functional and aesthetic value. Writing this chapter was a problem-solving process. My starting point was a blank document. The end goal was a finished chapter, explaining the ideas I wanted to present.

一旦你习惯了观察它们，就会发现问题空间无处不在。科学家们在问题空间中探索，以发现新的规律。起点是一组令人困惑的数据，终点是能够解释这些数据的理论。解决问题既需要探索可能解释数据的假设空间，也需要探索能够检验理论的实验空间。建筑师设计建筑时，也是在可能的设计方案问题空间中寻找方案，既要满足成本、空间和建筑规范的限制，又要尽可能优化其功能和美学价值。撰写本章也是一个解决问题的过程。我的起点是一份空白文档，最终目标是完成一个章节，阐述我想要表达的观点。

The Tricky Thing About Hard Problems

难题的棘手之处

Simon and Newell’s formulation of problem solving has an immediate consequence: most problems are not solvable. The space of possibilities is too large to find a solution. Without a clever method, random guessing would never work. A Rubik’s Cube has over forty-three quintillion configurations. Exploring them one by one, even for only one second each, would require five thousand times the age of the universe. Yet Wiles’s task was to chart a course in waters incomparably vaster. While a computer program can be written to mechanically solve a Rubik’s Cube, it is impossible, even in principle, to build such a device that can prove any piece of mathematics. The mathematician, armed with finite knowledge, must navigate an infinite sea with no guarantee of arriving safely on the other shore. Wiles himself was aware of the likelihood of failure: “Perhaps the methods I needed to complete the proof would not be invented for a hundred years. So even if I was on the right track, I could be living in the wrong century.”

西蒙和纽厄尔提出的问题解决理论直接得出了一个结论：大多数问题都是无解的。可能性的空间太大，根本无法找到解决方案。如果没有巧妙的方法，随机猜测是行不通的。一个魔方有超过4300亿亿种不同的排列组合。即使每种组合只探索一秒钟，也需要宇宙年龄的五千倍。然而，怀尔斯的任务是在无比浩瀚的海洋中寻找方向。虽然可以编写计算机程序来机械地解魔方，但即使在理论上，也不可能制造出能够证明任何数学命题的装置。数学家凭借有限的知识，必须在无垠的海洋中航行，却无法保证能够安全抵达彼岸。怀尔斯本人也意识到失败的可能性：“也许我完成证明所需的方法要一百年后才会被发明出来。所以，即使我的方向是对的，我也可能生活在错误的世纪。”

If most problem spaces are too big to search through, how do we cope? Simon’s answer was that we “satisfice”: instead of choosing the best possible solution, we go with one that is good enough. A manager doesn’t explore every possibility and piece of information before making an urgent business decision. Instead, she searches until she finds a good enough option, given her limited time and attention. But satisficing has two major drawbacks. The first is that, in choosing the option that is good enough, we may never learn the better option. For unique problems this may not be an issue. But if we expect to face the same problem again and again, our tendency to go with whatever works in the moment may limit our eventual progress. The person who solves a typing problem by hunting and pecking on the keyboard with one finger will manage just fine, but that will also make it harder to learn the touch-typing method. The second drawback is that even finding an acceptable solution can be quite difficult. In Wiles’s search, he may have been willing to satisfice on the elegance or length of the proof, but certainly not on its mathematical rigor. A proof that was somewhat clunky or verbose might have been good enough, but certainly not one that violated the rules of logic.

如果大多数问题领域过于庞大，无法逐一搜索，我们该如何应对？西蒙的答案是“满意原则”：我们不选择最佳方案，而是选择一个足够好的方案。管理者在做出紧急业务决策之前，不会去探索每一种可能性和每一条信息。相反，在有限的时间和精力下，她会搜索直到找到一个足够好的选项。但满意原则有两个主要缺陷。首先，选择足够好的方案可能会让我们永远无法了解更好的方案。对于独特的问题，这或许不是问题。但如果我们预期会反复遇到相同的问题，那么我们倾向于选择当下有效的方案，这可能会限制我们最终的进步。用一根手指在键盘上“一指一指”解决打字问题的人或许也能应付，但这也会使他们更难学习盲打。第二个缺陷是，即使是找到一个可以接受的解决方案也可能相当困难。在怀尔斯的探索中，他或许愿意在证明的优雅或简洁程度上妥协，但绝不会在其数学严谨性上妥协。一个略显笨拙或冗长的证明或许足够好，但绝不能违背逻辑规则。

Beyond lowering our standards, another way that we reduce our problem-solving difficulty is by using knowledge to constrain our search to more fruitful directions. At an extreme, this eliminates problem solving entirely. I don’t need to conduct a problem-solving search to figure out 5 + 7. I simply remember that the answer is 12. In a similar way, much of our daily life is problem-free because we have saved the solution in memory. Driving a car, making a doctor’s appointment, or doing our laundry is not a problem for most adults because they remember the path to a solution. However, you might still remember a time when figuring out how to use a washing machine was a genuine puzzle. Where do you put the detergent? Which clothes go together and which need to be separated? Experience transforms problems into routines.

除了降低标准之外，我们降低问题解决难度的另一种方法是利用知识将搜索范围缩小到更有效的方向。极端情况下，这甚至完全消除了问题解决的过程。我不需要进行问题解决式的搜索就能算出 5 + 7，我只需要记住答案是 12。同样地，我们日常生活中的许多事情之所以顺利，是因为我们已经把解决方案保存在了记忆中。开车、预约医生或洗衣服对大多数成年人来说都不是问题，因为他们记得解决问题的路径。然而，你可能仍然记得，曾经弄明白如何使用洗衣机是一个真正的难题。洗衣液应该放在哪里？哪些衣服应该放在一起洗，哪些需要分开洗？经验将问题转化为惯例。

In some cases, memory can provide a method, even if it can’t provide an answer. I can’t recall the answer to 128 + 47 directly. However, by following the multi-digit addition algorithm I learned in grade school, I can easily arrive at the answer 175. Not all problems have such convenient algorithms. This fact came as a surprise to mathematicians. In 1900, the mathematician David Hilbert posed a list of twenty-three questions he hoped to see resolved in the coming century. One was an algorithm for figuring out whether equations like the one in Fermat’s Last Theorem had whole-number solutions. Seventy years later, mathematicians proved that no such algorithm can exist! For other problems, there is a method that can be guaranteed to find a solution, but it isn’t much better than the strategy of simply trying out every possibility. Sudoku, chess, and even Tetris can all be shown to belong to this class of problems. Our experience with classroom problems may be deceiving, therefore, as the vast majority of real-life problems have no method that ensures the right answer.

在某些情况下，记忆可以提供方法，即使它无法直接给出答案。我无法直接回忆起 128 + 47 的答案。然而，通过运用小学时学过的多位数加法算法，我可以轻松得出答案 175。并非所有问题都有如此便捷的算法。这一事实令数学家们感到惊讶。1900 年，数学家大卫·希尔伯特提出了 23 个问题，他希望这些问题能在未来一个世纪得到解决。其中一个问题是寻找一种算法，用于判断像费马大定理这样的方程是否存在整数解。70 年后，数学家们证明，这样的算法根本不存在！对于其他一些问题，虽然存在一种可以保证找到解的方法，但它并不比尝试所有可能性的策略好多少。数独、国际象棋，甚至俄罗斯方块，都可以被证明属于这类问题。因此，我们在课堂问题上的经验可能会具有欺骗性，因为绝大多数现实生活中的问题都没有方法可以保证得到正确答案。

Even if a method can’t promise a solution, it can still reduce the amount of searching. Heuristics are methods that offer no guarantees but may work decently in many cases. Facing tech troubles, one heuristic is simply to turn the device off and turn it back on again. This won’t always work, but it does solve the problem in a surprising proportion of cases. Wiles had no textbook algorithm he could apply—the refutation of Hilbert’s tenth problem showed there weren’t any. Yet he had many heuristics he had acquired through years of study and practice doing math. Applying proof by induction, for instance, is a relatively general mathematical strategy whenever you want to prove that a property holds for an infinite number of things. All you need to do is show that it holds for the first thing, and then show that the property doesn’t change as you move from one thing to the next. Like knocking over a row of dominos, this trick allows you to prove something is true for an infinite number of items without actually checking an infinite number of times. This heuristic was essential for linking each element of the elliptic curve in Wiles’s proof with each element of a modular form.

即使一种方法不能保证一定能找到解决方案，它仍然可以减少搜索量。启发式方法就是不提供任何保证，但在许多情况下却能取得不错的效果的方法。例如，遇到技术故障时，一个启发式方法就是简单地关闭设备再重新启动。这种方法并非总是有效，但在相当一部分情况下确实能够解决问题。怀尔斯并没有现成的算法可以应用——他对希尔伯特第十问题的反驳就证明了根本不存在这样的算法。然而，他通过多年的数学学习和实践积累了许多启发式方法。例如，归纳法是一种相对通用的数学策略，当你想证明某个性质对无穷多个事物都成立时，就可以使用这种方法。你只需要证明这个性质对第一个事物成立，然后证明当你从一个事物过渡到下一个事物时，这个性质不会改变。就像推倒一排多米诺骨牌一样，这个技巧让你无需实际检查无穷多次就能证明某个性质对无穷多个事物都成立。这种启发式方法对于将怀尔斯证明中的椭圆曲线的每个元素与模形式的每个元素联系起来至关重要。

Another common mathematical heuristic is to look for an invariant. If you can find something that doesn’t change in a problem, no matter how you modify it, you can avoid a lengthy problem-solving search. Consider the problem of the mutilated chessboard. In this problem, you’re asked whether you can lay dominos to perfectly cover a chessboard that has the top-left and bottom-right squares removed.

另一种常见的数学启发式方法是寻找不变量。如果你能找到一个无论如何修改问题都不会改变的变量，就可以避免冗长的解题过程。考虑一下残缺棋盘问题。在这个问题中，你需要问的是，能否用多米诺骨牌完美地覆盖一个左上角和右下角被移除的棋盘。

Given the sixty-two remaining squares, and each domino covering two squares, at first blush the problem would seem to involve a lot of searching. A lot of different combinations of thirty-one dominos might need to be attempted to decide, one way or another, whether they can fit. However, if you’re clever you might look for an invariant. One such invariant is that each domino covers exactly one white and one black square, regardless of how it is placed. Once we recognize that the two squares deleted were both white, it now becomes clear why we can never tile the board—it would require a domino to go on two black squares, which we just showed was impossible. Applying the right heuristic just saved us a lengthy search.

考虑到剩下的 62 个方格，以及每张多米诺骨牌覆盖两个方格，乍一看，这个问题似乎需要大量的搜索。可能需要尝试 31 张多米诺骨牌的多种组合，才能最终确定它们是否能够铺满整个棋盘。然而，如果你足够聪明，或许可以寻找一个不变式。其中一个不变式是：无论多米诺骨牌如何摆放，它都恰好覆盖一个白色方格和一个黑色方格。一旦我们意识到被移除的两个方格都是白色，那么我们就能明白为什么永远无法铺满整个棋盘——这需要一张多米诺骨牌覆盖两个黑色方格，而我们刚刚已经证明这是不可能的。运用正确的启发式方法，我们就能省去大量的搜索。

Proof by induction and searching for an invariant are used throughout mathematics and logic. Still, they work only on a fairly narrow range of problems compared to those we might encounter in life. Understanding induction won’t help much with painting a portrait or creating a marketing plan. Psychologists call these kinds of methods domain-specific, because they apply to a circumscribed range of problems. This raises an interesting question: Are there any heuristics or strategies that work on many different kinds of problems?

数学和逻辑学中广泛运用归纳法和寻找不变量的方法。然而，与我们在生活中可能遇到的问题相比，它们适用范围相当有限。理解归纳法对绘制肖像或制定营销计划帮助不大。心理学家称这类方法为领域特定方法，因为它们仅适用于特定范围的问题。这就引出了一个有趣的问题：是否存在适用于多种不同类型问题的启发式方法或策略？

Figure 3

图 3

Is it possible to completely tile the mutilated chessboard with dominos?

是否有可能用多米诺骨牌将残缺的棋盘完全铺满？

Are There Strategies for Solving All Kinds of Problems?

是否存在解决所有类型问题的策略？

In their study of problem solving, Simon and Newell observed a number of generic problem-solving strategies that people applied to a diverse set of problems. They argued that people use these strategies as a fallback when more specific methods are unavailable. Simon and Newell called these weak methods, to contrast with the strong methods of guaranteed algorithms or domain-specific heuristics that drastically cut down the problem-solving search. These weak methods include generate-and-test, means-ends analysis, planning, and hill-climbing.

在对问题解决的研究中，西蒙和纽厄尔观察到人们会运用一些通用的问题解决策略来应对各种各样的问题。他们认为，当没有更具体的方法可用时，人们会将这些策略作为备选方案。西蒙和纽厄尔将这些策略称为弱方法，以区别于那些能够大幅缩短问题解决搜索范围的强方法，例如保证有效的算法或特定领域的启发式方法。这些弱方法包括生成测试法、手段-目标分析法、规划法和爬山法。

Weak Method #1: Generate-and-Test

弱方法一：生成并测试

The most basic strategy Simon and Newell observed in participants was to simply try something and see if it worked. If I’ve forgotten my computer log-in for an old account, I might cycle through a half-dozen passwords I know I’ve used in the past. With luck, one of them will be correct and I won’t need to go through a more extensive problem-solving attempt to reset the password. Similarly, if I can’t find my keys, I might randomly guess a few likely spots, before trying to retrace my steps. When writing an essay, I might overcome my writer’s block by simply writing anything and then editing it later. It’s likely that a random utterance isn’t going to be good prose, but the first thought generated from memory may not be half-bad, provided I already have a lot of experience with a topic. The obvious disadvantage of generate-and-test is that it is disastrous when the problem space becomes large. Generate-and-test only works when the problem is already constrained or familiar enough that guessing is likely to produce reasonable answers.

西蒙和纽厄尔观察到参与者最基本的策略就是直接尝试，看看是否有效。如果我忘记了旧账户的电脑登录信息，我可能会尝试六个以前用过的密码。运气好的话，其中一个会是正确的，这样我就不用费劲地去重置密码了。同样地，如果我找不到钥匙，我可能会先随意猜测几个可能的地方，然后再尝试回溯。写文章时，我可能会先随便写点什么来克服写作障碍，然后再进行编辑。随口写下的东西很可能写不出好文章，但如果我对某个主题已经很熟悉，那么凭记忆想到的第一个想法可能还不错。生成测试法的明显缺点是，当问题范围变大时，这种方法会非常糟糕。生成测试法只适用于问题本身已经比较有限或足够熟悉的情况，以至于猜测就能得出合理的答案。

Weak Method #2: Means-Ends Analysis

弱方法二：手段-目的分析

Another near-universal strategy observed in problem solving is means-ends analysis. This is a back-and-forth reasoning strategy that starts by first identifying gaps and then finding moves that will reduce those gaps in the problem space. Consider this example presented by Simon and Newell:

另一种在问题解决中几乎普遍存在的策略是手段-目标分析。这是一种来回推理策略，首先识别问题空间中的差距，然后寻找能够缩小这些差距的措施。请看西蒙和纽厄尔提出的这个例子：

I want to take my son to nursery school. What’s the difference between what I have and what I want? One of distance. What changes distance? My automobile. My automobile won’t work. What is needed to make it work? A new battery. What has new batteries? An auto repair shop. I want the repair shop to put in a new battery; but the shop doesn’t know I need one. What is the difficulty? One of communication. What allows communication? A telephone . . . and so on.

我想送儿子去幼儿园。我拥有的和我想要的有什么区别？区别在于距离。什么会改变距离？我的车。我的车坏了。需要什么才能修好它？一块新电池。哪里有新电池？汽车修理店。我想让修理店帮我换一块新电池；但是修理店不知道我需要换电池。难点在哪里？沟通。什么能实现沟通？电话……等等。

Means-ends analysis works by alternating between a goal, observing a difference between the current state and the goal state, and then finding a suitable method to close the distance. This can repeat in a recursive fashion, as Simon and Newell’s story illustrates.

手段-目标分析法的工作原理是：设定目标，观察当前状态与目标状态之间的差异，然后找到合适的方法来缩小差距。正如西蒙和纽厄尔的故事所示，这个过程可以递归地重复进行。

Weak Method #3: Planning

弱方法三：计划

Another general tool people use for solving problems is planning. Planning can be seen as reformulating a problem in a simpler problem space, solving it in the simpler space, and then trying to generalize that approach to the real problem space. For instance, when writing an essay I may start with an outline, which is a kind of simplified version of the essay, only including the main points I want to state and ignoring all the detail. Once I’m satisfied that I’ve solved the problem in the planning space, I can use that to guide my search in the larger space of writing the entire essay.

人们解决问题的另一个常用工具是计划。计划可以看作是将问题简化，在更简单的空间中解决问题，然后尝试将这种方法推广到实际问题空间。例如，写文章时，我可能会先列一个提纲，它是文章的简化版本，只包含我想表达的要点，而忽略所有细节。一旦我确信自己在计划空间中已经解决了问题，我就可以用它来指导我在更大的空间中寻找解决方案，从而完成整篇文章。

Weak Method #4: Hill-Climbing

弱方法四：爬山法

Suppose you’re in a large landscape, shrouded in mist, and you want to find the highest possible point. One strategy would be to simply walk in whatever direction is steepest. Hill-climbing applies this notion to problem solving. Start with a tentative solution to the problem, no matter how lousy, and then make small adjustments in the direction that improves your starting point the most. In certain classes of problems, simply following the direction of best improvement is sufficient to eventually reach the optimal point. Editing an essay is often a process of hill-climbing, as you make successive adjustments to the text in whatever way best improves the quality of the writing as a whole. Similarly, applying hill-climbing to solving a Rubik’s Cube might involve trying to increase the number of colors segregated to each side with each move. This approach fails with Rubik’s Cubes, but the fact that people often attempt it shows our built-in hill-climbing heuristic at work.

假设你身处一片广袤的、被迷雾笼罩的土地上，想要找到最高点。一种策略就是沿着最陡峭的方向前进。爬山法正是将这种概念应用于问题解决。先从一个初步的解决方案开始，无论多么糟糕，然后朝着能够最大程度改善初始状态的方向进行微调。在某些类型的问题中，只需沿着最佳改进方向前进，最终就能到达最优解。修改文章通常就是一个爬山法的过程，你需要不断地调整文本，以尽可能提高文章的整体质量。类似地，将爬山法应用于解魔方可能意味着每次移动都试图增加每个面上的颜色数量。这种方法在魔方上是行不通的，但人们经常尝试这一事实表明，我们内在的爬山启发式思维正在发挥作用。

Why Weak Methods Frequently Fail

为什么弱方法经常失败

Weak methods apply broadly, but they often fail us. Generate-and-test fails with large problem spaces. Means-ends analysis multiplies goals, which can make it harder to keep track of the problem. Planning may oversimplify the problem, leading to a solution that works on paper, but fails in practice. Hill-climbing fails in exactly those situations where things first need to be made worse, in order to be made better. What we call puzzles may themselves be the category of problems where one of our weak methods conspicuously fails, so that the only way to solve the problem is to ignore a tempting heuristic. The Tower of Hanoi puzzle involves moving disks between pegs. The overall space of the problem has only twenty-seven states, so it shouldn’t pose a serious problem even for generate-and-test. Yet the solution often takes a little practice, both because reaching the desired end state requires you to move disks away from the destination (violating hill-climbing) and necessitates many nested subgoals (making means-ends analysis more complicated).

弱方法应用广泛，但往往失效。生成测试法在大问题空间中会失败。手段-目标分析法会增加目标数量，这会使问题难以追踪。规划可能会过度简化问题，导致方案在纸面上可行，但在实践中却行不通。爬山法恰恰在那些需要先恶化才能改善现状的情况下失效。我们所谓的难题本身可能就是这类问题，在这些问题中，某种弱方法明显失效，以至于解决问题的唯一途径是忽略一个诱人的启发式方法。汉诺塔难题涉及在柱子之间移动圆盘。该问题的整体空间只有27个状态，因此即使对于生成测试法来说，它也不应该构成严重问题。然而，解决方案通常需要一些练习，这既是因为达到期望的最终状态需要将圆盘移离目标（违反了爬山法），也是因为需要许多嵌套的子目标（使手段-目标分析更加复杂）。

Figure 4

图 4

Tower of Hanoi: Goal is to move all disks from the left to right peg. Only one disk can be moved at a time. Larger disks cannot be placed on top of smaller disks.

汉诺塔：目标是将所有圆盘从左侧的柱子移动到右侧的柱子上。一次只能移动一个圆盘。较大的圆盘不能放在较小的圆盘上面。

A deeper question about weak methods is whether they are innate or acquired. Psychologists André Tricot and John Sweller argue that there is little evidence for the teachability of weak methods, showing that people tend to apply means-ends analysis or hill-climbing instinctively. In this view, general problem-solving ability is something that can be neither taught nor practiced. Accordingly, we can’t learn better methods for dealing with problems in general, but only acquire a larger library of specific skills and methods that we apply to different situations. Wiles was able to prove Fermat’s Last Theorem, not because he had extensive practice in weak methods, but because he possessed an enormous library of strong methods that drastically reduced the problem space. Yet that same knowledge would probably be of minimal use in helping him fix a car or file his taxes.

关于弱方法，一个更深层次的问题是：它们是与生俱来的还是后天习得的？心理学家安德烈·特里科和约翰·斯韦勒认为，几乎没有证据表明弱方法是可教授的，这表明人们倾向于本能地运用手段-目标分析或爬山法。在他们看来，一般的解决问题的能力既无法教授也无法练习。因此，我们无法学习更好的通用问题解决方法，而只能积累更丰富的特定技能和方法，并将其应用于不同的情境。怀尔斯之所以能够证明费马大定理，并非因为他广泛练习弱方法，而是因为他掌握了大量强方法，这些方法极大地缩小了问题的范围。然而，同样的知识在帮助他修车或报税时可能几乎毫无用处。

The Knowledge Frontier: The Two Types of Problems

知识前沿：两种类型的问题

This picture suggests we face two distinct types of difficulties in solving problems. The first kind of difficulty occurs when we face a problem that stumps us, but would be routine for someone else. This is a difficulty of learning from others. What are the strong methods experts use to solve those problems effortlessly? Without that knowledge, we’re forced to engage in a potentially lengthy and failure-prone problem-solving search. If the problem isn’t too far outside our zone of problem-solving ability, we may uncover the answer with some effort. But if the space is too large, we may never land on the best approach.

这张图表明，我们在解决问题时会面临两种截然不同的困难。第一种困难是，当我们遇到一个令我们束手无策，但对其他人来说却轻而易举的问题时。这便是向他人学习的难点。专家们是如何轻松解决这些问题的呢？如果我们缺乏这方面的知识，就只能被迫进行漫长且容易失败的寻找答案的过程。如果问题没有超出我们解决问题的能力范围太远，我们或许可以通过一些努力找到答案。但如果范围太大，我们可能永远也找不到最佳方法。

The second kind of difficulty occurs when we’re venturing into the unknown frontier beyond any individual’s problem-solving ability. This was Wiles’s challenge as he searched for the proof for Fermat’s Last Theorem. He had to find the solution to a problem that no mathematician had uncovered in over three centuries. Given his eventual path through huge swaths of the problem space that were utterly unknown to Fermat, it seems quite likely that the long-deceased Frenchman himself didn’t have a correct proof. Perhaps Fermat had uncovered a flawed proof, like Cauchy or Lamé. Or perhaps he had found an alternative route, so surprising and creative that it has gone untrodden by the best mathematical minds for hundreds of years. In either case, this knowledge died with Fermat, and so Wiles had to venture into the unknown when charting his mathematical course.

第二种困难出现在我们探索超出个人解题能力的未知领域时。怀尔斯在寻找费马大定理的证明时就面临着这样的挑战。他必须找到一个三个多世纪以来数学家都未曾发现的问题的答案。考虑到他最终探索了费马完全未知的广阔问题空间，这位早已逝世的法国人很可能也没有找到正确的证明。或许费马发现了一个有缺陷的证明，就像柯西或拉梅那样。又或许他找到了一条截然不同的路径，这条路径如此出人意料、如此富有创造性，以至于数百年来最杰出的数学家都未曾涉足。无论如何，这些知识都随着费马的逝去而失传，因此怀尔斯在探索数学道路时，不得不冒险进入未知领域。

Most of us will not embark on a problem as difficult as Wiles’s. Yet we’ll never eliminate the need for problem solving because most situations are unique. You only have to type a sentence or two before you’ve written something that has never before been uttered in human history. Every essay written, song composed, or building designed is a novel problem, and thus can’t merely be copied from solutions of the past. But even if many problems are new, the knowledge that is best served to solve them usually isn’t. Seeing further into the problem space depends on standing on the strong methods of the giants that came before us.

我们大多数人不会去挑战像威尔斯那样棘手的问题。然而，我们永远无法消除解决问题的必要性，因为大多数情况都是独一无二的。你只需敲下一两句话，就能写出人类历史上从未出现过的文字。每一篇文章、每一首歌、每一座建筑都是一个全新的问题，因此不能简单地照搬过去的解决方案。即便许多问题是新的，解决这些问题的最佳知识通常并非如此。要更深入地理解问题，就必须借鉴前人卓著的方法。

Practical Takeaways of Problem-Solving Search

问题解决搜索的实用技巧

Many psychologists doubt that problem solving, as a general ability, can be taught or practiced. The weak methods appear universal. Instead, it appears the path to mastery is through acquiring the specific knowledge and methods of the expert. Even if we can’t become better problem solvers in general, I’d nonetheless like to suggest a few practical takeaways suggested by this theory of problem solving.

许多心理学家怀疑，作为一种普遍能力，问题解决能力是否可以被教授或练习。那些看似普遍却效果不佳的方法似乎并不适用。相反，通往精通之路似乎在于习得专家的特定知识和方法。即便我们无法普遍提升问题解决能力，我仍然想根据这一问题解决理论提出一些实用建议。

Takeaway #1: Start with the Right Representation

要点一：从正确的代表开始

Search is only half of the difficulty of solving problems. The other half is in finding the right way of representing the problem, so that you know the best problem space to work in. Prior to Newell and Simon’s pathbreaking work, the Gestalt psychologists also explored problem solving, except their focus was on how experimental subjects perceived the problem and how those perceptions could inhibit or enable insightful solutions. As an example, consider the famous nine-dot puzzle. The aim is to draw four straight lines without lifting your pencil that intersect all nine dots.

搜索只是解决问题难点的一半。另一半在于找到合适的问题表征方式，从而确定最佳的解决问题空间。在纽厄尔和西蒙的开创性工作之前，格式塔心理学家也探索过问题解决，但他们的关注点在于实验对象如何感知问题，以及这些感知如何阻碍或促进富有洞察力的解决方案。例如，著名的九点拼图。目标是在不抬笔的情况下画出四条直线，使其与所有九个点相交。

Figure 5

图 5

Nine-Dot Puzzle: Draw four straight lines through all nine dots, without lifting your pencil between lines.

九点拼图：用铅笔画四条直线穿过所有九个点，画线之间不要抬笔。

Can you do it? For those who haven’t seen it before, they can view the answer in the Notes section. The key insight revolves not around how we search through the problem space, but how we represent it. If the successful answer is mistakenly excluded from the initial possibilities, we will miss it even in an exhaustive search. Problem solving in messy, real-life situations often involves switching back and forth between searching our problem space and trying to find new ways of representing the problem that may be more tractable.

你能做到吗？之前没看过的人可以在“备注”部分查看答案。关键在于我们如何搜索问题空间，而不是如何表示问题空间。如果正确的答案被错误地排除在初始可能性之外，即使进行穷举搜索，我们也会错过它。在错综复杂的现实情境中解决问题，往往需要在搜索问题空间和尝试寻找更易于处理的问题表示方法之间来回切换。

Begin any new project by finding out how competent people think about the problem. What do they view as the problem space? The major moves you can make to solve it? While knowing how to think about a problem doesn’t guarantee a solution, it is an essential first step.

启动任何新项目之前，首先要了解那些能力出众的人是如何看待这个问题的。他们认为问题的范围是什么？你可以采取哪些主要措施来解决问题？虽然了解如何思考问题并不能保证一定能找到解决方案，但这却是至关重要的第一步。

Takeaway #2: Seek Out Promising Problems

要点二：寻找有发展前景的问题
