The realization that many problems are impossible to solve suggests an immediate application: don’t work on impossible problems. Unfortunately, the problem of figuring out which problems are solvable is also unsolvable! The solution may always be just around the corner, or it might result in a century of unrewarded effort. Despite our inability to know precisely which problems are genuinely impossible, we can, with experience, make better guesses. Wiles only began working on Fermat’s Last Theorem when Gerhard Frey made the connection to the Taniyama-Shimura conjecture, as it suggested to him that the problem was ripe. Entrepreneurs, scientists, and inventors all make calculated bets on what levels of technological advances they predict in the near future, even if they cannot know exactly how far they will need to venture into uncharted regions of the problem space.

意识到许多问题根本无法解决，便可立即应用一个原则：不要在不可能解决的问题上浪费时间。然而，不幸的是，弄清楚哪些问题可解决本身也是个无解的问题！解决方案或许近在咫尺，也或许会让我们徒劳无功地奋斗一个世纪。尽管我们无法精确地知道哪些问题真的无法解决，但凭借经验，我们可以做出更准确的判断。怀尔斯之所以开始研究费马大定理，是因为格哈德·弗雷将费马大定理与谷山-志村猜想联系起来，这让他意识到这个问题已经成熟。企业家、科学家和发明家都会对他们预测的近期技术进步水平进行权衡，即使他们无法确切地知道自己需要在未知领域探索多远。

The best way to discover promising problems is to work with people who are actively pushing at the frontier. The advantage of working at firms, research labs, or in groups of people who are making new contributions is that you can get strong hints as to which aspects of the problem space are ripe for exploration and which are unlikely to immediately yield fruit.

发现有前景的问题的最佳方法是与那些积极开拓前沿的人合作。在公司、研究实验室或致力于做出新贡献的团队中工作的好处在于，你可以获得关于问题领域哪些方面值得探索以及哪些方面不太可能立即产生成果的有力线索。

Takeaway #3: Explore the Problem Space, One Room at a Time

要点三：逐个房间地探索问题空间

To explain how he approaches mathematics, Wiles draws an instructive analogy:

为了解释他如何看待数学，怀尔斯举了一个很有启发性的类比：

I could best describe my experience of doing mathematics in terms of entering a dark mansion. One goes into the first room, and it’s dark, completely dark. One stumbles around bumping into the furniture, and gradually, you learn where each piece of furniture is, and finally, after six months or so, you find the light switch. You turn it on, and suddenly, it’s all illuminated. You can see exactly where you were.

我感觉自己学习数学的经历就像走进一座漆黑的宅邸。你走进第一个房间，里面一片漆黑，伸手不见五指。你跌跌撞撞地摸索着，磕磕碰碰地撞到家具，渐渐地，你才摸清每件家具的位置，最后，大约过了六个月，你终于找到了灯的开关。你打开开关，突然间，一切都亮了起来。你清楚地看到了自己刚才身处何处。

As we’ll discuss in more detail in the next chapter, when we have no one we can learn from and must find our way in an unfamiliar problem space, it helps to first explore the space rather than solve problems. Approaching an unfamiliar branch of mathematics, Wiles not only equipped himself with mathematical tools discovered by others, but spent considerable time applying them until they became a familiar part of his repertoire.

正如我们将在下一章详细讨论的那样，当我们没有可以学习的对象，必须在一个陌生的领域中摸索前进时，先探索这个领域比直接解决问题更有帮助。怀尔斯在接触一个陌生的数学分支时，不仅学习了他人发现的数学工具，还花费大量时间应用这些工具，直到它们成为他知识体系中不可或缺的一部分。

Exploring the problem space can proceed by trying things out and observing what happens, without deliberately trying to reach particular goals. The aim here is not to accomplish anything in particular, but to pay attention to patterns that may result in new strong methods. A painter trying out different techniques to “see what happens” rather than produce a saleable work will end up with a lot of lousy compositions. But occasionally he may stumble upon a technique that gives his work a unique look.

探索问题空间可以通过尝试各种方法并观察结果来进行，而无需刻意追求特定目标。这里的目的并非达成任何具体成就，而是关注可能孕育出新方法的模式。一位画家如果尝试不同的技法只是为了“看看会发生什么”，而不是为了创作一件可以出售的作品，最终可能会得到很多糟糕的构图。但偶尔，他或许会偶然发现一种能赋予作品独特风格的技法。

From Solving Problems to Learning How to Solve Them

从解决问题到学习如何解决问题

Simon and Newell’s early work focused on how people solve difficult problems. They believed that understanding how we solve problems was a prerequisite for understanding how we learn to solve problems. Only once you know how a person is performing a skill, they reasoned, do you have much hope in figuring out how they learn to perform it. * In the next chapter, we’ll shift from how people solve problems to how they learn to solve problems. Along the way, we’ll discover how a quirk of our psychology becomes one of the most important limits on this process.

西蒙和纽厄尔早期的研究重点在于人们如何解决难题。他们认为，理解我们如何解决问题是理解我们如何学习解决问题的前提。他们推断，只有了解一个人如何运用某项技能，才能更有希望弄清楚他们是如何学习运用这项技能的。* 在下一章中，我们将从人们如何解决问题转向他们如何学习解决问题。在此过程中，我们将发现我们心理上的一个特殊之处如何成为这一过程最重要的限制因素之一。

# ↩

Chapter 2

第二章

Creativity Begins with Copying

创造力始于模仿

Rules are not the fetters of genius. They are the fetters of men with no genius.

规则不是天才的枷锁，而是庸人的枷锁。

—Joshua Reynolds, painter

——约书亚·雷诺兹，画家

  • Can you solve a problem without learning how to solve it?
    你能在不学习如何解决问题的情况下解决问题吗？
  • How much of creativity comes from borrowing others’ ideas?
    创造力有多少来自于借鉴他人的想法？
  • Does imitation lead to a shallow understanding?
    模仿会导致理解肤浅吗？

I n November 2017, records were shattered when Leonardo da Vinci’s Salvator Mundi sold for over $450 million. This more than doubled the previous record-high price for a painting, when Pablo Picasso’s Woman of Algiers sold for slightly below $180 million in 2015. A Da Vinci selling for astronomical sums isn’t surprising. The artist left few completed paintings in his lifetime. Those that exist are universally recognized as masterpieces, from the immense crowds drawn daily to the Mona Lisa at the Louvre, or his enigmatic depiction of The Last Supper . Nor is Da Vinci alone in veneration. Botticelli, Raphael, Titian, Caravaggio, and Michelangelo all rightfully deserve the status of master painters. Although we tend to fixate on their genius, I’d instead like to turn to their training.

2017年11月，达·芬奇的《救世主》以超过4.5亿美元的价格售出，打破了多项纪录。这一价格是此前绘画作品最高成交价的两倍多，此前的最高纪录是毕加索的《阿尔及尔的女人》，该画作于2015年以略低于1.8亿美元的价格售出。达·芬奇的作品拍出天价并不令人意外。这位艺术家生前完成的画作寥寥无几。而他留下的作品，无论是卢浮宫每天吸引无数游客的《蒙娜丽莎》，还是他那充满神秘色彩的《最后的晚餐》，都堪称举世公认的杰作。达·芬奇并非唯一一位备受尊崇的艺术家。波提切利、拉斐尔、提香、卡拉瓦乔和米开朗基罗也都当之无愧地享有大师级绘画的地位。尽管我们往往关注他们的天赋，但我更想探讨一下他们的艺术训练。

Artistic training in the Renaissance followed an apprenticeship model. At twelve or thirteen, novices would submit themselves to a master’s workshop. Italian painter Cennino Cennini describes the process at the turn of the fifteenth century:

文艺复兴时期的艺术训练遵循学徒制模式。十二三岁的初学者会进入一位大师的工作室学习。意大利画家切尼诺·切尼尼在十五世纪初描述了这一过程：

Know that there ought not to be less time spent in learning than this: to begin as a shopboy studying for one year, to get practice in drawing on the little panel; next, to serve in a shop under some master to learn how to work at all the branches which pertain to our profession . . . for the space of a good six years. Then to get experience in painting, embellishing with mordants, making cloths of gold, getting practice in working on the wall for six more years; drawing all the time, never leaving off, either on holidays or on workdays. And in this way your talent, through much practice, will develop into real ability.

要知道，学习的时间不应少于此：先当一年学徒，在小木板上练习绘画；然后，在师傅的指导下，在店铺里学习所有与本行相关的技艺……至少六年。之后，再花六年时间，学习绘画、使用媒染剂装饰、制作金丝织物，以及在墙上作画；并且要时时练习绘画，无论节假日还是工作日，都不能停歇。如此，你的天赋，通过大量的练习，才能发展成为真正的技艺。

Apprentices proceeded through a structured sequence of both subjects and media to slowly introduce themselves to the skills of the craft. First was copying masterworks. This enabled a novice to closely study how an adept translated light and form into marks on a panel. Next was drawing from plaster casts of sculptures. This added the difficulty of translating a three-dimensional object into a two-dimensional representation, but avoided the challenges of a live model who might move around during a sitting. By the time apprentices worked from life, their mastery of the fundamentals was secure enough that all their attention could be paid to subtleties such as posture or expression. Artistic media went through a similar progression, from charcoal drawings, to grisaille paintings done in shades of black and white, and finally to full color in oil or tempera paints.

学徒们循序渐进地学习各种主题和媒介，逐步掌握绘画技巧。首先是临摹大师作品。这使初学者能够仔细观察大师如何将光影和形体转化为画板上的笔触。接下来是根据雕塑的石膏模型进行绘画。这增加了将三维物体转化为二维图像的难度，但避免了真人模特在摆姿过程中可能移动带来的挑战。当学徒们开始写生时，他们对基本功的掌握已经足够扎实，可以专注于姿态或表情等细微之处。绘画媒介的学习也经历了类似的演进过程，从炭笔画，到黑白灰阶绘画，最终到油画或蛋彩画等全彩绘画。

Copying from masterworks formed the backbone of artistic instruction. Da Vinci himself argues for the proper sequence of study: “ Of the order of learning to draw: first draw from drawings by masters done from works of art,” only then, “having acquired that practice, under the criticism of his master, he should next practice drawing objects in relief of a good style.” The idea of spending considerable time copying seems antithetical to modern perceptions of artistic training. Artists are supposed to be fountains of originality and drills are alleged to kill the creative spirit. Yet despite the imitativeness of the training, artists of the periods in which such methods were widespread often produced work of breathtaking originality. Even though the Renaissance-era training methods were apparently successful, they are largely out of fashion today. To understand why, we need to briefly review the history in the evolution of artistic training methods.

临摹大师作品是艺术教学的核心。达·芬奇本人也论证了正确的学习顺序：“学习绘画的顺序是：首先临摹大师根据艺术作品所作的素描”，然后，“在老师的指导下，熟练掌握了这种技巧之后，才能练习绘制风格优美的浮雕作品。” 花费大量时间临摹的想法似乎与现代艺术训练的理念背道而驰。艺术家被认为是原创性的源泉，而刻板的练习则被认为会扼杀创造力。然而，尽管这种训练方式带有模仿的成分，但在文艺复兴时期，艺术家们往往创作出令人叹为观止的原创作品。尽管文艺复兴时期的训练方法看似成功，但如今却已基本过时。为了理解个中缘由，我们需要简要回顾一下艺术训练方法的发展历程。

A Brief History of Artistic Training

艺术训练简史

The history of art education in the West begins in Greece. The ancient Greeks celebrated art, but not the artist. Visual arts were the province of an artisanal class that was barely above the slaves who upheld an aristocratic society. Poetry and philosophy were the proper study for a member of the elite; painting was not. This attitude persisted through the Middle Ages, when the artistic production was controlled by the guild system. Only in the Renaissance, with the arrival of painters like Da Vinci and Michelangelo, did the status of individual artists begin to rise above that of mere craftworkers. Instrumental to this shift in perception was Renaissance painter and art historian Giorgio Vasari. His major book, Lives of the Most Excellent Painters, Sculptors and Architects , created the image of the artist as an intellectual, on par with scholars and philosophers. To that end, Vasari convinced Cosimo de’ Medici to found the first art academy in Florence in 1561.

西方艺术教育史始于古希腊。古希腊人推崇艺术，却不推崇艺术家本身。视觉艺术是工匠阶层的专属领域，他们的地位仅略高于维系贵族社会的奴隶。诗歌和哲学才是精英阶层的恰当学习对象，绘画则不然。这种观念一直延续到中世纪，当时的艺术生产由行会制度控制。直到文艺复兴时期，随着达·芬奇和米开朗基罗等画家的出现，艺术家的地位才开始超越普通工匠。文艺复兴时期的画家兼艺术史学家乔治·瓦萨里对这种观念的转变起到了至关重要的作用。他的代表作《最杰出的画家、雕塑家和建筑师传》将艺术家塑造成与学者和哲学家同等重要的知识分子形象。为此，瓦萨里说服科西莫·德·美第奇于1561年在佛罗伦萨创立了第一所艺术学院。

Yet this elevation of the status of the artist had a paradoxical effect on the craft. As historian of art education Arthur Efland writes, “ When the artist rose to the position of genius, new educational questions presented themselves, for how does one instruct a genius? Is it appropriate to train the potential genius like a lowly apprentice?” This tension grew during the Romantic movement. Philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau writes of his suggested artistic training regimen: “ So I shall take good care not to provide him with a drawing master, who would only set him to copy copies and draw from drawings. Nature should be his only teacher, and things his only models.” In the nineteenth century, this attitude would be further exaggerated by Viennese art educator and champion of the creative self-expression movement Franz Cižek. “ Cižek has been compared to Rousseau in his insistence on avoiding all adult influence, but in some sense Cižek was more extreme,” Efland writes. “Rousseau recognized some need for adult guidance, while Cižek’s class was not taught at all in the usual sense of teaching.” This tension between craftsmanship and creativity, which was largely absent in Da Vinci’s time, persists today. “ In our arts climate,” artist and educator Juliette Aristides writes, “historical education and art training are often considered antithetical to genius. Rising artists are frequently expected to tap their knowledge directly from the ether, disconnected from history and labor. However, when the instincts of the individual are elevated above education, the artist can become stuck in a perpetual adolescence where his passion outstrips his ability to perform.”

然而，艺术家地位的提升却对艺术创作产生了矛盾的影响。正如艺术教育史学家亚瑟·埃夫兰德所写：“当艺术家被奉为天才时，新的教育问题便随之而来：如何培养天才？像训练卑微的学徒一样训练潜在的天才是否合适？”这种矛盾在浪漫主义运动时期愈演愈烈。哲学家让-雅克·卢梭在其提出的艺术训练方案中写道：“因此，我将谨慎地不给他安排绘画老师，以免他只会临摹和临摹画作。自然应该是他唯一的老师，万物应该是他唯一的模特。”到了十九世纪，维也纳艺术教育家、创意自我表达运动的倡导者弗朗茨·齐泽克进一步强化了这种观点。埃夫兰德写道：“齐泽克因坚持避免一切成人影响而被拿来与卢梭相提并论，但在某种程度上，齐泽克更为极端。”卢梭意识到需要成人的指导，而齐泽克的课堂则完全不是传统意义上的教学。这种工艺与创造力之间的张力，在达·芬奇时代几乎不存在，但如今依然存在。“在当今的艺术氛围中，”艺术家兼教育家朱丽叶·阿里斯蒂德斯写道，“历史教育和艺术训练常常被认为与天才背道而驰。人们常常期望崭露头角的艺术家能够直接从虚空中汲取知识，而无需接触历史和劳动。然而，当个人的本能凌驾于教育之上时，艺术家可能会陷入一种永无止境的青春期，他们的热情远远超过了他们的创作能力。”

Patiently learning from examples, before creating original work, was central to a classical artistic education. Yet the power of examples is not limited to artistic skills. Somewhat surprisingly, cognitive psychologists have found that, in some situations, studying an example can lead to more useful skills than solving the same problem on your own.

在创作原创作品之前，耐心地从范例中学习是古典艺术教育的核心。然而，范例的力量并不局限于艺术技能。令人颇感意外的是，认知心理学家发现，在某些情况下，研究范例比独立解决同样的问题更能带来实用的技能。

Can You Solve a Problem Without Learning How to Solve It?

你能在不学习如何解决问题的情况下解决问题吗？

“ A first principle not recognized by scientific methodologists,” wrote the great psychologist B. F. Skinner, is, “when you run into something interesting, drop everything to study it.” Such a maxim might have been on John Sweller’s mind when, in the early 1980s, the psychologist encountered some odd results from his experiments. “[We were] running an experiment on problem solving, testing undergraduate students,” Sweller reflected. “The problems required students to transform a given number into a goal number where the only two moves allowed were multiplying by 3 or subtracting 29.” A puzzle might be to go from 15 to 16, for instance, which would require first multiplying by three to yield 45 and then subtracting 29 to get to 16. “Each problem had only one possible solution and that solution required an alternation of multiplying by 3 and subtracting 29 a specific number of times,” Sweller explained. “My undergraduates found these problems relatively easy to solve with very few failures, but there was something strange about their solutions. While all problems had to be solved by this alternation sequence . . . very few students discovered the rule,” Sweller wrote. “Whatever the problem solvers were doing to solve the problems, learning the alternating solution sequence rule did not play a part.”

伟大的心理学家B·F·斯金纳曾写道：“科学方法论家们没有意识到的一条基本原则是：当你遇到有趣的事情时，放下一切去研究它。” 20世纪80年代初，心理学家约翰·斯威勒在实验中遇到了一些奇怪的结果，当时他可能也想到了这条格言。“我们当时正在进行一项关于问题解决能力的实验，测试对象是本科生，”斯威勒回忆道，“这些问题要求学生将给定的数字转换成目标数字，而允许的运算只有两种：乘以3或减去29。” 例如，一个难题可能是将15转换成16，这需要先乘以3得到45，然后再减去29得到16。“每个问题都只有一个可能的解，而这个解需要交替进行乘以3和减去29的特定次数，”斯威勒解释道。 “我的本科生们发现这些问题相对容易解决，失败的案例很少，但他们的解法却有些奇怪。虽然所有问题都必须用这种交替顺序来解决……但很少有学生发现了这条规则，”斯威勒写道。“无论解题者们用什么方法解决问题，学习交替解题顺序规则似乎都没有起到作用。”

How could students solve a problem, but not learn the method they used for solving it? This was shortly after Herbert Simon and Allen Newell’s treatise on problem solving, discussed in the previous chapter. Building on their work, Sweller’s investigation found a potential culprit: means-ends analysis. This was one of the weak methods Simon and Newell had found in many of their studies, the back-and-forth spotting of gaps between your current position and the ends you’d like to reach, as well as finding means to close those gaps. This strategy works, but it requires you to keep many aspects of the problem in mind simultaneously. This mental overhead might not leave enough capacity for generalizing the procedures for solving similar problems in the future. “It seemed plausible to me that the same processes might apply when students were asked to solve problems in an educational context,” Sweller reflected. “ Perhaps we should be showing students how to solve problems rather than having them solve the problems themselves?”

学生怎么可能解决问题，却不学习解决问题的方法呢？这发生在赫伯特·西蒙和艾伦·纽厄尔关于问题解决的专著发表之后不久，我们在前一章中讨论过这个问题。斯韦勒的研究在此基础上，发现了一个潜在的罪魁祸首：手段-目标分析。西蒙和纽厄尔在他们的许多研究中都发现，这种方法存在缺陷，即反复寻找当前状态与目标之间的差距，并寻找弥合这些差距的方法。这种策略虽然有效，但要求你同时考虑问题的诸多方面。这种认知负担可能会让你没有足够的精力去概括解决类似问题的程序。“在我看来，当要求学生在教育环境中解决问题时，同样的流程可能也适用，”斯韦勒反思道，“或许我们应该向学生展示如何解决问题，而不是让他们自己去解决问题？”

This suggested to Sweller an experiment: if you could somehow suppress means-ends analysis, students would have more cognitive capacity left over to learn from their actions. Sweller and his colleagues tested his hunch in a series of experiments, including one using trigonometry puzzles. These puzzles involving angles and line lengths typically have several unknown quantities. They’re also mentally taxing for beginners. Finding the missing quantity requires a lot of means-ends analysis. Sweller split students up into two groups. One was given standard find-the-missing-angle problems. The other group was given the same puzzles but with the advice to find as many unknown quantities as they could. Without a distant goal, students no longer needed to engage in means-ends analysis, and could freely explore the problem space. After a brief practice session, Sweller gave the students a novel problem. Instead of trying to find missing angles in a diagram, he asked them to draw a diagram, given a description of the values of the sines and cosines. This was done to test how well students understood the patterns within the trigonometry puzzles, rather than just memorizing a response. The results weren’t even close—eight of the ten students in the goal-free condition managed to solve the novel geometry problem, while only three in the traditional problem-solving condition did.

这启发了斯韦勒进行一项实验：如果能够以某种方式抑制学生的手段-目标分析，他们就能腾出更多认知资源来从自己的行动中学习。斯韦勒和他的同事们通过一系列实验验证了他的这一想法，其中一项实验使用了三角函数谜题。这些涉及角度和线段长度的谜题通常包含多个未知量，而且对初学者来说也颇具挑战性。找到缺失的量需要大量的手段-目标分析。斯韦勒将学生分成两组。一组学生做标准的求未知角度题，另一组学生做同样的谜题，但被告知要尽可能多地找出未知量。由于没有了远期目标，学生不再需要进行手段-目标分析，可以自由地探索问题空间。经过短暂的练习后，斯韦勒给学生们布置了一个新问题。他没有让他们尝试在图表中找到缺失的角度，而是让他们根据正弦和余弦值的描述画出图表。这样做是为了测试学生对三角函数谜题中规律的理解程度，而不仅仅是死记硬背答案。结果差距悬殊——在无目标条件下，十名学生中有八名成功解决了新的几何问题，而在传统解题条件下，只有三名学生做到了。

Goal-free problems free up the heavy cognitive toll imposed by means-ends analysis but they have an obvious drawback. When the problem space is too large, people easily get lost. Sweller found an alternative in the form of worked examples. A worked example is a problem with a solution, and all the intervening steps that the solver went through to reach the answer. Sweller again tested his hunch, this time with algebra problems. One group studied worked examples for algebra problems pairing a worked-out solution with an immediate problem of the same type. Another group solved the problems themselves, without the examples. Any student from the problem-solving group who failed to find the answer after five minutes was shown a worked example, just as in the first group. This ensured that members of the problem-solving group wouldn’t underperform simply because they didn’t figure out as many answers as the worked examples group. When a test of similar problems was presented, both groups performed about equally. Yet, when a novel question format was presented, 75 percent of the worked example group was able to solve it, while none of the problem-solving group could. This was despite the fact that the problem-solving group had spent three times as long in training.

无目标问题虽然减轻了手段-目的分析带来的沉重认知负担，但其缺点也很明显：当问题空间过大时，人们很容易迷失方向。斯威勒找到了一个替代方案，即提供例题。例题是指包含答案的问题，以及解题者得出答案的所有步骤。斯威勒再次验证了他的想法，这次他选择了代数题。一组学生学习代数题的例题，例题中包含一个已解答的问题和一个同类型的实际问题。另一组学生则不参考例题，直接解题。对于解题组中五分钟后仍未找到答案的学生，会像第一组一样，向他们展示一个例题。这样就确保了解题组的学生不会因为解题数量少于例题组而表现不佳。当进行类似题目的测试时，两组学生的表现基本相同。然而，当出现一种新的题型时，75%的例题练习组能够解答，而问题解决组却无人能够解答。尽管问题解决组的训练时间是例题练习组的三倍。

The goal-free and worked-example effects showed up repeatedly in experiments, but they went against the prevailing intuitions at the time. “It was the worst possible time to be publishing papers calling into question the efficacy of using problem-solving as a learning device,” Sweller recounted. Following Simon and Newell’s work, the study of problem solving had reached new heights in psychology and artificial intelligence. “ Most of the field leapt on the problem-solving bandwagon. The research on worked-examples was treated with hostility, or more commonly, ignored, a state of affairs that lasted about two decades.”

无目标效应和例题效应在实验中反复出现，但这与当时的普遍直觉相悖。“在那个时候发表质疑问题解决作为学习手段有效性的论文，简直是最糟糕的时机，”斯韦勒回忆道。在西蒙和纽厄尔的研究之后，问题解决的研究在心理学和人工智能领域达到了新的高度。“该领域的大多数学者都纷纷涌向问题解决领域。对例题的研究则遭到敌视，或者更常见的是被忽视，这种情况持续了大约二十年。”

While Sweller’s research may have been initially controversial, the property of the mind he based his findings on was not. Researchers have known for the better part of a century that the mind is fantastically limited in the amount of information it can hold on to simultaneously. This history of our understanding of the mind’s bottleneck begins with the number seven, plus or minus two.

尽管斯威勒的研究最初可能引发争议，但他的研究结论所依据的思维特性却并非如此。近一个世纪以来，研究人员早已认识到，思维能够同时处理的信息量极其有限。我们对思维瓶颈的理解，其历史可以追溯到数字七，上下浮动二。

The Magical Number Seven, Plus or Minus Two

神奇的数字七，加减二

“ I have been persecuted by an integer,” wrote the Harvard psychologist George Miller in the opening of his now-famous 1956 paper. “This number assumes a variety of disguises, being sometimes a little larger and sometimes a little smaller than usual, but never changing so much to be unrecognizable.” Miller presented a variety of seemingly unrelated experiments revealing his magical number seven, plus or minus two. Ask people to distinguish tones based on pitch, for instance, and people do quite well when there are only two or three to separate. Beyond six, however, people increasingly make mistakes. The same effect occurs for loudness, with only about five different volumes being distinguishable. Yet the magic number doesn’t just show up when classifying sounds. It occurs when study participants are asked to judge the saltiness of water in a taste test, the area of squares perceived visually, or variations in hues. Nor is the number limited to perceptual discrimination. Memory experiments show the same falloff for performance when subjects have to remember more than seven items, whether those items be digits, numbers, or words. The magic number, Miller argued, was more than just an experimental coincidence, but pointed to a fundamental limit in the number of things we can keep in mind at the same time. Thinking had a bottleneck and Miller had provided evidence for how wide it was. *

“我一直被一个整数所困扰，”哈佛大学心理学家乔治·米勒在他那篇如今广为人知的1956年论文的开篇写道。“这个数字会以各种伪装出现，有时比通常略大，有时略小，但变化之大却始终无法辨认。”米勒展示了一系列看似无关的实验，揭示了他神奇的数字——七，正负二。例如，如果让人们根据音调来区分不同的音调，当只有两三个音调需要区分时，人们的表现相当不错。然而，超过六个之后，人们的错误率就会显著上升。响度也存在同样的情况，人们只能区分大约五种不同的音量。然而，这个神奇的数字并非只出现在声音分类中。当研究参与者被要求在味觉测试中判断水的咸度、视觉感知到的正方形面积或色调的变化时，它同样会出现。而且，这个数字也不仅限于感知辨别。记忆实验表明，当受试者需要记住超过七个项目时，无论这些项目是数字、文字还是单词，他们的表现都会出现同样的下降。米勒认为，这个神奇的数字不仅仅是实验上的巧合，它还指向了我们同时能够记住的事物数量的根本极限。思维存在瓶颈，而米勒提供的证据证明了这个瓶颈有多宽。*

Observations such as Miller’s led to a number of theories for how the mind processes information. This included a proposal by psychologists Richard Atkinson and Richard Shiffrin in 1968 that came to be known as the modal model of human memory. Their model suggested that we process sensory information—sights from our eyes, sounds from our ears, and sensations from our bodies—simultaneously, but that all this diversity of information must squeeze through a central bottleneck in order to become active in our thoughts. This short-term storage was also connected to our long-term memory, a repository of lifelong knowledge and experience that lay dormant, until we actively recalled its contents. Later, the psychologists Alan Baddeley and Graham Hitch proposed a theory of working memory, combining the short-term storage of the modal model with the ability to manipulate and transform its contents. All thinking occurred in this narrow window of awareness, filtering out most of the outside world of sensations, as well as the deep histories of our past experience.

像米勒这样的观察催生了许多关于大脑如何处理信息的理论。其中包括心理学家理查德·阿特金森和理查德·希夫林于1968年提出的“模态模型”。该模型认为，我们同时处理感官信息——眼睛接收到的视觉信息、耳朵接收到的声音以及身体接收到的感觉——但所有这些信息必须通过一个中央瓶颈才能进入我们的思维。这种短期存储也与我们的长期记忆相连，长期记忆是储存终身知识和经验的仓库，它处于休眠状态，直到我们主动回忆其内容。后来，心理学家艾伦·巴德利和格雷厄姆·希奇提出了工作记忆理论，将模态模型的短期存储与操纵和转换其内容的能力结合起来。所有思维都发生在这个狭窄的意识窗口内，过滤掉了大部分外部世界的感觉信息以及我们过去经验的深层历史。

If thinking is so constrained, how can we possibly function? In his original paper, Miller pointed to one possibility for loosening the constraint. His experiments observed that the bottleneck was limited to the number of items, not the amount of information they contained. For instance, consider trying to keep track of the letters N U F H S B L A I. Most people would struggle to keep all of them in mind at once. But reorganize them to be FBI, USA, and NHL and most people would have little difficulty remembering the Federal Bureau of Investigation, United States of America, and National Hockey League. Both representations have the same letters, but the latter was reorganized into meaningful chunks. Those chunks, tied together through past experience, allowed you to easily keep track of nine letters, at the high upper bound of Miller’s magic number. We overcome our limited working memories by assembling increasingly complex patterns of information. Because each pattern only requires one slot, the working memory demands for an expert are quite different than the strain on a novice, even for exactly the same problem and solution method.

如果思维如此受限，我们又如何运作呢？米勒在其最初的论文中指出了一种突破这种限制的可能性。他的实验观察到，瓶颈在于项目的数量，而非它们所包含的信息量。例如，假设你要记住字母 N U F H S B L A I。大多数人很难同时记住所有这些字母。但如果将它们重新排列成 FBI、USA 和 NHL，大多数人就能轻松记住美国联邦调查局、美国和国家冰球联盟。两种表示方式都使用了相同的字母，但后者被重新组织成了有意义的信息块。这些信息块通过过去的经验联系在一起，使你能够轻松记住九个字母，这几乎是米勒提出的“神奇数字”的上限。我们通过构建越来越复杂的信息模式来克服工作记忆的局限性。由于每个模式只需要一个存储槽，即使面对完全相同的问题和解决方法，专家和新手的工作记忆需求也截然不同。

In 1995, Anders Ericsson and Walter Kintsch proposed another way around the mind’s bottleneck. Experience may allow us to make more efficient use of our long-term memory when dealing with short-term tasks. In Atkinson and Shiffrin’s model, long-term memory is a near-infinite repository, storing every memory of our lives. Unlike the bottleneck of working memory, long-term memory is a vast reservoir. Yet most of our long-term memories lie inert. We may have the answer to a problem somewhere in memory, but if we can’t recall it at the right time, it might as well not exist. With routine tasks, Kintsch and Ericsson argued, we learn to create retrieval cues that allow us to keep track of more information than the bottleneck normally allows. Kintsch offered evidence of this in story comprehension. Subjects read a story about the development of the steam engine, with distractor sentences inserted into every other line. In traditional memory experiments using meaningless words or digits, such distractions would quickly wipe out anything you were trying to keep in mind. This is why you need to constantly repeat a phone number to yourself to remember it before dialing—any interruption can easily erase patterns of information that aren’t already chunked in memory. Yet subjects in the story condition were able to proceed with only minimal disruption, suggesting they had converted some of the story into more permanent memory and created retrieval cues to pick up where they left off.

1995年，安德斯·埃里克森和沃尔特·金奇提出了另一种绕过思维瓶颈的方法。经验或许能帮助我们在处理短期任务时更有效地利用长期记忆。在阿特金森和希夫林的模型中，长期记忆是一个近乎无限的存储库，储存着我们生活中的所有记忆。与工作记忆的瓶颈不同，长期记忆是一个巨大的信息库。然而，我们的大部分长期记忆都处于休眠状态。我们或许在记忆的某个地方找到了问题的答案，但如果我们无法在合适的时间回忆起它，它就如同不存在一样。金奇和埃里克森认为，通过日常任务，我们学会创建检索线索，从而能够记住比通常情况下更多的信息。金奇在故事理解实验中提供了这方面的证据。受试者阅读一篇关于蒸汽机发展历程的故事，故事中每隔一行就插入了干扰句。在传统的记忆实验中，使用无意义的词语或数字时，这类干扰会迅速抹去你试图记住的所有内容。这就是为什么你需要在拨号前反复默念电话号码才能记住它——任何干扰都可能轻易抹去尚未在记忆中形成组块的信息模式。然而，故事组的受试者却能以最小的干扰继续进行实验，这表明他们已经将部分故事内容转化为更持久的记忆，并创建了提取线索以便从中断的地方继续记忆。

Both Miller’s chunking and Kintsch and Ericsson’s theory have an important limitation: they’re only possible after extensive practice. Chunks must first be assembled—we’re not born knowing the acronyms FBI or USA, and many non-Americans might have failed to recognize NHL. Lacking efficient chunks, the beginner is effectively juggling more items in working memory than the expert. Similarly, fluent readers have mechanisms for keeping track of stories that aren’t available to novices. Beginners, like those studied by Sweller, have tighter constraints in working memory than those who are already proficient.

米勒的组块理论和金奇与埃里克森的理论都存在一个重要的局限性：它们只有在大量练习之后才能实现。组块必须先被构建起来——我们并非生来就知道FBI或USA这些缩写，许多非美国人可能也认不出NHL。由于缺乏有效的组块，初学者实际上需要在工作记忆中处理比专家更多的信息。同样，流畅的读者拥有一些新手所不具备的机制来追踪故事情节。像斯韦勒研究的那些初学者一样，他们的工作记忆容量比已经熟练的人要小得多。

Learning Within the Mind’s Bottleneck

在思维瓶颈内学习

In the four decades since Sweller’s initial experiments, numerous other impacts of working memory on learning have been studied by a diverse set of researchers. Collectively, these effects have coalesced into cognitive load theory, which argues that optimizing working memory space is a central issue for both educators and learners alike.

自斯威勒最初的实验以来的四十年间，众多研究者对工作记忆对学习的诸多影响进行了研究。这些研究成果共同构成了认知负荷理论，该理论认为，优化工作记忆空间对于教育者和学习者而言都是一个核心问题。

A central distinction in cognitive load theory is between intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load. Intrinsic load refers to the necessary mental effort that accompanies learning. To benefit from a worked example, students need to study it, and this mental engagement requires an unavoidable amount of mental bandwidth. Extrinsic load, in contrast, is all the mental effort that is not directly associated with learning. Means-ends analysis, which requires juggling goals and methods to reach them, is a useful heuristic for solving problems. Yet it may be less useful for learning, because the extra burden it imposes on working memory leaves less space for observing the basic patterns used in solving the problem.

认知负荷理论的核心区别在于内在认知负荷和外在认知负荷。内在负荷指的是学习过程中必然产生的心理努力。例如，学生需要认真学习例题才能从中获益，而这种心理投入必然会占用一定的认知带宽。与之相反，外在负荷则是指所有与学习没有直接关联的心理努力。手段-目标分析需要权衡目标和实现目标的方法，这是一种有效的解决问题的启发式方法。然而，它对学习的帮助可能不大，因为它会给工作记忆带来额外的负担，从而减少观察解决问题基本模式的空间。

Not all extrinsic load is associated with problem solving. The split-attention effect refers to the added burden imposed by learning materials that require learners to move information around in order to understand the problem. Consider the following two diagrams. The left diagram has information located separately from its associated place in the diagram, requiring a key to reference the correct anatomical part. This mental juggling, not being essential to learning what the diagram teaches, becomes an added source of extrinsic load. In contrast, the right image places labels directly where they are located on the diagram and would presumably not create the additional cognitive load associated with the split-attention effect.

并非所有外在负荷都与问题解决相关。注意力分散效应指的是学习材料带来的额外负担，这些材料要求学习者为了理解问题而需要挪动信息。请看以下两幅图。左图的信息与其在图中对应的位置是分开的，需要图例才能找到正确的解剖部位。这种信息挪动并非学习图表内容的必要步骤，反而增加了外在负荷。相比之下，右图的标签直接标注在图表上对应的位置，因此应该不会产生与注意力分散效应相关的额外认知负荷。

Figure 6

图 6

In the left diagram of the anatomy of a heart, labels are separate from their associated location on the diagram. This results in more cognitive work to interpret the diagram and would presumably make it harder to learn from, according to the split-attention effect.

在左侧的心脏解剖图中，标签与其在图中的位置是分离的。根据注意力分散效应，这会增加解读图表的认知负担，并可能使学习变得更加困难。

The redundancy effect refers to the surprising interference from duplicated information. A diagram that presents the same information both visually and textually results in worse learning outcomes than one that only offers one. It appears that redundant information, such as saying aloud the exact same thing written on your slides, creates an additional working memory burden because the viewer gets distracted filtering out the irrelevant reproductions. “Most people assume providing learners with additional information is at worst harmless, and might be beneficial,” Sweller argues. “ Redundancy is anything but harmless. Providing unnecessary information may be a major reason for instructional failure.”

冗余效应指的是重复信息带来的意想不到的干扰。如果图表同时以视觉和文字两种方式呈现相同的信息，其学习效果会比只提供一种信息的图表更差。冗余信息，例如重复幻灯片上的内容，会增加工作记忆的负担，因为观众需要花费精力去过滤掉无关的重复信息。“大多数人认为，向学习者提供额外信息充其量无害，甚至可能是有益的，”斯韦勒指出，“但冗余绝非无害。提供不必要的信息可能是教学失败的主要原因。”

While the origins of cognitive load theory come from domains such as algebra and geometry, research has recently expanded into less abstract domains. Studies with eye-tracking software show that students learn more when they can follow the eye movements of experts. It seems we are innately hardwired to follow people’s gazes as a directive about where to pay attention, further reducing our cognitive load when we are presented with a complex scene and aren’t sure what’s important. This effect may also explain the success of Renaissance-era workshops in artistic production: being able to observe masters at work gives you not only their methods, but their eye for an artistic problem.

认知负荷理论起源于代数和几何等领域，但近年来研究已扩展到不那么抽象的领域。利用眼动追踪软件进行的研究表明，当学生能够跟随专家的眼动轨迹时，他们的学习效果会更好。似乎我们天生就倾向于跟随他人的目光来判断注意力所在，这在面对复杂场景、难以分辨轻重缓急时，能够进一步降低我们的认知负荷。这种效应或许也能解释文艺复兴时期艺术作坊的成功：观摩大师们的工作不仅能学习他们的技法，还能领悟他们对艺术问题的敏锐洞察力。

Does Discovering the Answer for Yourself Lead to Deeper Understanding?

自己寻找答案是否能带来更深刻的理解？

Critics of worked examples often allege that it leads to shallower understanding. The Swiss psychologist Jean Piaget famously remarked, “ Each time one prematurely teaches a child something he could have discovered for himself the child is kept from inventing it and consequently from understanding it completely.” Being shown how to solve a problem, this line of reasoning goes, is inherently a shallower experience than solving the problem by yourself. One way we might test such a belief is by looking at how students apply a method they learned to more distant settings and problem types. If learning by example is just “teaching to the test,” then we should be able to detect that: give students a different test, and those with a superficial grasp of the skill should fail.

批评者常常认为，通过实例讲解会导致理解肤浅。瑞士心理学家让·皮亚杰曾说过一句名言：“每次过早地教孩子一些他本可以自己发现的东西，都会阻止孩子自己去发现，从而无法彻底理解。” 按照这种逻辑，被演示如何解决问题本质上比自己解决问题更浅显。检验这种观点的一个方法是观察学生如何将所学方法应用到更广泛的情境和问题类型中。如果通过实例学习仅仅是“应试教育”，那么我们应该能够发现这一点：给学生布置不同的测试，那些对技能掌握不透彻的学生应该会失败。

Psychologists David Klahr and Milena Nigam examined this question in the context of learning to perform scientific experiments. The main reason for performing an experiment is to find out whether one thing affects another. For example, you might want to know whether the steepness of a ramp influences how fast a ball will roll down that ramp. The best way to do this would be to compare a pair of ramps that differ only in their steepness, while you make sure that the ramps have the same surface, same kind of ball, and so on. Klahr and Nigam wanted to know whether students who were given explicit instruction and examples of the strategy of varying only one thing at a time in an experiment would apply it to new situations less often than the students who managed to figure out the strategy through their own experimentation. They divided 112 third- and fourth-grade students into two groups. One was instructed in the strategy and shown examples of it working. The other was not told anything, but given a chance to discover the principle for themselves. The instructed group did much better on immediate performance—77 percent managed to conduct at least three out of four unconfounded experiments in the testing phase compared to 23 percent of those students in the discovery condition. This is not entirely surprising; it’s obviously easier to learn something you’ve been taught than to figure it out on your own. More interestingly, Klahr and Nigam found that, regardless of how they learned it, those students who had done well in the original test also did better at applying the strategy to a later science fair contest. This suggests that not only was learning through example successful for more students, but it didn’t seem to hamper their ability to apply the knowledge in diverse situations.

心理学家大卫·克拉尔和米莱娜·尼格姆在学习进行科学实验的背景下研究了这个问题。进行实验的主要目的是探究一个因素是否会影响另一个因素。例如，你可能想知道斜坡的陡峭程度是否会影响小球沿斜坡滚动的速度。最好的方法是比较两个仅陡峭程度不同的斜坡，同时确保斜坡表面相同，小球类型相同等等。克拉尔和尼格姆想知道，那些接受过明确指导并被展示过每次只改变一个因素的实验策略的学生，是否会比那些通过自身实验发现该策略的学生更少地将其应用于新的情境中。他们将112名三、四年级学生分成两组。一组学生接受了策略指导并观看了相关示例。另一组学生则没有被告知任何信息，而是被给予机会自行发现其中的原理。接受指导的学生在即时表现上明显优于自主探索组——77%的学生在测试阶段成功完成了至少四项无干扰实验中的三项，而自主探索组仅有23%的学生做到了这一点。这并不完全出乎意料；显然，学习别人教过的东西比自己摸索要容易得多。更有趣的是，克拉尔和尼格姆发现，无论学习方式如何，那些在最初测试中表现优异的学生，在之后的科学竞赛中运用该策略时也表现得更好。这表明，通过实例学习不仅对更多学生有效，而且似乎并没有妨碍他们将知识应用于各种情境中的能力。

Examples alone are not always enough. Research finds that breaking apart worked examples into subgoals can help illustrate the reasoning behind a problem-solving procedure, and that encouraging students to engage in self-explanations of examples can enhance understanding. Worked examples are also more difficult to follow when steps are omitted. Few amateur artists could learn to paint like the Renaissance masters simply by looking at finished copies—it was also important to observe the painting process. And, as we shall see in chapter 4 , experts often omit mental steps of a solution in their explanations. For abstract or intellectual subjects, we might need considerable training before we can hope to understand what an expert is doing just by watching their physical actions. However, Klahr and Nigam’s experiment, along with the work of cognitive load theorists, challenge the assumption that knowledge acquired through seeing examples is inherently shallower than that acquired through direct experience.

单凭例子并不总是足够。研究发现，将例题分解成子目标有助于阐明问题解决过程背后的逻辑，鼓励学生对例题进行自我解释也能加深理解。此外，省略步骤的例题也更难理解。很少有业余艺术家能仅凭临摹作品就学会像文艺复兴大师那样作画——观察绘画过程同样重要。而且，正如我们将在第四章看到的，专家在解释时也常常省略解题过程中的思考步骤。对于抽象或理论性较强的学科，我们可能需要大量的训练才能仅凭观察专家的实际操作就理解他们的思路。然而，克拉尔和尼甘的实验，以及认知负荷理论家的研究，挑战了这样一种假设：通过观察例题获得的知识必然比通过直接经验获得的知识更浅薄。

When Is Copying More Effective than Creating?

什么时候模仿比原创更有效？

The mind’s bottleneck suggests a reason for learning failure: complex subjects and skills aren’t broken down into simple enough parts. Faced with a confusing situation, novices must rely on means-ends analysis and other effortful search processes to solve their problems. This problem-solving investment is often necessary for arriving at answers, but crowds out cognitive capacity that could be used for learning and generalizing patterns that could be applied to future challenges. Worked examples, goal-free exploration, and organizing materials to minimize split attention and redundancy can all make learning more effective.

思维瓶颈揭示了学习失败的原因之一：复杂的学科和技能没有被分解成足够简单的部分。面对令人困惑的情况，新手不得不依赖手段-目的分析和其他费力的搜索过程来解决问题。这种解决问题的投入通常是找到答案所必需的，但却挤占了原本可以用于学习和概括模式的认知资源，而这些模式可以应用于未来的挑战。通过实例讲解、无目标探索以及整理学习材料以减少注意力分散和重复信息，都可以提高学习效率。

This focus on complexity also means cognitive load theory is most relevant when solving a problem or understanding a concept requires integrating many different unfamiliar pieces of information simultaneously. This is certainly the case in producing art. Each brushstroke in a painting requires the simultaneous consideration of chromatic hue, color saturation, and tonal value. Each element of the painting must consider perspective, lighting, and size. Da Vinci’s notebooks are filled with rule-of-thumb heuristics for the proportions of body parts and detailed anatomical studies of skeletal and muscular structures. A realistic depiction requires integrating far more information than a geometry puzzle, which is why few students can do so without considerable practice.

这种对复杂性的关注也意味着，认知负荷理论在解决问题或理解概念需要同时整合许多不同的陌生信息时最为适用。艺术创作正是如此。绘画中的每一笔都需要同时考虑色调、饱和度和明度。画作的每个元素都必须考虑透视、光线和尺寸。达·芬奇的笔记中充满了关于人体比例的经验法则，以及对骨骼和肌肉结构的详细解剖学研究。一幅逼真的描绘需要整合的信息远比几何拼图多得多，这就是为什么很少有学生能在不经过大量练习的情况下做到这一点。

Not all problems of learning are an issue of complexity, however. Compare grammar and vocabulary when learning a second language. Grammar can be quite mentally demanding. An English speaker beginning to learn Japanese, for instance, must deal with the mental juggling of converting her thoughts from the familiar order of subject-verb-object (“Dog bites man”) to the subject-object-verb order in that language (“Dog man bites”). For lengthy sentences such mental juggling can easily consume all of our cognitive capacity, which is why clear exemplification and practice on textbook exercises can be so helpful. Learning vocabulary, in contrast, is relatively low in cognitive load. Each word simply needs to be memorized. Thus it is much more feasible to acquire a wide vocabulary through immersion in conversations. In a similar way, chemistry involves concepts both complex (understanding quantum-mechanical electron orbitals) and simple (memorizing masses on the periodic table), and driving a car requires the complex process of simultaneously manipulating the steering wheel, gas pedal, and brakes, along with the simple process of recognizing what different traffic signs mean.

然而，并非所有学习问题都源于复杂性。以学习第二语言为例，语法和词汇的学习就截然不同。语法学习对认知负荷相当高。例如，一个以英语为母语的人开始学习日语时，必须应对将熟悉的“主-谓-宾”句式（“狗咬人”）转换为日语中“主-宾-谓”句式（“狗咬人”）的心理转换。对于较长的句子，这种转换很容易耗尽我们所有的认知能力，因此清晰的例句和课本练习至关重要。相比之下，词汇学习的认知负荷相对较低。每个单词只需记忆即可。因此，通过沉浸于对话中来积累丰富的词汇量要容易得多。类似地，化学既包含复杂的概念（理解量子力学电子轨道），也包含简单的概念（记住元素周期表上的质量），而驾驶汽车既需要同时操控方向盘、油门和刹车的复杂过程，也需要识别不同交通标志的含义的简单过程。

Because complex problems become simpler with experience, many of the effects of cognitive load theory disappear, or even reverse, as expertise develops. The expertise-reversal effect demonstrates that while problem solving is often ineffective for beginners compared to studying worked examples, this advice flips once students become more advanced. With the patterns of problem solving secured in memory, students benefit more from practice than simply watching. Just as nobody could become a skilled painter without actually painting, mastery requires doing, not just observation. The worked-example effect has its strongest influence when the patterns of problem solving are still unfamiliar. This is why, despite his advice to begin with copies, Da Vinci was a strong proponent of learning directly from nature as one’s artistic abilities developed. Eventually, copying must be replaced with original observations for creativity to flourish.

由于复杂问题会随着经验的积累而变得简单，认知负荷理论的许多影响会随着专业技能的提升而消失，甚至逆转。这种“专业逆转效应”表明，虽然对于初学者来说，相比学习例题，直接解决问题往往效率较低，但一旦学生水平提高，这种说法就会发生转变。当解决问题的模式牢记于心后，学生从实践中获益远胜于单纯的观察。正如没有人能在不实际绘画的情况下成为技艺精湛的画家一样，精通技艺需要实践，而不仅仅是观察。当解决问题的模式尚不熟悉时，例题效应的影响最为显著。这就是为什么尽管达·芬奇建议从临摹开始，但他本人却大力提倡在艺术能力发展的过程中直接从自然中学习。最终，为了使创造力蓬勃发展，临摹必须被原创观察所取代。

This tension between the strategies of learning that work best when beginning in a field and those that work better as experience develops may also explain part of the tension in art education. Experienced artists, who benefit more from problem solving than from additional instruction, may incorrectly extrapolate the mental processes they use when creating new art with the methods that work best for teaching someone who lacks their extensive experience. Psychologist Paul Kirschner calls this the fallacy of confusing epistemology, or how experts invent new ideas and knowledge, and pedagogy, or how we ought to teach people to master the techniques already known. Because the mind’s bottleneck is more constrained when learning new information than applying old information, problems can look trivial or excruciating depending on your past experience. Learning is the process of acquiring patterns in memory that help us cross that chasm.

这种学习策略在初学者和经验积累后更为有效的策略之间的张力，或许也能解释艺术教育中部分矛盾的根源。经验丰富的艺术家从解决问题中获益良多，而非从额外的指导中获益，他们可能会错误地将自己创作新作品时的思维过程，套用到那些最适用于缺乏经验的初学者的教学方法上。心理学家保罗·基尔什纳称之为混淆认识论（即专家如何创造新思想和知识）和教学法（即我们应该如何教导人们掌握已知技巧）的谬误。由于学习新信息时大脑的瓶颈比应用旧信息时更为严格，因此，问题看起来可能微不足道，也可能极其棘手，这取决于你过去的经验。学习的过程就是在记忆中获取模式，帮助我们跨越这道鸿沟。

Applications of Cognitive Load Theory

认知负荷理论的应用

Cognitive load theory suggests a few steps we can take in order to learn new skills and subjects more efficiently.

认知负荷理论提出了一些我们可以采取的步骤，以便更有效地学习新技能和新学科。

Application #1: Seek Out Worked Examples

应用方法一：寻找实例

Whenever you’re facing a new subject of any complexity, look for resources that have a lot of problems with worked-out solutions. In the beginning, these can offer a way to rapidly assimilate the problem-solving patterns. As you progress, you can cover up the answers to use them as practice opportunities.

每当你遇到任何复杂程度的新课题时，寻找包含大量习题及完整解答的资源。在初期，这些习题可以帮助你快速掌握解题模式。随着学习的深入，你可以遮盖住答案，将它们作为练习的机会。

Application #2: Reorganize Confusing Materials

应用二：重新整理混乱的材料

Avoid the split-attention effect by reorganizing materials so that minimal mental manipulation is required. If you encounter a diagram that requires looking back and forth, recopy it so that the labels are right next to their referents. Comprehend formulas better by rewriting them with the plain-English meaning of each variable placed in context.

为了避免注意力分散，请重新整理资料，尽量减少所需的脑力操作。如果遇到需要来回查看的图表，请重新复制，使标签紧挨着对应的符号。将公式中的每个变量用通俗易懂的语言解释，并结合上下文，有助于更好地理解公式。

Application #3: Use the Power of Pretraining

应用案例三：利用预训练的力量

Before embarking on a complex skill, see if it has any component parts that you’re likely to find difficult. If you can practice these components, committing them to memory, you’ll free up capacity for performing the skill later. Memorizing words in a new language with flash cards won’t solve the problems of speaking, but it will ease one thing you need to think about while doing so. Similarly, understanding how color mixes, light shifts to shadow, or the rules of perspective before you begin a new painting can help you focus on expressing a vision rather than getting tripped up by technical problems.

在学习一项复杂的技能之前，先看看它是否包含你可能觉得比较难掌握的组成部分。如果你能练习这些组成部分并记住它们，就能腾出更多精力来更好地运用这项技能。用单词卡片记忆新语言的单词并不能解决口语问题，但它可以减轻你说话时需要考虑的一项任务。同样地，在开始一幅新画作之前，了解色彩混合、光影变化或透视原理可以帮助你专注于表达构想，而不是被技术问题所困扰。

Application #4: Introduce Complexity Slowly

应用案例四：循序渐进地引入复杂性

Since the working memory demands of a skill decrease with experience, this provides a rationale for starting on simple problems and proceeding to more complicated ones. Video game designers use this brilliantly when they design tutorial levels that have a few of the game’s features, allowing players to use goal-free exploration to learn the mechanics without laborious instruction. As you progress, introduce new complexities in a steady fashion.

由于技能对工作记忆的需求会随着经验的积累而降低，因此从简单的问题入手，逐步过渡到更复杂的问题，就显得合情合理。电子游戏设计师巧妙地运用了这一点，他们在设计教学关卡时会包含一些游戏功能，让玩家可以在没有明确目标的情况下自由探索，从而学习游戏机制，而无需繁琐的指导。随着游戏的进行，再逐步引入新的复杂度。

Application #5: Put Craft Before Creativity

应用案例五：将工艺置于创意之上

Originality is simply an exploration of an undervisited region of the problem space. There’s certainly a difference between technical virtuosity and visionary creativity. Yet too often we put the two in tension, when they really are complementary. It is easier to see further when you have first mastered the techniques. It is only possible to bend the rules when you know which ones can be broken.

原创性本质上是对问题领域中尚未被充分探索的区域的探索。技术上的精湛技艺与富有远见的创造力之间固然存在差异。然而，我们常常将二者对立起来，而实际上它们是相辅相成的。当你首先掌握了技术之后，就更容易看得更远。只有当你了解哪些规则可以打破时，才有可能灵活运用规则。

From Beginnings to Mastery

从入门到精通

Much has changed since Da Vinci’s day. Photography and mechanical reproduction of artwork mean that the skill of meticulously representing reality is no longer so remarkable. The avant-garde of art has shifted toward concepts, further removed from the verisimilitude of the Renaissance. It would be silly to suggest that all new artists should be trained in a style that flourished centuries ago. Art changes, and with it the techniques of great artists.

自达·芬奇时代以来，许多事情都发生了变化。摄影和艺术作品的机械复制意味着，一丝不苟地再现现实的技艺已不再那么令人惊叹。艺术先锋派已转向概念，与文艺复兴时期追求的写实主义渐行渐远。如果认为所有新艺术家都应该接受几个世纪前盛行的艺术风格的训练，那就太荒谬了。艺术在不断变化，伟大艺术家的技法也随之改变。

Yet, just as training regimens cannot remain static, it is important not to throw out the principles that worked well. Whether the goal is to produce the moody, chiaroscuro portraits of the Renaissance, the airy alla prima landscapes of the Impressionists, or even the bold arrangements of abstract art, creating something beautiful requires not just originality, but the means and methods to transform vision into a concrete manifestation. Studying the methods of those who came before us is not an impediment to originality, but an inescapable ingredient. In the next chapter, we’ll look at how building that foundation is essential, not just for temporarily reducing cognitive load, but for motivation and long-term mastery.

然而，正如训练方法不能一成不变一样，我们也不应抛弃那些行之有效的原则。无论目标是创作文艺复兴时期充满情绪张力的明暗对比肖像画、印象派轻盈灵动的直接画法风景画，还是抽象艺术中大胆奔放的构图，创造美的作品不仅需要原创性，更需要将构想转化为具体表现形式的方法和手段。研究前人的方法并非阻碍原创性，而是不可或缺的组成部分。在下一章中，我们将探讨构建这一基础的重要性，它不仅能暂时减轻认知负荷，更能激发动力，最终实现长期的精通。

Chapter 3

第三章

Success Is the Best Teacher

成功是最好的老师

It is the duty of a student to get everything out of a teacher, and the duty of a teacher to get everything out of a student.

学生有责任从老师那里学到一切，老师也有责任从学生那里学到一切。

—Kevin Kelly, founding executive editor of Wired

——凯文·凯利，《连线》杂志创始执行主编

  • Does early success fuel future motivation?
    早期的成功是否会激发未来的动力？
  • Are there skills that can bootstrap intelligence?
    是否存在可以提升智力的技能？
  • Does a failure to learn stem from a lack of talent, or missing fundamentals?
    学习失败是由于缺乏天赋，还是基本功薄弱？

T hroughout her life, Helen Keller would celebrate two birthdays: one for the day she was born, and the second, her “soul’s birthday” for the day her beloved teacher, Anne Sullivan, arrived at her home in Tuscumbia, Alabama. At only nineteen months old, Keller fell ill with what doctors at the time deemed a “brain fever”—most likely scarlet fever or cerebral meningitis. She recovered, but completely lost both her hearing and sight. Deaf and blind, Keller’s communication was limited to a few dozen improvised hand signs to express her desires. More often, however, she threw tantrums. “ Sometimes I stood between two persons and touched their lips,” she wrote in her autobiography years later. “I could not understand and was vexed. I moved my lips and gesticulated frantically without result. This made me so angry I kicked and screamed until I was exhausted.” By age six, those outbursts were occurring almost hourly. Exasperated, Keller’s mother stumbled upon a story about another deafblind woman, Laura Bridgman, who had been educated. Hopeful that something similar might be done for her daughter, she reached out to Michael Anagnos from the Perkins Institute for the Blind. Anagnos recommended Anne Sullivan.

海伦·凯勒一生中会庆祝两个生日：一个是她的出生日，另一个是她“灵魂的生日”，是她挚爱的老师安妮·沙利文来到她位于阿拉巴马州塔斯卡姆比亚的家中的日子。凯勒只有19个月大时，就患上了当时医生诊断为“脑热”的疾病——很可能是猩红热或脑膜炎。她康复了，但却完全失去了听力和视力。又聋又盲的凯勒只能用几十个临时拼凑的手势来表达自己的意愿。然而，更多的时候，她会大发脾气。“有时我会站在两个人中间，摸他们的嘴唇，”多年后她在自传中写道，“我听不懂他们在说什么，这让我很恼火。我胡乱地动着嘴唇，做着各种手势，却毫无效果。这让我非常生气，我又踢又叫，直到筋疲力尽。”到了六岁，这种情绪爆发几乎每小时都会发生一次。凯勒的母亲万般无奈之下，偶然间看到了一篇关于另一位聋盲女性劳拉·布里奇曼接受教育的故事。她希望女儿也能获得类似的教育机会，于是联系了帕金斯盲人学校的迈克尔·阿纳格诺斯。阿纳格诺斯推荐了安妮·沙利文。

“ The most important day I remember in all my life is the one on which my teacher, Anne Mansfield Sullivan, came to me,” Keller would later write. Sullivan began by giving Keller a doll to play with. After letting her hold the doll for a while, Sullivan took Keller’s hand and spelled “d-o-l-l” into her palm. “ I was at once interested in this finger play,” Heller recalls, “and tried to imitate it. When I finally succeeded in making the letters correctly I was flushed with childish pleasure and pride. Running downstairs to my mother I held up my hand and made the letters for doll.” Over the next several weeks, Sullivan showed Keller dozens of new objects and their spellings. For Keller, the activity was still just a game, as she had not yet realized that each gesture represented a word. After confusing the words mug and water Sullivan took Keller to the well house and allowed the water to flow over Keller’s hand. The moment, immortalized by William Gibson’s 1957 play The Miracle Worker , was a revelation to Keller. “I knew then that ‘w-a-t-e-r’ meant the wonderful cool something that was flowing over my hand. That living word awakened my soul,” Keller wrote. “ I left the well-house eager to learn. Everything had a name, and each name gave birth to a new thought.”

“我一生中最重要的一天，就是我的老师安妮·曼斯菲尔德·沙利文来找我的那天，”凯勒后来写道。沙利文先给了凯勒一个娃娃玩。让她玩了一会儿娃娃后，沙利文握住凯勒的手，在她掌心拼出了“d-o-l-l”这个词。“我立刻对这种手指游戏产生了兴趣，”凯勒回忆说，“并试着模仿。当我终于正确地拼出这些字母时，我感到无比的喜悦和自豪。我跑下楼去找妈妈，举起手，拼出了‘doll’这个词。”接下来的几周，沙利文向凯勒展示了几十种新的物品以及它们的拼写。对凯勒来说，这仍然只是一个游戏，因为她还没有意识到每个手势都代表一个单词。在把“mug”（杯子）和“water”（水）这两个词混淆之后，沙利文带凯勒去了井房，让水流过凯勒的手。威廉·吉布森1957年的戏剧《奇迹创造者》将这一刻永恒地记录了下来，而对凯勒来说，这又是一次启示。“我那时才明白，‘水’指的是流过我手上的那种奇妙清凉的东西。这个鲜活的词语唤醒了我的灵魂，”凯勒写道。“我离开井屋时，渴望学习。万物皆有名，每个名字都孕育着新的思想。”

Over the next eight decades of her life, Keller would graduate from Radcliffe College of Harvard University; write twelve books; master Latin, French, and German; and become an ardent political activist, campaigning for women’s suffrage, pacificism, socialism, and the rights of the disabled. Following her transformative education, it was arguably social attitudes, not her absence of sight and hearing, that ultimately held Keller back. As a young woman, she briefly became engaged, before the affair was called off by those who considered it inappropriate that a deafblind woman be married. Similarly, her lifelong regret was not the inability to see or hear, but that she could not speak clearly enough to be easily understood, making her perpetually reliant on those who knew the manual alphabet to interpret for her. In the years since Keller’s time, other deafblind people have gone further than Keller was allowed to, including Leonard Dowdy, who not only married but was gainfully employed for thirty years before retiring, and Haben Girma, the first deafblind woman to graduate from Harvard Law School. Keller’s final legacy may not be in how far she was able to go, but how much further others have gone because of her example.

在接下来的八十年里，凯勒从哈佛大学拉德克利夫学院毕业；著有十二本书；精通拉丁语、法语和德语；并成为一名热忱的政治活动家，积极投身于妇女选举权、和平主义、社会主义和残疾人权益运动。在经历了意义非凡的教育之后，最终阻碍凯勒发展的，或许并非她的视障和听障，而是当时的社会态度。年轻时，她曾短暂订婚，但这段婚约最终因人们认为聋盲女性结婚不妥而告吹。同样，她终生的遗憾并非失明或失聪，而是无法清晰地表达自己的想法，导致她始终需要依赖懂手语的人为她翻译。自凯勒时代以来，其他聋盲人士取得了比她更大的成就，其中包括伦纳德·道迪，他不仅结婚，而且在退休前还拥有长达三十年的收入；还有哈本·吉尔玛，她是第一位从哈佛法学院毕业的聋盲女性。凯勒最终的遗产或许不在于她取得了多大的成就，而在于她的榜样激励了其他人走得更远。

Bootstrapping Learning: How the Right Foundation Enables Future Progress

自主学习：正确的基础如何促进未来的进步

Keller’s story illustrates the dramatic potential of education. Being taught the manual alphabet enabled her to learn words and communicate. From that foundation she learned to read, write, and have an active intellectual life. Without that early opportunity, Keller might have remained in perpetual isolation. While Keller’s complete deafblindness from such an early age might be comparatively rare—one estimate suggests as few as fifty people in the twentieth century have had such dramatic hearing and vision loss from such a young age—the basic phenomenon of missing an important, foundational skill in acquiring further skills is commonplace.

凯勒的故事展现了教育的巨大潜力。学习手语字母使她能够学习词汇并进行交流。以此为基础，她学会了阅读、写作，并拥有了积极的智力生活。如果没有早期的学习机会，凯勒可能永远与世隔绝。虽然凯勒从小就完全失聪失明的情况相对罕见——据估计，20世纪只有不到50人像她一样从小就遭受如此严重的听觉和视觉障碍——但错过一项重要的基础技能，从而无法习得其他技能，这种现象却十分普遍。

Consider reading. Without the ability to read, the vast majority of the world’s knowledge is off-limits. Because of this, researchers have found that prior reading ability is closely linked to further development of intelligence. Stuart Ritchie and colleagues measured the reading abilities and intelligence scores of identical twin children at ages seven, nine, ten, twelve, and sixteen years old. At an early age, reading ability and intelligence were not highly correlated. However, the researchers found that when one twin of a pair had a stronger reading ability in an earlier period of time, it was correlated with higher intelligence scores at a later period of time. A suggestive interpretation from this study is that stronger reading ability makes it easier to learn other knowledge and skills, bootstrapping intelligence. Even more interestingly, the researchers found that the benefits to intelligence were not limited to verbal intelligence scores, suggesting strong reading abilities may have broader benefits than simply increased book knowledge.

以阅读为例。如果没有阅读能力，世界上绝大多数的知识都将与你无缘。正因如此，研究人员发现，早期的阅读能力与智力的进一步发展密切相关。斯图尔特·里奇及其同事分别在7岁、9岁、10岁、12岁和16岁时测量了同卵双胞胎儿童的阅读能力和智力水平。在早期，阅读能力和智力的相关性并不高。然而，研究人员发现，如果一对双胞胎中有一个人在早期拥有更强的阅读能力，那么他在后期往往也拥有更高的智力水平。这项研究的一个启发性解释是，更强的阅读能力使学习其他知识和技能变得更容易，从而促进智力的发展。更有趣的是，研究人员发现，这种对智力的益处不仅限于语言智力，这表明强大的阅读能力可能具有比单纯增加书本知识更广泛的益处。

Despite its importance, many struggle to read well. Data from the Program for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) finds that, as of 2013, roughly one in five American adults lacks the reading ability to “ complete tasks that require comparing and contrasting information, paraphrasing, or making low-level inferences.” Nearly 10 percent are “functionally illiterate” in English. Nor is the issue limited to poor reading at the lowest levels. According to the same survey, less than 15 percent scored in the highest two levels of literacy, which includes test items such as pointing out a sentence in both an email and newspaper article that make the same criticism of a product, and reviewing a table of exercise equipment to identify the muscle group best exercised by a particular piece of equipment. With low levels of advanced literacy, even among adults, it is no wonder that many adults read few books. According to a Gallup poll, the average American in 2021 reported that they read almost a third fewer books than they did in 1999. While social media and internet articles might compensate for this decline somewhat, there’s something special about the deep sustained engagement in an idea or story that only comes from a book. These statistics show that we should never take reading ability for granted.

尽管阅读能力至关重要，但许多人却难以有效阅读。国际成人能力评估项目（PIAAC）的数据显示，截至2013年，大约五分之一的美国成年人缺乏“完成需要比较和对比信息、释义或进行低层次推理的任务”所需的阅读能力。近10%的人英语水平属于“功能性文盲”。而且，阅读能力差的问题不仅限于最低水平。同一项调查显示，只有不到15%的人达到了最高的两个识字水平，这些水平的测试项目包括：指出电子邮件和报纸文章中对同一产品提出相同批评的句子，以及查看健身器材表格，确定特定器材最适合锻炼的肌肉群。即使在成年人中，高级识字水平也普遍较低，因此许多成年人很少读书也就不足为奇了。根据盖洛普民意调查，2021年美国人平均阅读的书籍数量比1999年减少了近三分之一。虽然社交媒体和网络文章或许能在一定程度上弥补这一下降，但只有书籍才能带来的那种对某个想法或故事的深入而持久的投入感，却是独一无二的。这些数据表明，我们永远不应将阅读能力视为理所当然。

Why is learning to read so difficult? One reason is that the alphabetic principle that underlies most writing systems is powerful, but unintuitive. Learning it requires memorizing an expansive set of arbitrary symbols—fifty-two, if we count only uppercase and lowercase letters; a few hundred if symbols, numerals, and alternative fonts are taken into account. Next, the sounds of a language must be consciously pulled apart into individual units that can be manipulated. Phonological awareness—which underlies the ability to say what the word stink would be without the t , or be able to point out which word of tub , rug , mud and bean doesn’t belong—is one of the strongest predictors of early reading ability. Unfortunately, it does not come easily. Children are not spontaneously able to demarcate individual words in the sentences they can speak and comprehend, never mind individual sounds. * Then, those arbitrary symbols must be systematically associated with the freshly discovered building blocks of sound. This is a major task even in languages with highly regular spelling, such as Spanish or Italian. In English, it is an excruciating chore, with children forced to manage our highly irregular orthography, resulting in thousands of sound-spelling patterns, few of which apply entirely consistently. Finally, all of this mental work must be overlearned to the point where it can be done completely automatically. Only when the cognitive load for recognizing words is at a minimum can extra capacity be freed up for dealing with difficulties of interpretation, problem solving, and learning new concepts.

为什么学习阅读如此困难？原因之一是，大多数书写系统所依据的字母原则虽然强大，却并不直观。学习阅读需要记忆大量任意符号——如果只算大小写字母，就有52个；如果算上符号、数字和各种字体，则有几百个。接下来，必须有意识地将语言的语音分解成可以操作的独立单元。音位意识——即说出去掉“t”的“stink”是什么，或者指出“tub”、“rug”、“mud”和“bean”中哪个词不属于这个类别——是早期阅读能力的最强预测指标之一。然而，音位意识并非唾手可得。孩子们无法自发地在他们能够说和理解的句子中区分单个单词，更不用说单个音素了。* 然后，必须将这些任意符号与新发现的语音构成单元系统地联系起来。即使是拼写规则性很强的语言，例如西班牙语或意大利语，这也是一项艰巨的任务。在英语中，这简直是一项极其艰巨的任务，孩子们被迫应对我们极不规则的拼写规则，导致成千上万种音形对应模式，其中很少有完全一致的。最终，所有这些脑力劳动都必须经过反复练习，直到能够完全自动化。只有当识别单词的认知负荷降至最低时，才能腾出额外的精力来应对理解、解决问题和学习新概念等方面的难题。

Given the importance of learning to read, and our difficulties in acquiring literacy, what is the best way to teach it? “ By an overwhelming margin, the programs that included systematic phonics resulted in significantly better word recognition, better spelling, better vocabulary, and better reading comprehension,” writes psychologist and reading expert Marilyn Adams in her comprehensive review of the published literature. In systematic phonics programs the basic letter-sound correspondences are explicitly taught and practiced. In comparison, reading methods that encourage students to guess at the identity of unfamiliar words by their overall shape, accompanying illustrations, or the context implied by the story have more difficulties learning to read. An obvious advantage to systematic phonics is that memorizing the basic sound-spelling patterns is a fantastically helpful, if imperfect, tool for sounding out unfamiliar words. By giving new readers a tool for making sense of words they haven’t already memorized, they gain the ability to learn more from their independent reading than they would if they were restricted to words they knew by sight. Sounding out words, however, may not be the most important reason phonics works. Instead, encouraging new readers to systematically pay attention to the letter combinations that make up words facilitates an automatic and effortless processing that frees up resources for other parts of the reading experience. Research shows that strong readers are particularly good at pronouncing pseudowords—nonwords that conform to the rules of English spelling like bluck or squimper —compared to weaker readers. This facility comes not from laboriously spelling them out, but from the fluent spelling-to-sound associations stored in memory.

鉴于学习阅读的重要性以及我们在习得读写能力方面遇到的困难，最佳的教学方法是什么？心理学家兼阅读专家玛丽莲·亚当斯在她对已发表文献的全面综述中写道：“绝大多数情况下，包含系统拼读法的课程都能显著提高学生的单词识别率、拼写能力、词汇量和阅读理解能力。”在系统拼读法课程中，基本的字母-发音对应关系会被明确地教授和练习。相比之下，那些鼓励学生根据单词的整体形状、插图或故事上下文来猜测生词的阅读方法，在学习阅读方面会遇到更多困难。系统拼读法的一个显著优势在于，记忆基本的音形对应模式虽然并非完美无缺，但却是拼读生词的绝佳工具。通过为初学者提供一种理解他们尚未记住的单词的工具，他们能够从自主阅读中学到比仅限于视觉记忆的单词更多的知识。然而，拼读单词或许并非自然拼读法奏效的最重要原因。相反，鼓励初学者系统地关注构成单词的字母组合，有助于他们进行自动化的、毫不费力的语音处理，从而释放资源用于阅读体验的其他方面。研究表明，与阅读能力较弱的人相比，阅读能力强的人尤其擅长发音伪词——即符合英语拼写规则的非单词，例如 bluck 或 squimper。这种能力并非源于费力地拼写，而是源于记忆中流畅的拼写与发音之间的联系。

Successful early experiences can create a virtuous cycle. The early reader who has a strong grasp of the sound-spelling patterns in English will read with less effort than her peers. That reduced effort will also make her more likely to read. Reading more, she will further master the sound-spelling patterns, including those that were not explicitly taught. In a study, Connie Juel and Diane Roper-Schneider compared the word recognition abilities of students who were given phonics instruction and one of two different series of books to practice with. One group was given a reading series that stressed words that were decodable by the phonics rules the children were being taught. The other focused on frequently used words instead. At the end of the year, those in the phonics-oriented program were more successful at recognizing new words than those in the frequency-oriented readers. What’s more, on separate tests, the phonics-oriented students did better at sounding out pseudowords that had spelling-sound correspondences that had not been explicitly taught. This suggests that they were extending their early phonics lessons to new patterns. This virtuous cycle may help to explain how those taught in some phonics programs see sustained advantages: their students experience success, see themselves as readers, and continue to practice, further entrenching their proficiency.

成功的早期阅读经历可以形成良性循环。早期阅读者如果能牢固掌握英语的音形规律，阅读起来就会比同龄人更轻松。这种轻松的阅读方式也会让她更愿意阅读。阅读越多，她就能进一步掌握音形规律，包括那些未被明确教授的规律。在一项研究中，康妮·朱尔和黛安·罗珀-施耐德比较了接受自然拼读教学并使用两套不同书籍进行练习的学生的单词识别能力。一组学生使用的阅读系列侧重于孩子们正在学习的自然拼读规则可以解码的单词，而另一组学生则侧重于常用词。一年结束时，接受自然拼读教学的学生在识别新词方面比使用常用词阅读的学生表现更佳。此外，在另一项测试中，接受自然拼读教学的学生在拼读那些拼写和发音对应关系未被明确教授的伪词时表现也更好。这表明他们将早期的自然拼读知识运用到了新的模式中。这种良性循环或许可以解释为什么一些拼读课程的学生能够获得持续的优势：他们的学生体验到成功，将自己视为读者，并继续练习，从而进一步巩固他们的熟练程度。

Just as learning to read is a foundation for other knowledge, mastering the sound-spelling patterns present in English is a foundation for reading. Some precocious students will figure this out on their own, but many will not. For those who don’t, their early reading experiences will be frustrating ones, perhaps turning them off reading forever.

正如阅读是其他知识的基础一样，掌握英语的音译规律也是阅读的基础。有些早慧的学生能自行领悟，但很多学生却无法做到。对于那些无法领悟的学生来说，他们早期的阅读经历将会充满挫败感，甚至可能从此对阅读失去兴趣。

The Two-Sigma Problem: How Can We Make Classrooms as Effective as One-on-One Tutoring?

双西格玛问题：如何使课堂教学与一对一辅导一样有效？

The research on reading illustrates an important principle: early experiences with a subject are important, not only to build the cognitive foundations for executing the skill, but for sustaining interest that will lead to long-term engagement. Unfortunately, in many classrooms students who struggle in the beginning simply get left behind. Failure to master prerequisite material means they find it harder to follow subsequent lectures, homework becomes frustratingly difficult, and opportunities for applying the skill in real life become increasingly unlikely. Continued far enough and it’s not hard to see how those early experiences can calcify into a negative self-concept: “I’m not a math person,” “I’m not artistic,” or “I’m not good with languages.” Instead, we would like to create a positive feedback loop, where early mastery experiences encourage further investment of effort in learning and practice.

阅读研究揭示了一个重要原则：早期接触某一学科至关重要，这不仅能为掌握该技能奠定认知基础，还能维持兴趣，从而促进长期学习。然而，在许多课堂上，那些一开始学习吃力的学生往往会被落下。由于无法掌握先决知识，他们后续的课程学习会更加困难，作业也会变得异常棘手，在现实生活中运用所学技能的机会也越来越少。如果这种情况持续下去，不难理解这些早期经历是如何固化成一种负面的自我认知，例如“我不擅长数学”、“我没有艺术细胞”或“我不擅长语言”。相反，我们希望建立一个积极的反馈循环，让早期掌握知识的经历能够鼓励学生投入更多精力进行学习和练习。

One way to achieve this virtuous cycle of early success generating greater learning outcomes is through one-on-one tutoring. Helen Keller’s deep relationship with her teacher was a striking example. Not only did Anne Sullivan teach Keller the manual alphabet, and how to read and write, but she even accompanied her to college, dutifully transcribing the content of spoken lectures so her pupil could follow them. A direct tutoring relationship is powerful because the tutor can quickly adjust the material to suit the pupil’s needs, jumping in with explanations when they’re needed, holding back when the student needs practice applying the knowledge herself. In a famous paper, psychologist Benjamin Bloom discussed the strong benefit that one-on-one tutoring appears to impart onto students, arguing that tutoring can raise student achievement by two standard deviations above the average without it. This “two-sigma problem,” following the statistical convention to represent standard deviations with the Greek letter σ (sigma), he presented as a challenge to educators. Bloom argued that because we know such increases of achievement occur with tutoring, it cannot be said that such gains in learning are simply not possible, owing to deficits in the students’ ability to learn or the intrinsic nature of the subject. But tutoring is also expensive. Schools can scarcely afford to hire one teacher for every student. Hence the two-sigma problem was a call to find methods of teaching that could approach the benefits of one-on-one support, but which were feasible to implement in a classroom with dozens of children. Bloom believed he had found such a technique with mastery learning.

实现早期成功带来更高学习成果的良性循环的一种方法是进行一对一辅导。海伦·凯勒与她的老师安妮·沙利文之间深厚的师生情谊就是一个鲜明的例子。安妮不仅教凯勒手语字母、阅读和写作，甚至还陪同她上大学，尽职尽责地记录课堂讲授的内容，以便凯勒能够跟上。直接的辅导关系之所以有效，是因为辅导老师可以根据学生的需求快速调整教学内容，在需要时及时提供讲解，在学生需要练习运用知识时适时放慢节奏。心理学家本杰明·布鲁姆在一篇著名的论文中探讨了一对一辅导对学生的显著益处，他认为，辅导可以使学生的成绩比没有辅导的学生平均水平高出两个标准差。他将这个“双西格玛问题”（按照统计学惯例，用希腊字母σ表示标准差）视为对教育工作者的一项挑战。布鲁姆认为，既然我们知道辅导能够显著提高学生的学习成绩，就不能断言这种学习上的进步仅仅是由于学生学习能力的不足或学科本身的性质所致。然而，辅导成本高昂。学校几乎不可能为每个学生都聘请一位老师。因此，双西格玛问题旨在寻找一种教学方法，既能达到一对一辅导的效果，又能在拥有数十名学生的课堂上切实可行。布鲁姆相信他已经找到了这样一种方法——掌握学习法。

Mastery learning breaks the curriculum down into cycles of teaching, practice, and feedback. Units are first taught, and then students are given a test. Unlike the typical tests given in classrooms, however, these ones are not for grades. Students are not penalized for failing to do well on these tests. Instead, the tests are used purely for assessing which students have mastered the material and which have not. Those students who have not mastered the material are then given new explanations and practice to ensure that they can pass the test before moving on. Those who pass the first time are given enrichment activities instead. While mastery learning can take more time initially, proponents argue that the total time spread over the entire semester is usually only slightly more than a typical classroom. That is because, having their difficulties corrected early, many more students are able to follow the classroom lectures and assignments in later units without difficulty.

精熟学习法将课程分解为教学、练习和反馈的循环。首先教授单元内容，然后进行测试。与课堂上常见的测试不同，这些测试不计入成绩。学生不会因为测试成绩不佳而受到惩罚。相反，这些测试纯粹用于评估哪些学生已经掌握了知识，哪些学生尚未掌握。对于尚未掌握知识的学生，老师会提供新的讲解和练习，以确保他们能够通过测试后再继续学习。而那些第一次就通过测试的学生则会参加拓展活动。虽然精熟学习法初期可能需要花费更多时间，但支持者认为，整个学期的总耗时通常只比传统课堂略长。这是因为，由于学习上的困难能够及早得到纠正，许多学生在后续单元的课堂讲授和作业中都能顺利进行。

Mastery learning upends many of the conventions we take for granted about classroom learning. A central assumption of mastery learning is that 95 percent of the students in a class have the ability to master the material. Contrast that with the practice of grading on a curve—the assumption that for any material, some students will get it, some won’t, and a passing grade merely means being better than one’s peers. Such a practice may be fine if the skills and knowledge taught are only useful as a sorting mechanism, to separate students by their natural aptitude, with no intrinsic value. But it’s a terrible mechanism if the aim is to teach all students useful skills. Grading on a curve encourages students to be competitive, where one’s gains equal another’s losses. Why would students in such a classroom feel inclined to help a struggling peer? Proponents of mastery learning argue that classes should never be graded on a curve. Instead, teachers should get a clear idea of what skills and knowledge students ought to be able to perform, and then create an environment where every student is expected to succeed.

精熟学习颠覆了许多我们习以为常的课堂学习传统。精熟学习的核心假设是，班级中95%的学生有能力掌握学习内容。这与曲线评分的做法截然不同——曲线评分假设对于任何学习内容，有些学生能理解，有些学生则不能，及格仅仅意味着比同龄人更优秀。如果所教授的技能和知识仅仅是一种筛选机制，根据学生的自然天赋进行区分，而没有内在价值，那么这种做法或许无可厚非。但如果目标是教授所有学生有用的技能，那么曲线评分就是一种糟糕的机制。曲线评分鼓励学生竞争，一个人的进步就等于另一个人的失败。在这样的课堂上，学生又怎会愿意帮助学习有困难的同学呢？精熟学习的支持者认为，课堂永远不应该采用曲线评分。相反，教师应该清楚地了解学生应该掌握哪些技能和知识，然后创造一个让每个学生都能取得成功的环境。

Or consider another assumption of most classrooms: that early test scores should contribute to the final grade. Such an assumption isn’t unreasonable. After all, many teachers would argue that without offering class credit for completing homework or interim exams many students might not put in any effort to study. But offering grades for early quizzes has a pernicious effect on students who struggle initially. By failing at the beginning, those students see their chances of succeeding in the class steadily diminish. A student who failed early homework and tests might see the only way to pass with a C+ is if they get a perfect score on the final exam. But this is ridiculous! Unless the final exam is not truly comprehensive, a perfect score should mean the student has mastered the material. Yet this is the inevitable logic of a system that punishes early learning stumbles rather than quickly correcting them. In mastery learning, in contrast, tests aren’t used to punish students who don’t understand the material, but to identify and support them. By quickly intervening when some students are struggling, some of the magic of one-on-one tutoring can be replicated in a classroom environment.

或者考虑一下大多数课堂的另一个假设：早期测试成绩应该计入最终成绩。这种假设并非不合理。毕竟，许多老师会认为，如果不给完成作业或期中考试的学生提供学分，很多学生可能就不会努力学习。但是，给早期小测验成绩计入最终成绩会对那些一开始学习吃力的学生产生有害的影响。由于一开始就失败，这些学生会觉得自己在这门课上成功的机会越来越小。一个早期作业和测试都不及格的学生可能会认为，要想拿到C+，唯一的办法就是在期末考试中拿到满分。但这太荒谬了！除非期末考试并非真正全面，否则满分应该意味着学生已经掌握了所学内容。然而，这正是惩罚早期学习失误而不是迅速纠正这些失误的制度的必然逻辑。相比之下，在精熟学习中，测试不是用来惩罚不理解学习内容的学生，而是用来识别和帮助他们。通过及时干预一些学习有困难的学生，可以在课堂环境中复制一对一辅导的一些神奇效果。

Another major tenet of mastery learning is that the material shouldn’t be taught the same way twice. If a student struggled with some of the initial lessons, the same explanations shouldn’t simply be provided again. Instead, students who are working through a unit they struggled on should be provided with new material to try to present the information in a different way. Different examples, explanations, or practice activities ensure that if the previous route to learning was a dead end, those students will have an alternative path.

精熟学习的另一个重要原则是，教学内容不应以相同的方式重复教授。如果学生在最初的课程中遇到困难，不应简单地重复相同的讲解。相反，应该为正在学习某个单元的学生提供新的材料，尝试用不同的方式呈现信息。不同的示例、讲解或练习活动可以确保，如果之前的学习路径行不通，这些学生将有其他的学习途径。

This sounds nice in theory, but does mastery learning work? Systematic meta-analyses find that mastery learning is one of the more effective educational interventions. Effect sizes find mastery learning tends to improve student achievement between one-half and one standard deviation. These analyses show that mastery learning appears to work in elementary, high school, and college classrooms, with particularly large effects among lower-ability students. This is still shy of Bloom’s original goal, to raise student achievement by as much as one-on-one tutoring does. But given the constraints of delivering material to a large student body, mastery learning provides one of the more promising educational interventions that has been studied to date.

理论上听起来不错，但掌握学习法真的有效吗？系统性的元分析发现，掌握学习法是目前最有效的教育干预措施之一。效应量分析表明，掌握学习法通常能将学生的学业成绩提高0.5到1个标准差。这些分析表明，掌握学习法在小学、中学和大学课堂中都有效，尤其对学习能力较弱的学生效果显著。虽然这距离布鲁姆最初的目标——将学生的学业成绩提高到与一对一辅导相当的水平——还有一段距离，但考虑到向大量学生传授知识的局限性，掌握学习法仍然是迄今为止研究过的最有前景的教育干预措施之一。

A related approach, Direct Instruction, may have even stronger effects than mastery learning. While mastery learning is focused on ensuring early success, it is agnostic to the specific teaching strategy used. Direct Instruction curricula, in contrast, work by systematically breaking down complex skills into their component parts, and rigorously testing the sequence of instruction to be delivered. The end product is a highly scripted set of lessons, which quickly alternate between examples, teacher-led practice, and feedback. DISTAR, the Direct Instruction system for learning to read, which applies systematic phonics, was found to be the most successful program studied for reading achievement in a large-scale experiment. Despite some technical differences, mastery learning and Direct Instruction have considerable overlap in their aims and philosophy. Both are committed to the principle that all students can learn, regardless of talent, and that the way to ensure this occurs through closely monitored cycles of examples, practice, and corrective feedback.

与此相关的直接教学法可能比精熟学习法效果更佳。精熟学习法侧重于确保早期成功，但它并不依赖于具体的教学策略。相比之下，直接教学法课程通过系统地将复杂技能分解成各个组成部分，并严格测试教学顺序来发挥作用。最终成果是一套高度脚本化的课程，其中快速交替呈现示例、教师指导练习和反馈。DISTAR（一种用于学习阅读的直接教学系统，采用系统化的自然拼读法）在一项大规模实验中被证明是阅读成绩提升最显著的教学项目。尽管存在一些技术上的差异，精熟学习法和直接教学法在目标和理念上却有相当大的重叠之处。两者都秉持着这样的原则：所有学生无论天赋如何都能学习，而确保学习成功的关键在于通过密切监控的示例、练习和纠正性反馈循环来实现。

Why Success, Not Failure, Is the Best Motivator

为什么成功而非失败才是最佳动力

Motivation plays an outsize role in learning. Some students show up to class eager to learn. Others arrive with barely concealed contempt for the subject. We’ve all personally experienced moments where we became engrossed in a subject that captivated us, and we’ve all experienced torturous moments in the classroom, watching as the second hand on the clock slowly swept out the remaining minutes of the lecture. As important as motivation is, it often feels mysterious, perhaps something that’s impossible to understand in a fully rational way.

学习动机在学习中扮演着至关重要的角色。有些学生带着求知若渴的热情走进课堂，而另一些学生则对这门学科几乎毫不掩饰地表现出轻蔑。我们都曾有过这样的经历：全神贯注于某个引人入胜的学科，也都曾在课堂上饱受煎熬，眼睁睁地看着秒针缓缓扫过课时所剩无几的时光。动机固然重要，但它往往给人一种神秘莫测的感觉，或许难以用完全理性的方式来理解。

In this history of psychological theories of motivation, one strand of thought firmly rejected the supposed irrationality of our motivations. Independently, psychologists Kurt Lewin and Edward Tolman each proposed that motivation was a calculation of expected benefits. We were motivated, they argued, when we anticipated the likely outcomes of our efforts were valuable. Yet this explanation seems to falter when we consider our actual behavior. Why do we fail to feel motivated to study for an important exam, even though we know the consequences if we don’t pass? If our motivation were purely rational, we’d experience fewer inner conflicts over the seemingly right thing to do and our own inability to push ourselves to do it. A purely rational calculus also seems at odds with explaining the diversity of motivation we see. Why do some students study hard while others slack off? Explaining the desire of some to work hard and think deeply in terms of “achievement motivation” or a “need for cognition” borders on circular reasoning. The question isn’t whether some people have greater motivations to learn, but why?

在心理学动机理论的发展历程中，有一种观点坚决反对动机的非理性。心理学家库尔特·勒温和爱德华·托尔曼分别独立地提出，动机是对预期收益的计算。他们认为，当我们预期努力的可能结果有价值时，我们就会被激励。然而，当我们审视自身的实际行为时，这种解释似乎站不住脚。为什么我们明知考试不及格的后果，却仍然缺乏学习的动力？如果我们的动机完全出于理性，那么我们在看似正确的选择和自身无力坚持之间就不会经历如此多的内心冲突。纯粹的理性计算似乎也无法解释我们所观察到的动机多样性。为什么有些学生努力学习，而有些学生却懈怠懈怠？用“成就动机”或“认知需求”来解释某些人努力学习和深入思考的愿望，近乎循环论证。问题不在于有些人是否拥有更强的学习动力，而在于为什么？

The psychologist Albert Bandura helped to clarify the issue by arguing that it wasn’t only our expectations of the possible outcomes of our actions that led to motivation, but also our beliefs about how capable we were at taking those actions. Self-efficacy formed an intervening link, and could explain why two people, in similar life circumstances and with similar options, might nonetheless feel radically different motivations about what course of action to pursue. The person who chooses not to study for an exam may not do so because she believes passing is unimportant. Rather, she might fail to be motivated to study if she doesn’t believe she’s capable of learning the material.

心理学家阿尔伯特·班杜拉澄清了这个问题，他认为，驱动我们行动的不仅是对行动可能结果的预期，还有我们对自身行动能力的信念。自我效能感在其中扮演了中间角色，可以解释为什么两个生活境遇相似、拥有相似选择的人，在选择行动方案时，动机却可能截然不同。选择不复习考试的人，可能并非因为认为考试及格无关紧要，而是因为不相信自己有能力掌握考试内容，所以缺乏学习动力。

Formulated this way, self-efficacy is distinct from related ideas like self-concept or self-esteem. Self-concept is a global property, how you think about yourself as a whole. Similarly, self-esteem is a valuation of your self-worth. Someone can have high self-esteem or a favorable self-concept and still have low self-efficacy for a particular task. I might be confident in myself as a person, perhaps valuing my athletic skills, but still believe I’m unlikely to succeed on a math test. Similarly, I might feel like I’m a whiz at programming but wilt at the thought of giving a presentation onstage. Self-efficacy is much more granular than your personal identity and can vary between different situations and tasks. Yet, as Bandura argued, our self-efficacy for a particular course of action goes a long way in explaining our motivation to pursue it.

这样看来，自我效能感与自我概念或自尊等相关概念截然不同。自我概念是一种整体性的属性，指的是你如何看待自己。类似地，自尊是对自身价值的评价。一个人可能拥有很高的自尊或良好的自我概念，但对某项特定任务的自我效能感却很低。我可能对自己这个人充满自信，或许很看重自己的运动技能，但仍然认为自己不太可能在数学考试中取得成功。同样，我可能觉得自己编程能力很强，但一想到要在台上做演讲就紧张得不行。自我效能感比个人身份认同要细致得多，而且会因不同的情境和任务而异。然而，正如班杜拉所论证的那样，我们对特定行动方案的自我效能感在很大程度上解释了我们追求该方案的动机。

Figure 7

图 7
