Bandura’s concept of self-efficacy links motivation to two types of expectancies: the chance that I’ll be able to perform the necessary action (self-efficacy expectations) and the chance that action will achieve a desired result (outcome expectations).

班杜拉的自我效能概念将动机与两种类型的期望联系起来：我能够执行必要行动的机会（自我效能期望）和行动将达到预期结果的机会（结果期望）。

If self-efficacy is so important, how does it come about? Bandura argued there were four major influences, with two being particularly important. The two minor influences were bodily state and persuasion. Someone who is highly agitated may feel like they’re unable to take an exam, simply because their hands are shaking and their heart is racing. Verbal persuasion refers to encouragement, like the cheering crowd that gives you energy to cross the finish line. In contrast to these two minor moderators of self-efficacy, Bandura argued there were two more important factors: vicarious experience and personal mastery. Vicarious experience refers to seeing someone else succeed or cope with the situation faced. As we’ve already seen, learning from others forms an important cognitive component in learning skills—by eliminating the trial-and-error experimenting needed to figure out the best way to perform a skill, we are able to learn much more quickly through instructions and examples than individual invention. Bandura argued that such experiences have a motivational role to play as well. When we can witness someone succeed, particularly when we have reason to believe we could imitate their success, then we’re more likely to be motivated to take the same actions. This is why role models, particularly those who we can see ourselves in, are so important. They not only illustrate the way to solve a problem or the correct technique, but they can build our self-efficacy, and thus motivation, to achieve the same outcomes. Personal mastery refers to directly experiencing success ourselves. This is particularly powerful, since while vicarious success experiences can be discounted based on perceived differences between ourselves and our role models, nothing gives a greater boost to our confidence than seeing ourselves succeed.

如果自我效能感如此重要，它是如何产生的呢？班杜拉认为有四个主要影响因素，其中两个尤为重要。这两个次要影响因素分别是身体状态和劝说。例如，一个极度焦虑的人可能会觉得自己无法参加考试，仅仅是因为他们的手在颤抖，心跳加速。言语劝说指的是鼓励，就像人群的欢呼声能给你力量，让你冲过终点线。与这两个次要的自我效能感调节因素相比，班杜拉认为还有两个更重要的因素：替代经验和个人掌控。替代经验指的是看到其他人成功或应对所面临的情况。正如我们已经看到的，向他人学习是学习技能的重要认知组成部分——通过避免反复试错来摸索最佳技能方法，我们能够通过指导和示例比个人摸索更快地学习。班杜拉认为，这种经验也具有激励作用。当我们亲眼目睹他人成功时，尤其当我们有理由相信自己也能效仿他们的成功时，我们更有可能受到激励，采取同样的行动。这就是为什么榜样，特别是那些我们能从中看到自己影子的人，如此重要。他们不仅展示了解决问题的方法或正确的技巧，还能增强我们的自我效能感，从而激发我们实现相同目标的动力。个人精通指的是亲身经历成功。这一点尤其重要，因为尽管人们可能会因为自身与榜样之间的差异而低估间接的成功经验，但没有什么比亲眼见证自己的成功更能增强我们的自信心了。

Bandura summarizes the essential role of direct experiences of success in setting up conditions favorable to future learning:

班杜拉总结了直接成功经验在创造有利于未来学习的条件方面的重要作用：

Performance accomplishments provide the most dependable source of efficacy expectations because they are based on one’s own personal experiences. Successes raise mastery expectations; repeated failures lower them, especially if mishaps occur early in the course of events. After strong efficacy expectations are developed through repeated success, the negative impact of occasional failures is likely to be reduced. Indeed occasional failures that are later overcome by determined effort can strengthen self-motivated persistence through experience that even the most difficult of obstacles can be mastered by sustained effort. The effects of failure on personal efficacy therefore partly depend on the timing and the total pattern of experiences in which they occur. Once established, efficacy expectancies tend to generalize to related situations.

绩效成就提供了最可靠的效能预期来源，因为它们基于个人的亲身经历。成功会提升掌控感预期；而反复的失败则会降低这种预期，尤其是在事件早期阶段发生的失误。通过反复成功建立起强大的效能预期后，偶尔失败的负面影响可能会降低。事实上，那些后来通过坚定的努力克服的偶尔失败，能够通过经验增强自我激励的坚持性，使人明白即使是最艰难的障碍，只要持续努力也能克服。因此，失败对个人效能的影响部分取决于失败发生的时机和整体经历模式。一旦建立起来，效能预期往往会推广到相关情境中。

Success, not failure, is the best teacher. The outcome of repeated early failure experiences is more likely learned helplessness or avoidance, not grit. Failure, when it is helpful, tends to be built on top of a history of previous successes. It’s only when we believe we can eventually succeed within a pursuit that persisting through failure even makes sense. While it may be beneficial to have some humbling moments in a long process of mastery, both as a corrective to overconfidence and to make our motivation robust in the face of difficulties, repeated, sustained failures are hardly motivating.

成功而非失败才是最好的老师。早期反复的失败经历更有可能导致习得性无助或逃避，而非毅力。失败若能有所助益，往往建立在过往成功经验之上。只有当我们相信自己最终能够在某个领域取得成功时，坚持不懈地克服失败才有意义。虽然在漫长的精进过程中，经历一些挫折或许有益，既能纠正过度自信，又能增强我们面对困难时的动力，但反复持续的失败却难以激发动力。

As we’ve seen, the benefits of early mastery experiences to later learning are multiple. Mastering the basic building blocks of complex skills gives the cognitive foundation for further learning. Repeated practice reduces the total effort needed to use the skill, which further expands the range of situations that passes our internal cost-benefit test, making using the skill outside the classroom more likely. Finally, a history of success within a domain tends to bolster self-efficacy, making it more likely we’ll be motivated to continue learning as well. Let’s examine some ways we can apply these lessons, both to our own learning and to the skills we’d like to cultivate in those around us.

正如我们所见，早期掌握技能的经验对后续学习益处良多。掌握复杂技能的基本组成部分，能为进一步学习奠定认知基础。反复练习可以减少运用技能所需的总努力，从而扩大技能适用的情境范围，使我们更有可能在课堂之外运用该技能。最后，在某个领域取得成功的经验往往能增强自我效能感，从而激发我们继续学习的动力。接下来，让我们探讨如何将这些经验应用到我们自身的学习以及我们希望培养的他人的技能中。

Lesson #1: Begin with the Basics

第一课：从基础开始

A lesson from reading instruction is that many of the skills we struggle with are those for which we lack the basic building blocks. Unfortunately, omissions of needed knowledge are the rule, not the exception, in most classrooms. As we’ll discuss in the next chapter, as we gain expertise, we often lose the ability to articulate the building blocks of our own skills. Since most teachers generally know their topic already, this can make them ill-equipped to notice their own assumptions of what students should already know upon entering a classroom. Yet it’s not simply having knowledge that makes the difference, but fluent, overlearned skills. Solving algebra problems is really hard if you haven’t adequately memorized your multiplication tables. Similarly, literary analysis is impossible if it takes all of your mental bandwidth just to decode the letters. By getting the right foundation, and following it up with extensive practice, we can free up mental resources for handling more complex tasks. Therefore, before declaring that you’re unfit to learn a particular subject, you should always ask yourself if you’ve actually mastered the prerequisite material that’s assumed before you start.

阅读教学给我们带来的启示是，我们许多难以掌握的技能，恰恰是因为我们缺乏这些技能的基础。不幸的是，在大多数课堂上，知识缺失是常态而非例外。正如我们将在下一章讨论的那样，随着我们专业知识的积累，我们往往会失去清晰阐述自身技能基础的能力。由于大多数教师通常已经掌握了所教授的内容，这可能导致他们难以意识到自己对学生进入课堂时应具备的知识的假设。然而，真正起作用的并非仅仅是拥有知识，而是熟练掌握的技能。如果你没有充分记住乘法表，那么解决代数题就会非常困难。同样，如果你的全部精力都耗费在解读字母上，那么文学分析也是不可能的。通过打好基础，并辅以大量的练习，我们可以释放出更多的脑力资源来处理更复杂的任务。因此，在断言自己不适合学习某个特定科目之前，你应该先问问自己是否真正掌握了开始学习之前所需的先决知识。

Lesson #2: Hire Help

第二课：雇佣帮手

Bloom’s challenge was to find teaching methods that worked as well in a classroom as we know is possible from one-on-one tutoring. But that’s a strong argument in favor of individualized tutoring! While we may not be able to afford private tutors for every subject, all of the time, hiring help can be well worth the cost, especially if it is applied at the right moments. Hiring a tutor or coach or finding a personal mentor can be helpful if you have them view some of your practice efforts. Since even a small amount of instruction usually requires a large dose of practice to make the skills automatic, the ratio of coaching to practice can still be beneficial, even if it is small.

布鲁姆面临的挑战是找到一种既能在课堂上有效，又能像一对一辅导那样行之有效的教学方法。但这恰恰有力地证明了个性化辅导的优势！虽然我们可能无法负担所有科目的私人辅导，但聘请辅导老师绝对物有所值，尤其是在合适的时机。聘请辅导老师或教练，或者寻找一位私人导师，让他们看看你的练习成果，会很有帮助。因为即使是少量的指导通常也需要大量的练习才能使技能自动化，所以即使指导与练习的比例不高，仍然会是有益的。

Unfortunately, tutoring often comes with a stigma that it is only for struggling students. As a result, stronger students often scoff at the idea of using a tutor. But this is not a useful attitude. Many of the intellectual greats had strong tutor-like relationships that enabled them to master their material. Robert Boyle, one of the first scientific chemists, was extensively tutored by George Starkey in the chemical arts. Terence Tao, one of the greatest living mathematicians, received tutelage from Paul Erdős. In many fields, one can even trace out an intellectual lineage of teacher-student relationships extending back to the founders of the discipline. While tutoring may not be affordable in all situations, that doesn’t mean we shouldn’t take advantage of it when it is feasible.

遗憾的是，辅导常常被贴上“只适合学习困难学生”的标签。因此，一些能力较强的学生往往对请家教的想法嗤之以鼻。但这种态度并不可取。许多伟大的知识分子都曾与良师益友建立过密切的联系，这帮助他们精通了所学知识。罗伯特·波义耳，早期科学化学家之一，曾接受乔治·斯塔基的化学指导。陶哲轩，当今最伟大的数学家之一，曾师从保罗·埃尔德什。在许多领域，我们甚至可以追溯到该学科的创始人，找到师生关系的学术传承。虽然辅导并非在所有情况下都负担得起，但这并不意味着我们不应该在条件允许的情况下利用它。

Lesson #3: Confidence Comes from Competence

第三课：自信源于能力

The lesson of self-efficacy is not that we should try to psych ourselves up to be more confident (for example, “fake it until you make it”) nor that we should try to shower ourselves with phony praise. In Bandura’s research, both arousal and persuasion were relatively weak moderators of our self-efficacy. Instead, we become confident through seeing other people succeed and experiencing success ourselves. This suggests that when we lack confidence, the key is to build a positive track record, starting with easier, simpler tasks, and getting plenty of help from other people who can do what we want to do. Kindling a fire is a good metaphor: igniting a spark requires careful sheltering from the wind and an abundance of material that will easily catch flame. Once motivation is higher, we can increase the challenge level. A heavy log that might have smothered a spark is robust fuel for a roaring fire.

自我效能的真谛并非在于我们应该如何给自己打气以增强自信（例如，“假装自信直到真正自信”），也不是我们应该如何用虚假的赞美来粉饰自己。班杜拉的研究表明，唤醒和说服对自我效能的影响相对较弱。相反，我们是通过观察他人的成功以及亲身经历成功来建立自信的。这表明，当我们缺乏自信时，关键在于建立积极的过往记录，从更简单、更容易完成的任务开始，并从能够完成我们想做的事情的人那里获得充足的帮助。生火是一个很好的比喻：点燃火花需要小心地避风，并准备充足的易燃物。一旦动力增强，我们就可以提高挑战难度。一根可能扼杀火花的粗木柴，却是熊熊烈火的充足燃料。

For complex skills the best way to achieve these conditions is to get thorough instructions on the basics of the skill you’re trying to perform, plenty of practice on examples that aren’t too far outside your ability, and support and guidance for whenever you get stuck. Focusing on a sequence of tasks, building from simple to more complex, and ensuring that you’re hitting high levels of success on the simpler ones before moving on can also be a good tool for ensuring fluency. For language learning that might mean working through a series of graded readers that use mostly vocabulary you’ve already learned. For math that might mean mastering the equations before moving on to the word problems. Building a foundation of success makes tackling thorny challenges later much more likely.

对于复杂的技能，达到这些条件的最佳方法是：全面学习该技能的基础知识，进行大量练习，练习内容最好是难度适中且与自身能力相符的例题，并在遇到困难时获得支持和指导。此外，循序渐进地完成一系列任务，由简入繁，确保在掌握较简单任务后再进行更复杂的任务，也是提高技能流畅度的有效方法。例如，对于语言学习，这意味着阅读一系列分级读物，这些读物主要使用你已经学过的词汇；对于数学学习，这意味着先掌握公式，再去解答应用题。打好成功的基础，会让你在日后更容易应对棘手的挑战。

From Early Success to Eventual Expertise

从早期成功到最终精通

As we’ve seen with reading, well-practiced skills can become so automatic that we lose awareness of the underlying process we use to execute them. For a fluent reader, the idea that we recognize every word by its letter-by-letter combination strains credulity. We read too fast to do that! And yet that’s exactly what psychologists find. Eye-tracking studies show that expert readers fixate on nearly every word on the page, and that we resolve the identity of words by recognizing their letter patterns. It’s simply that, with years of experience reading, this cognitive work happens at an unconscious level so that, most of the time, we’re only aware of the meaning of the text, not how we’re actually reading it.

正如我们在阅读中所看到的，熟练的技能会变得如此自动化，以至于我们意识不到执行这些技能背后的过程。对于流畅的读者来说，能够逐字逐句地识别每个单词的想法简直难以置信。我们阅读速度那么快，根本不可能做到这一点！然而，心理学家却发现了事实。眼动追踪研究表明，阅读高手几乎会注视页面上的每一个单词，并通过识别字母组合来辨别单词。这仅仅是因为，经过多年的阅读经验，这种认知过程会在无意识层面进行，所以大多数时候，我们只意识到文本的含义，而没有意识到我们是如何阅读的。

In the next chapter, I’ll delve deeper into the research on expertise, showing that deep mastery of skills often comes with a subsequent fading of awareness of the basis for how we execute them. For the experts themselves, this can be a great boon. Not needing to pay attention to the individual letters is how we’re able to analyze the meaning of texts. Yet for learners, this can create a disadvantage in learning from others, as the experts that we want to model are often only unconsciously aware of how it is that they’re able to perform complex skills.

在下一章中，我将深入探讨关于专业技能的研究，指出对技能的精通往往伴随着对技能执行基础的意识逐渐淡化。对于专家而言，这可能是一大优势。无需关注单个字母，我们就能分析文本的含义。然而，对于学习者来说，这在向他人学习时却可能成为劣势，因为我们想要效仿的专家往往只是无意识地意识到自己是如何掌握复杂技能的。

# ↩

Chapter 4

第四章

Knowledge Becomes Invisible with Experience

经验使知识变得无形

We know more than we can tell.

我们知道的比我们能说出来的要多。

—Michael Polanyi, philosopher and chemist

——迈克尔·波兰尼，哲学家和化学家

  • Why are experts not always the best teachers?
    为什么专家不一定是最好的老师？
  • How does expertise transform explicit thinking into tacit knowledge?
    专业技能如何将显性思维转化为隐性知识？
  • Can we make experts’ intuitions clearer, so we can learn from them?
    我们能否让专家的直觉更清晰，以便我们能够从中学习？

F ew molecules are more recognizable in the public imagination than the structure of DNA. The twisted ladder signifies the triumph of our scientific understanding of life itself, appearing everywhere from company logos to movie posters. Given its prominence, it’s hard to appreciate that as recently as 1950, nobody knew what it looked like. That image of a spiral staircase, and the consequences it has had on our understanding of ourselves, owe much to the work of the intrepid X-ray crystallographer Rosalind Franklin. Although her contribution was initially overlooked, it was her photographs that made it possible to unravel the mystery of the world’s most iconic molecule.

在公众的想象中，很少有分子比DNA的结构更具辨识度。这个螺旋状的梯子象征着我们对生命本身科学认知的胜利，从公司标志到电影海报，无处不在。鉴于它如今的知名度，很难想象直到1950年，人们还不知道它长什么样。这种螺旋楼梯的形象，以及它对我们理解自身所产生的深远影响，很大程度上要归功于勇敢的X射线晶体学家罗莎琳德·富兰克林的工作。尽管她的贡献最初被忽视，但正是她拍摄的照片，才使得揭开这个世界上最具标志性分子的奥秘成为可能。

X-ray crystallography makes a peculiar kind of picture. The images taken are not light reflected off an object, as the light bouncing off a bowl of fruit illuminates a still life. Nor are they silhouettes, like the shadows cast by an X-ray when imaging a broken bone. Instead they’re created by the quantum-mechanical principle of diffraction. X-rays, like all light, are made up of waves. When the waves hit something, like atoms in a crystal, they scatter in all directions. Like stones cast into calm water, ripples from different sources travel outward and eventually overlap. In some places, where a crest of one wave meets the crest of another, those waves amplify. In other places, where a crest meets a trough, they cancel out. When shone on a crystal, most waves cancel out, except for those that exactly correspond to the regular spacings of the atoms inside. Put a light-sensitive film in the way and you can deduce the structure of the molecule that generated it. Decoding the image requires not only a detailed understanding of the theory of diffraction, but the practical experience needed to make clear pictures out of unruly materials.

X射线晶体衍射成像技术能生成一种奇特的图像。它所拍摄的图像并非物体反射的光线，就像光线照射在一碗水果上照亮静物一样；也不是像X射线成像骨折时投射的阴影那样的轮廓。相反，它们是由量子力学的衍射原理产生的。X射线和所有光一样，都是由波组成的。当这些波遇到物体，例如晶体中的原子时，它们会向各个方向散射。就像投入平静水面的石子一样，来自不同来源的涟漪会向外传播并最终重叠。在某些地方，当一个波的波峰与另一个波的波峰相遇时，这些波会增强；而在另一些地方，当波峰与波谷相遇时，它们会相互抵消。当X射线照射到晶体上时，大多数波都会相互抵消，只有那些与晶体内部原子间距完全对应的波才会被保留下来。在晶体上放置一块感光胶片，就可以推断出产生该波的分子的结构。解码图像不仅需要对衍射理论有深入的了解，还需要从不规则的材料中制作出清晰图像的实践经验。

Rosalind Franklin was such an expert. Trained as a physical chemist at the University of Cambridge, she had mastered the technique of X-ray crystallography by conducting cutting-edge studies on the crystal structure of coals. Her work helped determine why some pieces of coal reduced to graphite when heated while others did not. Although far removed from biology, the subject had important industrial applications and provided excellent practice in crystallographic techniques. Coal is not a perfect crystal, with impurities and irregularities making interpreting images more difficult. After being recruited to King’s College London, she was asked to study biology’s most enigmatic molecule: DNA.

罗莎琳德·富兰克林就是这样一位专家。她在剑桥大学接受物理化学训练，通过对煤炭晶体结构的前沿研究，精通了X射线晶体学技术。她的研究有助于解释为什么有些煤炭在加热时会还原成石墨，而有些则不会。尽管与生物学相去甚远，但这项研究具有重要的工业应用价值，并为晶体学技术提供了绝佳的实践机会。煤炭并非完美晶体，其中的杂质和不规则结构增加了图像解读的难度。在被伦敦国王学院聘用后，她受邀研究生物学中最神秘的分子：DNA。

Imaging a biological molecule like DNA isn’t easy. For one thing, living molecules are wet. There are two different crystal forms of DNA—the compact “A” form and the slightly stretched “B” form. Which form predominates depends on the humidity of the sample. Earlier photographs were smudged because the sample changed from one form to the other in the middle of a long imaging process. Another complication was that getting a good picture of DNA required finding a tractable sample to work with. This meant grinding up animal organs and purifying extracts. But despite the precision to which science aspires, the processes for generating usable samples weren’t well understood. Rudolf Signer, a Swiss chemist, had found a technique for generating samples where the molecule hadn’t broken down much—what chemists refer to as high molecular weight. “ It’s just like snot!” commented Maurice Wilkins, another researcher working on DNA, about the high quality of the Signer samples. Despite the fact that the molecule is in every living cell on the planet, the Signer DNA formed a near monopoly for usable samples. Getting good pictures meant carefully pulling the threads of DNA, using a series of salt solutions to keep them ideally wet, and beaming X-rays for exposure times of a hundred hours or more.

对DNA等生物分子进行成像并非易事。首先，生物分子是湿润的。DNA有两种不同的晶体结构——紧凑的“A”型和略微伸展的“B”型。哪种结构占主导地位取决于样本的湿度。早期的照片模糊不清，是因为在漫长的成像过程中，样本会在两种结构之间发生转变。另一个难题是，要获得清晰的DNA图像，需要找到易于处理的样本。这意味着需要研磨动物器官并纯化提取物。尽管科学追求的是精确性，但人们对如何制备可用样本的过程却知之甚少。瑞士化学家鲁道夫·西格纳（Rudolf Signer）发现了一种制备分子结构未发生太多破坏的样本的技术——化学家称之为高分子量。“简直就像鼻涕一样！”另一位研究DNA的学者莫里斯·威尔金斯（Maurice Wilkins）如此评价西格纳样本的高质量。尽管这种分子存在于地球上每一个活细胞中，但西格纳家族的DNA几乎垄断了可用的样本。要获得高质量的图像，就必须小心翼翼地拉出DNA丝，使用一系列盐溶液来保持其理想的湿润状态，并用X射线照射一百小时或更长时间。

The images Franklin created were exquisite. The British crystallographer J. D. Bernal remarked that they were “ among the most beautiful x-ray photographs of any substance ever taken.” Her experimental dexterity was matched with theoretical insights into attacking the problem. When James Watson and Francis Crick showed her their first model, with three phosphate backbones on the inside and the bases sticking out, she immediately saw what was wrong. The model they had suggested had far too little water and the sodium ions they had placed on the outside would be wrapped in water molecules, unable to bind as their model predicted. Later, when the world-renowned chemist Linus Pauling entered the race with a similar three-chain model, she had no compunctions against writing directly to the celebrated genius to point out his mistake. Her photographs helped her see that the phosphates had to be on the outside, with the bases in the middle. For months she went back and forth with her assistant, Raymond Gosling, producing images of the A and B forms, carefully narrowing down the exact atomical structure.

富兰克林拍摄的图像精美绝伦。英国晶体学家J·D·伯纳尔评价说，这些图像是“迄今为止拍摄过的最美丽的物质X射线照片之一”。她不仅实验技巧娴熟，而且在解决问题方面也极具理论洞察力。当詹姆斯·沃森和弗朗西斯·克里克向她展示他们的第一个模型时——该模型中三个磷酸骨架位于内部，碱基则向外突出——她立刻发现了问题所在。他们提出的模型含水量过低，他们放置在外部的钠离子会被水分子包裹，无法像模型预测的那样结合。后来，当世界著名化学家莱纳斯·鲍林也提出了类似的三链模型时，她毫不犹豫地直接写信给这位天才，指出他的错误。她的照片帮助她认识到，磷酸基团必须位于外部，而碱基则位于中间。在接下来的几个月里，她与助手雷蒙德·戈斯林反复修改，拍摄了A型和B型晶体的图像，仔细地缩小了原子结构的精确范围。

In the end, it was James Watson and Francis Crick who first cracked the puzzle of DNA. In an infamous moment from scientific history, they relied on X-ray photographs taken by Franklin used without her knowledge or consent. Without those photographs the duo might not have moved past their mistaken three-chain models. Similarly, had Franklin been given a few more months to analyze her own data, the correct structure might have been hers to discover. By 1962, when Watson and Crick received the Nobel Prize for the discovery, Franklin had died four years earlier from cancer. Despite not receiving science’s highest honor—the Nobel is not given posthumously—Franklin’s work has since been appreciated as pivotal in unraveling one of life’s greatest secrets.

最终，是詹姆斯·沃森和弗朗西斯·克里克率先破解了DNA之谜。在科学史上一个臭名昭著的时刻，他们未经富兰克林本人知情或同意，就使用了她拍摄的X射线照片。如果没有这些照片，沃森和克里克或许永远无法摆脱他们错误的三链模型。同样，如果富兰克林能多几个月的时间来分析自己的数据，她或许就能发现正确的DNA结构。1962年，沃森和克里克因这项发现获得诺贝尔奖时，富兰克林已于四年前因癌症去世。尽管未能获得科学界的最高荣誉——诺贝尔奖不授予已故科学家——但富兰克林的工作此后一直被认为是揭开生命最伟大秘密之一的关键。

The Elusive Nature of Expertise

专业技能的难以捉摸

How did Franklin know at a glance that Watson and Crick’s first model of DNA couldn’t possibly be right? How did she immediately infer the right way to prepare the delicate fibers, despite never having handled the molecule before? Furthermore, how did Watson and Crick, being shown only a momentary glimpse of Franklin’s X-ray diffraction picture, manage not only to recognize the overall shape of the molecule, but eliminate enough possibilities to reach the necessary answer? Science is often seen as the pinnacle of rationality—a priesthood using pure reason to deduce the nature of the world, divorced from sentiment or intuition. Yet the examples from working scientists betray this philosophy. Intuition seems to play as large a role as deliberate method in the annals of great discoveries.

富兰克林是如何一眼就看出沃森和克里克的第一个DNA模型不可能是正确的？她从未接触过这种分子，又是如何立即推断出制备这种精细纤维的正确方法的？此外，沃森和克里克仅仅瞥见了富兰克林的X射线衍射图，又是如何不仅识别出分子的整体形状，还能排除足够多的可能性最终得出正确答案的？科学通常被视为理性的巅峰——一种纯粹运用理性来推断世界本质的“神职人员”体系，它摒弃了情感和直觉。然而，科学家们的实际工作却与这种理念相悖。在伟大的发现史册中，直觉似乎与严谨的方法一样重要。

Hungarian philosopher and chemist Michael Polanyi defined the term “tacit knowledge” to describe the things we know, but cannot say how we know them. Science, he argued, depended as much on inexpressible know-how as it did on explicit reasoning. Contrary to the vision of the impartial researcher, Polanyi saw science as being inextricably tied up in the personal convictions of the individual scientist. Tacit knowledge could not be eliminated from science, and attempts to rid science of its intuitive foundations would destroy the very thing philosophers had hoped to protect. *

匈牙利哲学家兼化学家米歇尔·波兰尼（Michael Polanyi）定义了“隐性知识”这一术语，用来描述我们知道却无法解释其原理的事物。他认为，科学既依赖于难以言喻的诀窍，也依赖于显性推理。与客观公正的研究者形象相反，波兰尼认为科学与科学家的个人信念密不可分。隐性知识无法从科学中剔除，任何试图剥离科学直觉基础的尝试，都将摧毁哲学家们原本希望保护的东西。

The mathematician and physicist Henri Poincaré similarly argued for the importance of intuition in making great discoveries. In his 1908 book, Science et méthode , he wrote:

数学家兼物理学家亨利·庞加莱也同样强调直觉在伟大发现中的重要性。他在1908年出版的《科学与方法》一书中写道：

The sterile combinations do not even present themselves to the mind of the inventor. Never in the field of his consciousness do combinations appear that are not really useful, except some that he rejects but which have to some extent the characteristics of useful combinations. All goes on as if the inventor were an examiner for the second degree who would only have to question the candidates who had passed a previous examination.

发明家甚至不会想到那些无用的组合。在他的意识中，除了那些他虽然否定但在某种程度上具备有用组合特征的组合之外，从未出现过任何真正无用的组合。一切都仿佛发明家是一位二级考试的考官，他只需要询问那些已经通过一级考试的考生。

If we can anachronistically interpret this in the language of Herbert Simon and Allen Newell, Poincaré was arguing that the expert’s thinking does not seem to search through large, random swaths of the problem space. Good ideas occur automatically, allowing one’s initial guesses to be more accurate than pure chance would predict.

如果我们用赫伯特·西蒙和艾伦·纽厄尔的语言来解读这段话，庞加莱的论点是，专家的思考似乎并非在问题空间的广阔随机区域内进行搜索。好的想法是自动产生的，这使得最初的猜测比纯粹随机的预测更为准确。

Since Polanyi and Poincaré’s speculations, psychologists have gathered a wealth of evidence on the nature of expertise. Different theories support the idea that expertise involves considerable tacit knowledge, although the exact role of intuition differs in each. What is recognized, however, is that the process of becoming an expert often involves knowledge receding from conscious awareness. The right move appears obvious, often without much reflection, even if experts themselves cannot always explain how they reached their conclusion.

自波兰尼和庞加莱提出相关推测以来，心理学家们已经收集了大量关于专业知识本质的证据。不同的理论都支持专业知识包含大量隐性知识的观点，尽管直觉在不同理论中的具体作用有所不同。然而，人们普遍认为，成为专家的过程往往伴随着知识从意识层面淡出。正确的做法似乎显而易见，通常无需过多思考，即便专家自身有时也无法解释他们是如何得出结论的。

Grandmasters, Firefighters, and the Power of Recognition

大师、消防员与认知的力量

The origin of the scientific study of expertise is often dated to the work of Dutch psychologist and chess master Adriaan de Groot. His 1946 thesis, Het denken van den schaker (Thought and Choice in Chess), compared the performance of elite chess masters to weekend club players. By asking players to think aloud as they planned chess moves, de Groot could compare the thinking styles of the stronger and weaker players. An initial hypothesis might be that good chess players are able to think more moves ahead. The rational mind hypercharged, perhaps they dive deep into the problem space to see moves the lesser player cannot imagine. Yet, in the range of experts de Groot studied, players did not differ much in terms of depth of search. Another hypothesis might be that chess masters simply have higher-powered intellects, able to solve all sorts of problems much better. Yet studies have found that experts of all stripes, including grandmasters, typically show little enhanced ability to perform in problems outside their experience. Whatever separates the grandmasters, it seems to be neither deeper analysis, nor generic smarts.

对专业技能的科学研究起源通常可追溯到荷兰心理学家和国际象棋大师阿德里安·德·格鲁特（Adriaan de Groot）的著作。他于1946年发表的论文《国际象棋中的思考与选择》（Het denken van den schaker）比较了顶尖国际象棋大师和周末俱乐部棋手的表现。德·格鲁特要求棋手在计划棋步时大声说出他们的思考过程，从而比较了强弱棋手的思维方式。最初的假设可能是，优秀的棋手能够预判更多步棋。或许是因为他们拥有超强的理性思维，能够深入问题空间，找到水平较低的棋手无法想象的走法。然而，在德·格鲁特研究的专家范围内，棋手在搜索深度方面并没有太大差异。另一个假设可能是，国际象棋大师拥有更强的智力，能够更好地解决各种问题。然而，研究发现，包括特级大师在内的各类专家，在处理超出自身经验范围的问题时，通常并没有表现出更强的能力。究竟是什么让大师们彼此区分开来，似乎既不是更深入的分析，也不是普遍的智慧。

William Chase and Herbert Simon replicated and extended de Groot’s work on chess in the early 1970s. They confirmed de Groot’s finding that stronger chess players do not seem to rely more heavily on deeper search. Instead, chess masters seem to intuit better moves. The initial moves they choose to explore are better than the weaker players, explaining their superior performance. Chase and Simon explained this intuitive ability in terms of better memory. Experienced chess players, when shown a naturally occurring board configuration for a brief period, are able to quickly re-create the complex patterns of the board. Novices, in contrast, can usually only recall a few pieces, poorly. But when the board positions were scrambled, experts performed no better than novices. This enhanced recall ability was first documented in chess, but has since been shown to be a nearly universal feature of expertise. Experts in medicine, programming, electronics, athletics, and music all show enhanced recall of naturally occurring patterns, but their advantage sharply declines when the same information is presented in formats atypical for the discipline.

威廉·蔡斯和赫伯特·西蒙在20世纪70年代初复制并扩展了德·格鲁特关于国际象棋的研究。他们证实了德·格鲁特的发现：棋艺高强的棋手似乎并不更依赖于深入的搜索。相反，国际象棋大师似乎更擅长凭直觉选择更优的走法。他们最初选择的走法比棋艺较弱的棋手更胜一筹，这解释了他们卓越的棋艺表现。蔡斯和西蒙用更强的记忆力来解释这种直觉能力。经验丰富的棋手在短暂地观察一个自然出现的棋盘布局后，能够迅速重现棋盘上复杂的图案。相比之下，新手通常只能勉强记住几个棋子。但当棋盘布局被打乱后，专家的表现并不比新手更好。这种增强的记忆力最初是在国际象棋中被发现的，但后来被证明几乎是所有棋手的普遍特征。医学、编程、电子、体育和音乐领域的专家都表现出对自然发生的模式的更强记忆力，但当相同的信息以该学科不典型的形式呈现时，他们的优势就会急剧下降。

Another feature of Chase and Simon’s grandmasters was the order in which they placed their chess pieces. Experts tended to set down meaningful configurations of pieces in chunks, with pauses between. An expert might first recognize a forking position with a knight and two rooks, or that the king was castled queenside. They suggested that the expert is able to better recall the game positions because they perceive chessboards in terms of a collection of meaningful arrangements. Novices, who lack these patterns, cannot help but see each piece in an arbitrary position, and thus must juggle the remaining pieces in their working memory. Intuition, according to Simon, “is nothing more and nothing less than recognition.” The expert, having saved countless patterns in memory, perceives that a position is like one she has seen before and merits the same response. This enables her to avoid extensive search through the possibilities.

蔡斯和西蒙研究的国际象棋大师的另一个特点是他们摆放棋子的顺序。专家们倾向于将棋子组合成有意义的局面，并在组合之间稍作停顿。例如，专家可能首先识别出一个马和两个车的双重攻击局面，或者国王已经完成后翼易位。他们认为，专家之所以能够更好地回忆棋局，是因为他们能够将棋盘视为一系列有意义的排列组合。而缺乏这些模式的新手，只能看到每个棋子任意的位置，因此必须在工作记忆中不断调整剩余的棋子。西蒙认为，直觉“无非就是识别”。专家由于在记忆中保存了无数的模式，能够感知到某个局面与她之前见过的局面相似，因此会做出相同的反应。这使她能够避免在各种可能性中进行大量的搜索。

Psychologist Gary Klein, conducting field research with experienced firefighters, found that they also seemed to diagnose the right course of action from an intuitive process. Under the danger and time pressure of needing to react in a burning building, few firefighters acted the way formal models of decision making said they ought to: generating multiple options, weighing the pros and cons of each, and taking action. Instead, Klein argued, experts in real situations used a process he described as recognition-primed decisions. Looking at a situation, if it conforms to a typical one from memory, experts go forward automatically with their initial option. Only when factors intrude suggesting the current situation is strange in some way do they engage in more extensive problem solving. Continuing the tradition of research in expertise, Klein also conducted a study of chess players, finding that the first move generated was much better than would be predicted by chance, and was frequently the best move considered, even when given longer periods to think it over. Five-time World Chess Champion Magnus Carlsen seems to agree, explaining in an interview that “I usually know what I am going to do after 10 seconds; the rest is double checking,” adding, “ Often I cannot explain a certain move, only know that it feels right, and it seems that my intuition is right more often than not.” Just as Poincaré observed, our intuitive hunches seem much more accurate than random guessing would allow.

心理学家加里·克莱因（Gary Klein）对经验丰富的消防员进行实地研究后发现，他们似乎也能凭借直觉判断出正确的行动方案。在火灾现场，消防员需要在危险和时间压力下做出反应，但很少有消防员会按照正式的决策模型来行事：提出多种方案，权衡利弊，然后采取行动。克莱因认为，在实际情况下，专家们会使用一种他称之为“识别启动决策”的过程。观察当前情况，如果符合记忆中的典型情况，专家们就会自动选择最初的方案。只有当出现一些因素表明当前情况有些异常时，他们才会进行更深入的问题解决。克莱因延续了对专家经验的研究传统，还对国际象棋棋手进行了一项研究，发现棋手的第一步棋比随机预测的要好得多，而且即使给予他们更长的思考时间，第一步棋也往往是最终考虑的最佳方案。五届世界国际象棋冠军马格努斯·卡尔森似乎也认同这一点，他在一次采访中解释说：“我通常在10秒钟后就知道自己要做什么；剩下的时间就是反复确认。”他还补充道：“很多时候我无法解释某个特定的走法，只知道感觉是对的，而且我的直觉似乎总是正确的。”正如庞加莱所观察到的，我们的直觉似乎比随机猜测要准确得多。

Does this mean intuition is simply memory, in disguise? This would suggest that experts are only skilled when working from cases they have seen before—either the same situation or a similar situation which calls for the same response. This explanation of intuition isn’t entirely satisfying. Chess has an enormously large problem space. While many situations in the opening and the endgame may be nearly identical to ones from memory, the middle game often puts experienced chess players in positions no one has ever encountered. Adaptive expertise requires finding a good move in the presence of a novel combination of constraints. Evidence that experts can do this comes from studies showing that, while recall ability doesn’t seem to be better than novices for atypical board positions, the masters do seem to be able to pick better moves.

这是否意味着直觉只是伪装的记忆？这岂不是说专家只有在处理他们之前遇到过的案例时才能展现出高超的技艺——无论是相同的情况，还是需要相同应对的类似情况。这种对直觉的解释并不完全令人满意。国际象棋的问题空间极其庞大。虽然开局和残局中的许多局面可能与记忆中的局面几乎完全相同，但中局往往会将经验丰富的棋手置于从未遇到过的局面。适应性专家的技能要求在面对全新的限制条件组合时找到最佳着法。一些研究表明，虽然专家在面对非典型棋局时的记忆能力似乎并不优于新手，但大师们确实能够选择更优的着法，这证明了他们能够做到这一点。

An alternative to the simple recognition account of intuition argues that experts comprehend the meaning of situations by first unconsciously creating multiple, conflicting representations of the situation, which stabilize into a single, most-likely interpretation. Walter Kintsch’s Construction-Integration model of reading performance provides an example. The sentence “He met the man at the bank” would simultaneously activate an understanding of a meeting at a financial institution and at the side of a river. As we read further, inappropriate meanings are suppressed. The subsequent sentence, “They withdrew two hundred dollars,” would support the notion that the duo met at a financial bank and not a riverbank. Studies that measure how quickly people process words like river or money suggest that both meanings are temporarily activated, but that the inconsistent understanding is suppressed before it rises to the level of conscious awareness. Intuition, in this account, works because the expert comprehends the meanings of patterns. Initially, those patterns produce conflicting ways of understanding the situation, which, as more data comes in, suppresses less likely explanations. When a novel combination shows up, the comprehension process suggests a coherent answer. *

另一种解释直觉的理论认为，专家理解情境意义的方式是：首先无意识地构建多个相互冲突的情境表征，最终这些表征稳定为一个最可能的单一解释。沃尔特·金奇的阅读表现建构-整合模型就提供了一个例子。例如，“他在银行遇到了那个人”这句话会同时激活两种理解：一种是在金融机构，另一种是在河边。随着阅读的深入，不恰当的含义会被抑制。接下来的句子“他们取了两百美元”则支持了两人是在银行而不是河边相遇的观点。一些研究测量了人们处理“河流”或“金钱”等词语的速度，结果表明，这两种含义都会被暂时激活，但不一致的理解会在上升到意识层面之前就被抑制。在这种理论中，直觉之所以有效，是因为专家理解的是模式的意义。最初，这些模式会产生对情境相互冲突的理解方式，随着更多数据的输入，这些冲突会抑制可能性较小的解释。当出现新的组合时，理解过程会提示一个合理的答案。*

Both the recognition account of expertise, and the more complex process of comprehension through conflicting representations that compete for consciousness, suggest a role for tacit knowledge. Expertise may begin with application of formal rules and procedures. However, over time, this may come to be replaced by recognition of specific situations. In this case, the expert’s knowledge is tacit because there is no reasoning at all—the process of getting the correct answer is simply remembering it. Similarly, in the intuition-as-comprehension account, knowledge is hidden because the web of associations that make sense of a situation is not open to conscious introspection.

无论是基于识别的专业知识理论，还是通过相互冲突、争夺意识的表征而形成的更为复杂的理解过程，都暗示了隐性知识的作用。专业知识可能始于对正式规则和程序的运用。然而，随着时间的推移，这可能会被对特定情境的识别所取代。在这种情况下，专家的知识是隐性的，因为其中根本不存在任何推理——获得正确答案的过程仅仅是记住答案。类似地，在直觉即理解的理论中，知识是隐藏的，因为构成情境意义的联想网络无法被意识层面的内省所触及。

Why Experts Don’t Always Make the Best Teachers

为什么专家未必是最好的老师

Tacit knowledge provides one barrier to learning from experts. Relying on recognition and intuition, experts generate good answers but aren’t always able to explain how they spot them. Another obstacle is knowledge that could be stated but is often omitted because the expert believes it is obvious. Rosalind Franklin’s objection to Watson and Crick’s three-chain model was of this type. She had no difficulty explaining why their model didn’t work—the phosphate backbones had to be on the outside of the model to account for the water content. This was clear to Franklin, but apparently not to Crick or Watson, neither of whom was an expert in chemistry. Communication naturally omits information that interlocutors believe is redundant. Anyone who has dealt with the incessant “why” questions of a toddler knows how painstaking it can be to explain every detail of what you’re doing. Yet when two groups of people have vastly different levels of skill, what is obvious to one person can be inscrutable to another. This has been called the “curse of knowledge” whereby expertise causes you to take knowledge for granted, thus overestimating the knowledge possessed by those you are talking to. It’s the reason why many world-class experts make lousy teachers for introductory subjects, and it’s also the reason many popular scientific books alternatively swing between aggressive dumbing down of the topic and confusing sections—the author, usually an expert in the field, struggles to calibrate just what will be obvious and what will be confusing to her audience.

隐性知识是向专家学习的一大障碍。专家依靠识别和直觉，能够给出很好的答案，但并非总能解释他们是如何发现这些答案的。另一个障碍是，有些知识明明可以陈述，却常常被专家忽略，因为他们认为这些知识显而易见。罗莎琳德·富兰克林对沃森和克里克的三链模型的反对就属于这种情况。她毫不费力地解释了为什么他们的模型行不通——磷酸骨架必须位于模型外部才能解释水的含量。富兰克林很清楚这一点，但显然克里克和沃森却不明白，而他们两人都不是化学专家。沟通中，人们自然会省略那些对话者认为多余的信息。任何应对过幼儿没完没了的“为什么”问题的人都知道，要解释你正在做的每一件事的细节是多么费力。然而，当两组人的技能水平相差悬殊时，对一个人来说显而易见的事情，对另一个人来说可能却难以理解。这被称为“知识的诅咒”，即专业知识使人想当然地认为别人拥有的知识是理所当然的，从而高估了与你交谈的人的知识水平。这就是为什么许多世界级专家不适合教授入门课程，也是为什么许多科普书籍会在过度简化主题和晦涩难懂的章节之间摇摆不定——作者通常是该领域的专家，他们难以把握哪些内容对读者来说是显而易见的，哪些内容会让他们感到困惑。

Another obstacle to learning from experts is the presence of lore, or knowledge that is known within a particular community but is not written down. An instructive case occurred during Watson and Crick’s model-building efforts. They had initially explored the possibility that DNA’s bases might fit on the inside. But the possibility seemed remote because they had learned from textbooks that the shape of the nucleic acids was unstable. Two similar structures, an enol form and a keto form, with hydrogen atoms in slightly different positions, were thought to occur in about equal ratios. This meant trying to squeeze them in the middle would make joining their structure difficult. Imagine fitting Lego pieces together when the shape of the bricks keep oscillating back and forth. Jerry Donohue, a crystallographer, claimed that the textbook they were using was simply wrong. He argued, on the basis of only a few published studies, that the actual shape was the keto form. Sure enough, using this form, the bases clicked together nicely.

向专家学习的另一个障碍是“秘传知识”的存在，也就是特定群体内部流传但未被记录下来的知识。沃森和克里克在构建DNA模型的过程中就遇到了一个很有启发性的例子。他们最初探索了DNA碱基可能位于DNA内部的可能性。但由于教科书上说核酸的形状不稳定，这种可能性似乎微乎其微。当时人们认为有两种相似的结构——烯醇式和酮式，氢原子的位置略有不同，而且这两种结构的比例大致相等。这意味着试图将它们挤到DNA内部会使它们的连接变得困难。想象一下，如果乐高积木的形状不断变化，那么拼搭起来会多么困难。晶体学家杰里·多诺霍声称他们使用的教科书是错误的。他仅凭少数已发表的研究就论证说，DNA的实际形状是酮式。果不其然，使用酮式结构，碱基就能完美地连接在一起。

Lore forms a greater role in the frontier of many fields, because many of the findings scientists must build upon to reach new heights haven’t yet solidified into established fact. When Franklin, Watson, and Crick began their investigations, it wasn’t even clear that genes were made of DNA. Many researchers still believed that proteins were the best candidate. A few years earlier, Oswald Avery had shown a compelling demonstration in favor of DNA being the molecule of heredity. He injected harmless bacteria with purified DNA from a pathogenic strain and watched the safe microbes become toxic—a trait that endured as they replicated. Watson’s dogged insistence to study DNA was based on his hunch, still not the scientific consensus, that Avery’s experiment was sound. Similarly, Erwin Chargaff had noted an unusual correlation between the ratios of the nucleic acids. The amount of adenine (A) always seemed eerily close to the amount of thymine (T), as were the guanine (G) and cytosine (C) similarly matched. Some DNA samples had more A-T, and others had more G-C, but the two ratios were fixed. In retrospect, this was a powerful clue to the structure of DNA—A’s match with T’s while G’s match with C’s inside the molecule’s structure. Yet this hard, scientific fact was much squishier when Watson and Crick were forming their models. Watson reports that his colleague Roy Markham was equally insistent that Chargaff’s results were incorrect. This might have been on the basis of studies where cytosine was absent, owing to some viruses using an alternative chemical instead.

在许多领域的前沿研究中，经验教训扮演着越来越重要的角色，因为科学家们赖以攀登新高峰的许多发现尚未被确立为既定事实。当富兰克林、沃森和克里克开始他们的研究时，甚至连基因是由DNA构成的这一点都还不清楚。许多研究人员仍然认为蛋白质才是最佳候选者。几年前，奥斯瓦尔德·艾弗里曾有力地证明了DNA是遗传分子。他将一种致病菌株的纯化DNA注入无害细菌，并观察到这些原本无害的微生物变得有毒——这种特性在它们复制的过程中一直延续了下来。沃森坚持不懈地研究DNA，是基于他当时的直觉，尽管这种直觉当时并未成为科学界的共识，但他相信艾弗里的实验是可靠的。同样，欧文·查加夫也注意到核酸比例之间存在一种不寻常的相关性。腺嘌呤（A）的含量似乎总是与胸腺嘧啶（T）的含量惊人地接近，鸟嘌呤（G）和胞嘧啶（C）的含量也同样如此。有些DNA样本中A-T的比例较高，有些样本中G-C的比例较高，但这两个比例是固定的。事后看来，这为DNA的结构提供了一个强有力的线索——在分子结构内部，A与T配对，G与C配对。然而，在沃森和克里克构建他们的模型时，这个确凿的科学事实却远没有那么清晰。沃森提到，他的同事罗伊·马克姆同样坚持认为查加夫的结果是错误的。这可能是因为当时的研究缺乏胞嘧啶，而某些病毒可能使用了其他化学物质来代替胞嘧啶。

Tacit knowledge, “obvious” facts, and unwritten lore all form barriers to learning advanced skills. Some have argued that the presence of such barriers is so extensive that a process of apprenticeship is needed to learn elite-level scientific work. Harriet Zuckerman, in her survey of American Nobel laureates, found that more than half had worked in an apprentice-like relationship with another laureate. In 69 percent of those cases, the master laureate had yet to win the prize when the mentorship began, suggesting the influence had more to do with the master’s acumen than institutional prestige. Being able to witness how skills are performed, access to the lore which has yet to be written in the textbooks, and hands-on practice may be prerequisites for the highest levels of scientific achievement. Of course, few of us will have the opportunity to study under Nobel-winning scientists, or the extreme elite of our chosen profession. Nonetheless, the ability to see what experts know is essential to accelerating our own improvement process.

隐性知识、“显而易见”的事实以及不成文的传统知识都会阻碍我们学习高阶技能。有人认为，这些障碍如此普遍，以至于需要通过师徒制的方式才能掌握顶尖的科学技能。哈丽雅特·祖克曼在对美国诺贝尔奖得主的调查中发现，超过半数的得主都曾与另一位诺贝尔奖得主有过类似师徒关系。在这些案例中，69%的案例中，导师在开始指导时尚未获奖，这表明这种影响更多地源于导师的才智，而非机构声望。能够亲眼目睹技能的运用、接触尚未写入教科书的传统知识以及进行实践操作，或许是达到最高科学成就的先决条件。当然，我们当中很少有人有机会师从诺贝尔奖得主或我们所选择领域的顶尖精英。然而，了解专家的知识对于加速我们自身的提升至关重要。

Cognitive Task Analysis: Extracting Expert Knowledge

认知任务分析：提取专家知识

Cognitive task analysis is a family of techniques designed to extract knowledge from experts. The practice grew out of a frustration with earlier behavioral task analyses. These older methods were developed to investigate the exact movements and actions people took when performing skills, such as a riveter fastening bolts on an assembly line. Cognitive task analysis attempts the more difficult job of trying to figure out what knowledge and skills are being used as the basis for a decision. As the authors of one handbook on cognitive task analysis explain, the technique “ becomes more valuable as the nature of the work becomes more conceptual than physical, when the tasks can’t be boiled down to procedures, and when experts clearly outperform novices.” The tools of cognitive task analysis have been used to understand the buying behavior of shoppers, develop curricula that reduce training time, engineer tools to help professionals in their work, and as basic research to understand psychological processes.

认知任务分析是一系列旨在从专家身上提取知识的技术。这项技术源于人们对早期行为任务分析的不满。早期的行为任务分析方法旨在研究人们在执行技能时的具体动作和操作，例如铆工在装配线上铆接螺栓。认知任务分析则试图完成一项更具挑战性的任务：探究人们在决策时所使用的知识和技能。正如一本认知任务分析手册的作者所解释的那样，当工作的性质从体力劳动转向概念性劳动，当任务无法简化为程序，以及当专家明显优于新手时，这项技术“就变得更有价值”。认知任务分析的工具已被用于理解消费者的购买行为、开发缩短培训时间的课程、设计辅助专业人员工作的工具，以及作为理解心理过程的基础研究。

The discipline of cognitive task analysis is itself quite large. One review lists over sixty different techniques that have been developed. This includes low-tech methods like structured interviews and concept-mapping, all the way to detailed computer simulations of expert performance. Conducting a cognitive task analysis is itself a skill that takes considerable training and practice to develop. A thorough analysis may involve hundreds of hours of work interviewing experts, organizing the data, and confirming conjectures about the nature of expert thinking. Even if applying the full power of a cognitive task analysis is impractical for most of our individual efforts at improvement, we can leverage informal methods to gather similar information, albeit imperfectly. By understanding the major lessons of cognitive task analysis, we can avoid some of the pitfalls typically encountered when trying to learn from experts.

认知任务分析本身就是一个相当庞大的学科。一份综述列举了六十多种已开发的不同技术。这涵盖了从结构化访谈和概念图等低技术方法，到专家表现的详细计算机模拟等各种技术。进行认知任务分析本身就是一项需要大量训练和实践才能掌握的技能。一次全面的分析可能需要数百小时的工作，包括访谈专家、整理数据以及验证关于专家思维本质的推测。即使对于我们大多数人的个人提升努力而言，全面运用认知任务分析并不现实，我们仍然可以利用非正式的方法来收集类似的信息，尽管这些信息可能并不完美。通过理解认知任务分析的主要经验，我们可以避免在向专家学习时通常会遇到的一些陷阱。

Insight #1: Ask for Stories, Not Advice

见解一：寻求故事，而非建议

Talking to experts is one of the best ways to figure out what they know. But there are many pitfalls to avoid. One is to assume that the expert can easily act as a teacher and directly provide the advice you need to move forward. As the authors of one guide argue, “self-report methods assume respondents are capable of ‘self [cognitive-task analysis]’ and of reporting tacitly held knowledge. . . . That assumption is not backed up by research—in fact the evidence suggests quite the opposite: people have considerable difficulty reporting on their own cognitive processes.” Ask for advice and you might get a sermon, when what you want to hear is the knowledge they think is too obvious to be worth mentioning.

与专家交流是了解他们知识的最佳途径之一。但其中也存在许多需要避免的陷阱。其中之一就是想当然地认为专家可以轻易地扮演老师的角色，直接提供你所需的指导。正如某指南的作者所言，“自我报告法假设受访者能够进行‘自我认知任务分析’，并能报告其隐性知识……然而，这一假设并没有得到研究的支持——事实上，证据表明情况恰恰相反：人们在报告自身的认知过程方面存在相当大的困难。” 如果你向专家寻求建议，他们可能会滔滔不绝地讲上一课，而你真正想听到的却是他们认为显而易见、无需赘述的知识。

One way around this is to focus on stories. The Critical Decision Method focuses on asking experts to recount a particularly challenging incident. Telling stories focuses on the concrete details of when decisions occurred, how they were made, and what their consequences were, in ways that asking for generic advice or routines often omits. This can also be beneficial when the situations you need to understand occur too infrequently to be easily observed. A difficult surgery, firefighting rescue, or tricky business decision occurs rarely enough that recalling stories may be the only way to gather information about the events.

一种解决办法是关注案例故事。关键决策法侧重于请专家讲述一个特别棘手的事件。讲述案例故事能够突出决策发生的具体细节，例如决策的时间、过程和后果，而这些细节往往是寻求通用建议或常规操作所忽略的。当需要了解的情况发生频率过低，难以观察时，这种方法也尤为有效。例如，一场复杂的手术、一次消防救援或一项棘手的商业决策，发生的频率极低，以至于回忆案例故事可能是获取事件信息的唯一途径。

A good protocol is to act like a journalist preparing for a story—focus on gathering facts, establishing a timeline, and walking through the decisions step-by-step. This provides the raw material for asking follow-up questions to investigate why the expert made certain choices. A focus on the facts tends to highlight details of a story that may be obscured when simply asking for the broader lessons from the experience.

一个好的做法是像记者准备报道一样——专注于收集事实、建立时间线，并一步步梳理决策过程。这为后续提问提供了素材，从而探究专家做出特定选择的原因。关注事实往往能凸显出故事中一些细节，而这些细节在仅仅询问经验教训时可能会被忽略。

Insight #2: Talk Through Tough Problems

见解二：坦诚沟通，共同解决难题

Another strategy in cognitive task analysis is to watch experts as they solve problems. The PARI method (Precursor, Action, Result, Interpretation) focuses on having experts generate typical problems they face, and then swapping those problems with other experts. By thinking aloud as they work on the peer problems, researchers can investigate the basic flow of the problem-solving process. After solving the problem, experts can rehash what they did so further details can be illuminated.

认知任务分析的另一种策略是观察专家解决问题的过程。PARI 方法（前因、行动、结果、解释）的核心在于让专家提出他们面临的典型问题，然后与其他专家交换这些问题。通过专家在解决同伴问题时进行思考，研究人员可以探究问题解决过程的基本流程。问题解决后，专家可以回顾他们的解题步骤，从而揭示更多细节。

Being able to watch an expert perform a task, along with the ability to ask why they made the choices they did, can often reveal much about the thinking behind it. The focus on solving an actual problem, rather than simply recollecting a story or giving advice, has two distinct advantages. First, the problem situation is likely to act as a reminder of knowledge that might be harder to retrieve outside of its natural context. Second, observing the problem-solving process itself can be one of the best ways to learn how it is done. Research often vindicates the power of learning from examples over explicit instructions. This may be an evolutionary adaptation from an era before instruction manuals, when watching other people was the only way to learn how to solve problems.

能够观察专家执行任务，并询问他们做出这些选择的原因，往往能揭示其背后的思考过程。专注于解决实际问题，而非仅仅复述案例或提供建议，具有两大显著优势。首先，问题情境本身就能唤起一些在非自然情境下难以提取的知识。其次，观察问题解决过程本身就是学习方法的最佳途径之一。研究常常证实，从实例中学习比直接指导更有效。这或许是源于没有使用说明书的时代，那时观察他人解决问题是学习的唯一途径。

Insight #3: See Where They Seek Answers

洞察三：观察他们从哪里寻求答案

Sociogrammetry is another method in the cognitive task analysis arsenal. This is a method for mapping out knowledge as a social network and starts by asking experts who they go to for advice on particular topics. Since knowledge needed to perform in tough problems is often held diffusely, it’s rarely possible to find a singular expert who knows all the answers. Instead, mapping out a list of useful contacts is often the first step to understanding a problem yourself. Herbert Simon noted this method as one of the most efficient processes he has found for answering questions:

社会关系图谱法是认知任务分析工具箱中的另一种方法。这种方法将知识绘制成社交网络图谱，首先询问专家在特定主题上会向谁寻求建议。由于解决难题所需的知识往往分散在各处，因此几乎不可能找到一位掌握所有答案的专家。相反，绘制一份有用的联系人列表通常是理解问题的第一步。赫伯特·西蒙指出，这是他发现的回答问题最有效的方法之一：

On the receipt of an inquiry, I pick up the phone and call the person, among my acquaintances, whose field of expertness is as close as possible to the target (it need not be very close at all). I ask my respondent, not for the answer to the question, but for the name of the person in his or her circle of acquaintance who is closest to being an expert on the topic. I repeat the process until I have the information I want. It will be a rare occasion when more than three or four calls are required.

收到问询后，我会拿起电话，联系我认识的人中，专业领域与目标尽可能接近的人（其实不必非常接近）。我询问对方的不是问题的答案，而是他/她认识的人当中，谁最接近该领域的专家。我会重复这个过程，直到获得所需的信息。通常情况下，只需要打三四个电话就够了。

Despite Google searches, Amazon books, and free public libraries, often the best method to answer a question is simply to pick up the phone and ask around for who knows the answer.

尽管有谷歌搜索、亚马逊图书和免费公共图书馆，但回答问题的最佳方法往往还是拿起电话四处询问谁知道答案。

From Seeing to Doing

从观察到行动

Over the last four chapters, we’ve discussed how people solve problems by exploring a problem space, the importance of managing cognitive load when learning new skills, the self-reinforcing cycle of early mastery experiences, and the tacit nature of expertise. But skill doesn’t come from observation alone—considerable practice is required to get good at anything. In the next four chapters, I’ll discuss the role doing plays in learning, from finding the difficulty sweet spot to the importance of creating a practice loop; the research that shows our mental abilities are more specific than we realize; and why variability beats repetition for acquiring flexible skills. Finally, I’ll talk about the importance of increasing our productive output if we wish to move beyond imitation and find truly creative solutions.

在过去的四章中，我们探讨了人们如何通过探索问题空间来解决问题，学习新技能时管理认知负荷的重要性，早期掌握经验的自我强化循环，以及专业知识的隐性本质。但技能并非仅靠观察就能获得——精通任何技能都需要大量的练习。在接下来的四章中，我将探讨实践在学习中的作用，从找到难度最佳点到建立练习循环的重要性；研究表明，我们的心智能力比我们意识到的更具针对性；以及为什么在习得灵活技能方面，变化性比重复性更有效。最后，我将讨论如果我们想要超越模仿，找到真正具有创造性的解决方案，提高生产力的重要性。

# ↩

Chapter 5

第五章

The Difficulty Sweet Spot

难度最佳点

This is a fundamental truth about any sort of practice: If you never push yourself beyond your comfort zone, you will never improve.

这是任何练习都遵循的一个基本真理：如果你从不让自己走出舒适区，你就永远不会进步。

—Psychologist Anders Ericsson and Robert Pool

——心理学家安德斯·埃里克森和罗伯特·普尔

  • When is difficulty helpful for learning?
    困难何时对学习有益？
  • Should you solve problems first or study an example?
    应该先解决问题还是先学习例子？
  • How can you integrate examples, action, and feedback into a practice loop?
    如何将示例、行动和反馈融入到练习循环中？

O ctavia Butler was one of the most celebrated science fiction writers of all time. Recipient of multiple Hugo and Nebula awards, she was the first science fiction author to receive a MacArthur “genius” grant. Her novels have reached bestseller lists and are taught in college English classrooms throughout the country. Her success is all the more remarkable for the fact that, for a time, she was the only Black woman writing science fiction professionally in America.

奥克塔维娅·巴特勒是有史以来最负盛名的科幻小说作家之一。她曾多次荣获雨果奖和星云奖，也是首位获得麦克阿瑟“天才奖”的科幻小说作家。她的小说屡次登上畅销书榜单，并被列入全美各大学英语课堂的教材。更令人瞩目的是，她曾一度是美国唯一一位从事科幻小说创作的黑人女性。

Butler’s literary triumphs had an unlikely start. Her father died when she was seven. Her mother, possessing only a third-grade education, worked as a domestic servant to put food on the table. Shy and awkward, she was bullied until, reaching six feet tall, she literally outgrew her attackers. For years Butler had no contact with any successful writers. Even the idea that she could become one was in doubt. “ Honey, negros can’t be writers,” an aunt told her when she confessed her aspirations.

巴特勒的文学成就开端并不寻常。她七岁时父亲去世。母亲只受过小学三年级的教育，靠做女佣维持生计。巴特勒性格腼腆内向，经常被欺负，直到她长到六英尺高，才真正摆脱了欺负她的人。多年来，巴特勒从未接触过任何成功的作家。甚至连她自己能否成为一名作家都成了未知数。“宝贝，黑人当不了作家，”当她向姑姑坦白自己的抱负时，姑姑这样对她说。

Butler began writing at age ten. At thirteen, she found a discarded copy of an industry magazine, The Writer , while riding the bus. The periodical explained how to submit short stories for publication. Soon after, Butler had mailed off her first story—and promptly received her first rejection. After she sought help, a fraudulent literary agent bilked her out of sixty-one dollars—more than a month’s rent for her and her mother. “I didn’t know what I was doing and I didn’t really have anyone to help me,” Butler later said of her early years of frustration, later adding, “ I had no examples, I had no idea what I was doing wrong in my work. This is true of a lot of people who are beginning to be writers. They don’t know what’s wrong. They don’t know why it keeps getting rejected.”

巴特勒十岁就开始写作。十三岁那年，她在公交车上捡到了一份被丢弃的行业杂志《作家》。这本杂志介绍了如何投稿短篇小说。不久之后，巴特勒寄出了她的第一篇小说——却很快收到了第一封拒稿信。在寻求帮助后，她被一个骗子文学经纪人骗走了六十一美元——这相当于她和母亲一个月的房租。“我当时什么都不懂，也没有人能帮我，”巴特勒后来回忆起早年的挫败感时说道，并补充道，“我没有榜样，也不知道自己的作品哪里出了问题。很多刚开始写作的人都是这样。他们不知道哪里出了问题，也不知道为什么总是被拒稿。”

Still, Butler wrote. Obsession, she stated, “is about not being able to stop just because you’re afraid and full of doubts. . . . It’s about not being able to stop at all.” A typical routine was to wake up at 3 a.m. and write all morning before leaving to work odd jobs. “I preferred blue-collar work,” she admitted, “ because with white-collar work you have to pretend you were enjoying it, and I wasn’t.” Avoiding stable employment allowed Butler mental freedom, but it came with financial costs. “I was lucky,” she explained, “ I had an extra typewriter. And anytime I got really low on food, I would go and pawn that.” Butler was rarely happier than when she was laid off from one of her dead-end jobs—for that gave her more time to pour into her writing.

尽管如此，巴特勒仍然坚持写作。她说道，痴迷“在于即便害怕和充满疑虑也无法停止……在于根本无法停止。”她通常凌晨三点起床，写作一上午，然后出门打零工。“我更喜欢蓝领工作，”她坦言，“因为白领工作你必须假装很享受，而我并不享受。”避免稳定的工作让巴特勒获得了精神上的自由，但也付出了经济代价。“我很幸运，”她解释说，“我有一台备用的打字机。每当我快没饭吃的时候，我就把它当掉。”巴特勒最快乐的时候，莫过于被那些毫无前途的工作解雇——因为这让她有更多的时间投入到写作中。

A turning point came during a free class put on by the Screen Writers’ Guild. One of the instructors was Harlan Ellison, himself a successful science fiction author. Ellison encouraged Butler to attend the six-week Clarion Workshop for science fiction. Butler was terrified at first. She had hardly ever left Pasadena, California, where she grew up. Despite her trepidation, she managed to scrape together the funds to take the Greyhound bus to Pennsylvania.

转折点出现在美国编剧工会举办的一堂免费课程上。其中一位讲师是哈兰·埃里森，他本人也是一位成功的科幻小说作家。埃里森鼓励巴特勒参加为期六周的克拉里昂科幻小说研习班。巴特勒起初非常害怕。她几乎从未离开过她长大的加利福尼亚州帕萨迪纳。尽管忐忑不安，她还是设法凑齐了钱，坐灰狗巴士去了宾夕法尼亚州。

At Clarion, most of the instructors were established authors. They understood the industry and what kind of writing was needed to get published. Butler discovered that “ the things I had been learning in English class weren’t that useful because it’s a different kind of writing. I mean, academic writing is just plain different from fiction.” Students at the workshop were pushed to write a new short story every night, so it could be dissected in class the following day. At first Butler struggled to deal with the aggressive pace. However, by the end of the workshop, she had sold her first story.

在克拉里昂，大多数导师都是资深作家。他们了解出版行业，也知道什么样的写作才能成功。巴特勒发现，“我在英语课上学到的东西并不怎么有用，因为写作方式完全不同。我的意思是，学术写作和小说写作截然不同。” 工作坊的学生们被要求每天晚上写一篇新的短篇小说，以便第二天在课堂上进行分析。起初，巴特勒很难适应这种高强度的节奏。然而，在工作坊结束时，她卖出了自己的第一篇小说。

After Clarion, Butler decided to switch from writing short stories to novels. The pay for short stories was meager. Writing novels, with larger publisher advances, was the best route to make writing full-time a reality. Yet the length of a novel intimidated her. “I had been able to finish some short stories, which were about twenty pages long, and I finally decided to try writing twenty-page chapters until I finished each novel,” Butler said of her strategy. These efforts allowed Butler to sell her first novel, Patternmaster , to Doubleday.

在克拉里昂之后，巴特勒决定从短篇小说转向长篇小说。短篇小说的稿酬微薄，而长篇小说能获得更高的预付款，是实现全职写作的最佳途径。然而，长篇小说的篇幅令她望而却步。“我之前写过一些短篇小说，每篇大约二十页，后来我决定尝试每章写二十页，直到完成一部长篇小说，”巴特勒这样描述她的策略。正是这些努力，让巴特勒成功地将她的第一部长篇小说《模式大师》（Patternmaster）卖给了道布尔戴出版社。

Following Patternmaster , Butler began the most prolific period of her writing career, producing five novels over the span of five years. By her third, she had earned enough money to write full-time. For her fourth novel, she wanted to try something more ambitious. As a child, she had been embarrassed by her mother’s work as a servant. Employers frequently spoke in degrading terms about her mother while she was within earshot. Yet, as she grew older, she saw the dignity in those who, like her mother, manage to endure. She imagined the story of a Black woman thrown back in time in the antebellum South, contrasting modern attitudes with the reality of slavery, as the perfect setting for exploring this theme. Requiring far more research and attention to historical accuracy than Butler was accustomed to, she used some of her advance money to plan a trip to Maryland, visiting plantations where she intended to set scenes for the novel. Her additional efforts paid off. Kindred became Butler’s most commercially successful work and secured Butler’s literary legacy.

在《模式大师》之后，巴特勒迎来了她创作生涯中最丰产的时期，五年内创作了五部小说。到第三部时，她已经赚够了钱，可以全职写作。在创作第四部小说时，她想尝试一些更具野心的东西。小时候，她曾因母亲做佣人的工作而感到羞耻。雇主经常在她耳边用侮辱性的语言谈论她的母亲。然而，随着年龄的增长，她看到了那些像她母亲一样能够忍受苦难的人身上所展现出的尊严。她设想了一个黑人女性穿越回南北战争前的南方，将现代社会的观念与奴隶制的现实进行对比的故事，认为这是探讨这一主题的完美背景。由于这需要比巴特勒以往习惯的更多的研究和对历史准确性的关注，她用预付稿费计划了一次马里兰州之旅，参观了她计划为小说设定场景的种植园。她的额外努力得到了回报。《亲属》成为巴特勒最畅销的作品，并奠定了她的文学地位。

The Writer’s Paradox

作家的悖论

According to the view of expertise discussed in the previous chapter, experience transforms problems into routines. Beginners struggle with searching through the problem space. Experts recognize the situation and proceed directly to the answer. If so, studying expert writers complicates this picture. Transcripts of expert writers thinking aloud as they work on a writing task make them appear like novices—effortful problem solving, frequent impasses, and means-ends analysis. In contrast, young children often write with expert-like fluency. There is little planning, organization, or thought about what might be interesting or persuasive for a potential reader. During one investigation, researchers Marlene Scardamalia and Carl Bereiter remarked that children were bewildered when it was explained to them that adults sometimes spend as much as fifteen minutes thinking about what they want to say before starting to write.

根据前一章讨论的专家观点，经验会将问题转化为常规操作。初学者往往难以在问题空间中摸索前进，而专家则能迅速识别问题并直接找到答案。然而，研究专家作家的写作方式却使这种观点变得复杂。专家作家在写作过程中边思考边朗读的文字记录，反而让他们看起来像新手——费力地解决问题、频繁陷入僵局，以及进行手段与目的的分析。相比之下，幼儿的写作往往流畅得如同专家一般。他们很少进行计划、组织，也很少思考什么内容可能对潜在读者有趣或有说服力。在一次研究中，研究人员玛琳·斯卡达马利亚和卡尔·贝雷特注意到，当孩子们被告知成年人在动笔前有时会花长达十五分钟思考自己想表达的内容时，他们感到非常困惑。

Writing seemingly violates the standard findings on expertise because a writing task isn’t a single problem. Solving a Rubik’s Cube, answering an algebra question, or even finding the proof to Fermat’s Last Theorem is the same puzzle, regardless of how you approach it. The starting point, maneuvers, and what counts as an acceptable solution are the same for everyone. In contrast, two different writers given the same writing prompt may conceive of the problem in completely different terms. Even a simple task like composing an email can be conceived as a perfunctory assignment or an opportunity for expressive prose. In short, children behave like experts while skilled writers behave like novices because the two groups of people are actually solving different problems. Children produce text fluently because their self-set aim is to write things as they come to mind on a particular topic, what Scardamalia and Bereiter call a knowledge-telling strategy. This strategy can even persist into adulthood, as anyone who has been forced to read a disorganized, stream-of-consciousness email from a colleague can readily attest. In contrast, experts usually choose for themselves more difficult problems to solve: crafting an original story, persuading an audience, or expressing something interesting.

写作似乎违背了关于专业知识的标准结论，因为写作任务并非单一问题。解魔方、回答代数题，甚至证明费马大定理，本质上都是同一个谜题，无论你采用何种方法。起点、步骤以及可接受的答案对每个人来说都是一样的。相比之下，两位不同的作者面对相同的写作提示，可能会以截然不同的方式理解问题。即使是撰写电子邮件这样简单的任务，也可能被视为敷衍了事，或是展现文采的良机。简而言之，儿童的行为如同专家，而熟练的写作者却像新手，因为这两类人实际上解决的是不同的问题。儿童之所以能流畅地写作，是因为他们的目标是围绕特定主题，想到什么就写什么，斯卡达马利亚和贝雷特称之为“知识表达策略”。这种策略甚至会延续到成年时期，任何被迫阅读过同事杂乱无章、意识流式邮件的人都能轻易证实这一点。相比之下，专家通常会选择更具挑战性的问题来解决：创作原创故事、说服受众或表达有趣的观点。

Butler’s literary growth was a steady progression of increasingly difficult problems. Her early writing was highly imitative. “ The short stories I submitted for publication when I was thirteen had nothing to do with anything I cared about. I wrote the kind of thing I saw being published—stories about thirty-year-old white men who drank and smoked too much.” As she wrote more, she developed original themes with personal significance. The first story she sold, “Childfinder,” dealt with a struggle between covert groups recruiting children with peculiar mental abilities. These early works would mature into lifelong interests in themes of hierarchy and dominance within society. After Clarion, she progressed from short stories to novels. With three novels under her belt, she deepened her ability to do research—from the historical setting of Kindred to later novels that drew upon indigenous languages and inspiration from scientific texts.

巴特勒的文学创作是一个循序渐进的过程，她不断挑战越来越复杂的问题。她早期的作品模仿性很强。“我十三岁时投稿的短篇小说和我真正关心的事情毫无关系。我写的是我看到出版的那种东西——关于三十岁白人男性酗酒抽烟的故事。”随着写作的增多，她逐渐发展出具有个人意义的原创主题。她卖出的第一篇小说《寻子者》讲述了秘密组织招募拥有特殊智力儿童的故事。这些早期作品逐渐演变为她终生关注的社会等级制度和支配主题。在《克拉里昂》之后，她从短篇小说转向长篇小说。在创作了三部长篇小说之后，她的研究能力得到了提升——从《亲族》的历史背景到后来的小说中对土著语言的运用以及从科学文献中汲取的灵感。

Owing to her progressive problem solving, writing never got easier for Butler. She dealt with creative blocks her entire life. A compulsive rewriter, she sometimes threw out large sections of books when they failed to meet her standards. At one point, she offered to give back the advance for a novel she had sold after it wasn’t turning out to her satisfaction. Asked in an interview during the peak of her success whether her writing was “organic,” Butler replied, “ No, it’s work,” adding, “It’s certainly not a matter of sitting there and having things fall from the sky.” Butler’s occasional frustration at her own writing is evidenced in her personal journals, yet I would argue that it was her very tendency to seek out increasingly challenging problems that allowed her to develop her literary talents. Ernest Hemingway stated it best when he supposedly uttered that writers “ are all apprentices at a craft where no one ever becomes a master.”

由于她解决问题的方式不断进步，写作对巴特勒来说从未变得轻松。她一生都在与创作瓶颈作斗争。她是个强迫症患者，经常会反复修改，有时甚至会因为作品达不到自己的标准而直接扔掉大段章节。有一次，她甚至提出要退还已售出的小说的预付款，因为这部小说最终的成品让她很不满意。在她事业的巅峰时期，有人在一次采访中问她，她的写作是否“自然而然”地发生，巴特勒回答说：“不，这是工作。”她补充道：“这绝不是坐在那里等着灵感从天而降。”巴特勒偶尔对自己的写作感到沮丧，这一点在她的个人日记中有所体现。但我认为，正是她不断寻求更具挑战性的问题的倾向，才使她得以发展自己的文学才能。欧内斯特·海明威曾说过一句至理名言，他说作家“都是这门技艺的学徒，没有人能成为大师”。

In this regard, writing is far from atypical. Physicists may breeze through textbook problems that stump an undergraduate. But in their jobs, they aren’t simply solving textbook problems more quickly. Instead they’re tackling the most challenging problems at the frontier of science. Similarly, chess grandmasters aren’t practicing how to checkmate novices, but engaging in deeper analysis to battle wits against tougher opponents. Indeed, the mindlessness of expertise seems mostly at play when we are dealing with skills we aren’t trying to improve. Driving, for most of us, becomes a thoroughly automated task, not because there aren’t deeper problems of driving-related skill for us to solve, but because we don’t care to solve them. Progressive problem solving is essential for mastery, even if it occasionally frustrates our performance.

在这方面，写作绝非特例。物理学家或许能轻松解决令本科生束手无策的教科书习题。但他们的工作并非仅仅是更快地解答教科书难题，而是攻克科学前沿最具挑战性的难题。同样，国际象棋大师练习的并非如何将新手将死，而是进行更深入的分析，与更强大的对手斗智斗勇。事实上，当我们面对那些我们并不想提升的技能时，专家的无意识似乎才会显现出来。对我们大多数人来说，开车已经变成了一项完全自动化的任务，这并非因为驾驶技能本身没有更深层次的问题需要解决，而是因为我们根本不在乎去解决这些问题。循序渐进地解决问题对于精通技能至关重要，即便它有时会让我们感到沮丧。

When Is Difficulty Desirable?

什么时候困难才是可取的？

As we’ve seen from previous chapters, added difficulties aren’t always helpful. Problems can be impossible to solve if they’re too far out in the problem space, given your current supply of strong methods to search for them. Even if you can reach the solution, the extra cognitive load of means-ends analysis can distract from recognizing reusable patterns. Finally, the tacit knowledge possessed by experts can make extraction tricky without direct access and observation. Butler certainly faced all of these difficulties in her early writing. “ Frustrating. Frustrating,” she said of her beginnings. “During those years I collected lots of frustrations and rejection slips.” It is a testament to her character that she persisted while wholly lacking guidance for so many years. It is also unsurprising that her biggest breakthroughs came after she finally had insider access to the world of science fiction writing.

正如我们在前几章中所看到的，增加难度并非总是有益的。如果问题过于偏远，超出了你现有搜索方法的范畴，那么这些问题可能根本无法解决。即使最终找到了解决方案，方法-目标分析带来的额外认知负担也会分散你识别可复用模式的注意力。最后，专家所拥有的隐性知识，如果没有直接接触和观察，提取起来也会非常棘手。巴特勒在早期写作中无疑也面临着所有这些困难。“令人沮丧，令人沮丧，”她这样描述自己的写作初期，“那些年里，我经历了无数的挫折和退稿信。” 她能在多年完全缺乏指导的情况下坚持不懈，这足以证明她的毅力。同样不足为奇的是，在她最终能够深入了解科幻小说写作领域之后，她取得了最大的突破。

Yet researchers have discovered that not all difficulties are unhelpful. Psychologists Robert Bjork and Elizabeth Bjork have studied the conditions under which more difficult practice leads to greater improvement than easier efforts. One of these desirable difficulties is the added effort of retrieving information from memory, compared to seeing it again. Successfully recalling a fact, procedure, or idea strengthens memory more than repeat viewing. This is why flash cards are such an excellent tool when studying for a test. Simply looking over your notes is far less efficient for improving your ability to recall it in the future.

然而，研究人员发现并非所有困难都无益。心理学家罗伯特·比约克和伊丽莎白·比约克研究了在哪些情况下，难度更高的练习比简单的练习更能带来显著的进步。其中一种有益的困难是，与再次查看相比，从记忆中提取信息需要付出额外的努力。成功回忆起某个事实、步骤或概念比重复查看更能强化记忆。这就是为什么记忆卡片是备考的绝佳工具。仅仅浏览笔记对于提高未来的回忆能力来说效率要低得多。

Another desirable difficulty is spaced practice. Practicing the same thing, multiple times in a row, rapidly improves performance. But it also results in equally fast forgetting. This explains why cramming is popular among students, but a bad way to study. Cramming does fill your head up before an test—temporarily—but you’ll quickly forget most of it before you get a chance to use it outside the examination hall. A better strategy is to space your reviews out, a little bit each day, so that the same amount of time has a greater impact.

另一种理想的学习方法是间隔练习。反复练习同一件事能迅速提高成绩，但也会导致遗忘同样迅速。这就解释了为什么考前突击很受学生欢迎，但实际上却是一种糟糕的学习方法。考前突击确实能让你在考试前暂时记住很多东西，但你很快就会忘记大部分内容，直到考场之外才有机会运用。更好的策略是把复习分散开来，每天复习一点，这样同样的时间就能产生更大的效果。

Why do some difficulties help? One reason is that the brain is a fantastic effort-saving machine. If you can access the solution pattern to a problem just by looking at it, there’s no need to store the answer in memory. Similarly, if you expose yourself to a problem multiple times in a burst, this suggests that the answer may only be needed temporarily—and can also be forgotten quickly. When helpful hints about what knowledge is needed are present, the brain can save effort retrieving it when those hints are absent. Psychologist John Anderson has proposed that these rules guiding memory can be understood as a rational adaptation to deal with the need for knowledge in the real world.

为什么有些困难反而有益？原因之一是大脑是一个绝妙的省力机器。如果你只需看一眼就能找到问题的解法，就无需将答案存储在记忆中。同样地，如果你在短时间内多次接触某个问题，这表明答案可能只是暂时的，而且也很容易被遗忘。当存在关于所需知识的有用提示时，大脑可以在这些提示消失后节省提取知识所需的精力。心理学家约翰·安德森提出，这些指导记忆的规则可以被理解为大脑为了应对现实世界中对知识的需求而做出的理性适应。

Creating a Practice Loop

创建练习循环

Desirable difficulties suggest a tension between seeing and doing in our practice. Without the opportunity to see a pattern for solving a problem, we have to invent it for ourselves. In the best case, this can involve added cognitive load. In the worst case, we may never learn the helpful strategy. Conversely, if we always have easy access to helpful hints, we may not internalize the lessons. One way to resolve this tension is to combine the three components of seeing an example, solving a problem, and getting feedback into a practice loop. By repeatedly cycling through the loop, we ensure that all three ingredients of successful learning are available to us.

理想的困难在于，它暗示着我们在实践中“观察”与“实践”之间存在着一种张力。如果我们没有机会看到解决问题的模式，就必须自己去摸索。在最好的情况下，这会增加认知负荷；而在最坏的情况下，我们可能永远无法掌握有效的策略。反之，如果我们总是能轻易获得有用的提示，就可能无法真正理解其中的道理。解决这种张力的一个方法是将“观察示例”、“解决问题”和“获得反馈”这三个要素整合到一个练习循环中。通过反复循环这个循环，我们可以确保成功学习的三个要素都触手可及。

Butler applied a similar process when advising new writers. “For instance, if they have difficulty with beginnings—they have wonderful stories to tell but don’t know where to begin or how to begin—I have them look at work they enjoy reading. . . . I then ask them to copy half a dozen beginnings; I ask them to copy directly, word for word.” Butler explains her strategy, “ This is not about imitating someone else’s beginnings; that’s why I want at least a half a dozen. It’s about learning what is possible. One of the problems we have as writers is that we either know too much or not enough. . . . We know that there is an ocean of possibilities out there, and we’re overwhelmed. We don’t know how to take from the ocean just what we need.” By studying how other authors have solved similar problems, you can sample from a range of options when dealing with your own stories. Seeing examples is the first step in building new skills.

巴特勒在指导新作家时也运用了类似的方法。“例如，如果他们写作开头有困难——他们有很多精彩的故事想讲，却不知道从何下手——我会让他们阅读一些自己喜欢的作品……然后我会让他们逐字逐句地抄写至少六个开头。”巴特勒解释她的策略时说：“这并不是要他们模仿别人的开头；所以我才要求至少六个开头。而是要让他们了解各种可能性。我们作为作家遇到的一个问题是，我们要么知道得太多，要么知道得太少……我们知道写作的可能性浩如烟海，却不知所措。我们不知道如何从这片海洋中汲取我们真正需要的东西。”通过研究其他作家如何解决类似的问题，你可以在创作自己的故事时从中选择多种方法。学习范例是培养新技能的第一步。

Next, you need to actually perform the skill you’re trying to practice. Seeing can assist with doing, but it can never replace it. To learn a skill, we need to overcome the brain’s effort-saving tendencies that avoid internalizing knowledge we aren’t actively using. Action guides attention. Researchers have found that students tend not to study worked examples until they encounter a problem that requires using them. By cycling back and forth between examples and practice questions, you ensure you’re attending to the lessons and not just skimming them over.

接下来，你需要实际练习你想要掌握的技能。观看可以辅助实践，但永远无法取代实践。要学习一项技能，我们需要克服大脑的省力倾向，这种倾向会避免我们内化那些我们不主动使用的知识。行动引导注意力。研究人员发现，学生往往只有在遇到需要运用例题的问题时才会去学习例题。通过在例题和练习题之间反复练习，你可以确保自己真正关注课程内容，而不是仅仅浏览一遍。

Finally, we need to get accurate feedback on the quality of our attempt. This is a clear stumbling block for skills like writing. Butler struggled for years owing to a lack of high-quality feedback telling her what mistakes she was making in her work. When given the opportunity, Butler aggressively sought feedback on her work. During her classes at the Screen Writers’ Guild, she sought out feedback from one of the teachers, Sid Steeple. “ Whatever you wrote he would go over it and talk to you about it and you might go home feeling like you didn’t much like him but it was the kind of criticism I needed,” Butler explained.

最后，我们需要获得关于作品质量的准确反馈。这对于写作等技能来说无疑是一大障碍。巴特勒多年来一直苦苦挣扎，因为缺乏高质量的反馈，无法了解自己作品中的错误。一旦有机会，巴特勒便积极寻求反馈。在编剧工会上课期间，她向一位老师西德·斯蒂普尔寻求反馈。“无论你写了什么，他都会仔细阅读并和你讨论，你回家后可能会觉得不太喜欢他，但这正是我需要的批评，”巴特勒解释道。

As you progress in a skill, the practice loop can be made more challenging. Seeing examples can fade away as you increasingly tackle problems using your internal reservoir of knowledge. The problems you choose can increase in complexity, as you can manage extra cognitive load from bigger projects. Finally, self-assessment can play an increasing role over external feedback as you develop refined intuitions as to what counts as excellent work. The practice loop creates an opportunity to optimize the level of difficulty.

随着技能的提升，练习循环可以逐渐增加难度。随着你越来越多地运用自身知识储备解决问题，示例的重要性会逐渐降低。你选择的题目也可以越来越复杂，因为你能够应对大型项目带来的额外认知负荷。最后，随着你对优秀作品的判断标准越来越清晰，自我评估的重要性也会逐渐超过外部反馈。练习循环为优化练习难度提供了可能。

Should You See Examples First or Try for Yourself?

应该先看例子还是自己尝试？

Seeing, doing, and feedback are all required for improvement. Pure discovery learning, where the aim is to omit instruction or examples and have the student find the best method, routinely underperforms guided forms of learning. Psychologist Richard Mayer suggests there ought to be a “three strikes rule” against pure discovery learning, owing to a number of prominent failures. Psychologists John Sweller, Paul Kirschner, and Richard Clark go further, arguing against all “minimally guided” forms of learning that ask students to solve problems prior to being taught required knowledge and methods. “ After a half century of advocacy associated with instruction using minimal guidance, it appears that there is no body of research supporting the technique. In so far as there is any evidence from controlled studies, it almost uniformly supports direct, strong instructional guidance,” the authors write.

观察、实践和反馈对于进步都至关重要。纯粹的发现式学习旨在省略指导或示例，让学生自行寻找最佳方法，但其效果通常不如指导式学习。心理学家理查德·梅耶（Richard Mayer）认为，鉴于纯粹发现式学习的诸多失败案例，应该对其采取“三次机会”的规则。心理学家约翰·斯韦勒（John Sweller）、保罗·基尔什纳（Paul Kirschner）和理查德·克拉克（Richard Clark）更进一步，反对所有“极少指导”的学习方式，即要求学生在学习所需知识和方法之前就解决问题。作者写道：“在极少指导的教学方式被提倡了半个世纪之后，似乎没有任何研究支持这种教学方法。就目前存在的对照研究证据而言，几乎一致支持直接、强有力的教学指导。”

On the opposite end, few can doubt the importance of practice. John Anderson, Herbert Simon, and Lynne Reder counter the claim that excessive practice leads to shallower understanding. “ Nothing flies more in the face of the last 20 years of research than the assertion that practice is bad. All evidence, from the laboratory and from extensive case studies of professionals, indicates that real competence only comes with extensive practice.” Omitting either seeing or doing from the learning experience is ineffective.

另一方面，很少有人会质疑练习的重要性。约翰·安德森、赫伯特·西蒙和琳恩·雷德反驳了过度练习会导致理解肤浅的说法。“没有什么比‘练习有害’的说法更与过去20年的研究结果背道而驰了。来自实验室和大量专业人士案例研究的所有证据都表明，真正的能力只能通过大量的练习才能获得。”学习过程中缺少观察或实践环节是无效的。

Yet between the extremes of completely omitting examples or practice, there is a question of sequencing. Do we learn better when we encounter problem situations first? Or should we start by seeing examples? In other words, is the ideal practice loop “see, do, feedback” or “do, feedback, see”? As of the writing of this book, this question is hotly debated. In favor of the problem-solving first approach, psychologist Manu Kapur has argued that the “productive failure” paradigm shows that some students can benefit when problem solving precedes instruction. In his experiments, groups of students are presented with difficult, but still comprehensible, problems to work on. Lacking instruction, they typically fail to solve the problem the way an expert would. After, they’re shown the canonical solution procedure and their early attempts are contrasted with the superior method. For instance, students might be given a problem of a baseball manager trying to draft the player with a more consistent batting average. After students experiment with various ways to calculate this, the concept of variance would be taught and compared with the methods they had initially tried. A 2021 meta-analysis conducted by Kapur reviewed over 160 experimental effects and found a benefit to students who were instructed under the productive failure paradigm. In a related experimental paradigm, Daniel Schwartz and Taylor Martin argue for allowing students to invent their own methods before explaining the correct one. Students are thought to benefit by observing gaps in their own knowledge and then recognizing problem situations where knowledge might apply.

然而，在完全省略示例或练习这两个极端之间，存在着一个顺序问题。我们是在先遇到问题情境时学习效果更好吗？还是应该先看示例？换句话说，理想的练习循环是“看、做、反馈”还是“做、反馈、看”？截至本书撰写之时，这个问题仍是争论的焦点。心理学家马努·卡普尔(Manu Kapur)支持先解决问题的方法，他认为“有效失败”范式表明，有些学生在先解决问题后学习指导时会受益匪浅。在他的实验中，他给学生们布置了一些难度较高但仍然可以理解的问题。由于缺乏指导，他们通常无法像专家那样解决问题。之后，他向他们展示了标准的解题步骤，并将他们早期的尝试与更优的方法进行对比。例如，学生们可能会遇到这样一个问题：一位棒球经理试图选拔一位击球率更稳定的球员。在学生尝试了各种计算方法后，会讲解方差的概念，并与他们最初尝试的方法进行比较。Kapur 在 2021 年进行的一项元分析回顾了 160 多项实验结果，发现采用“有效失败范式”教学的学生受益匪浅。在相关的实验范式中，Daniel Schwartz 和 Taylor Martin 主张在解释正确方法之前，先允许学生自行探索和创造方法。他们认为，学生可以通过观察自身知识的不足，并识别出可以应用这些知识的问题情境而获益。

Other studies have found the opposite pattern, with examples preceding problem solving to be more effective. Greg Ashman, Slava Kalyuga, and John Sweller compared the two sequences of instruction for a science lesson on the efficiency of lightbulbs and found students performed better in the example-first condition. A study led by Inga Glogger-Frey similarly found an advantage for seeing examples before attempting problems. The study’s authors argue that the results are in line with arguments that “ a worked example is more effective than working on an open (inventing) problem when providing equal time on task during such a preparatory activity.” In a study looking at teaching the strategy of controlling variables in experiments, Bryan Matlen and David Klahr found the group with the greatest guidance performed best, but found no difference for timing. They argue that students “ learned and transferred relatively well as long as they received high guidance at some point during instruction.”

其他研究则发现了相反的模式，即先举例再解决问题更为有效。Greg Ashman、Slava Kalyuga 和 John Sweller 比较了两种不同的科学课教学顺序，研究主题是灯泡的效率，结果发现先举例的教学方式效果更好。Inga Glogger-Frey 领导的一项研究也发现了类似的优势，即在尝试解决问题之前先看例子更有益处。该研究的作者认为，研究结果与以下观点相符：“在准备活动中，如果给予学生相同的时间，那么先看例子比先解决开放式（发明式）问题更有效。” Bryan Matlen 和 David Klahr 在一项关于实验中控制变量策略教学的研究中发现，获得最多指导的小组表现最佳，但时间安排对结果没有影响。他们认为，只要学生在教学过程中的某个阶段获得充分的指导，他们就能“相对有效地学习和迁移所学知识”。

Researchers are still probing the boundary conditions for when problem-first or example-first approaches are more successful. Yet, in some ways, this contrast is less significant than it seems. Provided you’re engaging in a practice loop, you should be able to cycle back and forth between encountering a problem situation, attempting to solve it for yourself, and seeing examples of how it is done. The effect of sequencing may be of theoretical interest, but it has fewer practical consequences than the harms of omitting one of the ingredients altogether.

研究人员仍在探索先解决问题还是先举例的方法更有效的界限。然而，在某些方面，这种差异远没有表面看起来那么显著。只要你进行的是循环练习，你就能在遇到问题、尝试自行解决以及观看示例这三个环节之间来回切换。顺序的影响或许具有理论意义，但其实际影响远小于完全省略其中一个环节所带来的危害。

Strategies for Fine-Tuning Difficulty

微调难度的策略

The idea that we need an optimal level of difficulty to make progress in skills is central to many theories of learning. The influential Russian psychologist Lev Vygotsky proposed that we learn through a zone of proximal development—the gap between what we can do with the assistance of others and what we can do on our own. Psychologist Walter Kintsch argued for a zone of learnability drawing from studies of text comprehension. His research found that students with low prior knowledge learned best from well-organized texts.
