Somewhat surprisingly, he found that texts with poorer organization led to better learning for high-knowledge students. In a similar light, the expertise reversal effect proposed by cognitive load theorists finds that changes that make learning easier for beginners become less helpful as they progress. Eventually, those same interventions can actually be negative, as students benefit more from retrieving knowledge in uncertain contexts than seeing further examples. Progressive problem solving is needed for mastery.

我们需要达到最佳难度水平才能在技能方面取得进步，这一观点是许多学习理论的核心。颇具影响力的俄罗斯心理学家列夫·维果茨基提出，我们通过最近发展区来学习——即在他人帮助下能够完成的事情与我们独立完成的事情之间的差距。心理学家沃尔特·金奇则基于文本理解研究，提出了可学习区的概念。他的研究发现，先验知识较少的学生从组织良好的文本中学习效果最佳。令人有些意外的是，他发现对于知识水平较高的学生来说，组织较差的文本反而能带来更好的学习效果。类似地，认知负荷理论家提出的“专家逆转效应”指出，那些使初学者更容易学习的改变，随着学习的深入，其帮助会逐渐减弱。最终，这些干预措施甚至可能产生负面影响，因为学生从不确定情境中检索知识比查看更多示例更有益。循序渐进的问题解决是掌握技能的必要条件。

While it’s easy to agree on the benefits of the optimal challenge level, it can be tricky to achieve it. Butler’s early days were beset with frustration. In contrast, her switch to novel writing, a move that eventually secured her professional status, was likely delayed by at least a few years owing to her apprehensions about tackling more complex works. Getting the difficulty right isn’t easy, but there are a few strategies we can pursue that can help.

虽然我们很容易认同最佳挑战水平带来的益处，但要真正实现却并非易事。巴特勒的早期创作生涯就充满了挫折。相比之下，她转向小说创作——这一最终奠定了她职业地位的举动——很可能因为对挑战更复杂作品的顾虑而至少推迟了几年。把握好难度并非易事，但我们可以采取一些策略来提供帮助。

Strategy #1: The Workshop Method

策略一：研讨会法

Butler credited the workshop environments she participated in Clarion and elsewhere as having a major influence on the development of her craft. “ A workshop is a way of renting an audience, and making sure you’re communicating what you think you’re communicating. It’s so easy as a young writer to think you’ve been very clear when in fact you haven’t.” A workshop environment, especially if it is led by an experienced teacher, also affords an excellent opportunity for a practice loop. By forcing her to write new stories daily, see the stories of her peers, and have them all compared and dissected in class, Butler’s experience at Clarion allowed her to more rapidly assimilate the patterns of good science fiction writing. Far from inhibiting creativity, this library of patterns gave her more space to pursue a unique vision rather than the superficial imitation she engaged in with her early stories.

巴特勒认为，她在克拉里昂及其他机构参与的工作坊对她的写作技艺发展产生了重大影响。“工作坊就像是租用一个听众平台，确保你表达的内容与你预想的一致。年轻作家很容易自以为表达得很清楚，但实际上并非如此。” 工作坊，尤其是由经验丰富的老师指导的工作坊，也为练习循环提供了绝佳的机会。在克拉里昂，巴特勒被迫每天创作新故事，阅读同伴的作品，并在课堂上进行比较和分析，这使她能够更快地掌握优秀科幻小说的写作模式。这些模式不仅没有抑制她的创造力，反而为她提供了更多空间，让她能够追求独特的视角，而不是像早期作品那样进行肤浅的模仿。

Workshop environments also act as a forcing mechanism. While Butler never struggled to submit her work for publication, many writers hold off on getting feedback for fear of scrutiny. Butler remarks that “ getting a rejection slip was like being told your child was ugly. You got mad and didn’t believe a word of it.” It’s easy to slip into desk-drawer syndrome, where work gets submitted to a dusty file folder, never to be seen by anyone. While such ego-saving maneuvers can reduce the sting of rejection, they also guarantee stagnation.

工作坊环境也起到了一种强制作用。虽然巴特勒从未为投稿而苦恼，但许多作家却因为害怕被审视而迟迟不愿寻求反馈。巴特勒曾说过：“收到拒稿信就像被告知自己的孩子长得丑。你会很生气，而且一个字都不相信。” 人们很容易陷入“抽屉综合症”，作品被束之高阁，尘封在文件柜里，无人问津。虽然这种维护自尊的做法可以减轻被拒稿的痛苦，但也注定了写作的停滞不前。

Strategy #2: Copy-Complete-Create

策略二：复制-完成-创建

Copying from an example is an underrated strategy for learning. Yet critics of mindless imitation have a point—it’s easy to cut-and-paste a solution without really understanding why it works. One workaround is to use completion problems. Instead of studying a fully worked-out example, you try to fill in the blank with one or more parts of the example omitted. Jeroen van Merriënboer has found completion problems help in speeding up the acquisition of programming skills by novices, since deleting a key step forces students to mentally engage with understanding the solution, but avoids overloading working memory by trying to generate a full answer. Cloze deletion is a similar strategy advocated by language learning enthusiasts—in this case, you create flash cards that ask you to fill in the blanks in a sentence. This avoids the problem of studying isolated words (which often omits the context needed to truly understand them) without creating the problem of needing to recall entire sentences.

照搬示例是一种被低估的学习策略。然而，批评盲目模仿的人也有道理——人们很容易直接复制粘贴解决方案，却不真正理解其背后的原理。一种解决方法是使用补全题。与其学习一个完整的示例，不如尝试在省略示例中的一个或多个部分后，填入相应的空白处。Jeroen van Merriënboer 发现，补全题有助于新手更快地掌握编程技能，因为删除关键步骤会迫使学生投入精力去理解解决方案，同时又避免了因试图生成完整答案而导致工作记忆过载。填空题是语言学习爱好者提倡的一种类似策略——在这种情况下，你需要制作单词卡片，并填写句子中的空白处。这既避免了学习孤立单词（通常会忽略真正理解单词所需的上下文）的问题，又避免了需要回忆整个句子的问题。

Ultimately, of course, the goal is not to copy or complete, but to generate a solution using the knowledge you have saved in your head. This is why completion problems should be viewed on a continuum, starting with simply studying the example, then filling in the blanks, and finally, producing it for yourself in varying contexts.

当然，最终目标并非复制或完成题目，而是运用你脑海中已有的知识生成解决方案。因此，完成题目应该被视为一个连续的过程：首先是简单地学习示例，然后填空，最后是在不同的情境下自己完成题目。

Strategy #3: Scaffolding

策略三：搭建脚手架

In architecture, a scaffold is a temporary structure that assists in constructing a building before it is completed. Following this analogy, instructional scaffolding is a technique for indirectly modifying the problem situation so as to reduce degrees of freedom. Training wheels are a kind of instructional scaffold, preventing novice cyclists from falling over when they’re still getting used to steering the handles. Motherese, the habit of talking to babies with exaggerated cooing sounds, may also be an instinctual kind of scaffolding that parents use to assist their infants in acquiring language. Marlene Scardamalia and Carl Bereiter, in their work on writing instruction, found that they could activate a more expert-like writing process from children by providing prompts the students could select to evaluate the sentences they just produced. By encouraging students to choose from statements like “ People may not believe this” or “I think this could be said more clearly” after each sentence, investigators were able to force a reflective process of writing that isn’t generally exhibited until later grades.

在建筑学中，脚手架是一种临时结构，用于在建筑物完工前辅助施工。以此类推，教学支架是一种间接改变问题情境以减少自由度的技巧。辅助轮就是一种教学支架，可以防止新手骑自行车时摔倒，避免他们还在适应车把。用夸张的咿呀声与婴儿说话的习惯，也是一种父母用来帮助婴儿习得语言的本能支架。玛琳·斯卡达马利亚和卡尔·贝雷特在写作教学研究中发现，通过提供一些提示，让学生选择来评估他们刚刚写的句子，可以激发儿童更专业的写作过程。通过鼓励学生在每个句子后从“人们可能不相信这一点”或“我认为这句话可以表达得更清楚”之类的陈述中进行选择，研究人员能够促使学生进行反思性写作，而这种写作过程通常在高年级才会出现。

Scaffolding can work by simplifying some of the difficulties encountered in realistic situations. But scaffolding can also be additive, as the intervention by Scardamalia and Bereiter demonstrates. Practicing a conversation in another language with the explicit aim of using a certain phrase or grammatical pattern may be contrived, but it also reduces the working memory burdens compared to trying to use the knowledge when you have genuine communication goals.

支架式教学可以通过简化现实情境中遇到的一些困难来发挥作用。但正如斯卡达马利亚和贝雷特的研究所示，支架式教学也可以起到叠加作用。虽然刻意练习用另一种语言进行对话，并明确地使用某个短语或语法模式可能显得有些刻意，但与在真正需要沟通的情况下尝试运用这些知识相比，它确实可以减轻工作记忆的负担。

What’s Your Practice Loop?

你的练习循环是什么？

Our ability to improve as writers, programmers, athletes, and parents depends on the quality of our practice. Only by integrating seeing examples, solving problems, and getting feedback are we likely to improve at the skills that matter most. Fine-tuning the difficulty is an essential part of that process. In the next chapter, we’ll look at what actually develops as we practice skills. Contrary to popular belief, our minds are not like muscles that strengthen broadly through training—the skills we learn are surprisingly specific.

我们作为作家、程序员、运动员和父母的进步能力取决于我们练习的质量。只有将学习范例、解决问题和获得反馈融会贯通，我们才能在最重要的技能上取得进步。调整练习难度是这一过程中至关重要的一环。在下一章中，我们将探讨练习技能的过程中究竟有哪些方面得到了发展。与普遍认知相反，我们的思维不像肌肉那样可以通过训练得到全面增强——我们所学习的技能往往具有惊人的针对性。

# ↩

Chapter 6

第六章

The Mind Is Not a Muscle

大脑不是肌肉。

Strengthening muscle in one task improves its performance in another task. It is now abundantly clear that the mind is not a muscle in this sense.

增强肌肉在某项任务中的表现，可以提高其在另一项任务中的表现。现在我们已经非常清楚地认识到，从这个意义上讲，大脑并非肌肉。

—Psychologists John Anderson and Mark Singley in The Transfer of Cognitive Skill

——心理学家约翰·安德森和马克·辛格利在《认知技能的迁移》一书中写道

  • Does brain training work?
    脑力训练真的有效吗？
  • Does learning chess, music, or programming make you smarter?
    学习下棋、音乐或编程会让你更聪明吗？
  • What are the building blocks of complex skills?
    复杂技能的构成要素是什么？

I n January 2016, Lumos Labs agreed to pay two million dollars to settle charges from the Federal Trade Commission that they deceived customers with their brain-training program Lumosity. According to the FTC complaint, the company claimed that users who participated in their specially designed games for “10 to 15 minutes three or four times per week” would “ perform better at work and in school and reduce or delay cognitive impairment associated with age and other serious health conditions.” The company was also barred from suggesting that their product “ improves performance in school, at work, or in athletics,” or that it “delays or protects against age-related decline in memory or other cognitive function,” unless it could back those claims with reputable scientific evidence.

2016年1月，Lumos Labs同意支付200万美元，以了结联邦贸易委员会（FTC）对其脑力训练程序Lumosity涉嫌欺骗消费者的指控。根据FTC的投诉，该公司声称，用户每周三到四次，每次10到15分钟参与其专门设计的游戏，就能“在工作和学习中表现更佳，并减少或延缓与年龄和其他严重健康状况相关的认知障碍”。该公司还被禁止暗示其产品“能够提高学习、工作或运动表现”，或“能够延缓或预防与年龄相关的记忆力或其他认知功能的衰退”，除非能够提供可靠的科学证据支持这些说法。

It’s easy to understand the appeal of brain-training programs like Lumosity. Intellectual ability is correlated with nearly every important life outcome psychologists have chosen to measure. Even a small boost to mental functioning could easily make the time investment worthwhile. Unfortunately, there’s scant evidence that brain training works. In a six-week cognitive-training experiment with a staggering 11,430 participants, Adrian Owen and colleagues found that while participants improved on the games they practiced, “ no evidence was found for transfer effects to untrained tasks, even when those tasks were cognitively closely related.” Another study looked at ninth graders as they went through working memory training. Even after two years of continued practice, improvements in the tasks trained didn’t extend to similar tests for measuring fluid intelligence. Nor does brain training appear to protect against age-related cognitive decline. One review of the literature finds that “most of [the studies] have failed to observe generalizable performance improvements.” Aggregating the results of eighty-seven studies in a meta-analysis, Monica Melby-Lervag and colleagues write, “ working memory training programs appear to produce short-term, specific training effects that do not generalize to measures of ‘real-world’ cognitive skills.” Brain training makes you better at the games you play, but little else.

像Lumosity这样的脑力训练项目之所以吸引人，原因显而易见。智力几乎与心理学家选择衡量的所有重要人生结果都相关。即使认知功能只有微小的提升，也能让时间投入物有所值。然而，令人遗憾的是，几乎没有证据表明脑力训练有效。在一项为期六周、参与者多达11430人的认知训练实验中，Adrian Owen及其同事发现，虽然参与者在练习的游戏中有所进步，但“没有证据表明训练效果能迁移到未训练的任务中，即使这些任务在认知上密切相关”。另一项研究观察了九年级学生的工作记忆训练。即使经过两年的持续练习，他们在训练任务中的进步也未能延伸到类似的流体智力测试中。脑力训练似乎也无法预防与年龄相关的认知衰退。一项文献综述发现，“大多数研究未能观察到可推广的认知能力提升”。莫妮卡·梅尔比-勒瓦格及其同事在一项荟萃分析中汇总了87项研究的结果，他们写道：“工作记忆训练项目似乎只能产生短期、特定的训练效果，而无法推广到‘现实世界’认知技能的衡量标准上。” 脑力训练可以提高你玩游戏的水平，但除此之外几乎没有其他作用。

The failure of brain training may not be surprising. Countless products promising to improve our bodies and minds fail to withstand scientific scrutiny. Yet unlike the case of fad diets or multivitamins, the failure of brain training gets to the heart of one of the oldest debates in psychology.

脑力训练的失败或许并不令人意外。无数声称能改善身心健康的产品都经不起科学的检验。然而，与节食减肥或服用复合维生素不同，脑力训练的失败触及了心理学中最古老的争论之一的核心。

The Enduring Allure of Formal Discipline

正规纪律的持久魅力

Brain training owes its justification to a tempting analogy: the mind is like a muscle. Just as lifting weights can later make your arms stronger for carrying groceries or hauling luggage, the analogy goes, so too can strenuous mental activity make the mind sharper for all sorts of unrelated tasks. But while playing digital games to strengthen thinking is a novelty, the mind-muscle analogy is ancient. Plato suggested in The Republic that training in arithmetic, even if it were not used, would nonetheless quicken the mind for other kinds of knowledge. The analogy became the basis for the doctrine of formal discipline, often credited to the English philosopher John Locke, which argued that the value of education came not only from the skills directly taught, but for the general improvement of mental faculties. Learning Latin improved memory, not just for the words studied, but for all sorts of knowledge. Similarly, geometry enhanced the powers of reasoning, poetry cultivated sensitivity, and drawing promoted accuracy.

脑力训练的理论基础源于一个引人入胜的比喻：大脑就像肌肉。正如举重可以增强手臂力量，方便日后搬运杂货或行李一样，高强度的脑力活动也能使大脑更加敏锐，从而胜任各种看似无关的任务。然而，尽管玩电子游戏来增强思维能力是一种新奇的做法，但“脑力与肌肉”的比喻却由来已久。柏拉图在《理想国》中提出，即使算术技能最终没有得到应用，对其进行训练也能使大脑更快地吸收其他类型的知识。这一比喻成为了正规教育学说的基础，该学说通常被认为是英国哲学家约翰·洛克的贡献。洛克认为，教育的价值不仅在于直接教授的技能，更在于对心智能力的全面提升。学习拉丁语可以提高记忆力，不仅能记住所学的单词，还能记住各种知识。同样，几何学可以增强推理能力，诗歌可以培养感性，绘画可以提高精确度。

Beginning in 1901, the psychologists Edward Thorndike and Robert Woodworth conducted a series of experiments to investigate the extent that improvements caused by practice of one skill transferred to other abilities. Thorndike found that geometry and Latin didn’t assist other school subjects more than mundane topics. In laboratory experiments, subjects who learned to estimate the size of small rectangles only improved by a third as much in estimating the size of larger rectangles. Children who practiced discriminating hues made no improvements in their accuracy for guessing lengths or weights. Subjects who greatly improved their ability to detect English verbs showed almost no improvement in recognizing other parts of speech. In contrast with the expansive view of formal discipline, Thorndike argued for a theory of transfer based on identical elements. Improvement in abilities transfer to the extent that those skills share overlapping components. Thorndike concluded that “ the mind is so specialized into a multitude of independent capacities that we alter human nature only in small spots.”

从1901年开始，心理学家爱德华·桑代克和罗伯特·伍德沃思进行了一系列实验，旨在探究一项技能的练习所带来的进步能在多大程度上迁移到其他能力上。桑代克发现，几何和拉丁语对其他学科的帮助并不比对一些日常琐事更大。在实验室实验中，学会估计小矩形大小的受试者，在估计大矩形大小方面的进步仅为前者的三分之一。练习辨别色调的儿童，在猜测长度或重量的准确性方面没有任何提高。英语动词识别能力大幅提升的受试者，在识别其他词性方面几乎没有进步。与形式学科的广义观点相反，桑代克提出了一种基于相同要素的迁移理论。能力的提升只有在这些技能共享重叠的组成部分时才能实现迁移。桑代克总结道：“人的思维已经高度专业化，分化成众多独立的功能，因此我们只能在很小的范围内改变人性。”

Learning Latin to strengthen memory sounds antiquated today, but the doctrine of formal discipline is hardly a relic of the past. It is implicitly invoked whenever advocates argue that we ought to teach chess for its ability to impart strategic reasoning, music in order to enhance creativity, or that programming teaches problem-solving independently of the ability to write actual code. Just as in Thorndike’s day, careful research casts doubt on the wide-ranging benefits often ascribed to these specific subjects. Giovanni Sala and Fernand Gobet conducted meta-analyses of the general cognitive benefits of chess and music instruction. Only small effect sizes were found on enhanced measures of mathematical reasoning or academic ability. “Overall these results may be considered ‘cautiously promising,’” the duo explain. “In fact they are not. The size of the effects was inversely related to the quality of the experimental design.” Considering only studies where the experiments were rigorously performed, “the overall effect sizes were minimal or null.” Similarly, programming does not appear to make you a better problem solver. As the authors of one study explain, “ The rationale for teaching computer programming is that it aids in the development of critical thinking, problem solving and decision-making skills. This contention is not supported by empirical data.” Whether the activity is brain training, chess, or programming, the results appear to be the same: training improves the tasks directly practiced, but there’s little evidence of substantial improvement to other topics.

如今，学习拉丁语来增强记忆力听起来有些过时，但形式主义的理论却并非历史遗迹。每当有人主张我们应该教授国际象棋以培养战略推理能力、教授音乐以增强创造力，或者认为编程可以独立于实际编写代码的能力来培养解决问题的能力时，这种理论实际上就被隐晦地引用了。正如桑代克时代一样，严谨的研究对这些学科通常被认为具有的广泛益处提出了质疑。乔瓦尼·萨拉和费尔南德·戈贝特对国际象棋和音乐教学的总体认知益处进行了元分析。结果发现，它们对数学推理能力或学术能力的提升效果甚微。“总的来说，这些结果可以被认为是‘谨慎的希望’，”两人解释道，“但实际上并非如此。效果的大小与实验设计的质量成反比。”如果只考虑那些实验设计严谨的研究，“总体效果微乎其微，甚至为零。”同样，编程似乎并不能让你成为更好的问题解决者。正如一项研究的作者所解释的那样，“教授计算机编程的理由是它有助于培养批判性思维、问题解决和决策能力。但这种说法并没有得到实证数据的支持。” 无论是脑力训练、下棋还是编程，结果似乎都一样：训练确实能提高直接练习的任务能力，但几乎没有证据表明它对其他方面有显著的提升。

How Much Does Learning One Skill Generalize to Another?

学习一项技能对学习另一项技能的泛化程度有多高？

Practice in one skill is unlikely to produce wide-ranging benefits. But Thorndike’s experiments didn’t settle the debate. Many critics were quick to latch on to the word identical , in his theory of identical elements, pointing out the absurdity of believing learning was limited to exact copies of the original training. “Think of learning to drive a nail with a yellow hammer, and then realize your helplessness if, in time of need, you should borrow your neighbors’ and finding it painted red,” mocked the educator Alexander Meiklejohn. Thorndike’s own experiments, while hardly providing support for the mind-muscle analogy, nonetheless showed more transfer than his own theory predicted. Training experimental subjects on a task to strike out words from a passage containing both the letters e and s , subjects performed better when only one of those letters was substituted (for example, crossing out words with e and r ) than when it involved two new letters. However, subjects who practiced the first task still did better than untrained controls. Similarly, in experiments with mathematical equations, subjects did better when formulas were presented in the form typically taught in school, but their ability didn’t drop to zero when new forms were presented. Whatever the identical elements among skills were, they seemed to be somewhat more general than straightforward pairings of stimulus with response.

练习一项技能不太可能带来广泛的益处。但桑代克的实验并没有平息这场争论。许多批评者很快就抓住他“相同元素”理论中的“相同”一词不放，指出认为学习仅限于对原始训练的精确复制是多么荒谬。“想象一下，你学会用黄色锤子钉钉子，然后到了需要的时候，你借了邻居的锤子，却发现它被漆成了红色，你会多么无助啊！”教育家亚历山大·米克尔约翰嘲讽道。桑代克自己的实验虽然几乎没有为“心智-肌肉”类比提供支持，但却显示出比他自己的理论预测的更多的迁移效果。在训练实验对象完成一项任务：从一段包含字母e和s的文字中划掉单词。当只替换其中一个字母时（例如，划掉包含e和r的单词），受试者的表现优于替换两个新字母的情况。然而，练习过第一种任务的受试者仍然比未经训练的对照组表现更好。同样，在数学方程式实验中，当公式以学校通常教授的形式呈现时，受试者的表现更好；但当呈现新的公式形式时，他们的能力并没有降至零。无论不同技能之间的共同要素是什么，它们似乎都比简单的刺激-反应配对更具普遍性。

Others pointed out that the transfer of improvements made from one skill to another depended on how it was taught. In one experiment, Charles Judd had boys practice throwing darts at an underwater target. One group was taught the principle of light refraction; the other was not. While both groups performed about the same while attempting to hit the first target, when the depth of the target was changed, those who knew how the direction of light bends as it exits the water’s surface adapted better to the new task. In a similar vein, the Gestalt psychologist Max Wertheimer showed that the extent of skill transfer depended on how the problem was perceived. He gave the example of finding the area of a parallelogram. It’s possible to memorize that the answer is base times height. However, if the student understands the logic behind the method, it’s possible to apply it to a wider range of shapes. Understanding leads to more flexible skills than memorizing by rote.

另一些人指出，技能提升能否迁移到其他技能取决于教学方式。查尔斯·贾德曾做过一个实验，让男孩们练习向水下目标投掷飞镖。一组男孩学习了光折射原理，另一组则没有。两组男孩在尝试击中第一个目标时表现相近，但当目标深度改变后，那些了解光线在水面折射方向的男孩更好地适应了新的任务。格式塔心理学家马克斯·韦特海默也指出，技能迁移的程度取决于对问题的理解。他举了计算平行四边形面积的例子。人们可以死记硬背答案是底乘以高，但如果学生理解了方法背后的逻辑，就能将其应用于更广泛的形状。理解比死记硬背更能带来灵活的技能。

The mind may not be a muscle, but the components that transfer between skills can’t be reduced to simple patterns of stimulus and response either. Memorizing an answer and understanding a method may both solve a problem, but the latter is considerably more flexible. Wertheimer and Judd demonstrated that predicting transfer unavoidably depends on how skills are represented in the mind of the student.

大脑虽然不是肌肉，但技能迁移的要素也不能简化为简单的刺激-反应模式。记忆答案和理解方法都能解决问题，但后者要灵活得多。韦特海默和贾德的研究表明，预测技能迁移必然取决于学生头脑中技能的表征方式。

Figure 8

图 8

The area for a parallelogram can be solved by cutting it vertically and moving the left side to the right, so it is transformed into the more familiar rectangle whose area equals length times width. Properly understood, this trick applies to many shapes that have the same abstract property, including the highly irregular shape at the bottom.

平行四边形的面积可以通过将其垂直切割并将左侧边向右移动来计算，这样它就变成了我们更熟悉的矩形，其面积等于长乘以宽。如果理解正确，这个技巧适用于许多具有相同抽象属性的形状，包括底部所示的极不规则形状。

What Are the Building Blocks of Skills?

技能的构成要素是什么？

Early psychologists were handicapped in discussions of transfer because they lacked a precise language for discussing mental representations. Notions of “identical elements” or “good gestalts” were too vague to make predictions about the degree of transfer expected between two tasks. This changed with the cognitive revolution in psychology. Researchers began couching their theories in a language of information processing, producing models that could be simulated on a computer and directly compared to subjects’ performance. From these theories, one of the most serious attempts to model the process of skill acquisition has been John Anderson’s career-spanning work on ACT-R theory.

早期心理学家在讨论迁移问题时受到限制，因为他们缺乏描述心理表征的精确语言。“相同元素”或“良好格式塔”等概念过于模糊，无法预测两个任务之间预期的迁移程度。这种情况随着心理学的认知革命而改变。研究者开始用信息加工的语言来阐述他们的理论，构建出可以在计算机上模拟并与受试者表现直接比较的模型。在这些理论的基础上，约翰·安德森毕生致力于ACT-R理论的研究，是构建技能习得过程模型的最重要尝试之一。

Skills, according to ACT-R, are built out of atomic units called production rules. A production rule is an if-then pattern that combines a condition with an action. Wertheimer’s parallelogram trick, for instance, could be described as the production rule, “IF the left side is congruent to the right side, THEN cut the shape and shift the right side to form a rectangle.” Production rules inherit the simplicity of stimulus-response associations, but with two key differences. The first is that production rules can be abstract. The reference to the “left side” of the shape in our hypothetical production rule doesn’t need to refer to any particular shape. In the same way, once you learn the algorithm for long division, you can perform it on any numbers—you don’t need separate practice on every possible combination of digits. The second difference is that production rules involve not just overt behavior, but mental actions as well. Complex skills can break down into multiple mental steps, such as setting subgoals or manipulating imagined contents. As a result, even if two problems are superficially different, there can be transfer if there are common psychological steps in their solution.

根据ACT-R理论，技能是由称为产生式规则的基本单元构建而成的。产生式规则是一种“如果……那么……”的模式，它将条件与动作结合起来。例如，韦特海默的平行四边形技巧可以被描述为产生式规则：“如果左侧与右侧全等，那么就切割图形并将右侧平移以形成一个矩形。”产生式规则继承了刺激-反应关联的简洁性，但有两个关键区别。首先，产生式规则可以是抽象的。在我们假设的产生式规则中，图形的“左侧”并不一定指代任何特定的图形。同样，一旦你学会了长除法的算法，你就可以对任何数字进行运算——你不需要单独练习每一种可能的数字组合。其次，产生式规则不仅涉及外在行为，还涉及心理活动。复杂的技能可以分解为多个心理步骤，例如设定子目标或操作想象的内容。因此，即使两个问题表面上不同，但如果它们的解决方法具有共同的心理步骤，则也可能存在迁移。

Abstraction and mental actions help explain how a programmer who learns one programming language can acquire a second one much faster. While the exact format of the commands in each language is different, a complex skill like coding also involves more abstract production rules like deciding to make a variable or a function. Similarly, artists and musicians can often pick up new media and instruments faster than untrained beginners because a lot of their knowledge may be abstract. The finger movements for playing the piano are completely different than for the violin, but timing, melody, and the ability to read sheet music are the same. Production rules offer a middle ground between Thorndike’s extremely narrow views on transfer, and the overly optimistic account suggested by the mind-muscle analogy.

抽象思维和心理活动有助于解释为什么程序员在学习一种编程语言后，可以更快地掌握另一种语言。虽然每种语言的命令格式各不相同，但像编程这样复杂的技能也涉及更多抽象的产生式规则，例如决定创建变量还是函数。同样，艺术家和音乐家通常比未经训练的初学者更快地掌握新的媒介和乐器，因为他们的许多知识可能都是抽象的。弹钢琴的手指动作与拉小提琴的手指动作完全不同，但节奏、旋律和识谱能力却是相同的。产生式规则在桑代克关于迁移的极其狭隘的观点和心智肌肉类比所暗示的过于乐观的解释之间提供了一种折衷方案。

One prediction the theory suggests is that with continued practice, skills will become asymmetric. Production rules flow from condition to action but not in the reverse direction. In support of this prediction, Anderson gave students the rule for integration and differentiation in calculus. Like addition and subtraction, these operators are opposites of each other, so the output for differentiation is the same as the input for integration for pairs of formulas. Those who repeatedly practiced applying the rule for making a derivative got better at this rule, but not with forming integrals and vice versa. Similar results have been found with second language learning. Robert DeKeyser showed that students who practice generating a particular sentence pattern made little improvement at understanding it, while those who practiced understanding improved little at generating the pattern. The asymmetry of skills has real-life consequences. Research has shown that French-immersion students in Canada, where schooling is conducted in French from kindergarten to grade 12, typically acquire fluent comprehension, but lag in productive abilities as they have fewer opportunities to practice speaking.

该理论的一个预测是，随着持续练习，技能会变得不对称。生成规则从条件流向动作，但反之则不然。为了验证这一预测，安德森向学生讲解了微积分中的积分和微分规则。与加法和减法类似，这些运算符互为相反数，因此对于公式对，微分的输出与积分的输入相同。反复练习求导规则的学生在运用该规则方面有所进步，但在构建积分方面却没有进步，反之亦然。类似的结果也出现在第二语言学习中。罗伯特·德凯瑟的研究表明，练习生成特定句型的学生在理解该句型方面进步甚微，而练习理解该句型的学生在生成该句型方面进步甚微。技能的不对称性会产生现实生活中的影响。研究表明，在加拿大，从幼儿园到12年级都使用法语进行教学的法语沉浸式教育的学生通常能够获得流利的法语理解能力，但由于口语练习机会较少，他们的表达能力却相对滞后。

Beyond the asymmetry of skills, how well do production rules predict transfer? Anderson tested his theory by having students acquire different skills that were each modeled as sets of production rules. The theory predicts that the speed of learning a new skill will depend on the number of production rules shared between skills (and the degree of learning for each individual production). Overall, the relationship between observed and predicted transfer is an almost perfectly straight line. Despite the near-uniform linear relationship, transfer observed is still somewhat higher than predicted by the model. Anderson argues that this might be because the model omits some of the more general production rules that would be shared between the skills trained.

除了技能的不对称性之外，生成规则对迁移的预测效果如何？安德森通过让学生学习不同的技能来检验他的理论，每种技能都被建模为一组生成规则。该理论预测，学习新技能的速度取决于技能之间共享的生成规则的数量（以及每个生成规则的学习程度）。总体而言，观察到的迁移和预测的迁移之间的关系几乎是一条完美的直线。尽管存在近乎均匀的线性关系，但观察到的迁移仍然略高于模型的预测值。安德森认为，这可能是因为模型忽略了一些在所训练的技能之间共享的更通用的生成规则。

Production rules are one component of the more elaborate ACT-R cognitive architecture. According to this theory, knowledge of facts, concepts, and examples relies on a separate memory system. Overlapping production rules are thus best equipped to explain the amount of transfer we can predict after repeated practice. Nor are all theories of skill are built on production rules. Connectionist systems model skills out of the interactions of countless, simple information-processing units, schema theories represent knowledge in terms of abstract templates, and exemplar-based accounts ground skilled performance on the accumulation of countless remembered instances. Given the amount we still don’t know about the human mind, it’s possible that future researchers will find even more elaborate explanations that fit the data better. What we can say is that production rules, and the ACT-R theory that uses them, is a strong candidate theory and that alternatives, even if they end up describing skills with completely different mechanisms, will have to fit to the same mountain of psychological data that has been amassed to provide support for the theory.

生成规则是更为复杂的ACT-R认知架构的一个组成部分。根据该理论，对事实、概念和例子的认知依赖于一个独立的记忆系统。因此，重叠生成规则最能解释我们在重复练习后能够预测的迁移量。并非所有技能理论都建立在生成规则之上。联结主义系统将技能建模为无数简单信息处理单元的交互作用，图式理论用抽象模板来表示知识，而基于范例的理论则将熟练的表现建立在无数记忆实例的积累之上。鉴于我们对人类思维的了解仍然非常有限，未来的研究者可能会发现更精细、更符合数据的解释。我们可以肯定的是，生成规则以及运用这些规则的ACT-R理论是一个强有力的候选理论，其他理论，即使最终描述的技能机制完全不同，也必须符合为该理论提供支持的大量心理学数据。

The Power and Limits of Abstraction

抽象的力量与局限

Production rules provide one account for how much we can expect practice in one skill to transfer to another. But even if two problems have overlapping solutions, we don’t always avail ourselves of this similarity. A representative example comes from an experiment conducted by Mary Gick and Keith Holyoak. They presented subjects with a story about a general attacking a fortress. The roads leading to the fortress were booby-trapped with pressure sensitive mines. If the general attacked with his full force along any road, the mines would detonate. A smaller force, while escaping the mines, would be easily rebuffed by the defenders. After presenting this story, they gave subjects a problem of treating a stomach tumor with a beam of radiation. A high-intensity beam would destroy the tumor, but also kill any surrounding healthy tissue. A low-intensity beam, in contrast, would spare the healthy tissue but not be enough to eradicate the tumor. The solution to both was structurally the same: split your attack up along multiple trajectories and converge on a central target. Yet few subjects spontaneously made use of the analogy. Despite them being presented side by side, only 20 percent of subjects made the connection, and of those, two-thirds reached only a partial solution. In contrast, when the researchers gave a hint to subjects to use the story when solving the problem, the solution rate jumped to 92 percent.

产生式规则提供了一种解释，说明我们能在多大程度上将一项技能的练习迁移到另一项技能上。但即使两个问题的解决方案有重叠之处，我们也并非总是能利用这种相似性。玛丽·吉克和基思·霍利奥克进行的一项实验就是一个典型的例子。他们给受试者讲述了一个将军攻打堡垒的故事。通往堡垒的道路布满了压敏地雷。如果将军全力进攻任何一条道路，地雷就会引爆。而兵力较少的部队虽然能够避开地雷，却很容易被守军击退。讲述完这个故事后，他们又给受试者提出了一个用放射线治疗胃部肿瘤的问题。高强度放射线可以摧毁肿瘤，但也会杀死周围的健康组织。相比之下，低强度放射线虽然不会损伤健康组织，但不足以根除肿瘤。这两个问题的解决方案在结构上是相同的：将攻击分散到多个路径上，然后汇聚到中心目标。然而，很少有受试者自发地运用这种类比。尽管题目并排呈现，只有20%的受试者建立了联系，而在这20%的受试者中，三分之二只找到了部分解决方案。相比之下，当研究人员提示受试者在解决问题时运用故事情节时，解决方案的完成率跃升至92%。

Another example of failing to use analogous knowledge and skills is the difficulty people have with the Wason four-card task. In this puzzle, subjects are given the rule that “if a card has a vowel on one side, it must have an even number on the opposite side.” Shown the cards K, E, 4, and 7, the task is to pick which cards have to be flipped over to verify if the rule is correct. Which cards would you choose?

另一个未能运用类似知识和技能的例子是人们在完成沃森四卡片任务时遇到的困难。在这个谜题中，受试者被告知“如果一张卡片的一面是元音字母，那么它的另一面一定是偶数”。屏幕上会显示卡片 K、E、4 和 7，受试者的任务是选择哪些卡片需要翻过来以验证规则是否正确。你会选择哪些卡片？

Figure 9

图 9

Wason Card Task: Which cards must you flip to verify that the rule “cards with vowels on one side must have even numbers on the opposite side” holds?

Wason 卡片任务：要验证“一面有元音字母的卡片，另一面必须是偶数”这条规则是否成立，你必须翻开哪些卡片？

In the original study, nearly half of subjects incorrectly choose E and 4. The correct answer is E and 7. While the rule would be violated if an odd number were on the reverse side of an E, there was no rule saying that consonants could not be behind even numbers. Instead, we need to check the 7 because a vowel on the opposite side would violate the rule. Only 7 percent of subjects made the right choice. Fascinatingly, subjects do not seem to perform better at this task even if they have formal training in logic.

在最初的研究中，近一半的受试者错误地选择了E和4。正确答案是E和7。虽然如果E的背面是奇数，规则就会被违反，但并没有规定辅音不能出现在偶数后面。相反，我们需要检查7，因为E的背面是元音会违反规则。只有7%的受试者做出了正确的选择。令人惊讶的是，即使受试者接受过正规的逻辑训练，他们在这项任务中的表现似乎也没有提高。

Now consider a different puzzle: You’re an inspector investigating underaged drinking at a bar. You see an old man, a teenager, a person drinking milk, and a person drinking beer. Whose ID or drink do you need to examine in order to see if the rule “nobody under the age of twenty-one is allowed to drink alcohol” is being violated? Obviously, you need to check the beer drinker and the teenager. Yet these two puzzles have the same structure and solution. * Why do so few people get the first question right, while the latter seems fairly straightforward? One explanation is that due to our experience dealing with norms in social situations, we have an ability to detect rule violations. This allows us to correctly spot the solution when framed in terms of enforcing a law, but it doesn’t get activated when solving the structurally identical card-sorting task.

现在考虑另一个谜题：你是一名酒吧巡查员，正在调查未成年人饮酒的情况。你看到一位老人、一位青少年、一位喝牛奶的人和一位喝啤酒的人。为了确定“21岁以下禁止饮酒”的规定是否被违反，你需要检查谁的身份证或饮料？显然，你需要检查喝啤酒的人和青少年。然而，这两个谜题的结构和答案却完全相同。* 为什么很少有人能答对第一个问题，而第二个问题却显得如此简单？一种解释是，由于我们在社交场合中处理规范的经验，我们具备识别违规行为的能力。这使得我们在执法问题上能够正确找到答案，但在解决结构相同的卡片分类任务时，这种能力却无法被激活。

The difficulty of transfer between analogous tasks isn’t limited to problems concocted in a laboratory. Psychologist Stephen Reed studied how students who had taken an algebra class but had yet to practice word problems would fare when given an example solution and a new problem to solve. When the example and problem shared both the same story and solution structure, students performed well. Yet when the story content differed between them, success rates dropped. If the problem required modifying the solution given in the example, few students could cross the gap. Word problems are challenging for most students, and a dominant strategy for dealing with them appears to be memorizing different problem subtypes and their appropriate responses. This is a far cry from the goal of most algebra teachers, who would hope that their students could readily apply their skills to real-life problems requiring algebra, not just the stereotyped problems used in textbooks. Worse, applying algebra skills spontaneously in real life is usually harder than word problems, as being in an algebra class is an enormously powerful hint as to what kind of knowledge is required. Problems outside the classroom requiring algebra rarely announce this fact when you encounter them. The mathematician and philosopher Alfred North Whitehead lamented the problem of “inert knowledge” in education, of those ideas and methods that could potentially apply broadly, but which lie dormant instead. Even if knowledge is potentially available to solve a problem, we often don’t use it.

类似任务之间的迁移难度并非仅限于实验室设计的问题。心理学家斯蒂芬·里德研究了那些上过代数课但尚未练习过应用题的学生，在获得一个例题答案和一道新题后，他们的表现如何。当例题和新题的故事背景和解题结构相同时，学生的表现良好。然而，当两者的故事背景不同时，成功率就会下降。如果新题需要修改例题的解法，那么很少有学生能够跨越这个鸿沟。应用题对大多数学生来说都是挑战，而应对应用题的主要策略似乎是记忆不同的题型及其相应的答案。这与大多数代数教师的目标相去甚远，他们希望学生能够将代数技能运用到需要代数知识的实际生活中，而不仅仅是教科书中那些千篇一律的例题。更糟糕的是，在现实生活中自发地运用代数技能通常比解决应用题更难，因为上过代数课本身就足以说明需要掌握哪些知识。课堂之外需要用到代数的问题，往往不会在你遇到时就明确地告诉你这一点。数学家兼哲学家阿尔弗雷德·诺思·怀特海曾感叹教育中“惰性知识”的问题，即那些本可广泛应用的思想和方法，却被束之高阁。即使某些知识可能已经存在，足以解决问题，我们却常常置之不理。

Not all findings on the transfer of analogous skills are entirely pessimistic. Geoffrey Fong, David Krantz, and Richard Nisbett found that students taught statistical heuristics like the law of large numbers were successfully able to apply that knowledge when given a quiz disguised as a phone survey. Subjects who practiced solving superficial variations of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle struggled at first to transfer knowledge between structurally identical puzzles. However, these problems lessened as they were given more opportunities to practice. Research on physics experts finds they tend to categorize problems in terms of deeper principles, rather than superficial features. A reasonable interpretation of this research seems to be that while knowledge has a potentially abstract character, it often takes considerable examples and experience to take advantage of even this constrained degree of generality.

并非所有关于类比技能迁移的研究结果都完全悲观。Geoffrey Fong、David Krantz 和 Richard Nisbett 发现，学习过大数定律等统计启发式方法的学生，在接受伪装成电话调查的测试时，能够成功地运用这些知识。练习解决汉诺塔谜题表面变体的受试者，起初难以将知识迁移到结构相同的谜题中。然而，随着练习机会的增加，这些问题逐渐减少。对物理专家的研究发现，他们倾向于根据更深层次的原理而非表面特征来对问题进行分类。对这项研究的一种合理解释似乎是，尽管知识具有潜在的抽象性，但即便如此，也往往需要大量的实例和经验才能充分利用这种有限的概括性。

Practical Consequences of Precise Skills

精准技能的实际后果

The research on transfer should temper our expectations about broad benefits derived from learning specific skills. The most sensible prediction about learning chess is that it will make you better at chess. There might be some benefit to learning to play similar games, such as from learning to manage your time or from sizing up an opponent. But most of what is learned will likely be specific to chess. Subjects like mathematics, whose abstract structure has broad potential uses in many other concrete tasks, may be more generally useful. Yet, here too the full generality of mathematics isn’t always achieved, as many students fail to spontaneously apply the math they’ve acquired in everyday life.

关于迁移学习的研究应该让我们对学习特定技能所带来的广泛益处保持谨慎的预期。学习国际象棋最合理的预测是它能提高你的棋艺。学习玩类似的游戏或许也有一些好处，例如学习时间管理或评估对手。但大部分学习内容可能都仅限于国际象棋。像数学这样的学科，其抽象结构在许多其他具体任务中具有广泛的潜在用途，可能更具普适性。然而，数学的普适性也并非总能得到充分发挥，因为许多学生无法自发地将所学的数学知识运用到日常生活中。

What about learning how to learn? After all, for a book such as this one to have any practical importance, presumably a reader like you would need to extract general ideas about learning and apply it to your specific pursuits. Here I’m cautiously optimistic. I think improving learning is possible, if only because few of the insights gained from research are widely known. The value of retrieval practice over passive review, or spacing over cramming, is not widely appreciated by students and many appear not to choose them when given the option. Yet controlled experiments repeatedly demonstrate they’re more effective generic strategies for learning. Similarly, I believe there are probably shared production rules involved in the planning that goes into a self-directed learning project, conducting research, or studying for classes that extends beyond the concrete material taught. We live in a world quite different from our ancestors, with incredible demands for the acquisition of knowledge and skills, so it wouldn’t be surprising if our instincts regarding learning in our modern environment were occasionally misleading.

那么，如何学习如何学习呢？毕竟，像这样的一本书要想具有任何实际意义，读者想必需要从中提炼出关于学习的普遍理念，并将其应用到自身的具体实践中。对此，我持谨慎乐观的态度。我认为改进学习是可能的，即便只是因为研究中获得的诸多洞见鲜为人知。学生们并不普遍认识到检索练习优于被动复习、间隔学习优于死记硬背的价值，而且许多学生在有选择的情况下似乎也不愿采用这些方法。然而，对照实验反复证明，它们是更有效的通用学习策略。同样地，我相信在规划自主学习项目、开展研究或备考课程的过程中，可能存在一些超越具体教学内容的通用规则。我们生活在一个与祖先截然不同的世界，对知识和技能的获取有着巨大的需求，因此，如果我们对现代学习的直觉偶尔会产生误导，也并不奇怪。

That exception notwithstanding, the research on transfer makes it clear that the broad-based abilities we see in others are built out of myriad smaller parts. Just as fluency in a language is inherently built upon knowing lots of words and phrases, so too is smart thinking built upon having large quantities of specific facts, methods, and relevant experiences. Below, I want to outline three practical consequences of the research just discussed.

尽管存在例外情况，但关于迁移能力的研究清楚地表明，我们所看到的他人广泛能力是由无数较小的部分构建而成的。正如流利的语言能力本质上建立在掌握大量词汇和短语的基础上一样，敏锐的思维也建立在拥有大量具体事实、方法和相关经验的基础上。下面，我想概述一下刚才讨论的研究的三个实际意义。

Takeaway #1: Focus on the Tasks You Intend to Improve

要点一：专注于你打算改进的任务

Broad abilities, like fluency in Spanish or proficiency in Python programming, are really collections of much smaller units of knowledge and skill. While transfer within subjects is certainly greater than zero, it’s also usually less than 100 percent. As we’ve seen, proficiency generating a sentence pattern does not necessarily lead to proficiency understanding it. It makes sense, therefore, to break down large goals into more specific sets of tasks you want to improve at. Knowing how to ask directions to the supermarket in Spanish is a much more modest goal than conversational fluency, but there’s every reason to believe the latter is simply the aggregation of success at the more specific tasks.

像流利的西班牙语或精通Python编程这样的通用能力，实际上是由许多更小的知识和技能单元组成的。虽然不同学科之间的迁移率肯定大于零，但通常也低于100%。正如我们所见，能够熟练地生成某种句型并不一定意味着能够熟练地理解它。因此，将大的目标分解成一系列更具体的、需要改进的任务是明智之举。知道如何用西班牙语问路去超市，这比达到会话流利的水平要容易得多，但我们完全有理由相信，后者仅仅是成功完成这些更具体任务的结果。

Selecting and sequencing the order of tasks to learn is an important part of any practical curriculum, but it can also apply to intellectual skills. After all, the value of subjects like economics and physics lies not in their generic mind-strengthening powers, but for giving you intellectual tools for dealing with concrete problems involving money or motion. Here too we should keep an eye on the tasks we want to be able to perform and ensure that they receive ample opportunity for practice.

选择和安排学习任务的顺序是任何实用课程的重要组成部分，这同样适用于智力技能的培养。毕竟，经济学和物理学等学科的价值不在于它们普遍的思维强化作用，而在于它们能为你提供处理涉及金钱或运动等具体问题的智力工具。同样，我们也应该关注自己想要掌握的技能，并确保它们获得充足的练习机会。

Takeaway #2: Abstract Skills Require Concrete Examples

要点二：抽象技能需要具体例子

The research on transfer suggests a tension exists in how skills should be taught. On the one hand, we want to teach skills in their most generic form possible, to ensure the maximum breadth of application. Students taught the same equations in the context of an algebra class, for instance, later applied this better to a physics class than vice versa. One explanation is that the algebra class is deliberately abstract, and so students take that as a cue to apply it more broadly. On the other hand, abstract skills may remain inert unless we can recognize that they apply in new situations. Avoiding particulars may end up omitting many needed specifics, which is one reason new college graduates often need more specific training before they can do anything useful on the job.

关于迁移的研究表明，技能教学方式存在一种矛盾。一方面，我们希望以尽可能通用的形式教授技能，以确保其应用范围最广。例如，学生在代数课上学习了相同的方程式，之后在物理课上应用这些方程式的效果比反过来要好。一种解释是，代数课本身就具有抽象性，因此学生会将其作为线索，从而更广泛地应用这些知识。另一方面，如果我们不能认识到抽象技能在新情境中的应用，它们可能仍然无效。回避细节最终可能会遗漏许多必要的细节，这也是为什么大学毕业生往往需要接受更多针对性的培训才能在工作中发挥作用的原因之一。

One fix seems to be that providing lots of examples is more likely to ensure students generalize a principle, rather than get stuck on concrete particulars. Instead of a single demonstration, most students probably need to see multiple examples in order to appreciate the full range of a method or idea. Similarly, abstract skills may require further training before they can be practically useful. A person who learns concepts in a computer science class may need additional knowledge and skills to bring that to bear in the particular software projects she encounters at work. Difficulties of application may be compensated for by faster learning when the connection between past skills and new knowledge is pointed out.

一种解决方法似乎是，提供大量示例更有可能确保学生将原理概括化，而不是纠结于具体细节。大多数学生可能需要看到多个示例，而不是单一的演示，才能充分理解一种方法或理念。同样，抽象技能可能需要进一步的训练才能在实践中发挥作用。在计算机科学课堂上学习概念的人可能需要额外的知识和技能，才能将这些知识应用到工作中遇到的具体软件项目中。如果能指出过去技能与新知识之间的联系，就能通过更快的学习速度来弥补应用上的困难。

Takeaway #3: Learn Things for Their Own Sake

要点三：学习本身就是目的

Skills genuinely worth learning shouldn’t need the false promise of generic mental enhancement. Chess is a fine game with a rich history. Mastering its intricacies doesn’t require the justification that it also assist with formulating business strategies. Appreciation of music doesn’t need the additional promise of enhancing one’s ability to brainstorm marketing campaigns, nor does the utility of being able to write computer code hinge on whether it enhances intelligence. Instead of doing the activities with questionable intrinsic merits, we can devote ourselves more fully to the skills and topics we care about for their own sake.

真正值得学习的技能不应该被虚假的承诺——即能够提升整体智力——所束缚。国际象棋是一项历史悠久的优秀游戏，掌握其精妙之处并不需要以它有助于制定商业策略为由。欣赏音乐也不需要额外承诺能够提升策划营销活动的能力，编写计算机代码的实用性也并非取决于它是否能够提升智力。与其从事那些本身价值存疑的活动，我们不如全身心投入到我们真正感兴趣的技能和领域中。

Replacing the Mind-Muscle Metaphor

取代心智肌肉隐喻

The history of thinking about the mind is a history of metaphors. Plato likened the soul to a chariot driver, pulled by the horses of righteous virtue and irrational passions. René Descartes saw the nerves as a system of hydraulics. Associationists argued habits organized the mind and Gestaltists viewed thinking through the lens of perception. More recently, the computer metaphor has become dominant, both in the serial machine formulation of classical cognitive science and the web of interconnected information-processing units of neuroscience. All metaphors reveal in some ways as they mislead in others. The metaphor that the mind is like a muscle is no different. Skills certainly strengthen with practice, so in this sense, the metaphor is correct. Where it misleads is the suggestion that strengthening on one task will lead to general mental fitness in many unrelated tasks. Perhaps a better metaphor is that the mind is a collection of tools, built out of knowledge. Each tool may be specific, but in total they can add up to sophisticated abilities.

关于心灵的思考史，实际上是一部隐喻史。柏拉图将灵魂比作战车车夫，由代表正义美德和非理性激情的骏马牵引。笛卡尔将神经系统比作液压系统。联想主义者认为习惯塑造了心灵，格式塔主义者则从感知的角度看待思维。近年来，计算机隐喻占据主导地位，无论是在经典认知科学的串行机器理论中，还是在神经科学的互联信息处理单元网络中，都得到了体现。所有隐喻在某些方面揭示真相，而在另一些方面则误导人。心灵如同肌肉的隐喻也不例外。技能的确会随着练习而增强，从这个意义上讲，这个隐喻是正确的。但它的误导之处在于，它暗示强化一项技能就能使人在许多不相关的任务中都拥有良好的思维能力。或许更好的隐喻是，心灵是由知识构建的工具集合。每一种工具可能各有侧重，但它们加起来就能构成复杂的能力。

“It may dishearten the teacher to be compelled to think that the gain in power in arithmetic, grammar or translation does not pass over to all other capacities and powers,” wrote Edward Thorndike over a century ago. “There is however, no real cause for discouragement in finding out these facts. There will be as much disciplinary value to studies as there ever was; indeed more, for having found out how little there is and how that little is obtained, teaching is more likely to have general value than it was so long as we trusted that the subjects themselves would in some mysterious way improve the mind as a whole. The real discouraging thing would be for teachers to delude themselves into wrong choices of subject matter and unwise methods on the basis of false notions about the improvement of one mental function upon another.” The value of learning is not diminished if we set aside the notion that the mind is like a muscle. Instead it provides clarity about the nature of the task ahead. Problem solving develops when you have learned how to solve many types of problems. Critical thinking comes from a broad base of knowledge to question dubious assumptions. Accuracy develops from meticulousness in all of your tasks. As Thorndike concludes, “The mind does not give something for nothing, but it never cheats.”

“如果教师不得不承认，算术、语法或翻译能力的提升并不能迁移到其他所有能力上，这或许会令他们感到沮丧，”爱德华·桑代克一个多世纪前写道。“然而，发现这些事实并无真正令人气馁之处。学习的学科价值依然如以往一样重要；事实上，它的价值更高，因为既然我们已经认识到能力的匮乏以及获取这些能力的方式，那么教学就更有可能具有普遍价值，而不是像过去那样，仅仅因为我们相信学科本身会以某种神秘的方式提升整体思维能力。真正令人沮丧的是，教师们基于关于某种心智能力会提升另一种心智能力的错误观念，而自欺欺人地选择错误的学科内容和不明智的教学方法。”如果我们摒弃“心智如同肌肉”的观念，学习的价值并不会降低。相反，它能帮助我们更清晰地认识到即将面临的任务的本质。当你学会如何解决多种类型的问题时，解决问题的能力自然就会发展起来。批判性思维源于广博的知识基础，它使人能够质疑可疑的假设。准确性则来自于对所有任务一丝不苟的认真态度。正如桑代克所总结的那样：“人的思维不会无缘无故地付出，但它也从不欺骗。”

The mind may not be a muscle, but we still want to ensure the greatest generality possible for the skills we learn. In the next chapter, we’ll look at how variable practice is one of the most promising approaches for achieving flexible skills.

大脑虽然不是肌肉，但我们仍然希望所学技能尽可能具有普适性。下一章，我们将探讨多样化练习如何成为培养灵活技能最有前景的方法之一。

# ↩

Chapter 7

第七章

Variability Over Repetition

重复性中的变异性

I used to think, “How could jazz musicians pick notes out of thin air?” I had no idea of the knowledge it took. It was like magic to me at the time.

我以前总想：“爵士乐手怎么能凭空弹奏出音符呢？” 我完全不知道这需要多么专业的知识。当时对我来说，这简直就像魔法一样。

—Calvin Hill, jazz bassist

——卡尔文·希尔，爵士贝斯手

  • How can we learn to improvise?
    我们如何才能学会即兴发挥？
  • How does varied practice lead to flexible thinking?
    多样化的练习如何培养灵活的思维？
  • When is varied practice more helpful than repetition?
    什么情况下多样化的练习比重复练习更有帮助？

I n the early 1940s, on the second floor of Minton’s Playhouse in Harlem, a new kind of music was born. There, musicians such as Thelonious Monk, Charlie Christian, Dizzy Gillespie, and Charlie “Bird” Parker played for each other during the customary Monday night off for performers. Bebop, as the new style came to be known, was a reaction to the swing music dominating dance halls across the country. Swing jazz was played by big bands, in prearranged melodies you could easily move your feet to. In contrast, bebop was limited to just a few instruments, with the emphasis on improvisational solos performed with complex chord changes and rhythms. Free from the demands of a paid performance, the players could challenge each other in increasingly virtuosic displays of technique and creativity. Recalling his time at Minton’s, a young Miles Davis remarked, “ You brought your horn and hoped that Bird or Dizzy would invite you to play with them up on stage. And when this happened, you’d better not blow it.” He recalls, “People would watch for clues from Bird and Dizzy, and if they smiled when you finished playing, then that meant your playing was good.” Just as often, however, the new demands for spontaneous performance could lead to failure. In one episode, stand-up bassist and Minton’s veteran Charles Mingus reduced a saxophonist to tears after talking over his solo with “ Play something different, man; play something different. This is jazz, man. You played that last night and the night before.” It is difficult to overstate the influence bebop has had on jazz, with the ability to improvise on complex material now considered an essential part of the craft.

20世纪40年代初，在哈莱姆区明顿剧院的二楼，一种全新的音乐诞生了。在那里，像塞隆尼斯·蒙克、查理·克里斯蒂安、迪兹·吉莱斯皮和查理·“伯德”·帕克这样的音乐家，利用演出人员惯常的周一休息时间，互相演奏。这种后来被称为比波普的新风格，是对当时席卷全国舞厅的摇摆乐的一种反叛。摇摆爵士乐由大型乐队演奏，旋律事先编排好，让人忍不住跟着节奏舞动。相比之下，比波普只使用几种乐器，强调即兴独奏，运用复杂的和弦变化和节奏。摆脱了演出报酬的束缚，乐手们可以尽情地挑战彼此，展现越来越精湛的技艺和无限的创造力。年轻的迈尔斯·戴维斯回忆起在明顿爵士俱乐部的时光时说道：“你带着你的萨克斯，盼望着伯德或迪兹能邀请你上台和他们一起演奏。而当这种情况真的发生时，你最好别搞砸了。”他回忆道：“人们会观察伯德和迪兹的反应，如果你演奏完毕后他们露出笑容，那就意味着你演奏得不错。”然而，这种对即兴演奏的新要求也常常导致失败。有一次，低音提琴手、明顿爵士俱乐部的老将查尔斯·明格斯在一位萨克斯手独奏时，对着他说道：“换个风格，伙计；换个风格。这是爵士乐，伙计。你昨晚和前天晚上都演奏过同样的曲子。”这番话让这位萨克斯手泪流满面。比波普爵士乐对爵士乐的影响之大，怎么强调都不为过，如今，在复杂的素材上进行即兴演奏的能力已被视为爵士乐技艺中不可或缺的一部分。

Improvisational ability has long been cherished in the African American musical culture where jazz originated. Music ethnologist Paul Berliner, in his fantastic survey of jazz improvisation, Thinking in Jazz , recounts an anecdote from a gospel singer, when a classically trained pianist filled in for her church’s choir:

在爵士乐发源地——非裔美国人的音乐文化中，即兴演奏能力一直备受推崇。音乐民族学家保罗·伯林纳在他那部精彩的爵士即兴演奏研究著作《爵士乐的思考》中，讲述了一个福音歌手的轶事：一位受过古典音乐训练的钢琴家曾代替她所在教堂的唱诗班演奏。

After an introduction to the choir, the pianist asked the director for her “music.” The director explained that they did not use “sheet music” and that the pianist should take the liberty to improvise her part in relation to the choir’s. Taken aback, she replied apologetically that, “[without] music,” she was unable to accompany them. She had never before faced such artistic demands. The choir members were equally astonished by the pianist’s remark, never having met a musician who was dependent upon written music.

在向合唱团成员做完自我介绍后，钢琴家向指挥要了“乐谱”。指挥解释说他们不用“乐谱”，钢琴家可以根据合唱团的演唱即兴发挥。钢琴家听后有些吃惊，抱歉地回答说，没有乐谱，她无法为他们伴奏。她从未遇到过如此特殊的艺术要求。合唱团成员也对钢琴家的这番话感到十分惊讶，他们从未见过一位需要依赖乐谱的音乐家。

This cultural emphasis on improvisational skills found its way directly into the new jazz. As early as 1944, Charlie Parker improvised multiple unique solos for different takes of the same song while recording for Tiny Grimes’s quintet. Miles Davis showed the extent of his improvisational prowess when he had a trumpet valve get stuck during a solo. Unperturbed, he simply carried on playing, treating the now-inaccessible notes as a new musical constraint. “ Energized by its vitality,” writes Berliner, “listeners might well imagine that jazz was thoroughly composed and rehearsed before its presentation. Yet artists commonly perform without musical scores and without a specialized conductor to coordinate their performances.”

这种对即兴演奏技巧的文化重视直接渗透到了新爵士乐中。早在1944年，查理·帕克在为蒂尼·格莱姆斯五重奏录音时，就为同一首歌的不同版本即兴创作了多段独特的独奏。迈尔斯·戴维斯在独奏时，小号阀门卡住，但他并未因此慌乱，而是继续演奏，将这些无法演奏的音符视为一种新的音乐限制，这充分展现了他卓越的即兴演奏能力。“贝林纳写道，‘爵士乐充满活力，听众可能会误以为爵士乐在演出前经过了详尽的创作和排练。’然而，艺术家们通常不看乐谱，也没有专门的指挥来协调他们的演奏。”

Spontaneity should not be confused for a lack of discipline. “ Jazz is not just, ‘Well, man, this is what I feel like playing,’” remarks trumpeter Wynton Marsalis. “It’s a very structured thing that comes down from a tradition and requires a lot of thought and study.” Experienced players liken jazz to a language, with both infinite expressive capabilities, but also strict rules of vocabulary and syntax that prevents those expressions from devolving into gibberish. Saxophonist James Moody likens notes played in the wrong context to “a scream in the middle of a peaceful street scene.” Similarly, Miles Davis once chewed out a young Lonnie Hillyer for not knowing his chords after he clashed with the band during an improvised solo. The anything-goes impression of improvisational jazz is best refuted by the fantastic precision experienced players possess when playing spontaneously. “ My teacher would have you improvise over a song,” one student recalls, “and when you tried, he’d sit at another piano and play your improvised lines a fraction of a second behind you. It could drive you nuts.”

即兴演奏不应与缺乏纪律混淆。“爵士乐并非只是‘嗯，伙计，我想怎么演奏就怎么演奏’，”小号手温顿·马萨利斯说道，“它是一种结构严谨的艺术形式，源于传统，需要大量的思考和学习。”经验丰富的乐手将爵士乐比作一门语言，它既拥有无限的表达能力，又有着严格的词汇和句法规则，防止这些表达沦为胡言乱语。萨克斯管演奏家詹姆斯·穆迪将演奏不当的音符比作“在宁静的街头突然发出尖叫”。同样，迈尔斯·戴维斯也曾严厉批评年轻的朗尼·希利尔，因为他在即兴独奏中与乐队发生冲突，导致希利尔不熟悉和弦。经验丰富的乐手在即兴演奏时所展现出的惊人精准度，有力地驳斥了人们对即兴爵士乐“随心所欲”的印象。一位学生回忆说：“我的老师会让你即兴演奏一首歌，当你尝试即兴演奏时，他会坐在另一架钢琴前，比你慢一瞬间演奏你的即兴部分。这会让人抓狂。”

Learning to improvise presents a serious challenge to the would-be jazz musician. How do you develop proficiency to flawlessly execute the complex chord changes and rhythms on your instrument, while maintaining the flexibility to avoid constantly repeating yourself? Decades after Minton’s Playhouse, aspiring players have used an assortment of techniques to master the ability to improvise. A key feature of many of these techniques is exploiting variability to deepen the effects of practice. Performing the same skills in varied orders, seeing the same concept in varied examples, and thinking about the music through varied representations are central not only to fluent performance, but to creative expression.

对于有志成为爵士乐手的人来说，即兴演奏是一项严峻的挑战。如何才能熟练地演奏出乐器上复杂的和弦变化和节奏，同时又能保持灵活性，避免不断重复？自明顿剧院问世数十年后，有抱负的乐手们运用了各种各样的技巧来掌握即兴演奏的能力。这些技巧的关键在于利用变化来加深练习的效果。以不同的顺序练习相同的技巧，用不同的例子理解相同的概念，并通过不同的方式思考音乐，这些不仅对流畅的演奏至关重要，而且对创造性的表达也至关重要。

Contextual Interference: Making Practice Less Predictable

情境干扰：使练习更难以预测

A first source of variability is simply mixing up what you practice within a session. While improvisational jam sessions clearly embody this kind of variability, many jazz musicians have applied systematic variability within their more structured practice efforts. A simple exercise like practicing the scales, for instance, can explode into endless variations by drilling not just their inversions, but also exploring all the possible intervals and chord combinations. A student of pianist Barry Harris remarked that he used to hate playing the scales as teachers would push students to play it “straight up and down the octave.” Working with Harris, however, he learned how to improvise with scales, remarking, “ I never get tired of playing with them.” Another student in one of trombonist Jimmy Cheatham’s workshops described his advice to “ exhaust all the possibilities” by working through each available permutation. Another example comes from trumpeter Henry “Red” Allen reportedly learning to play in all keys by playing along to records set to different speeds. Each speed would correspond to a different pitch, giving him greater variety with the same fundamental source material. Practicing multiple skills within the same session helps performers stay flexible.

第一个变化来源就是在练习中不断变换练习内容。即兴演奏显然体现了这种变化性，而许多爵士乐手也在结构化的练习中运用了系统性的变化。例如，练习音阶这样简单的练习，如果不仅练习音阶的转位，还探索所有可能的音程和和弦组合，就能衍生出无穷无尽的变化。钢琴家巴里·哈里斯的一位学生曾说过，他以前很讨厌练习音阶，因为老师总是强迫学生“按部就班地上下八度练习”。然而，在哈里斯的指导下，他学会了如何即兴演奏音阶，并说道：“我永远不会厌倦练习音阶。”另一位参加长号演奏家吉米·切瑟姆工作坊的学生则描述了切瑟姆的建议：通过尝试每一种可能的组合来“穷尽所有可能性”。另一个例子来自小号演奏家亨利·“雷德”·艾伦，据说他通过练习不同速度的唱片来学习所有调的演奏。每种速度都对应不同的音高，这使他能够用相同的基本素材演绎出更多样的风格。在同一次练习中掌握多种技巧有助于表演者保持灵活性。

Psychologist William Battig was one of the first to study the connection between practice variability and learning. In his contribution to a conference on the acquisition of skill in 1965, he observed the “ somewhat paradoxical principle” that training conditions which produced greater interference between items studied, and thus worse performance, nonetheless often accelerated learning for new tasks. For psychologists studying memory, interference was viewed as a major obstacle to learning. The observation that increasing interference on one task might improve performance on a different task surprised many. John Shea and Robyn Morgan extended Battig’s early observations to motor skills. In an experiment, they had subjects quickly knock down a sequence of wooden barriers using a tennis ball, in response to one of three different colored indicator lights: red, blue, or white. While the movement skill is purposefully unusual (otherwise some students might have had prior experience with it), it’s not entirely dissimilar to the difficulty faced by musicians, who produce notes and chords through correctly pressing a sequence of keys or valves. They split training into two groups. The first group had a blocked practice schedule, with training on one sequence at a time. The second group trained on all three sequences, in a random order. Consistent with Battig’s theory, the group that practiced in a blocked fashion was faster than the group that practiced under conditions of greater contextual interference. Yet when the groups later practiced two novel sequences—black and green—the group who trained in the varied order performed the new skill faster. This effect remained consistent even after a ten-day delayed test, suggesting the benefits of variable practice were relatively durable.

心理学家威廉·巴蒂格是最早研究练习变异性与学习之间联系的学者之一。1965年，他在一次关于技能习得的会议上发言，提出了一个“略显悖论的原则”：训练条件虽然会造成学习项目之间更大的干扰，从而导致表现更差，但却往往能加速新任务的学习。对于研究记忆的心理学家来说，干扰一直被视为学习的主要障碍。然而，增加一项任务的干扰反而可能提高另一项任务的表现，这一发现令许多人感到惊讶。约翰·谢伊和罗宾·摩根将巴蒂格的早期观察扩展到了运动技能领域。在一项实验中，他们让受试者根据三种不同颜色的指示灯（红色、蓝色或白色）快速击倒一系列木制障碍物。虽然这项运动技能是特意设计的（否则一些学生可能之前有过类似的经验），但它与音乐家面临的挑战并非完全不同——音乐家通过正确按下一系列琴键或阀门来演奏音符和和弦。他们将训练分为两组。第一组采用集中式练习计划，每次只练习一个序列。第二组则以随机顺序练习全部三个序列。与巴蒂格的理论一致，集中式练习组的速度比在情境干扰较大的条件下练习组更快。然而，当两组随后练习两个新的序列——黑色和绿色——时，以随机顺序练习的组更快地掌握了新技能。即使在十天后的延迟测试中，这种效应依然存在，表明随机练习的益处具有相对持久性。

One explanation for the benefit of contextual interference is that it helps the performer develop control processes for deciding which action to take. Practicing in a blocked fashion makes it easier to acquire the individual pattern being learned. However, because the practice is highly predictable, the process of deciding which action to take isn’t developed. Evidence for this view comes from studies that show that the benefits of a randomized practice schedule are higher when the practice involves choosing between different movements (for example, playing one note instead of another) rather than executing the same movement with varying intensities (for example, playing the same notes at different volumes). These results support the view that what variable practice assists with is the process of choosing which action to take, not the fine-tuning of those movements. Such control processes clearly play an outsize role in improvising jazz, where a considerable part of the difficulty is simply deciding which note to play next.

情境干扰益处的一种解释是，它有助于演奏者发展控制能力，从而决定采取何种动作。集中练习更容易掌握所学的特定模式。然而，由于练习高度可预测，决定采取何种动作的能力并未得到发展。支持这一观点的证据来自一些研究，这些研究表明，随机练习安排的益处在练习涉及不同动作的选择时（例如，演奏一个音符而不是另一个音符），比以不同强度执行相同动作（例如，以不同音量演奏相同音符）的效果更佳。这些结果支持这样一种观点：可变练习有助于的是选择采取何种动作的能力，而不是对这些动作的微调。这种控制能力在爵士乐即兴演奏中显然发挥着至关重要的作用，因为爵士乐即兴演奏的难点之一就在于决定接下来演奏哪个音符。

The value of varied practice isn’t limited to motor skills. Jeroen van Merriënboer, Marcel de Croock, and Otto Jelsma found a similar effect in training engineering students to troubleshoot a simulated chemical plant. In their experiment, one-half of the students worked on four different types of malfunctions, with twelve problems presented from each type as a block before moving onto the next. For the other half, the same forty-eight problems were presented in a random order. Once again, the random group did more poorly at solving the problems during practice, and no difference was observed on a later test that quizzed malfunctions previously studied. However, when a new malfunction was tested, the group that practiced under varied conditions performed better. Similar effects have been found in second language learning, where practicing multiple conjugations in Spanish led to better retention when practiced over multiple sessions (although not when the conjugations were first introduced). Another study reports that Japanese learners of English grammar did better on follow-up tests when they engaged in varied, rather than consistent, practice sequences.

多样化练习的价值不仅限于运动技能。Jeroen van Merriënboer、Marcel de Croock 和 Otto Jelsma 在训练工程系学生排除模拟化工厂故障时也发现了类似的效果。在他们的实验中，一半的学生练习四种不同类型的故障，每种类型先呈现十二道题，然后再进行下一种。另一半学生则以随机顺序呈现同样的四十八道题。结果再次表明，随机组在练习中解决问题的表现更差，而且在之后对先前学习过的故障进行测试时，两组学生的表现没有差异。然而，当测试一种新的故障时，在多样化条件下练习的组表现更好。类似的效果也出现在第二语言学习中，例如，在西班牙语中练习多种动词变位可以提高记忆力（尽管在首次学习这些动词变位时效果并不明显）。另一项研究表明，与采用固定的练习方式相比，采用多样化练习方式的日本英语语法学习者在后续测试中表现更佳。

Despite its potential benefit, variable practice remains underused. Most classroom homework assignments minimize contextual interference by carefully segregating questions taught in each unit. Some exams even feature an order of questions that mirrors their order taught within the curriculum, furthering the distortion. Variable practice may be less common because it falls into the unintuitive category of desirable difficulties discussed in chapter 5 . Recall that these were situations where an intervention, say spacing the presentation of material out over time or requiring students to practice recall instead of repeated review, resulted in worse immediate performance but greater long-term learning. Practicing multiple skills in the same session may be overlooked because it appears to result in slower progress.

尽管可变练习具有潜在益处，但它仍未得到充分利用。大多数课堂作业通过精心划分每个单元的习题来最大限度地减少情境干扰。有些考试甚至采用与课程教学顺序一致的题目顺序，进一步加剧了这种偏差。可变练习较少见的原因可能是它属于第五章讨论的“理想难度”这一反直觉的范畴。回想一下，这些情况指的是，一些干预措施，例如将学习内容的呈现时间拉长，或者要求学生练习回忆而非反复复习，虽然会导致短期表现下降，但长期学习效果却更好。在同一节课中练习多种技能可能会被忽视，因为它看起来似乎会导致进步缓慢。

Generating Abstraction: Hearing Sameness and Difference

生成抽象概念：聆听相同与差异

Jazz improvisation requires performers to generate something new, but which still sits comfortably within the language established by convention. Direct copying, while an important stepping-stone, cannot be the final interpretation or the performer will be seen as a mere plagiarist. Conversely, a performer who defies all convention wouldn’t be playing jazz at all. Meeting these contradictory constraints requires performers to develop an abstract representation of the music itself, both its restrictions and its possibilities.

爵士即兴演奏要求演奏者创造出新的东西，但同时又要巧妙地融入既定的音乐语言之中。直接模仿固然是重要的一步，但绝不能作为最终的诠释，否则演奏者就会被视为抄袭者。反之，如果演奏者完全无视传统，那就根本算不上爵士乐了。为了满足这些看似矛盾的限制，演奏者需要发展出一种抽象的音乐表达方式，既要理解音乐的局限性，也要把握其可能性。

Concept formation is the process of figuring out what different examples have in common, as well as what separates them from similar instances that nonetheless don’t count as an example. A child learning the concept “red” might initially include things that adult English speakers would call “brown” or “orange.” If the concept of “red” was only shown in the context of, say, a fire engine, it would be impossible for the child to properly evaluate whether the red of a tomato or a rose merits the same label. Being exposed to a wider range of stimuli that all fall under the same classification helps to generalize an abstraction. Trumpeter Tommy Turrentine recalls that during his early musical education, one teacher would sustain a B on the piano and ask him to remember it. As they walked home the teacher would hit iron poles along the way to set them ringing and quiz Turrentine on the note it created in comparison to the remembered piano key. Such sensory discrimination plays an important role in learning to recognize notes and chords after hearing them played. Musician Howard Levy argues that one of the best ways to learn is to transcribe music heard from recordings. It’s inevitable that you’ll make mistakes in the beginning, he argues, but the act of doing the work yourself to listen builds up perceptual discrimination skills. “In the beginning I couldn’t hear the chords,” a novice student explained. “I couldn’t feel where the chords changed in a piece. Today, I might not be able to identify all the chords in the tunes I hear, but I can hear it when they do change, and that’s a big step from where I started.”

概念形成是指弄清楚不同例子之间的共同点，以及它们与那些看似相似但实际上并非例子的例子之间的区别。例如，一个孩子在学习“红色”这个概念时，最初可能会把一些英语成年人称之为“棕色”或“橙色”的东西也包含在内。如果“红色”这个概念仅仅出现在诸如消防车之类的语境中，那么孩子就无法正确判断西红柿和玫瑰的红色是否应该被贴上同样的标签。接触更多属于同一类别的刺激有助于概括抽象概念。小号演奏家汤米·图伦廷回忆说，在他早期的音乐学习中，一位老师会弹奏一个持续的B音，并让他记住。在回家的路上，老师会敲击沿途的铁杆，让它们发出声响，然后考图伦廷，让他辨别铁杆发出的音符与他记忆中的钢琴音符是否一致。这种感官辨别能力在学习识别听过的音符和和弦方面起着重要作用。音乐家霍华德·莱维认为，学习音乐的最佳方法之一就是扒谱。他指出，一开始犯错是不可避免的，但亲自动手聆听的过程本身就能培养感知辨别能力。“一开始我根本听不出和弦，”一位初学者解释说，“我感觉不到乐曲中和弦的变化。现在，我或许还不能识别出所有听到的曲子中的和弦，但我能听出它们何时发生变化，这比我刚开始的时候进步很大。”

Learning sameness and difference in sensory qualities is only the beginning of the skills needed to improvise fluently. Composer Chuck Israels remarks that an “ essential ingredient in learning to be a musician is the ability to recognize a parallel case when you’re confronted with one.” In high school, Israels played games with his peers to learn to recognize a song solely from its chord progression. Transposition exercises, where the student shifts a familiar phrase into a new key, can be useful not just for increasing the variety of practice, but also for learning to recognize the hidden link between seemingly different pieces of music. “ Discovering that certain, apparently different phrases gleaned from disparate solos share a similar basis is a familiar revelation for students,” writes Paul Berliner. Making finer distinctions, not just revealing hidden commonalities, is an equal component of developing one’s knowledge base. Singer Carmen Lundy remarked that at first she could only recognize “jazz licks” but as her experience progressed, she could distinguish “bebop licks” and eventually “ Charlie Parker licks and Sonny Rollins licks.”

学习感知音色上的异同仅仅是流畅即兴演奏所需技能的开始。作曲家查克·伊斯雷尔斯（Chuck Israels）指出，“学习成为一名音乐家的关键要素之一是能够在遇到相似情况时识别出来。”高中时，伊斯雷尔斯曾与同学们玩游戏，学习仅凭和弦进行来识别歌曲。移调练习，即学生将熟悉的乐句移调到新的调上，不仅有助于增加练习的多样性，还有助于学习识别看似不同的乐段之间隐藏的联系。保罗·柏林纳（Paul Berliner）写道：“发现从不同的独奏中摘取的某些看似不同的乐句具有相似的基础，对学生来说是一种常见的顿悟。” 做出更细致的区分，而不仅仅是揭示隐藏的共性，是拓展知识体系的重要组成部分。歌手卡门·伦迪表示，起初她只能识别“爵士乐的即兴演奏”，但随着经验的积累，她能够区分“比波普乐的即兴演奏”，最终还能区分“查理·帕克的即兴演奏和桑尼·罗林斯的即兴演奏”。

Research on interleaving has confirmed the value of presenting different, but easily confused, concepts together, rather than the more typical approach of separately teaching examples of each concept in isolation. Rose Hatala and coauthors found that medical students studying electrocardiogram readings did better when patterns for different diseases were mixed together during presentation, compared to presenting patterns for one disease at a time. Similar results have been found in learning to recognize categories of molecules in organic chemistry, painting styles by different artists, and different species of birds and butterflies. Showing examples of different concepts in succession appears to assist with noticing the features that help to separate them, while showing seemingly different examples of the same phenomenon helps students to recognize what they have in common. Direct Instruction, the successful teaching methodology developed by Siegfried Engelmann and Wesley Becker we encountered in chapter 3 , exploits this effect by carefully sequencing examples and similar-seeming non-examples to illustrate concepts. For instance, in trying to teach children to recognize the letter d , the instructor wouldn’t just show the letter in a single typeface, but varied fonts to show the full range of visual displays that literate adults correctly categorize: d, d, d, d, d , etc. Then, mixed in with these presentations, the instructor would show similar, but distinct, letters. For instance, a has a similar visual shape to d , but a different sound and name; t has a similar sounding name, but different shape; and p has both a similar sounding name and shape, but all refer to different letters. Letter recognition tasks may seem trivial, but that’s largely because of our extensive experience with reading. If you’re not able to read Chinese characters, consider trying to discriminate 已 (for example, 已, 已 , 已 , 已) from the highly similar 己 (for example, 己, 己 , 己 , 己) in various fonts, and it’s easy to see why letter recognition takes considerable practice! By juxtaposing maximally different examples of the same concept, with minimally different examples of different concepts, the student can more quickly home in on the exact boundaries of the ideas.

交错教学法的研究证实，将不同但容易混淆的概念放在一起呈现，比单独教授每个概念的例子更有价值。Rose Hatala及其合作者发现，在学习心电图判读时，如果将不同疾病的模式混合在一起呈现，医学生的学习效果会更好，而如果每次只呈现一种疾病的模式，效果则更佳。在学习识别有机化学中的分子类别、不同艺术家的绘画风格以及不同种类的鸟类和蝴蝶时，也发现了类似的结果。依次展示不同概念的例子似乎有助于学生注意到区分它们的特征，而展示看似不同的同一现象的例子则有助于学生认识到它们的共同之处。我们在第三章中提到的由Siegfried Engelmann和Wesley Becker开发的直接教学法，正是利用了这种效应，通过精心安排例子和看似相似的反例来阐释概念。例如，在教孩子认字母 d 时，老师不会只用一种字体展示这个字母，而是会使用不同的字体，向孩子们展示所有视觉呈现方式，以便让识字的成年人能够正确区分：d、d、d、d、d、d 等等。然后，老师会在这些展示中穿插展示一些相似但不同的字母。例如，a 的视觉形状与 d 相似，但发音和名称不同；t 的发音和名称相似，但形状不同；p 的发音和形状都相似，但它们指的都是不同的字母。字母识别任务看似简单，但这主要是因为我们拥有丰富的阅读经验。如果你不识字，不妨尝试区分不同字体下的“已”（例如，已、已、已、已）和高度相似的“己”（例如，己、己、己、己），你就会明白为什么字母识别需要大量的练习！通过将同一概念的不同例子进行最大程度的对比，与不同概念的不同例子进行最小程度的对比，学生可以更快地掌握概念的确切界限。

Multiple Representations: Having More Ways to Play

多种表现形式：更多游戏方式

A final source of useful variability that jazz improvisors exploit is possessing multiple systems for thinking about music. “ The more ways you have of thinking about music, the more things you have to play in your solos,” remarks Barry Harris. One source of representational variety is training both the ear and the eye to understand music. Many great jazz improvisors, lacking formal music education, had extensive aural practice, being able to pick out what sounds good simply by listening to it. Trombonist Melba Liston remarks she “ knew what notes didn’t fit the chords and didn’t sound good,” and so she “tiptoed around” the notes that didn’t work. This knowledge, however, often runs into limitations as songs become more complex. Saxophonist Gary Bartz struggled during jam sessions to improvise on tunes like “You Stepped on a Dream,” relying on aural skills alone. It wasn’t until trombonist Grachan Moncur taught him the theoretical principles of harmony in jazz that he was able to understand how the music worked. Conversely, artists with more extensive formal education often find their overreliance on a visual understanding of the music to be a handicap. Paul Berliner documents one student, who was originally trained as a classical musician:

爵士即兴演奏者利用的最后一个有用的变化来源是拥有多种音乐思维系统。“你思考音乐的方式越多，你在独奏中可以演奏的东西就越多，”巴里·哈里斯说道。表现形式的多样性之一是训练耳朵和眼睛来理解音乐。许多伟大的爵士即兴演奏家虽然没有接受过正规的音乐教育，但他们拥有大量的听觉练习，能够仅凭聆听就分辨出哪些声音好听。长号演奏家梅尔巴·利斯顿曾说过，她“知道哪些音符与和弦不搭，听起来不好听”，所以她会“小心翼翼地避开”那些不合适的音符。然而，随着歌曲变得越来越复杂，这种知识往往会受到限制。萨克斯管演奏家加里·巴茨在即兴演奏《你踩碎了一个梦》这样的曲子时，仅仅依靠听觉技巧就显得力不从心。直到长号手格拉汉·蒙克尔向他讲解了爵士乐和声的理论原理，他才真正理解了这种音乐的运作方式。相反，接受过更系统正规教育的艺术家往往会发现，他们过度依赖对音乐的视觉理解反而成为了一种障碍。保罗·柏林纳记录了一位最初接受古典音乐训练的学生：

It was not until he was immersed in his jazz training that he discovered that his exclusive dependence on written music had, in fact, undermined the development of his aural skills. As a result, his retention of material learned from recordings greatly lagged behind that of musicians who had grown up in the jazz tradition. It required years of experience with the jazz community’s methods for him to close the gap.

直到他全身心投入爵士乐训练后，才发现自己对乐谱的过度依赖实际上阻碍了听觉能力的培养。结果，他对从录音中学习到的素材的掌握程度远远落后于那些在爵士乐传统中成长起来的音乐家。他需要多年与爵士乐界的训练方法相结合，才能弥补这一差距。

Just as being able to understand a song from a recording or sheet music gives performers more flexibility, so does having multiple mnemonic systems to recognize it. Chords, scales, and intervals all provide ways of representing pitch relationships within music. However, each divides up the musical possibilities in different ways. “For learners, the discovery of scales and their theoretical relationship to chords constitutes a major conceptual breakthrough with immediate application,” writes Berliner. Musician Greg Langdon reportedly had a “revelation” when he discovered that “G harmonic minor scale up from the fifth degree” had the same pattern as “ E-flat major arpeggio with half steps” added below each degree. Being able to see the same music in different ways gives improvisors more possibilities.

正如能够通过录音或乐谱理解歌曲能让演奏者拥有更大的灵活性一样，拥有多种记忆系统来识别歌曲也能起到同样的作用。和弦、音阶和音程都提供了在音乐中表示音高关系的方法。然而，它们各自以不同的方式划分了音乐的可能性。“对于学习者来说，发现音阶及其与和弦的理论关系构成了一项重要的概念突破，并能立即应用，”柏林纳写道。据报道，音乐家格雷格·兰登在发现“从五度音开始的G和声小调音阶”与“在每个音级下方添加半音的降E大调琶音”具有相同的模式时，获得了“顿悟”。能够以不同的方式看待同一首乐曲，为即兴演奏者提供了更多可能性。

The value of varied representations isn’t limited to jazz. Physicist and Nobel laureate Richard Feynman remarked on the exceptional usefulness of having multiple ways of thinking about the same phenomena:

多样化表达方式的价值并不局限于爵士乐。物理学家、诺贝尔奖得主理查德·费曼曾指出，用多种方式思考同一现象具有非凡的实用价值：

Suppose you have two theories A and B, which look completely different psychologically, different ideas in them and so on, but all the consequences that are computed from them are exactly the same. . . .

假设你有两种理论A和B，它们在心理学上看起来完全不同，包含不同的想法等等，但从它们推导出的所有结果却完全相同……

[In this case] people usually say in science that one doesn’t know how to distinguish them. However, for psychological reasons . . . these two things are very far from equivalent, because one gives a man very different ideas from another. . . .

[在这种情况下]，科学界通常说人们不知道如何区分它们。然而，出于心理学原因……这两者相去甚远，因为它们会给不同的人带来截然不同的想法……

Therefore, psychologically, we must keep all the theories in our head and any theoretical physicist that’s any good knows six or seven different theoretical representations for exactly the same physics.

因此，从心理学角度来说，我们必须把所有理论都记在脑子里，任何优秀的理论物理学家都知道同一物理现象有六七种不同的理论表述。

Multiple representations are equivalent to having the ability to formulate the same problem in different problem spaces. Herbert Simon and Allen Newell provide a helpful demonstration with the game of number scrabble. This is a two-player game where tiles having the digits one through nine are placed face up between them. Players then take turns choosing a tile, with the first player to possess three tiles that sum to fifteen winning the game. For instance, if the first player draws 2, 7, and 6 (2 + 7 + 6 = 15), they win the game. Interestingly, it can be shown that number scrabble is actually structurally identical to tic-tac-toe. A correspondence can be found simply by labeling the squares with the numbers 1–9 according to the diagram below. Drawing a tile is equivalent to putting an X or O on the square, and you’ll have a set of three that combine to fifteen if and only if you have made a corresponding row, column, or diagonal on the labeled tic-tac-toe board. Just because two representations are formally equivalent does not mean they are psychologically equivalent, and what might be obvious in one format may require intensive thinking to deduce in another.

多种表征等价于能够在不同的问题空间中构建同一个问题。赫伯特·西蒙和艾伦·纽厄尔用数字拼字游戏（Number Scrabble）提供了一个有用的示例。这是一个双人游戏，玩家将数字1到9的方块正面朝上放置在两人之间。然后，玩家轮流抽取方块，最先拥有三个数字之和为15的方块的玩家获胜。例如，如果第一个玩家抽到2、7和6（2 + 7 + 6 = 15），则他/她获胜。有趣的是，可以证明数字拼字游戏在结构上实际上与井字棋完全相同。只需根据下图用数字1到9标记方格，即可找到对应关系。抽取方块相当于在方格上放置一个X或O，当且仅当你在井字棋盘上组成了对应的行、列或对角线时，你才能拥有三个数字之和为15的方块。仅仅因为两种表述形式上等价，并不意味着它们在心理上等价，而且在一种形式中显而易见的事情，在另一种形式中可能需要深入思考才能推断出来。

Figure 10

图 10

By assigning each grid square the numbers above, the game of number scrabble transforms into the more familiar tic-tac-toe.

通过给每个方格分配上述数字，数字拼字游戏就变成了更熟悉的井字棋。

The psychologist Kurt Lewin famously opined, “ There is nothing so practical as a good theory.” In our current culture, theoretical and practical knowledge are often contrasted as belonging to different domains, or worse, being in active opposition. While it’s true that theoreticians and practitioners often belong to different groups, with differing goals and needs, theories themselves are simply tools. With more tools, better adapted to the reality we work on, we can solve a greater variety of problems.

心理学家库尔特·勒温曾说过一句名言：“没有什么比好的理论更实用。”在当今文化中，理论知识和实践知识常常被对立起来，认为它们属于不同的领域，甚至更糟的是，它们之间存在着激烈的冲突。虽然理论家和实践者往往属于不同的群体，有着不同的目标和需求，但理论本身仅仅是工具。拥有更多更贴合实际的工具，我们就能解决更多种类的问题。

When Is Variability Helpful?

何时需要引入变异性？

Practicing multiple skills in the same session, seeing a full range of examples with interleaving contrasting cases, and learning to represent the same ideas in multiple ways can all be beneficial. But obviously, there are limits to how much variability can help. As we saw in the last chapter, training that results in improvement to skills that don’t share overlapping knowledge or procedures has often been difficult to demonstrate. Most of the benefits of variable practice center around practicing patterns within the same overall skill. Juxtaposing different examples or exercises is beneficial to the extent that we’re likely to confuse the problems. We wouldn’t expect interleaving math questions with history homework to yield the same benefit (although there might be a separate benefit for spacing out the material, as discussed in chapter 5 ). Similarly, while abstractions generated from multiple examples may be beneficial, there are probably limits to how abstract concepts can become while still retaining their usefulness. While chess strategy and business strategy likely share some concepts in common, success at each requires a lot of specific knowledge that doesn’t really have an analogue in its counterpart, even if we can use the same word, strategy , to describe them.

在同一节课中练习多种技能，观看一系列穿插对比案例的完整示例，以及学习用多种方式表达相同的概念，这些都可能带来益处。但显然，多样化练习的益处也是有限度的。正如我们在上一章中看到的，训练如果能够提高那些知识或流程不重叠的技能，往往难以证明其效果。多样化练习的大部分益处都集中在练习同一整体技能中的模式。将不同的例子或练习并置练习之所以有益，是因为我们可能会混淆问题。我们不会指望将数学题和历史作业交错练习能带来同样的益处（尽管如第五章所述，分散学习材料可能还有其他好处）。同样，虽然从多个例子中提炼出的抽象概念可能是有益的，但抽象程度可能存在上限，超过这个上限，概念的实用性就会降低。虽然国际象棋战略和商业战略可能有一些共同的概念，但两者的成功都需要大量的专业知识，而这些知识在对方领域中并没有真正的对应物，即使我们可以使用同一个词“战略”来描述它们。

Another factor that determines the usefulness of variability is how much variation the final skill requires. A classical pianist, who doesn’t need to improvise new tunes, may benefit from a more repetitive practice schedule, since she can safely assume the notes from Beethoven’s Ninth Symphony will always be played in the same order. Learning is slower under a variable practice schedule, so benefits only emerge when a variety of skills are actually needed. A linguist studying Romance languages might develop a more abstract and flexible understanding of Latin if she practiced French, Spanish, and Portuguese in sessions close together. However, if a person only needs to live in France, then learning three languages is certainly slower than simply learning one. What variable practice shows is that if she needed to speak all three languages, she might benefit from practice sessions that alternated between the languages. How much variability is helpful depends critically on the skills that eventually need to be performed.

决定练习多样性是否有效的另一个因素是最终技能所需的变化程度。一位不需要即兴创作新曲子的古典钢琴家可能更适合重复性更高的练习计划，因为她可以肯定地认为贝多芬第九交响曲的音符总是以相同的顺序演奏。在多样化的练习计划下，学习速度会变慢，因此只有当实际需要多种技能时，其益处才会显现。一位学习罗曼语族语言的语言学家，如果将法语、西班牙语和葡萄牙语的练习安排在相近的时间，可能会对拉丁语形成更抽象、更灵活的理解。然而，如果一个人只需要在法国生活，那么学习三种语言肯定比只学习一种语言要慢。多样化的练习表明，如果她需要掌握这三种语言，那么交替练习这三种语言可能会对她更有益。多样性究竟有多大帮助，关键取决于最终需要掌握的技能。

A final moderation on practice variability is under what conditions variability is helpful. Gabriele Wulf and Charles Shea note that complex motor skills and performers with low prior experience to a domain often benefit from blocked practice rather than varied practice schedules.
