An easy way to understand the apparent contradiction is in terms of cognitive load theory. Variable practice creates greater cognitive load, and so if the task is too difficult to perform correctly in optimal conditions, adding extra load will tend to make it even harder to grasp. However, as performers gain familiarity with the underlying movements, the skill becomes more automatic and so practice schedules that cultivate the ability to discriminate between patterns become more useful. Evidence for this perspective comes from research that finds English learners with more experience benefited more from practice listening to multiple speakers, while lower-experience learners benefited more from listening to a single speaker. Similar results were found with practice variability in mathematics—students with less prior knowledge benefited from practice on questions that were minimally different, while students with greater prior knowledge learned more from practice questions that varied more substantially.

最后，关于练习多样性的最后一个需要探讨的问题是：在什么情况下多样性才有效？Gabriele Wulf 和 Charles Shea 指出，复杂的运动技能以及在某一领域经验较少的练习者，通常从集中练习而非多样化的练习安排中获益。理解这种看似矛盾的现象的一个简单方法是运用认知负荷理论。多样化的练习会增加认知负荷，因此，如果即使在最佳条件下，任务也难以正确完成，那么增加额外的负荷反而会使掌握它变得更加困难。然而，随着练习者对基本动作的熟悉程度提高，技能会变得更加自动化，因此，培养区分不同模式能力的练习安排会更加有效。支持这一观点的证据来自一项研究：研究发现，英语学习经验更丰富的学习者从聆听多位说话者的练习中获益更多，而经验较少的学习者则从聆听一位说话者的练习中获益更多。类似的结果也出现在数学练习的多样性中——先前知识较少的学生从练习差异较小的题目中获益更多，而先前知识较多的学生则从差异较大的练习题中获益更多。

This perspective suggests variability is something to ramp up over the course of learning, rather than simply start out at a maximal level. For skills that are extremely difficult to perform correctly even once, consistent repetition, rather than variation, is probably called for. This is also clear from Berliner’s study of jazz improvisors. Faithful imitation, produced through hours of attempting to play along to recordings—rather than improvisation—was the typical starting point for musicians. “Woodshedding,” where artists retreat into the figurative woodshed to repetitively practice in isolation, was a common habit among skilled performers. The strident efforts to replicate the published solos of master jazz players can themselves produce ingenious results. Bassist George Duvivier developed an unusual fingering technique to master a complex solo he heard recorded, repeating it endlessly until he had mastered it. It wasn’t until he heard the band play live that he discovered what he originally thought of as a solo was actually two musicians playing on the same instrument! Even Charlie Parker, one of the originators of bebop, reportedly retreated into lengthy practice sessions after finding himself outmatched at an early showing at Minton’s Playhouse. As we’ve seen in the previous chapters, repetition and imitation are not antithetical to spontaneous creativity, but essential precursors to it.

这种观点认为，学习过程中应该逐步增加练习的多样性，而不是一开始就追求极致。对于那些即使只练习一次也极其困难的技能，持续的重复练习而非变化练习或许更为必要。柏林纳对爵士即兴演奏者的研究也印证了这一点。忠实的模仿——通过数小时尝试跟着录音演奏——而非即兴创作，是音乐家们通常的起点。“苦练”（即艺术家们躲进隐喻意义上的“木棚”里，独自反复练习）是技艺精湛的演奏者们的常见习惯。对爵士大师已发表的独奏进行不懈的模仿，本身就能产生巧妙的成果。贝斯手乔治·杜维维尔为了掌握一段他听到的复杂独奏录音，发展出一种独特的指法技巧，他反复练习直到完全掌握。直到他现场聆听乐队演奏时，才发现他最初以为的独奏实际上是两位乐手在同一件乐器上演奏！据说，就连比波普爵士乐的创始人之一查理·帕克，在明顿剧院的一次早期演出中表现不佳后，也曾陷入长时间的练习之中。正如我们在前几章中所看到的，重复和模仿并非与自发创造力相悖，而是其必不可少的先决条件。

Part of the motivation for wording this maxim as “Variability Over Repetition” and not “Variability Instead of Repetition” was to acknowledge this tension between imitation and improvisation that exists in a complex skill like playing jazz. Variability is essential to flexibly execute skills in new ways. However, that variability grows on top of, and not opposed to, the continual repetition of component skills that ensures fluency.

之所以将这条格言表述为“变化胜于重复”，而非“变化取代重复”，部分原因是为了承认在演奏爵士乐这类复杂技能中，模仿与即兴发挥之间存在着一种张力。变化对于灵活地以新的方式运用技能至关重要。然而，这种变化是建立在而非与持续重复构成技能的基础之上的，而持续重复正是确保流畅演奏的关键所在。

Strategies to Make Use of Variable Practice

利用可变练习的策略

Variable practice is one of the best strategies researchers have uncovered to promote transfer of skills to new contexts. Unfortunately, it’s also a method that has remained underused. Classroom curricula often minimize variability, limiting questions to those from the most recent chapter or presenting a sequence of practice problems of exactly the same type. Below are four different strategies that you can use to make use of variable practice in your own efforts.

多样化练习是研究人员发现的促进技能迁移到新情境的最佳策略之一。然而，遗憾的是，这种方法却一直未得到充分利用。课堂教学往往尽量减少练习的多样性，例如只练习最新章节的内容，或者提供一系列完全相同的练习题。以下四种策略可以帮助你在自己的教学实践中运用多样化练习。

Strategy #1: Shuffle Your Studying

策略一：调整学习顺序

The easiest way to apply variable practice is simply to randomize what you practice within a studying session. Since most learning materials are carefully organized into different topics, this can take a little bit of extra work. If you’re studying flash cards, for instance, you might want to test yourself in a random order, rather than going through one topic at a time. If you’re working through practice problems for a test, you might want to shuffle the problems together so you can’t tell which ones come from which unit. If you’re practicing tennis shots on the court, you might want to mix up backhand and forehand shots, rather than work on them individually.

最简单的实现多样化练习的方法就是在学习过程中随机安排练习内容。由于大多数学习资料都按主题精心组织，这可能需要一些额外的工作。例如，如果你在学习记忆卡片，不妨随机进行测试，而不是一次只学习一个主题。如果你在做考试练习题，可以把题目打乱顺序，这样就无法分辨哪些题目来自哪个单元。如果你在球场上练习网球击球，可以把反手和正手击球混合练习，而不是单独练习。

One way to benefit from a randomized schedule is to start with a list of different problems you want to practice from a particular skill, and assign each a card from a deck of cards. A Spanish student could list out different conjugation exercises and assign each exercise a playing card. A similar approach can be applied to learning programming functions, guitar chords, badminton serves, or physics problems. The only thing that matters is that their performance is short enough that you would be able to work on more than one in a single practice session. Then shuffle a deck of cards with the ones you’ve assigned and draw them out, practicing one at a time.

随机练习安排的一个好处是，首先列出你想练习的特定技能的不同问题，然后从一副扑克牌中为每个问题分配一张牌。例如，西班牙语学习者可以列出不同的动词变位练习，并为每个练习分配一张扑克牌。类似的方法也适用于学习编程函数、吉他和弦、羽毛球发球或物理问题。关键在于每个练习的时长要足够短，以便你可以在一次练习中完成多个练习。然后将分配好的扑克牌洗牌，每次抽取一张进行练习。

Strategy #2: Play with More Performers

策略二：增加表演者数量

Randomizing your practice schedule is a highly structured way of approaching variability, but a more organic method is simply to increase the number of people you learn from and practice with. Jazz players frequently worked with a range of other players, often improvising onstage with band members they had only met that same evening. Since all players have their own idiosyncrasies, such frequent rotation exposes a performer to more potential music than playing for the same gig in a fixed band.

随机安排练习时间是一种高度结构化的应对变化的方式，但更自然的方法是增加学习和练习对象的数量。爵士乐手经常与其他乐手合作，常常与当晚才认识的乐队成员即兴演奏。由于每位乐手都有自己的演奏风格，这种频繁的轮换能让演奏者接触到比在固定乐队中为同一场演出演奏更多潜在的音乐。

For professional skills, look for job opportunities that put you in contact with a wider variety of cases typical of the discipline. Following his in-depth study of firefighters as discussed in chapter 4 , psychologist Gary Klein remarks, “ In research on firefighters, we observed that ten years with a rural volunteer fire department were not as valuable for skill development as a year or two in a decaying inner city. Urban firefighters are exposed to a wider variety of fires and a vastly higher incidence rate than rural firefighters are.” Similarly, the path to becoming elite in many professions often involves beginning work in stressful, highly variable environments before settling down to positions with a more routine set of duties. Accountants and lawyers often cut their teeth in big professional firms with a wide diversity of clients, before choosing a focus area. Doctors rotate through multiple emergency rooms before beginning a family practice. In situations where such professional opportunities are not the default, it may be beneficial to seek out high-variability workplaces when you’re still establishing yourself in your career.

为了提升专业技能，要寻找能让你接触到更多本领域典型案例的工作机会。心理学家加里·克莱因（Gary Klein）在第四章中深入研究了消防员的工作后指出：“在对消防员的研究中，我们发现，在乡村志愿消防队工作十年对技能提升的价值，远不如在衰败的内城消防站工作一两年。城市消防员接触到的火灾类型更多，发生率也远高于乡村消防员。” 同样，许多行业的精英之路往往需要在压力大、变化多的环境中起步，之后才会进入职责更为常规的岗位。会计师和律师通常会在拥有众多客户的大型专业事务所积累经验，然后再选择专注于某个领域。医生在开始家庭医生工作之前，也会在多家急诊室轮岗。如果这类职业机会并非普遍存在，那么在职业生涯初期寻找高变化性的工作场所或许会大有裨益。

Strategy #3: Learn the Theories

策略三：学习理论

Theoretical knowledge, as we’ve seen, helps foster multiple representations for dealing with a problem. This is also the kind of knowledge that’s difficult to develop through experimentation alone. Good theories are rare, and so you’re far more likely to find them by reading books. Deeper theoretical understandings are often an investment, however, as they usually assist largely with making other knowledge easier to acquire, not with getting results themselves. A musician who spends hours in the library isn’t immediately going to play any better. However, a deeper understanding of harmonies will make it easier to assimilate new patterns of music. Miles Davis, an alumnus of the Juilliard School, often rebuked the tendency he saw in fellow musicians to avoid studying music theory:

正如我们所见，理论知识有助于培养解决问题的多种方法。这种知识也很难仅通过实验获得。好的理论很少见，因此你更有可能通过阅读书籍找到它们。然而，更深入的理论理解通常是一种投资，因为它们通常主要有助于更容易地获取其他知识，而不是直接获得结果。一个音乐家花几个小时泡在图书馆里，并不会立刻提高演奏水平。但是，对和声的更深入理解会让他更容易吸收新的音乐模式。茱莉亚音乐学院的校友迈尔斯·戴维斯经常批评他看到的音乐家同行们不愿学习音乐理论的倾向：

I would go to the library and borrow scores by all those great composers, like Stravinsky, Alban Berg, Prokofiev. I wanted to see what was going on in all of music. Knowledge is freedom and ignorance is slavery, and I just couldn’t believe someone could be that close to freedom and not take advantage of it.

我会去图书馆借阅那些伟大作曲家的乐谱，比如斯特拉文斯基、阿尔班·贝尔格、普罗科菲耶夫。我想了解音乐界的方方面面。知识就是自由，无知就是奴役，我简直无法相信有人会如此接近自由却不去珍惜。

Of course, not all theories are academic. Practical theories, professional rules of thumb, and industry standards are just as valid ways of thinking, even if they aren’t derived from a scholastic source. Talking to people in the field, and finding out what tools they’re using and theories they’re working with, gives a road map for acquiring more tools to work with.

当然，并非所有理论都源于学术界。实践理论、专业经验法则和行业标准同样是有效的思考方式，即便它们并非来自学术机构。与业内人士交流，了解他们使用的工具和遵循的理论，可以为获取更多工具指明方向。

Strategy #4: Get It Right, Then Vary Your Practice

策略四：先把方法做对，然后再调整练习方式

Variability, as we’ve seen, is something best viewed as building on top of, rather than opposed to, repetition. However, finding the exact dividing line for where greater variability is helpful can be difficult. Most of the studies reviewed here have focused on a snapshot of learning, thus making the dividing line between when repetitive practice or variable practice is more helpful difficult to discern. Worse, variable practice falls into the unintuitive category of desirable difficulties, so people may not accurately gauge when it will be most useful. Nate Kornell and Robert Bjork found that, as with similar studies on retrieval practice and spacing, participants generally believed they learned better with a blocked presentation than a variable presentation, even though later tests indicated otherwise. This was true even after participants had completed a final task in which they performed better after the interleaved schedule—students still believed blocking worked better.

正如我们所见，变异性最好被视为建立在重复之上，而非与之对立。然而，要找到变异性何时更有益的确切界限并非易事。本文回顾的大多数研究都侧重于学习的某个阶段，因此难以区分重复练习和变异练习何时更有益。更糟糕的是，变异练习属于“理想难度”这一反直觉的范畴，因此人们可能无法准确判断它何时最有效。内特·科内尔和罗伯特·比约克发现，与关于检索练习和间隔的类似研究一样，参与者普遍认为集中呈现比可变呈现效果更好，即使后来的测试结果并非如此。即使在参与者完成最终任务后，他们在交错式学习安排下表现更佳，这一观点依然成立——学生们仍然认为集中呈现效果更好。

As the research on variable practice is still evolving, I’m not aware of any scientific guidance for deciding the dividing line. However, it seems fair to say that if you’re unable to perform a skill correctly in isolation, greater variability is probably not going to be helpful. Similarly, if you’re able to perform a skill correctly most of the time, while variability will probably make learning slower, it will also likely be beneficial in developing those control processes. Jazz soloists frequently begin by repeating a solo multiple times, checking their performance against the recording they are trying to emulate. Only once they can do this without mistakes do they start adding embellishments, interpretations, or entirely new sections. Variation, built over repetition.

由于关于可变练习的研究仍在不断发展，我目前还没有找到任何科学的指导原则来确定练习的分界线。然而，可以肯定的是，如果你无法单独正确地完成一项技能，那么增加练习的可变性可能并无益处。同样地，如果你大部分时间都能正确地完成一项技能，虽然可变性可能会减慢学习速度，但它也可能有助于培养这些控制能力。爵士独奏家通常会先反复练习一段独奏，并对照他们想要模仿的录音来检查自己的演奏。只有当他们能够毫无错误地完成独奏后，才会开始添加润饰、诠释或全新的乐段。这就是基于重复而逐步积累的变奏。

From Improvisation to Invention

从即兴创作到发明

Variable practice is an important contributor to flexible skills. Fluent improvisation, however impressive, is still firmly within the bounds of an existing tradition. Invention, the process of generating something that breaks with tradition, such as the development of bebop itself, seems further still. In the next chapter, we’ll move beyond the development of flexible skills to the roots of inventive creativity.

多样化的练习是培养灵活技能的重要因素。流畅的即兴演奏，无论多么令人印象深刻，仍然牢牢地扎根于既有的传统框架之内。而发明创造，即创造突破传统的事物，例如比波普爵士乐本身的形成，则似乎更进一步。在下一章中，我们将超越灵活技能的培养，探寻创造性思维的根源。

# ↩

Chapter 8

第八章

Quality Comes from Quantity

质量源于数量

Well, you just have lots of ideas and throw away the bad ones!

嗯，你只需要有很多想法，然后把不好的想法都扔掉就行了！

—Linus Pauling, on the secret to his scientific insights

——莱纳斯·鲍林谈其科学洞见的秘诀

  • Are geniuses typically prolific?
    天才通常都著作等身吗？
  • How large a role does chance play in invention?
    偶然性在发明创造中扮演着多大的角色？
  • How can you improve your creative output without sacrificing quality?
    如何在不牺牲质量的前提下提高创作效率？

F ew in history can compete with the inventive productivity of Thomas Edison. His creative accomplishments include multiplex telegraphy, the first practical system for sending multiple signals down a single telegraph wire; the fluoroscope, the first device for taking clear X-ray pictures; the kinetograph, one of the earliest motion picture cameras; the tasimeter, for measuring infrared light; the carbon microphone, a practical necessity for telephones; rechargeable batteries; and—most incredibly for someone who was almost completely deaf—the phonograph, the first audio recording device. His laboratory in Menlo Park, New Jersey, became a model for corporate innovation, later inspiring the industrial research facilities of Bell Labs, General Electric, and DuPont. Superstitious locals attributed his inventive genius to sorcery. For the “Wizard of Menlo Park” there seemed to be no device he couldn’t develop, at a cost that was affordable for everyday people.

历史上鲜有人能与托马斯·爱迪生的创造力相媲美。他的发明创造包括：多路电报，这是第一个能够通过单根电报线传输多个信号的实用系统；透视镜，第一个能够拍摄清晰X光片的设备；电影放映机，最早的电影摄影机之一；电波计，用于测量红外线；碳精麦克风，电话的必备工具；可充电电池；以及——对于一位几乎完全失聪的人来说，最令人难以置信的是——留声机，第一个录音设备。他在新泽西州门洛帕克的实验室成为了企业创新的典范，后来启发了贝尔实验室、通用电气和杜邦等公司的工业研究机构。迷信的当地人将他的发明天赋归功于巫术。对于这位“门洛帕克的巫师”来说，似乎没有什么设备是他无法研发出来的，而且价格也让普通人能够负担得起。

The most famous invention associated with Edison, the electric lightbulb, wasn’t, strictly speaking, his own. Electric arc lighting, whose blinding illumination came from the continuous spark created in the gap of a high-current circuit, was already available by the time Edison made his lighting experiments. Early incandescent bulbs also existed, although they burned out quickly and consumed too much power to be commercially viable. Yet, in some ways, crediting Edison with the lightbulb actually undersells his accomplishment. For it wasn’t just his insight to seek a high-resistance filament to make incandescent lighting practical, but his simultaneous invention of the surrounding infrastructure—including parallel circuit connections, high-efficiency electric dynamos, and the concept of a central power station—that enabled not just lighting, but the entire electric industry we know today. Edison produced an astonishing 1,093 patents in his lifetime, making a strong claim to having been the most inventive person in all of human history.

与爱迪生联系最紧密的发明——电灯泡，严格来说并非完全出自他之手。电弧灯——其耀眼的光芒源于高电流电路间隙中持续产生的火花——在爱迪生进行照明实验时就已经存在。早期的白炽灯泡也已出现，但它们寿命短、耗电量大，难以商业化。然而，在某种程度上，将电灯泡的发明归功于爱迪生实际上低估了他的成就。因为他不仅敏锐地发现了高阻灯丝，使白炽灯得以实用，而且还同时发明了相关的基础设施——包括并联电路连接、高效发电机以及中央发电站的概念——这些不仅使照明成为可能，也为我们今天所知的整个电力行业奠定了基础。爱迪生一生获得了惊人的1093项专利，堪称人类历史上最具创造力的人之一。

When Edison died in 1931, it was briefly considered that all electricity should be shut off for two minutes to pay respect for the deceased inventor. However, it was quickly realized that such an outage would cause widespread chaos. Edison’s legacy was so pervasive that the world couldn’t contemplate turning it back, even for a moment.

1931年爱迪生去世时，人们曾短暂地考虑过停电两分钟以示对这位已故发明家的敬意。然而，人们很快意识到，这样的停电会造成大范围的混乱。爱迪生的遗产影响如此深远，世界根本无法想象哪怕一瞬间要让它倒退。

Da Vinci or Picasso: Is Genius Typically Prolific?

达芬奇还是毕加索：天才通常都作品丰富吗？

Edison embodies the prolific creative. His inventions were as influential as they were numerous. But Edison’s example raises a question about creative productivity more generally: Do the creators who make the best works tend to make more or fewer works than their less eminent colleagues? Compare Leonardo da Vinci and Pablo Picasso. Both are regarded as eminent artists, albeit of vastly different time periods and styles. However, the two left markedly different bodies of work. Da Vinci completed fewer than two dozen works in his lifetime, and left many others unfinished. Picasso finished over thirteen thousand original paintings, bringing his total artistic output to over one hundred thousand works when including engravings and prints. Both figures spring to mind plausible, competing models of creativity: the dedicated artist who imbues a handful of works with the entirety of their vision, and the copious creator who spews forth ideas without pause. Yet the data suggest that Edison and Picasso are more typical of creative success than Da Vinci. The world’s most successful scientists, artists, and innovators are also the most prolific.

爱迪生堪称多产的创造者。他的发明数量众多，影响深远。但爱迪生的例子引出了一个关于更普遍的创造力的问题：那些创作出最优秀作品的创作者，其作品数量是多还是少？不妨比较一下达·芬奇和毕加索。两人都被认为是杰出的艺术家，尽管他们所处的时代和风格截然不同。然而，他们留下的作品数量却大相径庭。达·芬奇一生完成的作品不足二十四幅，还有许多作品未能完成。毕加索完成了超过一万三千幅原创画作，如果算上版画和印刷品，他的艺术作品总数超过十万件。这两个人物让人联想到两种截然不同的创造力模式：一种是全身心投入、将全部心血倾注于少数作品的艺术家，另一种是源源不断、灵感迸发的创作者。然而，数据表明，爱迪生和毕加索比达·芬奇更能代表成功的创造者。世界上最成功的科学家、艺术家和创新者也是最多产的。

One of the earliest investigators to consider this question was Belgian sociologist Adolphe Quetelet. In his 1835 treatise, he counted the number of works produced by French and English playwrights. He discovered that creative output was strongly correlated with literary impact. Nearly two centuries later, psychologist Dean Simonton has gathered research supporting Quetelet’s early observations: the most accomplished scientists, artists, and scholars are also those who produce the most. Simonton explains that across many domains, personal productivity and social creativity are highly correlated. If we look at the pattern of creativity across an individual’s career, Simonton argues, the periods when a person produces their best work also tend to be the periods when they produce the most work. Measuring the number of highly acclaimed works and dividing them by the total can produce a kind of quality ratio. “ This ratio of hits to total shots does not change in a regular pattern with age,” Simonton explains. “The ratio neither increases nor decreases, nor exhibits any other form. This remarkable result suggests that quality is a function of quantity.” Simonton proposes an “equal-odds baseline,” which suggests that, once a person begins contributing original work to their field, every attempt has roughly equal potential for world-changing impact. While we can look back in awe at Edison’s achievements in creating an electric lighting system, and be baffled at his failed venture applying electromagnets to iron mining, which squandered his previous fortune, Edison himself couldn’t foresee which of his innovations would have built his legacy.

最早研究这个问题的学者之一是比利时社会学家阿道夫·凯特勒。在他1835年的论文中，他统计了法国和英国剧作家的作品数量。他发现，创作产出与文学影响力密切相关。近两个世纪后，心理学家迪恩·西蒙顿收集的研究支持了凯特勒早期的观察：成就最高的科学家、艺术家和学者往往也是作品最多的人。西蒙顿解释说，在许多领域，个人生产力和社会创造力都高度相关。西蒙顿认为，如果我们观察一个人职业生涯中的创造力模式，就会发现，一个人创作出最佳作品的时期往往也是其作品数量最多的时期。衡量广受好评的作品数量并除以总作品数量，可以得出一种质量比率。“这种成功作品与总作品数量的比率并不会随着年龄的增长而呈现规律性的变化，”西蒙顿解释道。 “这个比例既不增加也不减少，也不呈现任何其他形式。这一非凡的结果表明，质量是数量的函数。”西蒙顿提出了“等概率基线”，这意味着，一旦一个人开始在其领域做出原创性贡献，每一次尝试都具有大致相同的改变世界的潜在影响。我们回顾爱迪生在创造电灯系统方面取得的成就时，会感到敬畏；而对于他将电磁铁应用于铁矿开采的失败尝试，我们也会感到困惑不解，因为那次尝试耗尽了他之前的财富。然而，爱迪生本人也无法预见他的哪一项创新会成就他的不朽传奇。

The equal-odds baseline suggests that creative potential doesn’t vary throughout an individual’s career. But what about between individuals? Is there evidence to support the idea that some people regularly churn out mediocre works while geniuses relentlessly perfect a few precious ideas? While perfectionists producing only a handful of high-quality works and mass-producers churning out mediocre products do exist, historical data supports the idea that prolific creators tend to be the most influential. Price’s law, named after British physicist and historian of science Derek John de Solla Price, finds that half of the scholarly output of a given field will be produced by a number of researchers that is approximately the square root of the total. A subdiscipline with one hundred authors producing papers will have approximately half of the total output produced by only ten researchers. Harriet Zuckerman’s work studying American Nobel laureates finds that the most highly cited scientists wrote almost twice as many papers as similar but less influential colleagues. Richard Davis similarly observes that the neurosurgeons with the most citations were those who wrote the most papers. Consistent with the equal-odds baseline, however, citations per paper did not depend on how prolific the author was. However, since more productive authors wrote more papers, they were also more likely to have generated highly cited works.

等概率基准线表明，创造潜力在个人的整个职业生涯中保持不变。但个体之间又如何呢？是否有证据支持这样一种观点：有些人经常创作平庸的作品，而天才则孜孜不倦地完善少数几个珍贵的想法？虽然完美主义者只创作少数高质量作品，而批量生产者也大量生产平庸产品的情况确实存在，但历史数据支持这样一种观点：高产的创作者往往最具影响力。普莱斯定律（以英国物理学家和科学史学家德里克·约翰·德·索拉·普莱斯的名字命名）指出，某一特定领域一半的学术产出将由大约是该领域总产出平方根的研究人员完成。例如，一个拥有100位作者发表论文的子学科，大约一半的总产出将由10位研究人员完成。哈里特·祖克曼对美国诺贝尔奖得主的研究发现，被引用次数最多的科学家发表的论文数量几乎是其他类似但影响力较小的同行的两倍。理查德·戴维斯也观察到，论文引用次数最多的神经外科医生往往也是论文发表数量最多的医生。然而，与等概率基线一致，每篇论文的引用次数并不取决于作者的论文发表量。但是，由于论文发表量更高的作者发表的论文更多，他们也更有可能发表高被引论文。

Despite the haphazard character of creative success, it isn’t as if all creators are made equal. Edison, as we have seen, was singularly productive—inventing far more than most inventors of his era, not to mention the millions who never invented anything. To make sense of this pattern of productivity, and what it means for how we should cultivate our own creative success, we need to consider three different explanations of creative accomplishment: expertise, environment, and randomness.

尽管创造性的成功具有偶然性，但这并不意味着所有创造者都生而平等。正如我们所见，爱迪生是一位极其高产的发明家——他的发明数量远远超过同时代的其他发明家，更不用说数百万从未进行过任何发明的人了。为了理解这种高产模式，以及它对我们如何培养自身创造性成功的启示，我们需要考虑三种不同的创造性成就的解释：专业知识、环境和随机性。

Explanation #1: Creativity as Expertise

解释一：创造力即专业技能

“Creativity,” wrote cognitive scientist Herbert Simon, “is ‘thinking writ large.’” In this view, creative success depends on the same mechanisms of thinking as ordinary problem solving. What distinguishes a world-changing invention from ordinary troubleshooting isn’t the kind of thinking, but the degree of difficulty and social significance. Creativity depends on the same search through a problem space that characterizes more trivial puzzle-solving efforts. Echoing this “nothing special” view of creativity, Albert Einstein once remarked that “science was nothing more than the refinement of everyday thinking.”

认知科学家赫伯特·西蒙写道：“创造力是‘宏观的思考’。” 在这种观点看来，创造性的成功依赖于与日常问题解决相同的思维机制。一项改变世界的发明与普通故障排除的区别不在于思维的类型，而在于其难度和社会意义。创造力依赖于对问题空间的探索，这与解决琐碎难题的过程如出一辙。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦也曾表达过类似的观点，他认为“科学只不过是日常思维的提炼”。

Examining Edison’s track record of inventing lends support to the creativity-as-expertise theory. The theory predicts that creative success will be concentrated in a particular field. Despite his aura of polymathic brilliance, Edison hews close to this prediction. Although his inventions impacted many disparate industries, Edison’s innovative progress was largely concentrated in novel applications of electrical circuitry. His decision to focus on the electric lightbulb came from his understanding of Ohm’s law, which showed that a high-resistance filament would draw less current than a low-resistance one. While many of his competitors were focusing on robust materials that could withstand intense heat and currents, Edison pursued increasingly delicate filaments for his lightbulb. By reducing their thickness, resistance would increase, using less current and making the product economically viable. Building on more than a decade of hands-on experience with electrical circuitry, Edison could narrow the search space to an area more likely to contain the desired result.

考察爱迪生的发明历程，可以佐证“创造力即专业知识”理论。该理论预测，创造性的成功会集中在特定领域。尽管爱迪生被誉为博学多才，但他的成就与这一预测基本吻合。虽然他的发明影响了众多不同的行业，但爱迪生的创新成果主要集中在电路的创新应用上。他之所以选择专注于电灯泡，源于他对欧姆定律的理解。欧姆定律表明，高电阻灯丝比低电阻灯丝消耗的电流更小。当许多竞争对手致力于研发能够承受高温和大电流的坚固材料时，爱迪生却在不断改进灯泡灯丝的材质。通过减小灯丝的粗细，电阻会增加，从而降低电流消耗，使产品在经济上可行。凭借十余年在电路方面的实践经验，爱迪生能够将搜索范围缩小到更有可能找到理想解决方案的领域。

Edison’s failures, as much as his successes, provide evidence for the expertise view of creativity. In his experiments with lightbulbs, Edison noticed that the interior of the bulb became blackened from the inside with continued use, except for a “shadow” left by the positive end of the filament. He reasoned, correctly, that particles of carbon must be shooting off the negative end. Connecting a second wire within the glass bulb, he found he could even get a current to pass through the vacuum. This “Edison effect” lamp, seen by the inventor as a mere curiosity, was actually the first step toward building vacuum tube electronics, the central building block of early computers. With more theoretical knowledge, it’s possible Edison might have pursued this development further, discovering the electron and ushering in the electronic age. As it stands, however, he left the path untrodden to focus on more commercial applications for his lightbulb.

爱迪生的失败，如同他的成功一样，都为“创造力源于专业知识”的观点提供了佐证。在对灯泡进行实验时，爱迪生注意到，灯泡内部会随着持续使用而逐渐变黑，只有灯丝正极留下的“阴影”依然可见。他正确地推断，一定是碳颗粒从负极喷射而出。在玻璃灯泡内连接第二根导线后，他发现甚至可以使电流通过真空。这种被发明家视为新奇事物的“爱迪生效应”灯泡，实际上是构建真空管电子器件的第一步，而真空管电子器件正是早期计算机的核心组成部分。如果爱迪生拥有更丰富的理论知识，他或许会继续深入研究，最终发现电子，开启电子时代。然而，他最终放弃了这条道路，转而专注于灯泡的商业应用。

Other evidence for creativity as an extension of expertise comes from the dependence on long periods of training. Psychologist John Hayes reviewed 76 famous composers and found that of the 500 notable works they produced, only three occurred before the tenth year of their musical instruction (and those occurred in years eight and nine). He conducted a similar analysis of 131 painters, finding at least six years was needed before a masterwork was recognized, with the quantity of masterworks steadily increasing for the subsequent six years. A similar analysis of poets revealed no notable poems before five years in a career and of the 66 poets studied, 55 did not have a notable poem until after their tenth year. Although Edison was largely unschooled, he was a voracious reader and extensive experimenter. Edison recounts, “ My refuge was the Detroit Public Library. I started with the first book on the bottom shelf and went through the lot, one by one. I didn’t read a few books. I read the library.” Still, it was not until he was twenty-two that he received his first patent, for an electronic voting machine, and not until he was twenty-seven that he produced his first widely celebrated invention for multiplex telegraphy.

创造力是专业知识延伸的其他证据来自对长期训练的依赖。心理学家约翰·海耶斯研究了76位著名作曲家，发现他们创作的500部杰出作品中，只有三部是在他们接受音乐训练的第十年之前完成的（而且这三部作品分别出现在第八年和第九年）。他对131位画家进行了类似的分析，发现至少需要六年时间才能创作出杰作，并且在接下来的六年里，杰作的数量稳步增长。对诗人的类似分析表明，在创作生涯的五年内，几乎没有诗人创作出杰出的诗作；在研究的66位诗人中，有55位直到创作生涯的第十年之后才创作出杰出的诗作。尽管爱迪生基本上没有接受过正规教育，但他却是一位博览群书、勇于尝试的学者。爱迪生回忆道：“我的避难所是底特律公共图书馆。我从最底层书架上的第一本书开始，一本一本地翻阅。我不是读了几本书，而是读了整个图书馆。”不过，直到他 22 岁才获得第一项专利，即电子投票机专利；直到 27 岁才发明出第一项广受赞誉的多路复用电报技术。

The importance of accumulated knowledge to creative success may also explain the overall changes in scientific innovation since Edison’s day. Edison lived through the transition from the “heroic” age of American innovation, characterized by the lone inventor attempting to profit from a novel gadget, to the institutional model, where innovation grows out of industrial laboratories and university research departments. If invention is a process of searching a problem space, then we might expect innovations to require more training and specialization as search delves deeper. Edison’s ability to make useful inventions with limited schooling may have been a side effect of the relatively impoverished state of electrical understanding at the time. Innovations in electrical engineering today involve refinements of integrated chips with billions of transistors per square inch, or finding superconducting materials at ultracold temperatures. These esoteric advances require far more abstract knowledge, explaining the trend toward large teams of doctorate-holding specialists in producing cutting-edge work.

积累的知识对创造性成功的重要性或许也能解释自爱迪生时代以来科学创新整体的变化。爱迪生经历了美国创新模式的转变：从以孤胆发明家试图从新奇装置中获利为特征的“英雄时代”，到以工业实验室和大学研究部门为创新源泉的制度化模式。如果发明创造是一个探索问题领域的过程，那么随着探索的深入，我们可以预期创新需要更多的培训和专业化。爱迪生在教育程度有限的情况下就能做出有用的发明，或许是当时人们对电学理解相对匮乏的必然结果。如今，电气工程领域的创新包括改进每平方英寸拥有数十亿个晶体管的集成芯片，或在超低温下寻找超导材料。这些深奥的进步需要更为抽象的知识，这也解释了为何在尖端研究中，需要由拥有博士学位的专家组成的大型团队来完成。

Yet the creativity-as-expertise view is not a full explanation. While it can explain why some creators are more successful than others, it doesn’t explain the equal-odds baseline. If steadily increasing expertise explained success, we should expect the quality of creative contributions to go up over a creator’s career, rather than remain flat beyond an initial training period. Similarly, equating creativity with expertise also leaves open the question of why some experts are exceptionally creative and others are entirely routine. Expertise may be a prerequisite to creative accomplishment, but it isn’t sufficient.

然而，将创造力等同于专业技能的观点并不能完全解释成功与否。虽然它可以解释为什么有些创作者比其他创作者更成功，但它无法解释成功的概率为何相等。如果专业技能的稳步提升能够解释成功，那么我们应该预期创作者在其职业生涯中，其作品的质量会不断提高，而不是在最初的训练期之后就停滞不前。同样，将创造力等同于专业技能也无法解释为什么有些专家极具创造力，而另一些专家却平庸无奇。专业技能或许是取得创造性成就的先决条件，但它并非充分条件。

Explanation #2: Creativity as Environment

解释二：创造力与环境

Francis Bacon, whose writing helped spur the Scientific Revolution, once wrote that his contribution was, “ a birth of time rather than of wit.” In this way, he was heralding another of the great explanations of scientific creativity: the theory that ideas are a product of their cultural moment, not merely individual genius. The zeitgeist, or “spirit of the times,” argues that cultural context provides the soil in which ideas germinate. That context not only defines where innovators tend to look for new ideas, but also which of those ideas, once found, receive broad acceptance. Even the most brilliant ideas will fade into obscurity if the environment is not receptive.

弗朗西斯·培根的著作曾推动了科学革命，他曾写道，他的贡献“并非源于才智，而是源于时代”。由此，他预示了科学创造力的又一伟大解释：思想并非仅仅是个人天才的产物，而是其所处文化时代的产物。时代精神，或称“时代脉搏”，认为文化背景为思想的萌芽提供了土壤。这种背景不仅决定了创新者倾向于从何处寻找新思想，也决定了哪些思想一旦被发现，就能被广泛接受。即使是最杰出的思想，如果缺乏适宜的环境，也会湮没无闻。

Evidence for the environmental view of creativity comes from the long and surprising list of multiple discoveries. The theory of evolution was simultaneously and independently worked on by Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace. Both Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz invented calculus. Alexander Bell and Elisha Gray famously submitted patents for the telephone within hours of each other. Four different scientists discovered sunspots, all in 1611. And no fewer than nine different inventors claim credit for the optical telescope. Even the concept of multiple discovery, often credited to sociologists William Ogburn and Dorothy Thomas, who published an extensive list of examples, has been rediscovered countless times. The sociologist Robert Merton counts eighteen instances where the concept of multiple discoveries was suggested independently, drawing from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries alone. The inevitability of certain discoveries is seared into the mentality of working scientists. Fierce debates over priority, with sealed and postdated manuscripts providing evidence about the timing of key discoveries, would not be necessary unless scientific innovations were already “in the air” before their exact formulation.

环境视角下的创造力证据来自一系列令人惊叹的多重发现。进化论是查尔斯·达尔文和阿尔弗雷德·罗素·华莱士同时独立研究的成果。艾萨克·牛顿和戈特弗里德·威廉·莱布尼茨共同发明了微积分。亚历山大·贝尔和伊莱沙·格雷在数小时内先后提交了电话专利，这在当时引起了广泛关注。四位不同的科学家在1611年发现了太阳黑子。至少有九位不同的发明家声称自己是光学望远镜的发明者。即使是多重发现的概念，尽管通常被认为是社会学家威廉·奥格本和多萝西·托马斯提出的（他们发表了大量实例），也已被无数次重新发现。社会学家罗伯特·默顿统计，仅在19世纪和20世纪，就有18个独立提出多重发现概念的例子。某些发现的必然性已经深深烙印在科学家们的思维模式中。除非科学创新在确切表述之前就已经“初露端倪”，否则围绕优先权的激烈争论，以及密封的、日期后标注的手稿所提供的关键发现时间的证据，都是没有必要的。

Social psychologist Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi argues that creativity cannot be judged in a vacuum. While many psychologists have endeavored to study creativity as a purely mental function, Csikszentmihalyi argues that such studies neglect the field of experts who collectively decide what counts as creative. He argues that perhaps ten thousand people constitute the modern art field, whose acceptance any new artist must receive if their work is to be considered innovative. Computer analyses of musical compositions lend support to this view, with those compositions of moderate “melodic originality” having the greatest popularity. Being original is important for artistic creativity, but being too original may make your work incomprehensible. Similar social gatekeeping occurs in science, where small communities of experts set the standards of peer review before findings can be published. Intellectual fashions can dictate the palatability of certain kinds of ideas: talk about mental states in psychology went from the wild conjecture of introspectionists to taboo under the influence of behaviorism, only to be resuscitated by cognitive psychologists. That scientific ideas are occasionally rehabilitated depending on the intellectual fashion suggests that many potential fruits of discovery wither on the vine. Nor is popular reception limited to cloistered groups of judgmental experts. Commercial products and mass media must face the gauntlet of public opinion that decides whether they’re popular or a flop.

社会心理学家米哈里·契克森米哈赖认为，创造力不能脱离语境来评判。虽然许多心理学家致力于将创造力作为一种纯粹的心理功能进行研究，但契克森米哈赖指出，这类研究忽略了专家群体，正是他们共同决定了何为创造力。他认为，现代艺术领域或许只有一万人，任何新晋艺术家的作品若想被视为创新，都必须得到他们的认可。对音乐作品的计算机分析也支持这一观点，那些“旋律原创性”适中的作品最受欢迎。原创性对于艺术创造力固然重要，但过于原创则可能使作品晦涩难懂。类似的社会把关机制也存在于科学领域，少数专家群体制定了同行评审的标准，研究成果才能发表。知识潮流会影响某些观点的接受度：心理学中关于心理状态的讨论，最初是内省主义者的大胆推测，后来在行为主义的影响下成为禁忌，最终又被认知心理学家重新启用。科学思想有时会因知识潮流而复兴，这表明许多潜在的发现成果最终都胎死腹中。此外，大众的接受度并非仅限于封闭的专家群体。商业产品和大众媒体也必须面对公众舆论的考验，最终决定其是成功还是失败。

Thomas Edison was acutely aware of the importance of the receptive environment, not mere technological possibility, in his inventive work. “ Anything that won’t sell, I don’t want to invent. Its sale is proof of utility and utility is success.” Yet this sentiment was hardly motivated by greed. “ My main purpose in life is to make enough money to make ever more inventions,” he remarked. Edison could have retired multiple times over on the profits generated from his early creations. Instead he invariably plowed all his earnings back into risky new ventures, often bringing him and his family to the brink of bankruptcy before he hit upon a new success. Edison seemed to have a keen understanding of the distinction between invention and innovation. An invention is a creative work, judged on its technical merits. An innovation, in contrast, is measured by its social impact. Ever the pragmatist, Edison wanted to create useful devices, not mere technical curiosities. His focus on a high-resistance filament for his lightbulb came not from technical considerations, but from a careful analysis of the cost of lighting. A bulb that used a lot of current wouldn’t be economical, even if it might be technologically feasible.

托马斯·爱迪生敏锐地意识到，在他从事发明创造的过程中，接受环境的重要性远胜于单纯的技术可能性。“任何卖不出去的东西，我都不想发明。销量才是实用性的证明，而实用性就是成功。”然而，这种想法并非出于贪婪。“我人生的主要目标就是赚足够的钱，以便进行更多的发明创造。”他曾这样说道。爱迪生完全可以凭借早期发明创造带来的利润退休好几次。但他却总是将所有收入投入到风险极高的新项目中，常常使他和家人濒临破产，直到他最终获得新的成功。爱迪生似乎对发明和创新之间的区别有着深刻的理解。发明是一种创造性的作品，其价值取决于技术水平。而创新则以其社会影响来衡量。作为一位务实主义者，爱迪生想要创造的是实用的设备，而非仅仅是技术上的奇观。他之所以专注于使用高电阻灯丝制作灯泡，并非出于技术考量，而是源于对照明成本的仔细分析。即使在技术上可行，耗电量大的灯泡也不经济。

A receptive environment for invention also explains many curious examples of world-changing inventions going unused. The wheel was invented in Mesoamerica centuries before the arrival of Europeans, yet it seemed to be used only in children’s toys rather than agriculture. An explanation for this missed opportunity comes from the lack of native beasts of burden that could have made wheel-driven carts practical. Similarly, movable type was created in Korea hundreds of years before Gutenberg’s world-changing printing press. Yet the literary language was written in Chinese characters. This meant printing books required representing thousands of unique symbols, greatly increasing the material cost. “ The common belief is that if creativity is rare,” Csikszentmihalyi argues, “it is because of supply-side limitations; in other words, because there are few geniuses. The truth seems to be that the limits to creativity lie on the demand side. If there is too little creativity, it is because both individually and collectively we cannot change our cognitive structures rapidly enough to recognize and adopt new ideas.”

有利于发明创造的环境也能解释许多改变世界的发明最终却无人问津的奇特例子。车轮在欧洲人到来几个世纪前就已在中美洲发明，但它似乎只被用于儿童玩具，而非农业。造成这种错失良机的原因在于，当时缺乏能够使轮式车实用化的本土役畜。同样，活字印刷术在古腾堡发明改变世界的印刷机几百年前就已在韩国发明。然而，当时的文字是用汉字书写的。这意味着印刷书籍需要呈现成千上万个独特的符号，大大增加了材料成本。“人们普遍认为，如果创造力稀少，”齐克森米哈里认为，“那是因为供给侧的限制；换句话说，是因为天才很少。但事实似乎是，创造力的限制在于需求侧。如果创造力太少，那是因为我们个人和集体都无法足够迅速地改变我们的认知结构，从而识别和接受新思想。”

Explanation #3: Creativity as Randomness

解释三：创造力即随机性

Both expertise and environment suggest creativity is a deterministic process. A more humbling explanation may be that chance plays a far greater role than either cognitive or sociological theories give credit. Paralleling the process underlying Darwin’s theory of natural selection, psychologist Donald Campbell proposed in 1960 that creative thinking can be understood as a similar process of blind variation with selective retention. Biological evolution is enormously creative, as witnessed by the incredible diversity of life. Yet Darwin famously showed that all that was required was chance mutation, along with heritable accumulation of useful adaptations. In a similar light, perhaps theories of creativity that seek complicated mechanisms are overwrought. Creativity, Campbell argued, might be better understood as simply a process of generating a lot of potential ideas and retaining those that work. As quoted in the epigraph to this chapter, Linus Pauling attributed his Nobel Prize–winning chemical insights to a similar process of generating copious ideas, retaining only the best.

专业知识和环境都表明创造力是一个决定论的过程。然而，一种更为谦逊的解释或许是，偶然性在其中扮演的角色远比认知理论或社会学理论所认为的要大得多。心理学家唐纳德·坎贝尔在1960年提出，创造性思维可以理解为一种类似的盲目变异与选择性保留的过程，这与达尔文的自然选择理论的原理相呼应。生物进化极具创造性，生命种类之丰富便是明证。然而，达尔文的著名论证表明，所有这一切只需要偶然突变以及可遗传的有用适应性积累。同样地，那些寻求复杂机制的创造力理论或许过于繁琐。坎贝尔认为，创造力或许可以更好地理解为产生大量潜在想法并保留其中有效想法的过程。正如本章引言所引述的，莱纳斯·鲍林将他获得诺贝尔奖的化学见解归功于类似的产生大量想法并只保留最佳想法的过程。

Evidence for the role of chance comes from the long history of accidental inventions. Penicillin was invented accidentally after the Scottish physician Alexander Fleming noticed mold growing that seemed to suppress the surrounding bacterial samples. The artificial sweetener saccharin was stumbled upon by Russian chemist Constantin Fahlberg after he accidentally ingested the products of one of his reactions. The recipe for superglue arrived unexpectedly after Harry Coover was looking for a way to create cheap, plastic gun sights for the military. Serendipity also explains the invention of Teflon, dynamite, vulcanized rubber, safety glass, and Viagra. “ Le principle de l’invention est le hasard,” wrote French philosopher Paul Souriau. Chance, not necessity, is the mother of invention.

偶然性在发明创造中扮演着重要角色，这可以从漫长的意外发明史中得到佐证。苏格兰医生亚历山大·弗莱明偶然发现青霉素，是因为他注意到某种霉菌似乎能抑制周围细菌的生长。俄罗斯化学家康斯坦丁·法尔贝格在意外摄入自己实验产物后，偶然发现了人工甜味剂糖精。哈里·库弗在寻找一种为军方制造廉价塑料枪瞄具的方法时，意外地获得了强力胶的配方。特氟龙、炸药、硫化橡胶、安全玻璃和伟哥的发明也都与偶然性有关。“发明的原则是偶然性，”法国哲学家保罗·苏里奥写道。偶然性，而非必然性，才是发明之母。

Edison was intimately familiar with the role of accident in discovery. “ In experimenting, I find a good many things I never looked for.” He tested countless materials for his incandescent lightbulb before finding a workable material with carbonized paper strips. With this observation made, he then proceeded to test thousands of other carbonized plant fibers, finally settling on bamboo as the ideal source. Later in his life, when looking for a substitute source for rubber, he examined fourteen thousand different plants, looking for one with sufficiently high latex content that could be cultivated in a temperate climate. His efforts to find a high-capacity, rechargeable battery were similarly cut-and-try. His friend Walter Mallory went to offer his sympathies after hearing that he had failed to gain any results despite months of work. Edison replied, “ Why, man, I’ve got a lot of results. I know several thousand things that won’t work!” Edison’s embrace of chance, and his willingness to test thousands of combinations in pursuit of an answer, were derided by his onetime employee and later rival Nikola Tesla. Of his working habits, Tesla remarked, “ If Edison had a needle to find in a haystack, he would proceed at once with the diligence of the bee to examine straw after straw until he found the object of his search.” Yet this embrace of trial and error may not have been as foolish as it sounds. The state of chemical research was still nascent, and few reliable predictions could be gleaned about which materials would work except from trying them out. Even today, innovations owe a great deal to chance. Despite the impressive advances in biological and chemical theory, pharmaceutical discovery still depends a great deal on serendipity, as the effects of drugs are often stumbled into rather than theoretically predicted. The weight-loss drug semaglutide, sold under the name Ozempic, was originally developed for diabetes, and sildenafil, sold as Viagra, was originally developed to treat hypertension. Chance, not design, led to their discovery.

爱迪生深谙偶然性在发现中的作用。“在实验中，我发现了许多我从未想过的东西。”为了制造白炽灯泡，他测试了无数种材料，最终才找到一种可行的碳化纸条材料。有了这一发现后，他又测试了数千种其他碳化植物纤维，最终确定竹子是理想的材料。晚年，为了寻找橡胶的替代品，他考察了一万四千种不同的植物，寻找一种乳胶含量足够高且能在温带气候下种植的植物。他寻找高容量可充电电池的努力也同样是反复试验的结果。他的朋友沃尔特·马洛里听说他几个月来一无所获后前来表示同情。爱迪生回答说：“哎呀，伙计，我有很多成果。我知道好几千种方法行不通！”爱迪生对偶然性的拥抱，以及他为了找到答案而尝试成千上万种组合的意愿，曾遭到他曾经的雇员、后来的竞争对手尼古拉·特斯拉的嘲讽。特斯拉曾评价爱迪生的工作习惯说：“如果爱迪生要在干草堆里找一根针，他会像蜜蜂一样勤奋地一根一根地检查，直到找到他要找的东西。”然而，这种反复试验的做法或许并不像听起来那么愚蠢。当时的化学研究尚处于起步阶段，除了尝试之外，几乎无法对哪些材料有效做出可靠的预测。即使在今天，创新也很大程度上依赖于偶然性。尽管生物学和化学理论取得了令人瞩目的进步，但药物的发现仍然很大程度上依赖于意外发现，因为药物的疗效往往是偶然发现的，而不是理论预测的。减肥药索玛鲁肽（商品名：Ozempic）最初是为治疗糖尿病而研发的，而西地那非（商品名：伟哥）最初是为治疗高血压而研发的。它们的发现并非出于设计，而是偶然。

Combining the Three Explanations

结合这三种解释

The three explanations of creativity—expertise, environment, and randomness—are not mutually exclusive. A fairly simple model of creativity incorporates all three. In this model, the existing stock of knowledge defines the possible innovations that can be made. Expertise is required because, unless you are at the frontier, your insights may be individually creative, but not socially creative. An illustration of the difference comes from a story about a six-year-old Carl Gauss. Asked to find the sum of 1 + 2 + 3 . . . all the way to 10, he quickly responded “55!” How did he answer so quickly, the teacher asked? He responded that he observed that the numbers can be paired off into five sets that each sum to eleven (1 + 10, 2 + 9, 3 + 8 . . .), so the answer must be 55. Although we can marvel at his cleverness, such a trick was not unknown to mathematicians, so the ingenious solution had no social influence, even if it heralded a particularly creative mathematical mind.

创造力的三种解释——专业知识、环境和随机性——并非互斥。一个相当简单的创造力模型就包含了这三者。在这个模型中，现有的知识储备决定了可能出现的创新。专业知识是必要的，因为除非你处于前沿领域，否则你的见解可能具有个人创造性，但缺乏社会创造性。一个关于六岁卡尔·高斯的故事可以很好地说明这种差异。当被要求计算1+2+3……直到10的和时，他迅速回答“55！”老师问他怎么回答得这么快？他回答说，他观察到这些数字可以两两分成五组，每组之和都是 11（1 + 10，2 + 9，3 + 8……），所以答案一定是 55。虽然我们可以惊叹于他的聪明才智，但这种技巧在数学家之间并不陌生，因此这个巧妙的解法并没有产生任何社会影响，即使它预示着一个特别有创造力的数学家的头脑。

Beyond the frontier of knowledge, chance plays two important roles in creative success. The first is within the problem-solving process itself. As we saw in chapter 1 , people use both general-purpose strategies like means-ends analysis and generate-and-test, as well as domain-specific heuristics to guide problem-solving search. But even if problem solving is far from an unthinking activity, there remain plenty of possibilities left over in the problem space. This is true by definition, since if the problem space collapsed to a single, obvious answer we wouldn’t consider it beyond the current frontier of knowledge. Thus random processes of exploration are needed, even for the most intelligent and knowledgeable experts, to venture beyond what has already been mastered. The second role of chance occurs with the receptive environment. Even the most astute technologists, investors, or scientific forecasters can only modestly predict which works will be supremely important and which will fizzle out. Creators themselves have only a limited ability to foresee the long-term impact of their works. This lack of predictability means that each invention, essay, product, or scientific paper is always partly a gamble.

在知识的边界之外，偶然性在创造性的成功中扮演着两个重要的角色。首先，它存在于问题解决过程本身。正如我们在第一章中所看到的，人们既会运用诸如手段-目标分析和生成-测试等通用策略，也会运用特定领域的启发式方法来指导问题解决的探索。但即便问题解决远非一种不假思索的活动，问题空间中仍然存在着大量的可能性。这是由定义决定的，因为如果问题空间最终只剩下一个显而易见的答案，我们就不会认为它超越了当前的知识边界。因此，即使是最聪明、最有学识的专家，也需要进行随机的探索过程，才能涉足已掌握的领域之外。偶然性的第二个作用体现在接受环境上。即使是最精明的技术专家、投资者或科学预测者，也只能大致预测哪些作品会极其重要，哪些作品会昙花一现。而创作者自身也只能有限地预见其作品的长期影响。这种不可预测性意味着每一项发明、文章、产品或科学论文都带有一定的赌博性质。

The difference between routine and creative experts can be seen in the decision to work on risky problems. Important work can be done entirely within the current frontier of knowledge. Even if creativity itself depends on chance, some experts will choose to stick to tried-and-true methods, while others will take risks to explore new areas of the problem space. This notion of the creative as a gambler is clearest in Robert Sternberg and Todd Lubart’s investment theory of creativity. In their model, creators are like stock pickers, making bets on which ideas, methods, or areas of investigation will rise in value. Like stock market speculation, this process depends a great deal on chance—some creators will gain fame, while others fade into obscurity. The difference between routine and creative experts is largely due to their appetite for risk. Edison was no stranger to economic tumult resulting from his risky inventive pursuits. “At least I did not have ennui,” he later reflected on the wild swings of fortune and failure of his inventing career. An investment theory also helps to reconcile why some individuals are unusually inventive, compared to their equally knowledgeable peers. Historian Anton Howes finds that inventors are much more likely to have had contact with another inventor prior to inventing something on their own, suggesting that the desire to engage in a risky line of business may be something culturally transmitted, beyond simply the expertise needed to be successful at it.

常规型专家和创新型专家之间的区别体现在他们是否愿意承担风险。重要的工作完全可以在现有知识的边界内完成。即使创造力本身依赖于偶然性，一些专家也会选择坚持行之有效的方法，而另一些专家则会冒险探索问题领域的新方向。罗伯特·斯滕伯格和托德·卢巴特的创造力投资理论最清晰地阐述了这种将创造者视为赌徒的观点。在他们的模型中，创造者就像选股者，押注哪些想法、方法或研究领域会升值。与股票市场投机一样，这个过程很大程度上依赖于偶然性——一些创造者会名声大噪，而另一些则会默默无闻。常规型专家和创新型专家之间的区别很大程度上在于他们对风险的承受能力。爱迪生就曾因其冒险的发明创造而饱受经济动荡之苦。“至少我没有感到厌倦，”他后来在回顾自己发明生涯中跌宕起伏的成败时如此说道。投资理论也有助于解释为什么有些人比同等知识水平的同龄人更具创造力。历史学家安东·豪斯发现，发明家在独立发明之前更有可能与其他发明家有过接触，这表明，从事高风险行业的意愿可能是一种文化传承，而不仅仅是成功所需的专业知识。

This model of creativity helps to explain the seeming contradiction between Simonton’s equal-odds baseline of creative accomplishment and the rarity of world-class innovators. Getting to the frontier is difficult and takes years of study and practice. However, once the frontier has been reached, since further developments depend a great deal on randomness, creative accomplishment comes from being willing to take a lot of chances.

这种创造力模型有助于解释西蒙顿提出的“等概率创造成就”基准线与世界级创新者稀缺性之间看似矛盾的现象。达到前沿领域并非易事，需要多年的学习和实践。然而，一旦抵达前沿领域，由于进一步的发展很大程度上依赖于随机性，创造性成就便源于勇于承担风险。

Does Increasing Creative Output Increase Creative Quality?

提高创意产出是否能提高创意质量？

Simonton’s research and the equal-odds baseline do not imply any effort to increase output will automatically increase the likelihood of creative success. After all, I could write more books if I simply banged on the keyboard and published whatever nonsense text emerged, but few would argue that was a reliable strategy to authorial eminence. The tight coupling between quality and quantity might emerge, for instance, if creators develop internal standards that they rarely violate when publishing work. A writer going through a creative drought may not find it impossible to write anything, but simply find it difficult to write anything that she judges publishable. Such a dearth of ideas would then show up as a productive slump, even if it might be equally described as a problem of creative quality. Similarly, if creators tend to adopt a dominant style or method, that may artificially mask any quantity-quality trade-off. Picasso’s oeuvre is much broader than Da Vinci’s, in part, because the Cubist style he cultivated lent itself to more prolific production. We don’t have access to data from a counterfactual scenario where the Spaniard labored for years to produce hyperrealistic work, or the Renaissance man switched to churning out paintings like a factory. But within the normal bounds of creative acceptability, and holding the usual variations in method and style, quantity and quality are closely correlated in creative careers.

西蒙顿的研究和等概率基准并不意味着任何增加产量的努力都会自动提高创作成功的概率。毕竟，如果我只是胡乱敲击键盘，把所有出现的无意义文字都发表出来，我当然可以写出更多的书，但很少有人会认为这是通往作家巅峰的可靠策略。例如，如果创作者建立起一套内部标准，并且在发表作品时很少违背这些标准，那么质量和数量之间的紧密联系就可能显现出来。一位正经历创作瓶颈的作家可能并非完全写不出任何东西，而是很难写出她认为可以发表的作品。这种灵感匮乏会表现为创作效率的低迷，即使它也可以被视为创作质量的问题。同样，如果创作者倾向于采用某种主导风格或方法，这可能会人为地掩盖任何数量与质量之间的权衡。毕加索的作品比达·芬奇的作品要丰富得多，部分原因在于他所推崇的立体主义风格更有利于高产创作。我们无法获得反事实情景的数据，例如西班牙画家花费数年时间创作超写实作品，或者文艺复兴时期的博学家转而像工厂一样批量生产绘画作品。但在通常的创作规范范围内，并考虑到方法和风格的常见差异，在创作生涯中，数量和质量是密切相关的。

A straightforward, if unappealing, implication of the equal-odds rule is that successful creatives will tend to be workaholics. Edison offers a striking example. One story puts the inventor, lost in thought, late at night in his laboratory. After being asked why he was working so late, he asked what time it was. “Midnight,” came the reply, to which Edison responded, “ Midnight! Is that so. I must get home then, I was married today.” Although certainly hyperbole, it appears more credible in light of the inventor’s habit of staying at the laboratory for weeks on end, returning home only to pass out in his soiled clothes. One of the most famous photos of the man has him slumped and disheveled, listening to his phonograph after a seventy-two-hour binge of nonstop tinkering to improve the quality of the sound.

等概率法则的一个直接却令人不快的推论是：成功的创意人士往往是工作狂。爱迪生就是一个鲜明的例子。一个故事讲述这位发明家深夜在实验室里沉思。有人问他为什么工作到这么晚，他便问现在几点了。“午夜，”有人回答。爱迪生惊呼：“午夜！真的吗？我得回家了，我今天结婚了。”虽然这显然是夸张的说法，但考虑到这位发明家经常连续几周待在实验室，回家后往往只是穿着脏衣服倒头就睡，这个故事似乎就更可信了。他最著名的照片之一，是他连续七十二小时不停地摆弄留声机，试图改善音质，然后瘫倒在地，听着留声机播放的音乐。

An extreme dedication to work can be found in countless other eminent creatives. Herbert Simon, whose work won a Nobel Prize in economics, reportedly worked one hundred hours per week during his most productive periods. Albert Einstein focused so intensively during his work on general relativity that he developed stomach problems. Honoré de Balzac wrote his eighty-five novels by working fifteen hours a day for twenty years. Research suggests this work ethic pays off, with distinguished researchers in physical and social sciences working sixty to seventy hours per week with few vacations. Other research finds that psychologists who fit the hard-charging “Type A” profile are more likely to be highly cited than their relaxed “Type B” counterparts. Given this pattern, it’s not surprising that Edison claimed “ genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.” Yet these intense work schedules often impose considerable costs. Edison was an absent father and husband, as his quest for inventing left little time for anything else.

对工作的极致投入在无数杰出的创意人士身上都能找到。赫伯特·西蒙凭借其在经济学领域的杰出贡献荣获诺贝尔奖，据说在他创作力最旺盛的时期，每周工作长达一百小时。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦在研究广义相对论时，全身心投入，甚至患上了胃病。奥诺雷·德·巴尔扎克为了创作八十五部小说，每天工作十五小时，持续了二十年。研究表明，这种工作态度确实能带来回报，杰出的物理和社会科学研究人员每周工作六七十小时，几乎没有假期。另一些研究发现，那些属于“A型”强势型的心理学家比那些较为放松的“B型”同行更容易获得高引用率。鉴于此，爱迪生宣称“天才是一分灵感加上九十九分汗水”也就不足为奇了。然而，如此高强度的工作安排往往会带来巨大的代价。爱迪生是一位缺席的父亲和丈夫，因为他对发明创造的追求几乎占据了他所有的时间。

Strategies for Creating More (Without Reducing Quality or Working Overtime)

提高产量的策略（不降低质量或不加班）

The key to creative success is phenomenal productivity. Assuming, for a moment, that you’re already working as many hours as you can (or would like to), this raises a question if there are any other ways to increase one’s creative output without making obvious sacrifices to the quality of one’s work or personal life. Here are four strategies to consider for making a bigger impact.

创意成功的关键在于极高的效率。假设你已经尽可能多地工作（或者说，尽可能多地工作），那么问题来了：除了提高工作效率之外，还有什么方法可以在不明显牺牲工作质量或个人生活的前提下，提高创意产出？以下四种策略或许能助你产生更大的影响力。

Strategy #1: The Assembly-Line Method

策略一：流水线作业法

Few images are as antithetical to the popular image of creativity as the assembly line. Mechanically reproduced sameness, at the surface, appears to be the opposite of ingenuity. However, if we take the idea of creativity-as-productivity seriously, then we might have more to learn from the assembly line than we think. Routinizing the noncreative aspects of creative work can streamline their production. The comedian Jerry Seinfeld, on his hit television show Seinfeld , chose to organize the writing of new episodes by separating different phases of the creative process to different writer’s rooms: one for pitching ideas, one for outlining, and another for edits. In keeping with the role of chance in creativity, ideas and story lines were drawn out of the real-life experiences of comedy writers. However, the workflow ensured that polished episodes, not just half-baked ideas, made it on-air.

很少有图像像流水线那样与人们普遍认为的创造力截然相反。机械复制的千篇一律，表面上看似乎与独创性背道而驰。然而，如果我们认真对待“创造力即生产力”这一概念，那么我们或许能从流水线中学到比想象中更多的东西。将创意工作中非创造性的环节常规化，可以简化其生产流程。喜剧演员杰瑞·宋飞在他的热门电视剧《宋飞正传》中，选择将新剧集的创作过程分为不同的阶段，分别由不同的编剧室负责：一个负责提出想法，一个负责撰写大纲，还有一个负责修改。秉持着创造力中偶然性的重要性，剧中的创意和故事情节都源于喜剧编剧们的真实生活经历。然而，这种工作流程确保了最终播出的是精雕细琢的剧集，而不是半生不熟的创意。

Routines, checklists, and systematic phases for different aspects of your creative work are a few ways you can automate the regular part of making new work. While you may not have control over the content of the ideas and insights, if you can systematize some of the other aspects, you can ensure that you’re able to consistently take chances. For instance, a scientist may not always know which research avenues are most promising, but she can streamline her process for writing grants and submitting papers to devote more time to her lab work. Adopting an assembly-line mindset can also help shake you of creative resistance, where anxiety or perfectionism hold you back from publishing regularly. When the working up and releasing of new creative works is on autopilot, there’s little time for paralytic self-censoring.

为创作的各个方面制定流程、清单和系统化的步骤，是实现创作常规环节自动化的几种方法。虽然你可能无法掌控灵感和想法的内容，但如果能将其他一些方面系统化，就能确保自己能够持续地尝试新事物。例如，科学家可能并不总是知道哪些研究方向最有前景，但她可以简化撰写科研基金申请书和提交论文的流程，从而将更多时间投入到实验室工作中。采用流水线式的思维方式也能帮助你摆脱创作阻力，避免焦虑或完美主义阻碍你定期发表作品。当创作和发布新作品的过程自动化时，你就没有时间进行自我审查了。

Strategy #2: Allow Ideas to Ripen

策略二：让想法成熟

The problem-solving aspect of creativity suggests some ideas may be “ripe” for implementation, while others are missing key components. An inventor may be stuck on a particular technical hurdle that she can’t seem to overcome. A novelist may have a great idea for a character, but no plot. Pursuing unripe ideas takes more time because the combinatorial process of trying alternatives has to be brought to bear to break through the impasses. While the celebrated image of creative genius often focuses on a persistence through difficult projects, it’s equally the case that successful creatives manage to avoid problems that are not ripe for discovery. Robert Kanigel, in his extensive review of the illustrious Johns Hopkins research dynasty, remarks that Lasker Award–winning neuroscientist Solomon Snyder “ had almost a sixth sense for scientific questions apt to leave him batting his head against the wall—and he avoided them.”

创造力的问题解决能力意味着有些想法可能已经“成熟”可以付诸实施，而另一些想法则缺少关键要素。一位发明家可能被某个难以逾越的技术难题所困扰。一位小说家可能有一个很棒的人物构思，但却没有情节。追求不成熟的想法需要更多时间，因为必须运用组合式方法尝试各种方案才能突破僵局。虽然人们通常将创意天才的形象聚焦于他们在困难项目中坚持不懈的精神，但成功的创意人士同样能够巧妙地避开那些尚未成熟到可以探索的问题。罗伯特·卡尼格尔在他对约翰·霍普金斯大学杰出研究王朝的详尽回顾中指出，拉斯克奖得主、神经科学家所罗门·斯奈德“几乎对那些可能让他碰壁的科学问题有着一种第六感——而他总是能避开这些问题。”

Edison dealt with this problem by pursuing many different inventive projects simultaneously. Having multiple irons in the fire at once, he could switch between efforts when he was stuck. He also was able to take advantage of chance discoveries, if a new possibility turned up that cleared a path that was previously obscure. Many authors maintain extensive notes on potential stories, waiting until a sufficient number of pieces have assembled in the background before doggedly pursuing the work. While it may be impossible to anticipate creative solutions, it is often possible to see how large the gaps are that separate the current reservoir of knowledge and what would be needed for a solution.

爱迪生解决这个问题的方法是同时开展多个不同的发明项目。他同时进行多个项目，这样在遇到瓶颈时就可以在不同项目之间切换。他还能利用偶然的发现，如果出现新的可能性，开辟出一条之前未曾涉足的道路。许多作家都会为潜在的故事做大量的笔记，等待足够的素材积累起来，然后才开始着手创作。虽然我们可能无法预见所有创造性的解决方案，但我们通常可以预见现有知识储备与解决方案所需知识之间存在多大的差距。

Strategy #3: Moderate the Risks

策略三：控制风险

The role of chance in creativity suggests another reason people fail to produce inspired work: they’re not able to take the risks required. Those who produce the most creative successes also have quite a few creative failures. While sufficient expertise and productivity can increase the average quality of the results, the volatility involved in creative work can prevent many people from embarking on innovative careers. Edison was able to stomach the risks of inventing by rationalizing to himself that he could always start over as a telegraph operator if things didn’t turn out well. It’s also possible that an early life of frugal living convinced him that falling back down in financial fortunes was not such a disastrous setback as it might have been for someone who had only known a comfortable existence.

偶然性在创造力中的作用揭示了人们无法创作出惊艳作品的另一个原因：他们无法承担必要的风险。那些取得最大创意成功的人，也经历过不少创意失败。虽然足够的专业知识和生产力可以提高作品的平均质量，但创意工作本身的不确定性却可能阻碍许多人投身创新事业。爱迪生之所以能够承受发明创造的风险，是因为他安慰自己，如果事情进展不顺利，他随时可以重新做一名电报员。此外，早年节俭的生活经历也可能让他相信，经济上的挫折并不像对那些一直过着舒适生活的人来说那样可怕。

For those of us without Edison’s stoicism, we can increase our creative risk taking by ensuring we have more reliable sources of work and income we can fall back on in the case of failure. Following the investment theory of creativity, we can think of our work as a kind of creative portfolio. Creative projects are like owning high-risk stocks—they may pay off spectacularly, or we may lose all our money. To make these investments palatable, we want to combine them with the intellectual equivalent of treasury bonds—low-risk investments we can fall back on in a crisis.

对于我们这些没有爱迪生那样坚忍不拔精神的人来说，我们可以通过确保拥有更可靠的工作和收入来源来增加我们的创造性风险承担能力，以便在失败时有所依靠。借鉴创造力的投资理论，我们可以将自己的工作视为一种创造性投资组合。创造性项目就像持有高风险股票——它们可能带来丰厚的回报，也可能让我们血本无归。为了让这些投资更具吸引力，我们需要将它们与智力上的“国债”——即在危机时刻可以依靠的低风险投资——结合起来。

Strategy #4: Spend Less Time in Noncreative Work

策略四：减少非创造性工作的时间

Not every working hour is used for new work. Much of our potential creative output is eaten up by meetings, email, administrative overhead, and other minutiae. In Harriet Zuckerman’s study of Nobel laureates, many scientists remarked that their research careers slowed considerably after having won the prize. While some of this might come from reduced motivation, many remarked that they felt overwhelmed by all the extra public attention. When they had labored in obscurity, they could put many hours solely toward their work. As they became famous, they were increasingly asked for interviews, invited to attend public functions, and offered to chair prestigious committees. Edison’s productivity also dipped as he aged, as his business interests grew more expansive and he managed ever-larger teams of engineers.

并非每个工作时间都用于新的工作。我们的大部分潜在创造力都被会议、电子邮件、行政开支和其他琐事所消耗。在哈丽雅特·祖克曼对诺贝尔奖得主的研究中，许多科学家表示，获奖后他们的研究事业明显放缓。虽然部分原因可能是动力下降，但许多人表示，他们感到不堪重负，因为公众的关注度大幅提升。在默默耕耘之时，他们可以全身心投入到工作中。而随着名声鹊起，他们越来越多地被邀请接受采访、出席公共活动，并被推选担任重要委员会的主席。爱迪生的生产力也随着年龄的增长而下降，因为他的商业版图不断扩大，管理的工程师团队规模也越来越大。

Creativity requires nimbleness and the ability to put in hours on uncertain projects, both of which may get harder as the obligations of success set in. Being more creative, then, requires a pushback against the encroachment of noncreative work. Nobel-winning physicist Richard Feynman used the strategy of feigning irresponsibility to avoid being roped into time-wasting assignments in his university department. Author and computer science professor Cal Newport advocates setting up strict boundaries to surround one’s “deep work” to ensure a sufficient supply of uninterrupted thinking time in order to make progress on difficult problems. Whatever strategy is used, only by maintaining a high ratio of hours worked on creative projects to hours worked in total can we possibly have a productive career without completely sacrificing our personal lives.

创造力需要敏捷的思维和在充满不确定性的项目上投入大量时间的能力，而随着成功压力的到来，这两点都可能变得更加困难。因此，要想更有创造力，就需要抵制非创造性工作的侵蚀。诺贝尔物理学奖得主理查德·费曼就曾利用“假装不负责任”的策略，来避免被大学系里那些浪费时间的任务所束缚。作家兼计算机科学教授卡尔·纽波特则提倡为自己的“深度工作”设定严格的界限，以确保有足够的、不受干扰的思考时间，从而在解决难题方面取得进展。无论采用何种策略，只有保持较高的创意项目工作时间占总工作时间的比例，我们才能在不完全牺牲个人生活的前提下，拥有高效的职业生涯。

From Practice to Feedback

从实践到反馈

Over the last four chapters, we’ve discussed finding the difficulty sweet spot, why the mind is not like a muscle, the power of variability to ensure flexible skills, and the surprisingly tight connection between quantity and quality in creative achievements. Over the next four chapters, we’ll look at the role feedback plays in learning. We’ll start with learning in environments with uncertainty, and see the importance of enhancing feedback to ensure accurate judgments. Next we’ll look at the problem of interaction in learning, where contact with reality is both necessary and fraught for mastering real-life skills. Then we’ll examine the role of unlearning, and how correcting our mistakes and misconceptions becomes increasingly important as our skills develop. Finally we’ll look at anxiety in learning, and how direct feedback from the situations that scare us is one of the most effective ways to overcome our fears.

在过去的四章中，我们探讨了如何找到难度的最佳平衡点、为什么大脑不像肌肉那样灵活、变化性对于确保技能灵活性的重要性，以及创造性成就中数量与质量之间令人惊讶的紧密联系。在接下来的四章中，我们将探讨反馈在学习中的作用。首先，我们将从不确定环境中的学习入手，了解增强反馈对于确保判断准确性的重要性。接下来，我们将探讨学习中的互动问题，在这种互动中，与现实的接触对于掌握实际生活技能既必不可少，又充满挑战。然后，我们将研究“遗忘学习”的作用，以及随着技能的提升，纠正错误和误解的重要性日益凸显。最后，我们将探讨学习中的焦虑，以及从令我们恐惧的情境中获得直接反馈如何成为克服恐惧最有效的方法之一。

反馈

Learning from Experience

从经验中学习

# ↩

Chapter 9

第九章

Experience Doesn’t Reliably Ensure Expertise

经验并不能可靠地保证专业技能

True intuitive expertise is learned from prolonged experience with good feedback on mistakes.

真正的直觉型专业技能是通过长期的经验积累，并在错误中得到良好的反馈而获得的。

—Daniel Kahneman, psychologist

——心理学家丹尼尔·卡尼曼

  • What are the prerequisites for intuitive expertise?
    具备直觉型专业技能的先决条件是什么？
  • How can we improve in uncertain environments with noisy feedback?
    在充满噪声反馈的不确定环境中，我们如何才能改进？
  • When should you trust your gut, and when should you stick to the numbers?
    什么时候应该相信直觉，什么时候应该坚持数据？

O n September 17, 2007, a day before her nineteenth birthday, Annette Obrestad made history by becoming the youngest-ever winner of a World Series of Poker tournament. Competing in Europe—she’d have two wait another two years before she was old enough to play in Las Vegas—the young Norwegian took home the one-million-pound prize. She had beaten out 362 other entrants, each having paid ten thousand pounds in order to participate. Although poker may be a game of chance, Obrestad’s win was hardly a fluke. She had already become a dominant player online. While still in high school, she was winning more money from poker than her mother was earning from her full-time job. Just a couple of months before the World Series of Poker event she entered an online tournament with 179 other players. For fun, she decided to see how far she could get while having a piece of tape on her computer screen, preventing her from seeing her own cards. She won.

2007年9月17日，安妮特·奥布雷斯塔德（Annette Obrestad）在她19岁生日前一天，创造了历史，成为世界扑克系列赛（WSOP）历史上最年轻的冠军。这位年轻的挪威选手在欧洲参赛——她还要再等两年才能达到在拉斯维加斯参赛的年龄——最终捧走了100万英镑的奖金。她击败了其他362名参赛者，每位参赛者都支付了1万英镑的参赛费。虽然扑克是一种运气游戏，但奥布雷斯塔德的胜利绝非偶然。她早已是线上扑克界的佼佼者。还在读高中时，她靠扑克赢的钱就超过了她母亲的全职工作收入。就在世界扑克系列赛开赛前几个月，她参加了一场有179名选手参加的线上锦标赛。为了好玩，她决定在电脑屏幕上贴一块胶带，不让自己看到自己的牌，看看自己能走多远。结果，她赢了。

Obrestad got her start after seeing an ad for an online poker site while watching bowling on television. She had enjoyed playing card games with her father as a young girl, and thought it might be fun. Only fifteen, she was too young to gamble with real money, so she joined the play-money games online. To her surprise, she found out she had a knack for it. “I just kind of had a thing for the game,” she later reflected. “You know when you start something and all of a sudden you realize you’re really good at it and everyone else sucks? That was my experience with poker.” A play-money tournament online led to her winning nine dollars. From that minuscule start, she steadily grew her bankroll. Despite never having invested any of her own cash, Obrestad was now playing—and winning—games involving real money against other players. Over the next four years, she won hundreds of thousands of dollars online. Once she was old enough to gamble legally in a casino, she started playing live games as well. By the end of her poker career, Obrestad had won over $3.9 million from live games alone.

奥布雷斯塔德的扑克生涯始于一次偶然的机会：她在电视上看保龄球比赛时，看到了一个在线扑克网站的广告。小时候，她就喜欢和父亲一起玩纸牌游戏，觉得扑克或许也很有趣。当时她只有十五岁，年纪太小不能玩真钱赌博，所以就加入了在线的虚拟货币游戏。令她惊讶的是，她发现自己在这方面很有天赋。“我就是喜欢上这个游戏了，”她后来回忆道，“你知道那种感觉吗？当你开始做某件事，突然发现自己在这方面很厉害，而其他人都很菜？我玩扑克就是这种感觉。” 一次在线虚拟货币锦标赛让她赢得了九美元。从这微不足道的起点开始，她的资金稳步增长。尽管从未投入过任何自有资金，奥布雷斯塔德现在却能和其他玩家玩真钱游戏，并且还能赢钱。在接下来的四年里，她在线赢得了数十万美元。一旦她到了可以合法进入赌场赌博的年龄，她也开始玩实体赌场游戏了。奥布雷斯塔德的扑克生涯结束时，仅通过现场游戏就赢得了超过 390 万美元。

Obrestad represents a new breed of poker player. Far from the stereotype of swaggering gamblers playing for high stakes in smoke-filled casinos, this new generation mastered the game at home, on their computers. To understand how Obrestad, and players like her, have gotten so good in such a short time, we have to see how the game of poker has evolved over time.

奥布雷斯塔德代表着新一代的扑克玩家。与人们印象中在烟雾缭绕的赌场里豪赌的赌徒截然不同，这一代玩家在家中，通过电脑，就掌握了扑克的精髓。要了解奥布雷斯塔德以及像她一样的玩家如何在如此短的时间内取得如此高的成就，我们必须了解扑克游戏的发展历程。

A Brief History of Poker

扑克简史

In the earliest days, being good at poker meant being a good cheat. Gambling riverboats took players—and their money—along the Mississippi River, spreading the game throughout the American South. From this era, we have accounts of people like George Devol, who bragged about his swindling exploits in his autobiography, Forty Years a Gambler on the Mississippi . A common trick was to use a marked deck—cards with subtle smudges on the back side—that could inform an unscrupulous player who held the better hand. Devol bragged about catching another player using a marked deck against him and turning the tables, cheating the cheater. In another episode, Devol’s reputation as a shrewd poker player attracted an investor who wanted to front four thousand dollars to Devol for a share of his winnings. He promptly lost it all to a conspirator, allowing him to walk away with most of the investment without needing to repay his backer. “ The common belief was that if you sat down to play a poker game on a Mississippi steamboat, you were basically asking to be cheated,” writes poker player and author Màrton Magyar.

在扑克游戏的早期，擅长打牌意味着擅长作弊。赌船载着玩家——以及他们的钱——沿着密西西比河航行，将这种游戏传播到美国南部各地。从那个时代，我们就能找到像乔治·德沃尔这样的人的记载，他在自传《密西西比河上的四十年赌徒生涯》中吹嘘自己的诈骗经历。一种常见的伎俩是使用记号牌——背面有细微污渍的牌——这样不择手段的玩家就能知道谁的牌更好。德沃尔吹嘘自己抓到另一个玩家用记号牌对付他，然后反过来欺骗了作弊者。在另一个故事中，德沃尔精明的扑克牌技吸引了一位投资者，这位投资者想先借给德沃尔四千美元，作为他赢钱的一部分。然而，他很快就被一个同谋者骗走了所有钱，德沃尔得以带着大部分投资扬长而去，而无需偿还投资者。 “人们普遍认为，如果你在密西西比河的汽船上坐下来玩扑克，你基本上就是在自找麻烦，”扑克玩家兼作家马顿·马扎尔写道。

Despite these unseemly beginnings, poker also acquired a reputation as a game of skill, not just deviousness. Mark Twain was an avid fan of the game. “ There are few things as unpardonably neglected in our country as poker,” he wrote. That neglect would not last for long. Franklin Delano Roosevelt regularly played stud games during his four-term stint in the White House, and Dwight Eisenhower counted himself a poker player. Richard Nixon even managed to fund part of an early congressional campaign with poker winnings. The game allowed players to size up not only the odds, but also their opponents. “Poker is a game of people,” wrote professional gambler and author of one of the first popular books on poker strategy Doyle Brunson. “ A man’s true feelings come out in a poker game.” In his book, Brunson mixed careful strategic reasoning based on probability with more fanciful additions, such as his belief in extrasensory perception and the importance of trusting gut feelings over a more rational analysis. Brunson’s book captured a popular perception of poker that remains to this day—that savvy poker playing is largely a matter of psychology, not probability.

尽管扑克起源于不光彩的时期，但它也逐渐赢得了技巧而非仅仅是诡计的声誉。马克·吐温就是扑克的忠实拥趸。他写道：“在我们国家，很少有像扑克这样被严重忽视的事物。” 然而，这种忽视并没有持续太久。富兰克林·德拉诺·罗斯福在四届总统任期内经常玩梭哈，德怀特·艾森豪威尔也自称是扑克玩家。理查德·尼克松甚至用扑克赢来的钱资助了他早期的国会竞选活动。扑克游戏不仅让玩家能够评估胜算，还能让他们了解对手。职业赌徒、扑克策略畅销书作家多伊尔·布伦森写道：“扑克是一场人与人之间的游戏。一个人的真实情感会在扑克游戏中流露出来。” 在他的书中，布伦森将基于概率的严谨策略推理与一些更具想象力的元素相结合，例如他对超感官知觉的信仰，以及相信直觉而非理性分析的重要性。布伦森的书捕捉到了一种至今仍然流行的扑克观点——即精明的扑克玩法很大程度上取决于心理，而不是概率。

Poker’s next revolution came in 2003, when Chris Moneymaker (that is his real name) won a seat at the World Series of Poker tournament after winning a $39 online tournament. The full-time accountant and amateur player bested 839 other entrants—each paying $10,000 to participate—for a grand prize of $2.5 million. Moneymaker’s surprise win over seasoned pros led to an explosion in the interest in online poker. Dubbed the “Moneymaker effect,” online poker websites ballooned in size, attracting tens of thousands of new players.

扑克的下一次革命发生在2003年，当时克里斯·莫尼梅克（Chris Moneymaker，这是他的真名）赢得了一场39美元的线上锦标赛，从而获得了世界扑克大赛（WSOP）的参赛资格。这位全职会计师兼业余玩家击败了其他839名参赛者——每位参赛者都支付了1万美元的参赛费——最终赢得了250万美元的巨额奖金。莫尼梅克爆冷击败经验丰富的职业选手，引发了线上扑克热潮。这场被称为“莫尼梅克效应”的事件，使得线上扑克网站迅速发展壮大，吸引了成千上万的新玩家。

Playing poker on a computer differs from a casino. Most obviously, there isn’t a lot of room for psychoanalysis. All you can see of your opponent is a screen name. This means carefully observing an opposing player for signs of a bluff takes a back seat to more fundamental analyses of the way the cards are dealt. Less obviously, online poker dramatically accelerates the pace at which someone could acquire experience in the game. “It used to be if you didn’t see a guy in Las Vegas playing in the high-stakes, then he probably wasn’t very good,” explains professional poker player Daniel Negreanu. He notes that the new breed of online player “is gaining experience so quickly because online you can play multiple tables. So, some of these guys are playing twelve games at once.” He adds, “ A guy like Doyle Brunson, who’s eighty-four years old right now, he’s been playing every day pretty much for fifty, sixty years. He still hasn’t played as many hands as some of these twenty-three-year-old kids.” Perhaps even more important than extensive experience is the enhanced feedback that can be gained by playing online. Old-school players largely had to rely on their memory for how key hands played. Online play allows players to replace frail human recollection with a hard drive, keeping track of their hand history and those they regularly play against. Obrestad, who began her poker journey at the beginning of the Moneymaker era, would be able to take advantage of that early opportunity to gain experience and feedback in a way no casual player, and few casino-bound professionals, could have imagined.

在电脑上玩扑克与在赌场玩扑克截然不同。最显而易见的是，电脑扑克几乎没有心理分析的空间。你只能看到对手的屏幕名称。这意味着，仔细观察对手是否有虚张声势的迹象，比起对发牌方式的分析，就显得不那么重要了。不太明显的是，在线扑克极大地加快了玩家积累经验的速度。“以前，如果你在拉斯维加斯没看到有人玩高额赌注的牌局，那他可能水平不高，”职业扑克玩家丹尼尔·内格里努解释道。他指出，新一代的在线玩家“经验积累如此迅速，是因为在线上可以同时玩多张牌桌。所以，有些人同时玩十二局。”他补充道，“像多伊尔·布伦森这样，现在84岁了，他几乎每天都玩，已经玩了五六十年了。但他玩过的牌局数量仍然不及一些23岁的年轻人。”或许比丰富的经验更重要的是，在线游戏能够提供更强大的反馈。老派玩家大多只能依靠记忆来记住关键牌局的走向。而在线游戏则允许玩家用硬盘取代脆弱的记忆力，记录自己的牌局历史以及经常遇到的对手。奥布雷斯塔德的扑克生涯始于“金钱大师”时代初期，她能够利用这一早期机会积累经验和反馈，这是普通玩家乃至少数职业玩家都难以想象的。

Poker and the Art of Learning Under Uncertainty

扑克与不确定性下的学习艺术

To understand the difficulty of mastering a game like poker, it helps to compare it to another famously cerebral game: chess. In chess, play is completely deterministic. Make the same moves and the outcome will be the same every time. In contrast, poker is a game of chance. Even being dealt two aces—the best starting cards in Texas Hold’em—your chances of losing against a random hand are still one in six. This randomness makes it much harder to learn from your mistakes. Did you lose because you were unlucky, or just unskilled? One remedy for randomness is simply more experience. Play enough and eventually luck averages out. Many of the earliest players, unschooled in probability, likely acquired their intuition simply through repetition. See the same hand dozens of times and your average sense of its potency will gradually approach the true value. But, given the vast quantity of possible poker hands, it becomes clear that this approach to gaining poker skill has serious shortcomings.

要理解掌握扑克这类游戏的难度，不妨将其与另一款以脑力著称的游戏——国际象棋——进行比较。在国际象棋中，棋局完全是确定性的。每次走同样的棋，结果都一样。相比之下，扑克则是一种机会游戏。即使拿到两张A——德州扑克中最好的起手牌——你输给其他玩家的概率仍然是六分之一。这种随机性使得玩家更难从错误中吸取教训。你输是因为运气不好，还是因为技术不够？应对随机性的方法之一就是积累经验。只要玩得足够多，运气最终会趋于平均。许多早期的玩家，由于缺乏概率论方面的知识，很可能只是通过反复练习就培养出了直觉。同样的牌型反复出现几十次，你对它威力的平均感知就会逐渐接近其真实价值。但是，考虑到扑克牌型的数量极其庞大，这种提升扑克技巧的方法显然存在严重的缺陷。

Fortunately, there’s an alternative: use probability theory to calculate the correct move and ignore the actual outcomes. Today, all aspiring poker players quickly become well versed in the basic math. Players count the number of “outs” or cards they need to complete their hand, and count the number of hands that could beat theirs. Calculating the odds, and comparing that to bet sizes, can make it clear whether a bet is for “value” (meaning it is made because the player thinks the odds of winning are worth the price) or a bluff. Poker may be random, but since the cards obey the laws of probability, calculation is a superior strategy to basing decisions on gut feelings alone.

幸运的是，还有另一种方法：运用概率论来计算正确的行动，而忽略实际结果。如今，所有有抱负的扑克玩家都会很快精通基本的数学知识。玩家会计算完成牌型所需的“补牌”数量，以及可能击败自己牌型的牌型数量。通过计算赔率并将其与下注额进行比较，可以清楚地判断下注是出于“价值”（即玩家认为获胜的概率值得投入）还是虚张声势。扑克虽然具有随机性，但由于牌面遵循概率规律，因此计算策略远胜于仅仅依靠直觉做出决定。

But luck isn’t the only thing that makes poker difficult. Comparing it again to chess, poker is a game of hidden information. A chess player never needs to worry about an opponent hiding a queen up her sleeve for a surprise checkmate. In contrast, you can rarely be sure of your opponent’s cards before you make a bet. This means the optimal strategy depends not just on the bare odds of your hand winning against a randomly selected hand, but on the odds of winning against the hands you think your opponent might have, and in turn, what your opponent thinks you have. This makes poker a game of calibration. If you only bet when you have good cards, your opponents will quickly realize your playing style and fold every time you make a big raise. In contrast, if you bluff frequently, opponents will realize that too and start calling you more often. Poker strategy requires a careful balancing to eliminate patterns in your playing style that could be exploited by your opponents.

但运气并非扑克游戏的唯一难点。再次将扑克与国际象棋进行比较，扑克是一款信息隐蔽的游戏。国际象棋棋手永远不必担心对手藏着一张皇后牌，伺机偷袭将死自己。相反，在下注之前，你几乎不可能确定对手的底牌。这意味着最佳策略不仅取决于你的牌型战胜随机对手牌型的概率，还取决于你预测对手可能持有的牌型的胜率，以及对手对你牌型的预测。这使得扑克成为一款需要精准权衡的游戏。如果你只在手握好牌时才下注，对手很快就会摸清你的打法，并在你每次大额加注时弃牌。相反，如果你频繁诈唬，对手也会意识到这一点，并开始更频繁地跟注。扑克策略需要谨慎权衡，以消除对手可以利用的打法模式。

Both the intrinsic randomness of poker outcomes, and the careful calibration needed to develop a good strategy, are made easier by playing online. While old-school casino players might have jotted down a handful of their key hands for later analysis, the new generation of players can download every hand they’ve ever played and run it through software analysis. This can not only help point out mistakes in the calculation of the probabilities, but also help you spot patterns in your own playing style that other players might exploit.

扑克结果本身的随机性，以及制定有效策略所需的精细调整，在线扑克都让这一切变得更加容易。老派赌场玩家或许会记下几手关键牌局以便日后分析，而新一代玩家则可以下载自己玩过的每一手牌，并通过软件进行分析。这不仅有助于指出概率计算中的错误，还能帮助你发现自身牌风中可能被其他玩家利用的套路。

The rise of analytical tools has already begun fueling the next evolution in poker. Players are applying increasingly sophisticated calculations from game theory—a branch of mathematics that deals with strategic choices in hidden-information games. These “game-theory optimal” strategies seek to find the exact calibration of bluffing and betting for any hand combination so that there’s no possibility of an opponent exploiting a pattern in your play. Many players today randomize their choices, say, by looking at the second hand on their watch and choosing one play if the number is even and another if it is odd, in order to escape the mind-reading abilities of veterans like Doyle Brunson. The Massachusetts Institute of Technology even offered a poker theory course at its Sloan School of Management, reflecting an appreciation for the mathematical sophistication of modern play. Regardless of the new directions poker takes, it’s clear that it will not stop evolving as players develop more sophisticated theory and learn from ever-more-detailed feedback to enhance their game.

分析工具的兴起已经开始推动扑克运动的下一个发展阶段。玩家们正运用博弈论中日益复杂的计算方法——博弈论是数学的一个分支，专门研究隐信息博弈中的策略选择。这些“博弈论最优”策略旨在为任何牌型组合找到诈唬和下注的精确平衡点，从而杜绝对手利用玩家打法模式的可能性。如今，许多玩家会随机选择策略，例如，通过观察手表上的秒针，如果秒针是偶数就选择一种打法，如果是奇数就选择另一种，以此来规避像道尔·布伦森这样的老手的“读心术”。麻省理工学院甚至在其斯隆管理学院开设了扑克理论课程，这体现了人们对现代扑克游戏中数学复杂性的认可。无论扑克运动朝着哪个方向发展，显而易见的是，随着玩家们发展出更复杂的理论并从日益详尽的反馈中学习以提升牌技，扑克的发展将永不停歇。

When Should You Trust Your Gut?

什么时候应该相信自己的直觉？

Poker illustrates some of the difficulties of learning under uncertainty. Players use probability theory and enhanced feedback to calibrate their decisions beyond what could be easily achieved from raw experience alone. But what about situations where strong theory or corrective feedback isn’t easily available. How do experts acquire useful intuitions then? The surprising answer may be that in many cases they simply don’t.

扑克游戏展现了在不确定性下学习的一些难点。玩家会运用概率论和强化反馈来调整决策，这远非仅凭经验所能轻易达到。但如果缺乏强有力的理论或纠正性反馈呢？专家们又该如何获得有效的直觉？令人惊讶的答案或许是：在很多情况下，他们根本无法获得这种直觉。

In 1954, the psychologist Paul Meehl wrote a slim volume titled Clinical versus Statistical Prediction: A Theoretical Analysis and Review of the Evidence . In it, he wanted to compare two modes of decision making. The first, which he called “clinical,” referred to the subjective impression of the doctor, counselor, teacher, or parole board judge in reviewing cases and making a prediction about the future of an individual.
