The second he referred to as the “statistical” or “actuarial” method. This method worked by a simple formula, taking basic data about the patient and computing an answer. Despite the complaints from countless experts that their professional opinion could never be substituted by a mechanical formula, Meehl found that the statistical method tended to outperform clinical judgment. Nor did the formulas need to be particularly sophisticated to beat gut feelings. In one experiment, sociologist Ernest Burgess looked at three thousand parole decisions for criminal offenders to predict rates of recidivism. Burgess took a list of twenty-one basic factors about each offender (for example, age, previous offenses, nature of crime, etc.) and simply added the number of factors in the parolee’s favor and subtracted those against. In comparison to this unweighted sum, Burgess compared the expert opinion of three psychiatrists. The result? Burgess’s simple arithmetic slightly underperformed the psychiatrists in predicting success, but greatly surpassed them in predicting failure. This was even under the somewhat unfair comparison that the actuarial tally was used in every case, where the psychiatrists omitted an opinion on some of the more difficult cases. In short, in a heads-up comparison between the intuition of an expert and a simple calculator, the calculator won.

1954年，心理学家保罗·米尔（Paul Meehl）撰写了一本名为《临床预测与统计预测：理论分析与证据回顾》的小册子。书中，他试图比较两种决策模式。第一种，他称之为“临床”方法，指的是医生、咨询师、教师或假释委员会法官在审查案例并预测个人未来时所作出的主观印象。第二种方法，他称之为“统计”或“精算”方法。这种方法通过一个简单的公式运作，利用患者的基本数据计算出结果。尽管无数专家抱怨他们的专业意见永远无法被机械公式所取代，但米尔发现，统计方法往往优于临床判断。而且，这些公式并不需要特别复杂就能胜过直觉。在一项实验中，社会学家欧内斯特·伯吉斯（Ernest Burgess）研究了三千例罪犯的假释决定，以预测他们的再犯率。伯吉斯列出了每位罪犯的二十一项基本因素（例如年龄、前科、犯罪性质等），然后简单地将有利于假释犯的因素数量相加，再减去不利因素的数量。与这个未经加权的总和相比，伯吉斯比较了三位精神科医生的专家意见。结果如何呢？伯吉斯的简单计算在预测成功方面略逊于精神科医生，但在预测失败方面却远胜于他们。即便是在这种略显不公平的比较中——即在所有案例中都使用了这种简单的计算方法，而精神科医生在一些更复杂的案例中没有给出意见——结果依然如此。简而言之，在专家直觉和简单计算器的直接比较中，计算器胜出。

At the time of the publication of Meehl’s book, fewer than two dozen studies existed directly probing the relative efficacy of intuitive judgment and statistical calculation. As a result, Meehl was unsure about which would win out in the long run. Perhaps there were some domains where subjectivity beat cold number-crunching? In his book, Meehl was sympathetic to the potential advantage of the clinician:

在米尔的著作出版之时，直接探讨直觉判断和统计计算相对有效性的研究不足二十项。因此，米尔并不确定哪种方法最终会胜出。或许在某些领域，主观判断胜过冷冰冰的数字运算？在书中，米尔对临床医生可能拥有的优势表示理解：

For instance, suppose . . . we are trying to predict whether a given professor will attend the movies on a given night. On the basis of [a hypothetical calculation] we arrive at a probability of .90 that he will attend the neighborhood theatre, the present night being Friday. The clinician, however, knows in addition to these facts that Professor A has recently broken his leg. This single fact is sufficient to change the probability of .90 to a probability of approximately zero.

例如，假设……我们试图预测某位教授是否会在某个晚上去看电影。根据[假设的计算]，我们得出他今晚（周五）去附近影院的概率为0.90。然而，这位临床医生除了知道这些情况外，还知道A教授最近腿骨折了。仅此一项就足以将0.90的概率变为接近于零的概率。

Broken legs occur rarely, but when they do they are highly informative. These kinds of cues, Meehl conjectured, might give the clinician a distinct advantage since they wouldn’t appear in a statistical algorithm, but knowing them, a clinician might be able to make a better guess. Meehl was hopeful that a niche for clinical judgment might be sought out, even if the twenty or so studies that existed at the time still favored the actuarial method.

腿部骨折虽然罕见，但一旦发生，却能提供极具价值的信息。米尔推测，这类线索或许能为临床医生带来显著优势，因为它们不会出现在统计算法中，但掌握了这些线索，临床医生就能做出更准确的判断。米尔希望，即使当时已有的二十余项研究仍然倾向于精算方法，临床判断仍能找到一席之地。

Unfortunately, Meehl’s cautious optimism wasn’t borne out. In the subsequent decades, over one hundred studies amassed, clearly favoring simple formulas to intuitive judgment in a wide range of decisions under uncertainty. Four decades later Meehl wrote, “As the evidence accumulated beyond the initial batch of research comparisons, it became clear that conducting an investigation in which informal clinical judgment would perform better than the equation was almost impossible.” He added that “in around two fifths of the studies [clinical versus actuarial] methods were approximately equal in accuracy, and in around three fifths the actuarial method was significantly better.” Interestingly, adding longer interviews with patients, a rich source of narrative information that can’t easily fit into an equation, actually made the clinician worse . Given these consistently pessimistic findings, Meehl suggests that simple rules and models ought to replace intuitive judgment in many domains of expertise. For instance, psychiatric diagnoses should depend on following a checklist of symptoms rather than the therapist going off her gut feeling. In the areas where calculations reliably outperform intuition, this could improve decision-making accuracy. In areas where the clinician equals the algorithm, it could save enormous costs, given that the status quo usually involves lengthy deliberation by highly paid experts, whereas simple models can be calculated effectively with only a little bit of data entry into a spreadsheet. The clinicians Meehl studied offer a marked contrast from skilled poker players, who until the recent advance of deep learning and supercomputer-fueled algorithms could edge out even sophisticated poker software.

不幸的是，米尔谨慎的乐观态度并未得到证实。在随后的几十年里，积累了一百多项研究，这些研究清楚地表明，在各种不确定情况下的决策中，简单的公式比直觉判断更胜一筹。四十年后，米尔写道：“随着研究证据的积累，超越了最初的研究比较，人们逐渐意识到，要开展一项研究，证明非正式的临床判断比公式更有效，几乎是不可能的。”他补充说，“在大约五分之二的研究中，[临床方法与精算方法]的准确性大致相当，而在大约五分之三的研究中，精算方法明显更胜一筹。”有趣的是，增加与患者的长时间访谈——这是获取丰富叙述性信息（难以用公式表达）的途径——实际上却让临床医生的判断变得更糟。鉴于这些持续悲观的研究结果，米尔建议在许多专业领域，应该用简单的规则和模型来取代直觉判断。例如，精神科诊断应该依据症状清单，而不是治疗师凭感觉行事。在计算结果可靠地优于直觉的领域，这可以提高决策的准确性。在临床医生与算法能力相当的领域，这可以节省大量成本，因为现状通常需要高薪专家进行长时间的讨论，而简单的模型只需在电子表格中输入少量数据即可有效计算。米尔研究的临床医生与技艺精湛的扑克玩家形成了鲜明的对比，后者在深度学习和超级计算机算法出现之前，甚至可以战胜复杂的扑克软件。

Why does the clinician perform so poorly compared to simple calculations? One hypothesis is that intuition works much like the weighted-sum approach used by the actuary, but it is simply less accurate. In this account, the psychiatrist making parole decisions is unconsciously doing the same sort of weighing of evidence from different factors, but she is simply less precise than the formulas, which leads to her difficulties. Testing that hypothesis, researcher Eric Johnson reviewed the transcripts of hospital staff making decisions about which graduate students to admit into their residency programs while they were asked to talk through their thoughts as they occurred. “Rather than being fallible approximations to a linear model, these judges seem to use information in quite a different manner,” Johnson remarked. Instead, judges seemed to make use of highly specific information that is unlikely to show up frequently enough to be represented in the statistical approach. To use Meehl’s example, it is as if intuitive experts mostly looked around for broken legs and ignored more mundane considerations, such as the fact that the professor tends to go to the movies on Fridays.

为什么临床医生的表现远逊于简单的计算？一种假设是，直觉的运作方式与精算师使用的加权求和法非常相似，只是准确度较低。在这种解释下，精神科医生在做出假释决定时，无意识地对来自不同因素的证据进行类似的权衡，但她的精确度不如公式，这导致了她的困难。为了验证这一假设，研究员埃里克·约翰逊（Eric Johnson）查阅了医院工作人员在决定录取哪些研究生进入住院医师项目时，被要求边思考边描述自己思路的记录。“这些判断者似乎并非是对线性模型的易错近似，而是以截然不同的方式使用信息，”约翰逊评论道。相反，判断者似乎利用了非常具体的信息，而这些信息出现的频率不足以被统计方法所涵盖。用米尔（Meehl）的例子来说，这就好比直觉专家主要关注的是别人是否骨折，而忽略了更日常的考虑因素，例如教授通常周五去看电影。

To see how intuitions that work by constructing a story can break down, consider a famous failure of intuition demonstrated by Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky. First, read a brief passage about Linda:

为了了解通过构建故事来判断直觉的有效性如何失效，不妨看看丹尼尔·卡尼曼和阿莫斯·特沃斯基所展示的一个著名的直觉失效案例。首先，请阅读一段关于琳达的简短文字：

Linda is 31 years old, single, outspoken, and very bright. She majored in philosophy. As a student, she was deeply concerned with issues of discrimination and social justice, and also participated in anti-nuclear demonstrations.

琳达今年31岁，单身，性格直率，非常聪明。她大学主修哲学。学生时代，她就非常关注歧视和社会正义问题，并且积极参与反核示威活动。

Now ask which of the following propositions is more likely:

现在请问以下哪个命题更有可能成立：

  1. Linda is a bank teller.
    琳达是一名银行柜员。
  2. Linda is a bank teller and is active in the feminist movement.
    琳达是一名银行柜员，同时也是女权运动的积极参与者。

Many people feel the second response is more likely, but it is strictly less probable than the first. The set of people who are bank tellers active in the feminist movement is a subset of the set of people who are bank tellers. Imagined as a Venn diagram, one wholly contains the other, so the probability of the first must be greater or equal to the second as a matter of logic. Nonetheless, our intuition often gives the opposite answer because Linda’s description makes her seem more similar to a bank teller who is active in the feminist movement. Subjective judgment tends to underperform statistical calculations because our intuition is a great storyteller, able to construct a highly vivid picture based on past experience, but fails to aggregate mundane information even if it is more predictive.

许多人认为第二个答案更有可能，但严格来说，它的可能性比第一个答案要小。积极参与女权运动的银行柜员群体是银行柜员群体的一个子集。如果用维恩图来表示，两者完全包含，因此从逻辑上讲，前者的概率必然大于或等于后者。然而，我们的直觉常常给出相反的答案，因为琳达的描述让她看起来更像是一位积极参与女权运动的银行柜员。主观判断往往不如统计计算准确，因为我们的直觉擅长讲故事，能够根据过去的经验构建生动的画面，但却无法整合那些看似平凡的信息，即使这些信息更具预测性。

Intuitive Expertise: Skill or Hubris?

直觉专长：是技能还是傲慢？

In chapter 4 , we discussed the incredible power of expertise to make knowledge invisible and seemingly arrive at a good decision without much reflection. Now we’re considering situations where expertise barely outperforms a simple tally. Which is it? Is expertise real or fake? Are quick judgments reliably accurate or overconfident bluster? Such questions were put to Gary Klein and Daniel Kahneman in their collaborative paper, “Conditions for Intuitive Expertise: A Failure to Disagree.” Klein, whose work was discussed in chapter 4 , worked with firefighters in naturalistic scenarios, finding that they often made rapid-fire decisions that were eerily prescient. Kahneman, in contrast, has a devoted a research career to the study of intuitive judgment and its frequent failings. Despite research programs that put them on opposite sides of a debate over the merits of expert intuition, the duo found that they largely agreed on the conditions that were necessary for genuine expertise to develop:

在第四章中，我们讨论了专业知识的强大力量，它能使知识隐形，并看似无需过多思考就能做出正确的决策。现在，我们来探讨一些情况，在这些情况下，专业知识的表现甚至略优于简单的统计。究竟哪种情况更胜一筹？专业知识是真实的还是虚假的？快速的判断是可靠的准确，还是过度自信的虚张声势？这些问题被提交给了加里·克莱因和丹尼尔·卡尼曼，他们在合作论文《直觉专业知识的条件：未能达成共识》中探讨。克莱因的研究在第四章中有所提及，他与消防员在自然情境下合作，发现他们经常做出快速且极具预见性的决策。相比之下，卡尼曼则毕生致力于研究直觉判断及其常见的缺陷。尽管研究项目使他们在专家直觉的价值问题上站在了对立的两方，但两人发现，对于真正专业知识发展的必要条件，他们基本达成了一致：

[T]wo conditions must be satisfied for an intuitive judgment (recognition) to be genuinely skilled: First the environment must provide adequately valid cues to the nature of the situation. Second, people must have an opportunity to learn the relevant cues.

要真正熟练地运用直觉判断（识别），必须满足两个条件：首先，环境必须提供足够有效的线索来表明情况的性质；其次，人们必须有机会学习相关的线索。

Expert judgment tends to do more poorly than statistical approaches when the power of prediction comes from combining a lot of different cues that are each individually weak. “Where simple and valid cues exist, humans will find them if they are given sufficient experience and enough rapid feedback to do so,” Klein and Kahneman write. “Statistical analysis is more likely to identify weakly valid cues, and a prediction algorithm will maintain above-chance accuracy by using such cues consistently.” In other words, when there are stable, highly predictive features of the environment when making a decision, expert intuition tends to do fairly well. In contrast, when making sound decisions requires consistently adding up a lot of features that are only poorly correlated with outcomes, simple rules tend to do better.

当预测能力来源于大量单独来看效力较弱的不同线索的组合时，专家判断往往不如统计方法有效。“如果存在简单有效的线索，只要给予足够的经验和及时的反馈，人类就能找到它们，”克莱因和卡尼曼写道。“统计分析更有可能识别出效力较弱的线索，而预测算法通过持续使用这些线索，就能保持高于随机水平的准确率。”换句话说，当决策过程中环境中存在稳定且高度可预测的特征时，专家直觉往往表现良好。相反，当做出合理的决策需要持续地将大量与结果相关性较弱的特征叠加起来时，简单的规则往往更有效。

Of course, expertise does not need to be limited to intuitive judgments. Poker players develop a recognition-primed intuition, derived from the experience of playing tens of thousands of hands. But good players also know the math, able to overrule a tempting intuition if the odds simply don’t allow it. Recognizing where intuitions may be limited can be a powerful advantage for a genuine expert who wants an edge over her competition, as she can appropriately defer to the data when that makes sense. Today bank loans are given out based on actuarial formulas, not the intuitions of lenders, and the banking profession is better for it. Using formulas hasn’t removed the need for loan officers, but it has reduced a potential source of bias and error in the bank’s policies.

当然，专业知识并非仅限于直觉判断。扑克玩家通过数万手牌的经验，培养出一种基于识别的直觉。但优秀的玩家也精通数学，能够在概率不允许的情况下，摒弃诱人的直觉。对于真正想要超越竞争对手的专家而言，认识到直觉的局限性至关重要，因为她可以在必要时恰当地运用数据。如今，银行贷款的发放依据的是精算公式，而非贷款人的直觉，这对银行业大有裨益。使用公式并没有完全取代信贷员，但它确实减少了银行政策中潜在的偏见和误差来源。

Can We Tame Wicked Learning Environments?

我们能否驯服棘手的学习环境？

Poker, while possessing greater uncertainty than chess or checkers, nonetheless has many of the features that Klein and Kahneman argue make for a learner-friendly environment. Cues are highly valid, feedback is instantaneous, and we have strong mathematical theories for interpreting outcomes. Most of the skills we’d like to master are not nearly so favorable. Many of us are in the situation more closely studied by Meehl, where a lifetime of experience has led to considerable confidence, but lackluster predictive power. Given this contrast, it might be worth asking whether our practice can be made a little bit more like poker and a little bit less like professionals in Meehl’s studies.

虽然扑克比国际象棋或跳棋更具不确定性，但它仍然具备克莱因和卡尼曼所认为的有利于学习者发展的许多特征。提示信息高度有效，反馈即时，而且我们拥有强大的数学理论来解释结果。我们想要掌握的大多数技能远没有这么有利。我们中的许多人都处于米尔研究的那种情况：毕生的经验带来了相当的自信，但却缺乏预测能力。鉴于这种对比，或许值得思考的是，我们的练习能否更接近扑克，而减少一些米尔研究中职业选手的练习方式。

Predicting the future of major political events is certainly a task with a wickedly difficult learning environment. Events have complex causes—no single cause or factor is sufficient to explain what happens. History doesn’t repeat itself—there’s no chance to experience the same situation, multiple times, learning from our mistakes. Small changes can amplify to big effects. Who could have predicted that a Tunisian fruit vendor’s act of protest would trigger the Arab Spring? Or that a viral outbreak in Wuhan, China, would lead to American high school students taking their exams at home a year later? Despite the difficulties, prediction is also incredibly important. Politicians, business leaders, stock traders, and pundits all depend on being able to see the future a little more clearly.

预测重大政治事件的未来无疑是一项极其艰巨的任务，其学习环境极其复杂。事件的成因错综复杂——没有任何单一的原因或因素足以解释事件的发生。历史不会重演——我们不可能多次经历相同的情况，从中吸取教训。微小的变化也可能引发巨大的影响。谁能预料到，一位突尼斯水果小贩的抗议行为竟会引发阿拉伯之春？又有谁能预料到，中国武汉爆发的一场病毒疫情，竟会导致一年后美国高中生在家参加考试？尽管困难重重，预测仍然至关重要。政治家、商界领袖、股票交易员和评论员都依赖于对未来的更清晰的洞察。

Given this immense importance, but fiendish difficulty, how well do experts do? This was the question posed by psychologist Philip Tetlock in his decade-spanning Expert Political Judgment Project. Experts of various stripes were asked to participate, offering to rate the probability of various events (that had yet to happen): the fall of apartheid in South Africa, the dissolution of the Soviet Union, or whether the province of Quebec would separate from Canada. Experts did manage to do better than chance, but just barely. While expertise conferred enormous confidence, that self-assuredness did not translate into more accurate predictions. Tetlock writes that there was “ a curious inverse relationship between how well forecasters thought they were doing and how well they did.” Consistent with other research on expertise under uncertainty, experts performed better than novices (they impressively beat psychology undergraduates at the University of California, Berkeley), but decidedly failed against simple models that extrapolated past trends. Experts in Tetlock’s study even managed to underperform compared to smart nonexperts who were answering questions outside their field.

鉴于政治判断的重要性和难度之大，专家们的表现究竟如何？心理学家菲利普·泰特洛克在其历时十年的“专家政治判断项目”中提出了这个问题。该项目邀请各领域的专家参与，让他们对一些尚未发生的事件的概率进行评估，例如南非种族隔离制度的垮台、苏联的解体，以及魁北克省是否会脱离加拿大。专家们的表现确实优于随机猜测，但也只是略胜一筹。虽然专业知识赋予了专家极大的自信，但这种自信并未转化为更准确的预测。泰特洛克写道：“预测者自认为的预测能力与实际预测能力之间存在一种奇特的反比关系。” 与其他关于不确定性下专业知识的研究一致，专家的表现优于新手（他们甚至在加州大学伯克利分校的心理学本科生中表现出色），但与那些基于过去趋势进行推断的简单模型相比，他们的预测能力明显不足。 Tetlock 的研究中，专家们的表现甚至不如那些回答自己领域之外问题的聪明的非专家。

Although the typical expert didn’t score much better than chance, Tetlock was able to identify subsets of forecasters who managed to make surprisingly good predictions. In particular, a major difference between the good forecasters and the lousy ones was how able they were to integrate multiple, conflicting perspectives. Bad forecasters tended to fit every situation into a single, overarching worldview. This confidence and coherence may help in writing forceful opinion essays and well-cited academic papers, but it tends to do poorly when trying to grapple with the complexity of the real world. Good forecasters, in contrast, tended to be more like the experts Harry Truman complained about when he said he was tired of “ one-handed economists”—people who constantly said, “Well, on the one hand . . .” That equivocation may be annoying, but it resulted in those forecasters being better able to hedge diverse perspectives and resulted in more accurate forecasts. While intellectual confidence may attract followers, it appears intellectual humility is better associated with being right about future events.

尽管普通专家的预测准确率并不比随机猜测高多少，但泰特洛克能够识别出一部分预测者，他们的预测准确率出乎意料地高。尤其值得注意的是，优秀预测者和糟糕预测者之间的一个主要区别在于他们整合多种相互矛盾的观点的能力。糟糕的预测者倾向于将所有情况都套入单一的、包罗万象的世界观中。这种自信和逻辑性或许有助于撰写强有力的评论文章和被广泛引用的学术论文，但在试图应对现实世界的复杂性时却往往表现不佳。相比之下，优秀的预测者更像是哈里·杜鲁门抱怨的那种“单手经济学家”——他们总是说“嗯，一方面……”。这种模棱两可的表达方式或许令人恼火，但却使这些预测者能够更好地权衡各种不同的观点，从而做出更准确的预测。虽然知识上的自信可能会吸引追随者，但似乎知识上的谦逊与对未来事件的正确预测更为相关。

Building on his research on expert political judgment, Tetlock wanted to see if good forecasters could be identified and trained. Competing in a massively funded forecasting tournament put on by the Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity (IARPA) to find better ways to improve the political predictions of the United States intelligence community, Tetlock’s superforecasting team managed to beat the control group by 60 to 78 percent, even out-predicting teams that had access to classified data. Throughout his project, Tetlock identified a few strategies that allowed his forecasters to deliver useful predictions:

基于他对专家政治判断的研究，泰特洛克希望探究能否识别并培养优秀的预测者。为了寻找提升美国情报界政治预测能力的更佳方法，泰特洛克带领他的超级预测团队参加了由美国情报高级研究计划署（IARPA）举办的一项资金雄厚的预测竞赛。该竞赛旨在考察参赛团队的表现，最终以60%至78%的准确率击败了对照组，甚至超越了那些能够获取机密数据的团队。在整个项目过程中，泰特洛克总结出了一些策略，这些策略能够帮助他的预测者做出有效的预测：

  1. Break larger judgments into smaller ones. Intuitions often work by swapping the question being asked with a similar-sounding question that’s easier to answer. Good forecasters resisted this temptation by breaking it down into smaller parts. When asked to predict the detection of a radioactive poison in Palestinian politician Yasser Arafat’s remains, a naive forecaster might substitute that with her opinion on the likelihood that he was poisoned by Israeli spies. However, a smart forecaster would begin by breaking it down into parts: How does the poison decay? How likely would it be to be detected after many years? What are the possible ways it could be found in his body? By dissolving a complex question into multiple parts, good forecasters resisted the temptation to swap the question with one that “feels right.”
    将较大的判断分解成较小的判断。直觉常常会通过用一个听起来相似但更容易回答的问题来代替实际提出的问题。优秀的预测者会通过将其分解成更小的部分来抵制这种诱惑。例如，当被问及是否会在巴勒斯坦政治家亚西尔·阿拉法特的遗体中检测到放射性毒物时，一个缺乏经验的预测者可能会用她认为阿拉法特是被以色列间谍毒害的可能性来代替。然而，一个聪明的预测者会首先将问题分解成几个部分：毒物是如何衰变的？多年后被检测到的可能性有多大？有哪些可能的途径可以在他的体内找到毒物？通过将复杂的问题分解成多个部分，优秀的预测者抵制住了用一个“感觉对了”的问题来代替实际问题的诱惑。
  2. Make use of base rates. A major reason simple formulas exceed the power of human intuitions is that people overweight the presence of highly vivid information, and comparably neglect the more mundane cues. Tetlock’s superforecasters worked against that tendency by explicitly trying to figure out the overall probability for events of a similar type. How often do military coups succeed? How often does the NASDAQ close at a higher value one year later? By comparing to common reference classes, we ensure our answers start out in the right ballpark before we make finer adjustments.
    利用基准概率。简单公式之所以胜过人类直觉，一个主要原因是人们过分重视生动鲜明的信息，而相对忽略了较为平凡的线索。泰特洛克的超级预测者们正是通过明确地计算类似事件的总体概率来克服这种倾向。军事政变成功的概率是多少？纳斯达克指数一年后收盘价高于年初的概率是多少？通过与常见的参考类别进行比较，我们可以确保在进行更精细的调整之前，答案就已经处于正确的范围内。
  3. Form discussion groups for constructive disagreement. Tetlock found that teams of forecasters did better than those alone. In particular, when groups of people are allowed to debate and share information, it is possible to aggregate more perspectives and reduce leaping to conclusions from a single viewpoint.
    组建讨论小组以促进建设性分歧。泰特洛克发现，预测团队的表现优于单打独斗。尤其重要的是，当允许群体成员进行辩论和信息共享时，就有可能汇集更多观点，并减少从单一视角仓促下结论的情况。
  4. Keep score and calibrate. Predicting on a precise probability scale is unnatural. Even for pundits who regularly make predictions, it can still be unusual to make claims about the future with a percentage likelihood attached. Tetlock draws an illustrative comparison: “Imagine a world in which people love to run, but they have no idea how fast the average person runs, or how fast the best could run, because runners have never agreed to basic ground rules—stay on the track, begin the race when the gun is fired, end it after a specified distance—and there are no independent race officials and timekeepers measuring results. How likely is it that running times are improving in this world? Not very.” Only by escaping the vague verbiage of typical pronouncements can forecasters gain valuable feedback and calibrate future decisions.
    记录并校准。用精确的概率尺度进行预测是不自然的。即使是经常做预测的评论员，用百分比概率来断言未来也仍然很不寻常。泰特洛克举了一个形象的例子：“想象一下，在一个人们热爱跑步的世界里，他们不知道普通人跑得有多快，也不知道最优秀的人能跑多快，因为跑者们从未就基本规则达成一致——留在跑道上，鸣枪起跑，跑完规定的距离——而且也没有独立的赛事官员和计时员来测量成绩。在这个世界里，跑步成绩提高的可能性有多大？微乎其微。” 只有摆脱典型预测中模糊不清的措辞，预测者才能获得宝贵的反馈，并校准未来的决策。

Tetlock’s superforecasters are not prophets. Even good forecasters can’t predict much a decade out. The world may simply be too unpredictable for learning to occur, even with enhanced feedback and a disciplined method for avoiding intuitive overconfidence. However, Tetlock’s experiment suggests that we may be able to partly tame some of the wickedness of many learning environments, allowing us to develop genuine, if imperfect, expertise.

泰特洛克的超级预测者并非先知。即使是优秀的预测者，也无法准确预测十年后的情况。世界或许太过变幻莫测，即便有了更完善的反馈机制和避免过度自信的严谨方法，学习也难以发生。然而，泰特洛克的实验表明，我们或许能够部分地驯服许多学习环境中的某些弊端，从而发展出真正意义上的、即便并不完美的专业知识。

Strategies for Learning Under Uncertainty

不确定性下的学习策略

Raw experience doesn’t guarantee genuine expertise. Even the relatively learner-friendly environment of a poker game can lead to superstitions and bad judgments if it isn’t properly disciplined with a good understanding of probability and calibrated feedback. In less precise domains, the result can be disastrous. Despite decades of hands-on experience, so-called experts can fail to outperform simple tallies. Nonetheless, as Tetlock’s forecasting experiments indicate, the situation is not hopeless. We can think and decide better, provided we adopt the right approach. Let’s look at four different strategies for learning better under uncertainty.

经验本身并不能保证真正的专业技能。即使是扑克这种相对容易上手的游戏环境，如果缺乏对概率的深刻理解和精准的反馈，也可能导致迷信和错误的判断。在精度较低的领域，后果可能不堪设想。即便拥有数十年的实战经验，所谓的专家也可能胜过简单的统计方法。然而，正如泰特洛克的预测实验所表明的那样，情况并非毫无希望。只要我们采取正确的方法，就能更好地思考和决策。接下来，我们将探讨四种在不确定性下更好地学习的策略。

Strategy #1: Use a Model

策略一：使用模型

The most obvious strategy for avoiding the weaknesses of intuitive judgment is simply not to use it. There’s no point feeling out whether a bet seems appropriately sized or not when you can simply calculate the odds of making your hand, and compare it to the odds needed to bet based on the size of the pot. Similarly, in many professional domains, our expertise would likely be enhanced if we could substitute intuitive guessing for models based on statistics. The models don’t need to be complicated. Counting the factors for or against a decision isn’t complicated, but it often outperforms subjective judgment. Put the information into a spreadsheet and you can easily get a weighted sum for the best fit to the data.

避免直觉判断缺陷最显而易见的策略就是干脆不用它。与其凭感觉判断下注金额是否合适，不如直接计算出成牌的概率，然后根据底池大小计算出合适的下注概率。同样地，在许多专业领域，如果我们能用基于统计的模型来代替直觉猜测，我们的专业水平很可能会得到提升。这些模型不必复杂。计算支持或反对某个决策的因素并不复杂，但通常比主观判断更有效。把这些信息输入电子表格，就能轻松得到加权总和，从而找到最符合数据的模型。

Even if you don’t use the model as the final arbiter of your decisions, it can still provide a good starting point for further analysis. As mentioned, human intuition tends to grasp on to rare features of the environment but often fails to appropriately aggregate lots of weakly predictive information. A model, then, can do the work of getting you a good starting point as a guess, which you can adjust upward or downward if you believe you have additional information that could be relevant.

即使您不将模型作为最终决策依据，它仍然可以为进一步分析提供良好的起点。如前所述，人类直觉往往能够把握环境中的罕见特征，但常常无法恰当地整合大量预测力较弱的信息。因此，模型可以为您提供一个良好的初始估计值，如果您认为掌握了其他相关信息，则可以对其进行向上或向下调整。

Strategy #2: Get More Than Just Outcome Feedback

策略二：获取的不仅仅是结果反馈

Outcome feedback is often not enough to develop accurate intuitions. The difference between a bet that is 55 percent in your favor, or against, may require hundreds of hands before the correct choice becomes obvious. However, such a slight edge is not inconsequential—it can be the difference between a winning and losing poker player in the long run. Similarly, the outcome feedback in many professions is spotty. Hiring managers pat themselves on the back for the great talent they scouted out. But how often do those same managers reflect on the gems they turned away after a lackluster interview? Research shows that simply providing forecasters with outcome feedback is not sufficient to improve performance—in one experiment, people even got worse after more experience.

结果反馈往往不足以培养准确的直觉。一场胜率55%的赌注，你可能需要玩上数百局才能看出哪局才是赢家。然而，这种微小的优势并非无关紧要——从长远来看，它可能决定扑克玩家的胜负。同样，许多行业的结果反馈也存在不足。招聘经理们会为自己发掘到的优秀人才而沾沾自喜。但是，他们又有多少次会反思那些因为面试表现平平而被他们拒之门外的人才呢？研究表明，仅仅向预测人员提供结果反馈并不足以提高他们的绩效——在一项实验中，人们的经验越丰富，绩效反而越差。

To improve, we need to enhance the quality of our feedback. That starts by keeping track of our decisions, so our fallible memories can’t distort what actually happened. Next, we need to calibrate our confidence. Tetlock’s forecasters were judged not just on the directionality of their decisions (that is, did the things they thought would happen in fact happen more often than not?) but also on how appropriately confident they were (for example, did the category of events they thought would occur with 99 percent probability actually occur 99 percent of the time?). Whether it’s predicting patient outcomes, future sales, or world events, getting feedback on our calibration matters because overconfidence can lead to decisions that don’t leave room for error in the presence of future mistakes.

为了改进，我们需要提升反馈的质量。首先，我们要记录自己的决策，以免记忆力衰退扭曲事实。其次，我们需要校准自己的信心。泰特洛克的预测员不仅要根据决策的方向性（即，他们预测的事情是否经常发生？）来评判，还要根据他们的信心是否恰当（例如，他们认为有99%概率发生的事件类别是否真的有99%的概率发生？）。无论是预测患者预后、未来销售额还是世界大事，获得关于信心校准的反馈都至关重要，因为过度自信会导致决策过于保守，无法在未来出现错误时留有余地。

Strategy #3: Build a Brain Trust

策略三：建立智囊团

More minds are better than one. Joining into groups that allow for friendly debate has two distinct advantages in improving the quality of your decisions. The first is that it allows you to aggregate more information. Francis Galton first attested the power of this effect when he observed a guessing game to estimate the weight of an ox at a county fair. None of the people guessing got the right answer, but the average of their guesses was nearly perfect. Holding debates allows you to put together information you might not have initially considered when making a decision. The second advantage is that debate sharpens your thinking. The sociologists Dan Sperber and Hugo Mercier have argued that human reasoning itself is adapted more for the social act of justifying one’s actions and beliefs than for the individual art of finding true answers to problems. In an intriguing experiment, psychologists David Moshman and Molly Geil gave individuals the Wason four-card task discussed in chapter 6 . Consistent with the tricky nature of the task, only 9 percent of participants got the question right. Things changed, however, when groups were allowed to discuss the question together. The success rate for small groups jumped to 75 percent. Were discussion simply a process of averaging, as with Galton’s ox weighers, this would mean that after debate the wrong answer that was picked most often would eventually win out. Placing the question in the context of a group, the people who found the correct solution could usually convince others, even if they were in the minority. Interestingly, in the experiment by Moshman and Geil, some groups arrived at the correct answer even when no individual member had initially suggested it. As the authors report, “[these] results suggest that levels of understanding that are difficult to elicit in situations of individual performance may emerge in the context of collaborative reasoning.”

集思广益胜过单打独斗。参与能够进行友好辩论的小组讨论，在提升决策质量方面具有两大显著优势。首先，它能让你汇集更多信息。弗朗西斯·高尔顿在一次乡村集市上观察人们猜测牛的重量时，首次证实了这种效应。虽然没有人猜对，但他们猜测的平均值却接近完美。通过辩论，你可以整合一些在做决定时可能并未考虑到的信息。其次，辩论能够提升你的思维能力。社会学家丹·斯珀伯和雨果·梅西耶认为，人类的推理能力更适应于为自己的行动和信念辩护的社会行为，而非寻找问题正确答案的个人艺术。在一项引人入胜的实验中，心理学家大卫·莫什曼和莫莉·盖尔让参与者完成第六章讨论过的沃森四卡片任务。正如该任务本身的难度所表明的那样，只有9%的参与者答对了问题。然而，当允许小组共同讨论问题时，情况发生了变化。小组的成功率跃升至75%。如果讨论仅仅是像高尔顿的牛秤那样取平均值，那就意味着经过辩论，被选次数最多的错误答案最终会胜出。但如果将问题置于小组讨论的情境中，找到正确答案的人通常能够说服其他人，即使他们只占少数。有趣的是，在莫什曼和盖尔的实验中，有些小组甚至在没有任何成员最初提出正确答案的情况下，最终也得出了正确答案。正如作者所言，“这些结果表明，在个人表现情境下难以获得的理解水平，可能会在协作推理的情境中涌现。”

While discussion doesn’t guarantee a convergence to the correct answer—ideology, groupthink, and domineering group members can derail debate—it’s more likely than when we think entirely in isolation. By forming a group of fellow practitioners, from different perspectives, to hash over tough problems, you’ll be more likely to embody the nimble, multiperspective thinking style Tetlock found was key to his successful forecaster’s accurate judgment.

虽然讨论并不能保证一定能得出正确答案——意识形态、群体思维和强势的群体成员都可能使辩论偏离正轨——但它比我们完全孤立地思考更有可能得出正确答案。通过组建一个由不同视角的同行组成的团队，共同探讨棘手的问题，你更有可能培养出泰特洛克发现的那种灵活、多角度的思维方式，而这种方式正是他那位成功的预测者做出准确判断的关键。

Strategy #4: Know When (and When Not) to Trust Your Gut

策略四：知道何时（以及何时不）相信你的直觉

Perhaps the most valuable lesson of the research on intuition is to delineate the situations where it is likely to succeed, and those places where it is likely to be overconfident. Intuition works best when discernible cues reliably predict events, and performers have the ability to learn from quick feedback. When these favorable conditions are absent, we need to proceed more cautiously. Genuine expertise here requires going beyond gut feelings and relying more on simple estimates based on past data and explicit reasoning that can avoid the tempting bait-and-swap maneuver our intuition often uses to change a hard question into an easy one.

或许，关于直觉研究最有价值的启示在于，要明确直觉在哪些情况下容易奏效，在哪些情况下容易过度自信。当可辨别的线索能够可靠地预测事件，且参与者能够从快速反馈中学习时，直觉最为有效。当这些有利条件缺失时，我们需要更加谨慎行事。真正的专业知识需要超越直觉，更多地依赖基于过往数据的简单估算和明确的推理，从而避免直觉经常使用的诱饵式策略——将难题转化为难题。

Experience and Reality

经验与现实

Feedback plays a role in calibrating our judgments. But it plays an even more important role in many dynamic skills. Interacting with the environment, both physical and social, is an essential part of ensuring that the practice we engage in ends up mastering the skills that are actually used in real practice.

反馈在校准我们的判断中发挥着作用。但它在许多动态技能的培养中扮演着更为重要的角色。与环境（包括物理环境和社会环境）的互动，是确保我们最终能够掌握实际应用中所需技能的关键所在。

# ↩

Chapter 10

第十章

Practice Must Meet Reality

实践必须符合现实

We learn how to behave as lawyers, soldiers, merchants or what not by being them. Life, not the parson, teaches conduct.

我们通过亲身经历，学习如何像律师、士兵、商人或其他任何职业那样行事。是生活，而非牧师，教会我们为人处世之道。

—Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr.

—小奥利弗·温德尔·霍姆斯

  • How important is realistic practice?
    实际练习有多重要？
  • Why do classroom skills often fail to translate to real-life proficiency?
    为什么课堂上学到的技能往往无法转化为现实生活中的实际能力？
  • How can you gain access to the situations where a skill is actually used?
    如何才能接触到实际运用某项技能的情境？

F og rolled in from the hills surrounding Los Rodeos Airport on the island of Tenerife in the late afternoon of March 27, 1977. Dutch pilot Jacob Veldhuyzen van Zanten was eager to get back in the air. His stop at Los Rodeos had not been scheduled. The original destination was Gran Canaria, part of the Canary Islands, a Spanish territory located just off the coast of Morocco. Canarian separatists had detonated a bomb at Gran Canaria Airport, diverting all traffic to the nearby island of Tenerife. After hours of waiting, Gran Canaria Airport reopened and Veldhuyzen van Zanten moved his plane onto the runway to take off and resume their journey.

1977年3月27日下午，浓雾从特内里费岛洛斯罗德奥斯机场周围的山丘涌来。荷兰飞行员雅各布·维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕急切地想要重返蓝天。他在洛斯罗德奥斯的停留并非事先安排。他原本的目的地是加那利群岛中的大加那利岛，加那利群岛是西班牙的海外领地，位于摩洛哥海岸附近。加那利群岛的分离主义分子在大加那利岛机场引爆了一枚炸弹，导致所有航班都改道飞往附近的特内里费岛。经过数小时的等待，大加那利岛机场重新开放，维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕将飞机移上跑道，准备起飞，继续他们的旅程。

The Dutch pilot pulled on the throttle when his first officer reminded him that they had not yet been given clearance for takeoff. “No, I know that” was his frustrated reply. The fog might thicken at any moment, putting visibility below the mandated minimum for takeoff, potentially keeping Veldhuyzen van Zanten, his crew, and all 235 passengers stuck on Tenerife overnight. “ Go ahead, ask,” he ordered. The first officer radioed the tower saying that they were “ready for takeoff.” The traffic control tower radioed back, “OK . . . stand by for takeoff, I will call you.” At this exact moment, another flight, Pan Am 1736, was using the same radio frequency to respond to the tower, “No . . . uh, we’re still taxiing down the runway.” As a result, the cockpit of the Dutch flight heard only “OK” from the traffic control tower followed by a squelch of interference. Mistakenly believing they had been authorized, an impatient Veldhuyzen van Zanten resumed his acceleration down the runway. By the time he spotted the taxiing Boeing 747 he was going too fast to stop. He pulled hard to lift his plane into the sky, scraping the tail along the tarmac. But his last-second maneuver wasn’t enough. The two planes collided, killing 583 people. To this day, it remains the worst aviation accident in history.

当副驾驶提醒他尚未获得起飞许可时，荷兰飞行员拉起了油门。“不，我知道。”他沮丧地回答道。雾随时可能加浓，能见度可能低于起飞的最低标准，这意味着维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕、他的机组人员以及所有235名乘客可能要在特内里费岛滞留一夜。“去问问吧。”他命令道。副驾驶通过无线电向塔台报告说他们“准备起飞”。塔台回复道：“好的……准备起飞，我会通知你们。”就在同一时刻，另一架航班，泛美航空1736号，正在使用同一无线电频率回复塔台：“不……呃，我们还在跑道上滑行。”结果，荷兰航班的驾驶舱只听到塔台的“好的”，随后便是一阵干扰声。范赞滕误以为已获得许可，急躁的他继续加速滑行。当他发现正在滑行的波音747时，速度已经太快，无法刹车。他猛拉油门，试图让飞机升空，机尾擦过跑道。但他最后一刻的尝试还是失败了。两架飞机相撞，造成583人死亡。时至今日，这仍然是历史上最严重的航空事故。

The disaster at Tenerife was a tragedy. But to learn from it, we first need to consider a different question: Why is flying in a plane generally so safe? Catastrophic accidents involving planes absorb our attention, in part, because flying is so routine. Per mile traveled, you’re far more likely to be harmed while driving a car, taking a bus, or riding a train. Flying wasn’t always this way. The early pilots faced grave danger as they took to the skies. Our safety today owes much to the quality of pilot training, and the man who found the way to teach it.

特内里费岛的空难是一场悲剧。但要从中吸取教训，我们首先需要思考另一个问题：为什么乘坐飞机通常如此安全？涉及飞机的灾难性事故之所以如此引人注目，部分原因在于飞行已成为一种日常活动。按行驶里程计算，开车、乘坐公共汽车或火车时受伤的概率要高得多。但飞行并非一直如此安全。早期的飞行员在翱翔蓝天时面临着巨大的危险。我们今天的安全很大程度上要归功于高质量的飞行员培训，以及发明这种培训方法的先驱者。

The Man Who Taught the World to Fly

教会世界飞翔的人

For good or ill, many new technologies prove themselves on the battlefield. The invention of the stirrup transformed European society, enabling aristocratic knights to dominate over a peasant infantry. Gunpowder cannons allowed the Ottomans to sack Constantinople, ending the reign of the last Roman emperor, fifteen hundred years after the death of Julius Caesar. The airplane was no exception. From the moment of its invention, a new arms race began over who would dominate the sky. The world would not have to wait long to see the new technology in action. Just over a decade after Orville and Wilbur Wright’s legendary flight, the Great War in Europe had begun.

无论好坏，许多新技术都在战场上证明了自己的价值。马镫的发明改变了欧洲社会，使贵族骑士能够凌驾于农民步兵之上。火药大炮使奥斯曼帝国攻陷君士坦丁堡，终结了罗马末代皇帝的统治，而此时距离尤利乌斯·凯撒去世已过去了一千五百年。飞机也不例外。从发明之日起，一场争夺天空霸权的军备竞赛便拉开了帷幕。世界无需等待太久便能亲眼目睹这项新技术的实际应用。在奥维尔和威尔伯·莱特兄弟完成传奇飞行仅仅十余年后，欧洲爆发了第一次世界大战。

England had long relied on its powerful navy to protect its shores and control overseas colonies. Yet in the battle for the skies, they were losing. Some of this disadvantage was technical. Germany had gained the upper hand with the introduction of Anthony Fokker’s Eindecker plane, whose innovative synchronization gear enabled a pilot to fire a machine gun directly through the spinning propeller blades. Earlier attempts to mount guns on the wings were wildly inaccurate, and armor plating designed to protect the propeller from the hail of bullets exposed the pilot to the risks of ricochet. The new invention allowed planes to serve not only as tools for reconnaissance but also as weapons in their own right. Aerial dogfighting became a necessity to take command of the skies, and the British were far behind. By 1916, over a third of pilots in the Royal Flying Corps were lost, one of the highest casualty rates in all the British armed forces.

英国长期以来依靠其强大的海军来保卫海岸线和控制海外殖民地。然而，在制空权的争夺战中，他们却节节败退。部分劣势源于技术层面。德国凭借安东尼·福克的单翼飞机（Eindecker）取得了优势，该飞机创新的同步装置使飞行员能够直接透过旋转的螺旋桨叶片射击机枪。此前尝试在机翼上安装机枪的尝试精度极低，而旨在保护螺旋桨免受弹雨侵袭的装甲板却使飞行员面临跳弹的风险。这项新发明使飞机不仅可以作为侦察工具，还能成为独立的武器。空中缠斗成为夺取制空权的必要手段，而英国在这方面远远落后。到1916年，英国皇家飞行队超过三分之一的飞行员阵亡，这是英国所有武装部队中伤亡率最高的部队之一。

Technical superiority was only a small part of Germany’s advantage. The greater contributor to Britain’s shortfall was lousy training. The curriculum, formulated during peacetime, emphasized the mechanical operation of the aircraft, its construction, and the theory of flight. In contrast, experience actually flying the plane was often sorely lacking. Instructors would take students up for test flights to show the operation of the controls. When a second seat was lacking, this often meant the student had to hold on to the wing spars during the demonstration. In theory, when the student was deemed ready, the two would switch places, with the pupil taking the pilot’s seat. In practice, however, many instructors were reluctant to allow the student to fly the plane, fearing a crash. The result was that many pilots were sent to the front lines never having actually flown the planes they were certified to operate. During April 1916 alone, Hugh Trenchard, commander of the Royal Flying Corps, wrote six letters to the Air Ministry and War Office to complain about the poor training. Another officer wrote in early 1916 that he had just received his third pilot that week who had “ never flown any of the type of aircraft I have in this country.” Many new recruits died in their first flights.

技术优势只是德国优势的一小部分。英国战败的主要原因是糟糕的训练。和平时期制定的课程侧重于飞机的机械操作、构造和飞行理论。相比之下，实际飞行经验却严重不足。教官会带学生进行试飞，演示操纵装置的操作。如果缺少第二个座位，学生往往只能在演示过程中抓住机翼翼梁。理论上，当学生被认为准备就绪时，两人会交换位置，由学生坐上驾驶座。然而，实际上，许多教官不愿让学生驾驶飞机，担心发生坠机事故。结果是，许多飞行员被派往前线时，从未真正驾驶过他们获得驾驶资格的飞机。仅在1916年4月，皇家飞行队指挥官休·特伦查德就曾六次致信空军部和陆军部，抱怨训练不足的问题。另一位军官在1916年初写道，他那周刚刚接收了第三位飞行员，这位飞行员“从未驾驶过我国现有的任何一种飞机”。许多新兵在首次飞行中丧生。

A fierce critic of this situation was Major Robert Smith-Barry. A survivor of a crash in 1914 that broke both his legs and left him with a permanent limp, he was an advocate for the undertrained pilots. “They’ve only seven hours flying sir—and it’s bloody murder,” he wrote in 1916. “ They’ve barely learned to fly, let alone fight.” Smith-Barry wrote a series of letters to Trenchard, complaining that with current training methods, the new recruits were little more than “ Fokker fodder.” An impatient Trenchard replied, “ [D]on’t worry us anymore with your complaints. If you think you can do better, go and do it,” putting Smith-Barry in charge of training at the facilities in Gosport.

罗伯特·史密斯-巴里少校对这种情况持强烈批评态度。1914年的一场坠机事故中，他双腿骨折，终身跛行，但他始终为训练不足的飞行员们奔走呼吁。“长官，他们只有七个小时的飞行时间——而且简直是折磨，”他在1916年写道，“他们几乎还没学会飞行，更别提战斗了。”史密斯-巴里给特伦查德写了一系列信件，抱怨说，按照当时的训练方法，新兵们只不过是“福克战斗机的炮灰”。不耐烦的特伦查德回复道：“别再用你的抱怨来烦我们了。如果你觉得自己能做得更好，那就去做吧。”随后，他任命史密斯-巴里负责戈斯波特训练基地的训练工作。

Smith-Barry radically redesigned the training program. He introduced dual-control systems that allowed pupils to steer the plane with backup controls for instructors to use in emergencies. Instead of smooth flying under ideal conditions, instructors deliberately put the plane in spins or dives and forced pupils to recover. In-flight communication was facilitated by the “Gosport tube”—a hose that connected student headphones to a funnel strapped over the instructor’s mouth. This enabled the trainers to provide instructions over the otherwise deafening noise of the aircraft. Smith-Barry also revised the classroom curriculum, cutting down on theoretical lessons in favor of more flying time. Smith-Barry believed students should “ always be in the pilot’s seat.” The best way to learn to fly a plane was by flying one, and Smith-Barry had found the means for teaching it safely.

史密斯-巴里彻底重新设计了飞行训练计划。他引入了双控制系统，使学员能够操控飞机，同时教员在紧急情况下可以使用备用控制系统。教员不再让学员在理想条件下平稳飞行，而是故意让飞机进入螺旋或俯冲状态，迫使学员改出。飞行中的通讯通过“戈斯波特管”实现——这是一种连接学员耳机和教员嘴部导管的软管。这使得教员能够在原本震耳欲聋的飞机噪音中发出指令。史密斯-巴里还修订了课堂课程，减少了理论课时，增加了飞行时间。他认为学员应该“始终坐在驾驶座上”。学习驾驶飞机的最佳方法就是亲自驾驶，而史密斯-巴里找到了安全教学的方法。

Smith-Barry’s reforms were an amazing success. Prior to the Gosport system, nearly one in ten training flights ended in a crash. Smith-Barry reduced this to around 3 percent, while increasing the difficulty of the maneuvers being taught to students. Enhanced training led to greater survival rates by pilots. The offensive buildup in 1918 led to a 354 percent rise in the size of the aircraft fleet, but only a 65 percent rise in casualties. Combat flying had gotten safer, even as the British pushed the offensive into German territory. Accidents, when they did occur, were less severe. Prior to Smith-Barry’s training reforms, the “majority of crashes were fatal and the result of grievous pilot error,” historian Robert Morley documents. In contrast, later accidents “ occurred almost entirely during landings and tended to be nonfatal. In many cases, they were not severe enough to destroy the aircraft.”

史密斯-巴里改革取得了惊人的成功。在戈斯波特体系实施之前，近十分之一的训练飞行以坠机告终。史密斯-巴里将这一比例降低到3%左右，同时提高了学员所学飞行技巧的难度。强化训练提高了飞行员的生存率。1918年的攻势扩张导致飞机数量增长了354%，但伤亡人数仅增长了65%。即使英国将攻势推进到德国领土，战斗飞行也变得更加安全。即使发生事故，其严重程度也较低。历史学家罗伯特·莫利记录道，在史密斯-巴里改革训练之前，“大多数坠机事故都是致命的，并且是飞行员严重失误造成的”。相比之下，后来的事故“几乎全部发生在着陆过程中，而且往往不会造成人员伤亡。在许多情况下，事故的严重程度不足以摧毁飞机。”

Following the war, Smith-Barry’s reforms for pilot training were widely adopted throughout English-speaking countries. “ The dual-control aircraft and the pupil-first philosophy remain bedrock principles of both civilian and military pilot training to this day,” writes Morley. Despite his early annoyance with Smith-Barry, Trenchard later recognized his contributions to pilot training, calling Smith-Barry “ the man who taught the air forces of the world how to fly.”

战后，史密斯-巴里对飞行员训练的改革在英语国家得到广泛应用。“双座飞机和以学员为先的理念至今仍是民用和军用飞行员训练的基石原则，”莫利写道。尽管特伦查德早期对史密斯-巴里颇有微词，但他后来认可了史密斯-巴里对飞行员训练的贡献，称他为“教会世界各国空军如何飞行的人”。

The Aftermath of Tenerife

特内里费岛事件的后续影响

Steady improvements in both aircraft engineering and pilot training have made flying in a commercial jet one of the safest forms of travel. Yet these advances also meant that “ raw flying skill no longer played a significant part in aviation accidents,” write pilot and educator Timothy Mavin and professor Patrick Murray. At the time of the accident, Jacob Veldhuyzen van Zanten was the chief pilot instructor for KLM, with over eleven thousand hours of flight experience. In the immediate aftermath of the disaster, KLM executives even suggested tasking Veldhuyzen van Zanten with conducting the investigation, not realizing that it had been his flight that caused the collision.

飞机工程和飞行员培训的稳步提升，使得乘坐商用喷气式飞机成为最安全的出行方式之一。然而，飞行员兼教育家蒂莫西·马文和帕特里克·默里教授指出，这些进步也意味着“飞行技能本身在航空事故中不再起决定性作用”。事故发生时，雅各布·维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕是荷兰皇家航空公司的首席飞行教官，拥有超过11000小时的飞行经验。灾难发生后，荷兰皇家航空公司的高管甚至提议由维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕负责事故调查，却浑然不知正是他执飞的航班导致了这场碰撞。

Tenerife caused a shift in thinking about pilot training. Beyond individualistic pilot skill, training began to emphasize the interpersonal aspects of flying. Investigators placed the blame for the accident on communication failures. The Dutch copilot’s “ready for takeoff” and air traffic control’s reply, “OK,” were both nonstandard and ambiguous, leading to mutual misunderstanding. The Pan Am flight had failed to clear the runway at the exit indicated, leading to confusion about their location. Above all, the accident was blamed on Veldhuyzen van Zanten’s disastrous decision to take off without confirming clearance. Although the Dutch captain had maintained a collegial attitude with his crew, his authority within the company likely made it harder for the copilot to assert his doubts that they were clear to depart. Following the incident, pilot education stressed standardized communication protocols that left no room for misunderstanding and interpersonal training to encourage lower-ranking pilots to assert themselves when they perceived risks.

特内里费岛事故促使人们对飞行员培训的理念进行了转变。除了飞行员的个人技能之外，培训开始强调飞行中的人际交往能力。调查人员将事故归咎于沟通失误。荷兰副驾驶发出的“准备起飞”和空中交通管制员的回复“好的”都不符合标准且含义模糊，导致了双方的误解。泛美航空的航班未能按指示从跑道出口起飞，导致飞行员对自身位置产生困惑。最重要的是，事故被归咎于维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕在未确认起飞许可的情况下就起飞这一灾难性决定。尽管这位荷兰机长与机组人员保持着良好的合作关系，但他在公司内部的权威地位可能使得副驾驶更难表达自己对起飞许可的疑虑。事故发生后，飞行员培训强调标准化的沟通协议，以避免任何误解，并加强人际交往方面的培训，鼓励级别较低的飞行员在感知到风险时勇于表达自己的意见。

As Smith-Barry’s experience showed, piloting a plane is something you can really only learn in a cockpit, not a classroom. A chief reason for this is that piloting skills are dynamic—the thinking that operates when flying a plane is a constant dialogue between pilot and aircraft, one that cannot be effectively practiced in isolation. At the same time, the disaster at Tenerife shows the perils of training that omits essential elements of that interaction. Piloting a plane is not just the dialogue between man and machine, but between a pilot and the surrounding social environment. As Veldhuyzen van Zanten’s case illustrates, one can achieve high levels of proficiency operating an aircraft, and still have dangerous blind spots.

正如史密斯-巴里的经历所表明的那样，驾驶飞机这项技能只能在驾驶舱内学习，而无法在课堂上习得。主要原因在于，驾驶技能是动态的——驾驶飞机时，飞行员的思维是与飞机之间持续不断的对话，这种对话无法在孤立的环境中有效练习。同时，特内里费岛的空难也揭示了忽略这种互动关键要素的训练所带来的危险。驾驶飞机不仅是人与机器之间的对话，也是飞行员与周围社会环境之间的对话。正如维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕的案例所示，即使飞行员的驾驶技术非常精湛，仍然可能存在危险的盲区。

How Important Is Realistic Practice?

实际练习有多重要？

Realistic practice may be necessary for learning dynamic skills, but it doesn’t always come easily. Pilot instructors prior to Smith-Barry’s reforms might have been negligent, but they weren’t irrational. It must not have been comforting to hand the throttle to a student who had a one-in-ten chance of crashing the plane. Cost cannot be ignored either. Extensive classroom preparation may not have led to proficient pilots, but it did effectively ration scarce aircraft. None of these problems are limited to aviation. Doctors face the same dilemma. The lack of qualified medical personnel owes more to a shortage of residency slots in teaching hospitals than it does to a lack of seats in classroom auditoriums. In many countries, English proficiency is prized, but access to native speakers is hard to come by. The result is that the immersive strategy that works so well for toddlers is impractical for many language learners. Given that realistic practice is often dangerous, costly, or scarce, many researchers have sought to understand when it is necessary. One area that’s received considerable attention in aviation training is flight simulators.

实战练习对于学习动态技能或许必不可少，但并非总是唾手可得。史密斯-巴里改革之前的飞行教员或许存在疏忽，但并非不理智。把油门交给一个有十分之一概率坠机的学员，想必令人不安。成本问题也不容忽视。大量的课堂准备或许未能培养出熟练的飞行员，但却有效地分配了稀缺的飞机资源。这些问题并非航空业独有。医生也面临着同样的困境。合格医务人员的短缺，更多地源于教学医院住院医师名额的不足，而非教室座位的匮乏。在许多国家，英语水平备受重视，但接触到以英语为母语的人却并非易事。因此，对幼儿行之有效的沉浸式教学策略，对许多语言学习者而言却并不实用。鉴于实战练习往往存在危险、成本高昂或资源匮乏等问题，许多研究人员致力于探究何时才是进行实战练习的必要时机。飞行模拟器是航空培训领域备受关注的一个方面。

Flight simulators were invented shortly after the airplane was developed. The Antoinette trainer, an early model, was constructed with a barrel sawn in half lengthwise that students could sit in. Instructors would shake the plane to simulate flight and have the student respond by adjusting controls attached to pulleys. But the flight simulator didn’t take off as an industry until 1929, when Edward Link developed the Link Trainer. Concerned about the cost of flight instruction, Link developed the simulator using compressed air and bellows from his father’s factory. Link originally marketed the device as a coin-operated toy. It was only when the United States military realized its potential for training pilots and began buying the device by the thousands that simulators became big business. Today flight simulators are a multibillion-dollar industry, with realistic computer graphics, cockpit replicas, and motion controls.

飞行模拟器在飞机发明后不久便被发明出来。早期的安托瓦内特训练器（Antoinette trainer）是用一个纵向锯成两半的圆筒制成的，学生可以坐在里面。教员会摇晃这个圆筒来模拟飞行，学生则通过调整连接在滑轮上的控制装置来做出反应。但直到1929年，爱德华·林克（Edward Link）发明了林克训练器（Link Trainer）之后，飞行模拟器才真正发展成为一个产业。林克担心飞行训练的成本，于是利用他父亲工厂里的压缩空气和风箱制造了这款模拟器。林克最初将这款设备作为投币玩具进行销售。直到美国军方意识到它在飞行员训练方面的潜力，并开始大量采购，飞行模拟器才真正成为一项大生意。如今，飞行模拟器已发展成为一个价值数十亿美元的产业，拥有逼真的计算机图形、驾驶舱模型和运动控制系统。

How useful are flight simulators? Research paints a consistent picture. Simulators tend to do better than actual aircraft at the earliest stages of learning to fly. After some experience, time in a simulator is still helpful, but less so than additional time in the pilot’s seat. Given that a simulator is usually in the range of 5 to 20 percent of the cost of an actual aircraft, however, even the reduced efficiency can be cost-effective. In some studies, time spent in a simulator eventually becomes harmful, as students learn to rely on features of the simulator that aren’t present in an actual aircraft. Stanley Roscoe, a psychologist who specialized in applications of flight simulators to aviation training, hypothesized that the benefit of further simulator training would appear as a decelerating curve. Commenting on the state of simulators in 1971, he wrote that “the first hour of instruction in a ground trainer can save more than one hour in pre-solo flight training. The fifteenth hour in a ground trainer surely would not.”

飞行模拟器究竟有多大用处？研究结果一致表明，在飞行学习的初期阶段，模拟器的效果往往优于实际飞机。积累一定经验后，模拟器训练仍然有益，但其效果远不及在驾驶舱内进行更多练习。然而，考虑到模拟器的成本通常仅为实际飞机的5%到20%，即使效率有所降低，其成本效益仍然可观。一些研究表明，在模拟器上花费的时间最终反而会造成损害，因为学员会逐渐依赖模拟器中实际飞机所不具备的功能。专门研究飞行模拟器在航空训练中应用的心理学家斯坦利·罗斯科（Stanley Roscoe）曾提出假设：进一步的模拟器训练所带来的益处会呈现递减曲线。他在1971年评论模拟器的现状时写道：“在地面训练器上进行的第一小时训练可以节省单飞前训练的一个多小时。而第十五个小时的地面训练则肯定无法做到这一点。”

Follow-up research supports the overall shape of his curve, even if there are questions about the exact numbers. A 1990 meta-analysis by John Jacobs, Carolyn Prince, Robert Hays, and Eduardo Salas found that over 90 percent of the studies reviewed favored simulator-plus-aircraft training to aircraft-only training. Similarly, a 1998 review by Thomas Carretta and Ronald Dunlap found that simulators helped, but that this benefit diminished after twenty-five mock sorties. A 2005 analysis by Esa Rantanen and Donald Talleur found a similar curve, with the benefits of simulators being greater than equal time in the pilot seat for the first few hours, being less effective (but still helpful) after that, and eventually becoming unhelpful compared to time in the pilot seat.

后续研究支持他提出的曲线总体形状，尽管具体数值尚存疑问。1990年，约翰·雅各布斯、卡罗琳·普林斯、罗伯特·海斯和爱德华多·萨拉斯进行的一项荟萃分析发现，超过90%的受访研究表明，模拟器加飞机训练优于仅飞机训练。同样，1998年托马斯·卡雷塔和罗纳德·邓拉普的一项综述发现，模拟器确实有帮助，但这种益处在25次模拟飞行后会逐渐减弱。2005年埃萨·兰塔宁和唐纳德·塔勒的一项分析也发现了类似的曲线：模拟器的益处在最初几个小时内大于同等时间的实际飞行训练，之后效果有所下降（但仍然有帮助），最终与实际飞行训练相比，模拟器的益处会降低。

Why might simulated practice be more useful than a real plane? In the beginning, flying is overwhelming and stressful. The simplifications created by the simulator may make it easier to understand the basics of flying. Researchers William and Brian Moroney write, “Despite the emphasis on high fidelity and ‘realism,’ simulators are not realistic . In a sense, the lack of realism may contribute to their effectiveness.” Evidence for the beneficial effects of simplification for beginners comes from a 1990 study that trained landing procedures in a simulator. One group trained with crosswinds and one without. Despite the test occurring with crosswinds, it was the group that trained without them that actually performed better. It seems the distortion created by the crosswinds made it harder to understand how the controls influenced the motion of the plane.

为什么模拟飞行练习可能比驾驶真飞机更有用？飞行初期，飞行往往令人不知所措，压力巨大。模拟器的简化操作或许能帮助飞行员更容易地理解飞行的基本原理。研究人员威廉·莫罗尼和布莱恩·莫罗尼写道：“尽管模拟器强调高保真度和‘真实感’，但它们并不真实。从某种意义上说，这种不真实感或许正是其有效性的原因之一。”一项1990年的研究证实了简化操作对初学者的益处。该研究使用模拟器训练着陆程序，一组学员在侧风条件下进行训练，另一组则在没有侧风条件下进行训练。尽管测试是在侧风条件下进行的，但实际上表现更好的却是没有侧风的那组学员。看来，侧风造成的干扰使得学员更难理解操纵杆如何影响飞机的运动。

The kind of realism matters too. New pilots often want an experience that matches closely with being in the air, but researchers find that the functional correspondence between the simulator and the actual plane matters more. William and Brian Moroney write, “ Precise replication of the control, display, and environmental dynamics is based on the unsupported belief that higher fidelity simulation results in greater transfer of training from the simulator to the actual aircraft.” Instead of fancy graphics, what matters is that the information used to make decisions and the actions taken inside the simulator are analogous to those that should be made on a real plane.

真实感的程度也很重要。新飞行员通常希望获得与实际飞行高度接近的体验，但研究人员发现，模拟器与真实飞机之间的功能对应性更为重要。威廉·莫罗尼和布莱恩·莫罗尼写道：“精确复制控制、显示和环境动态是基于一种未经证实的信念，即更高保真度的模拟能够更好地将训练成果从模拟器迁移到实际飞机上。” 重要的不是花哨的画面，而是模拟器中用于决策的信息和采取的操作是否与在真实飞机上应该采取的操作类似。

As we’ve seen, however, flying a plane is more than just manipulating the controls. The surrounding social environment cannot be ignored. As hard as it is to simulate a mechanical plane, it is nearly impossible to simulate a workplace culture. Standard operating procedures can be taught, but how they are actually used is always a process that emerges organically from people practicing the craft. Becoming proficient requires navigating a social world that both facilitates learning and restricts access.

然而，正如我们所见，驾驶飞机不仅仅是操控飞机。周围的社会环境不容忽视。模拟一架机械飞机固然困难，但模拟一种工作场所文化几乎是不可能的。标准操作程序可以教授，但如何实际运用这些程序始终是一个在人们实践中自然而然形成的动态过程。要精通这项技能，就需要在一个既促进学习又限制学习机会的社会环境中游刃有余。

Situated Cognition and the Culture of Learning

情境认知与学习文化

Just as the aviation industry was awakening to the importance of broader interactions in the performance of piloting skill, some psychologists were beginning to question their discipline’s detachment from thinking in everyday life. Ulric Neisser, whose book Cognitive Psychology heralded the revolution in the new science of thinking, wrote a follow-up book, Cognition and Reality , attacking many of the tenets of the new approach to psychology. In particular, he was concerned that studies of problem solving and list learning in the rarefied air of the laboratory might be overlooking important aspects of real thinking. Situated cognition began as a movement focused on not just how people think as individuals, but how that thinking is constrained and facilitated by the physical and social world that surrounds them.

正当航空业逐渐意识到更广泛的互动对飞行员技能表现的重要性时，一些心理学家也开始质疑心理学与日常生活思维的脱节。乌尔里克·奈瑟的著作《认知心理学》预示着思维科学新领域的革命，随后他又撰写了续作《认知与现实》，对心理学新方法的诸多信条提出了质疑。他尤其担忧，在实验室这种与世隔绝的环境中对问题解决和列表学习的研究，可能会忽略真实思维的重要方面。情境认知运动由此兴起，其关注点不仅在于人们作为个体如何思考，更在于这种思考如何受到他们所处的物理和社会环境的制约和促进。

A straightforward example of situated cognition is learning to catch a fly baseball. The exact trajectory of the ball is difficult to compute. It requires understanding differential equations that take into account gravity, wind, and even the spin of the ball itself. Calculating exactly where the ball will land is a feat outside most human’s mental abilities. So how do we play baseball? The answer is that we can use a shortcut. By running after the ball and maintaining a constant angle between you and the traveling projectile, you can catch up to where it will land without needing to know calculus. The skill requires a constant feedback loop between you and the environment in order to make a successful catch. The would-be physicist can practice calculating the ball’s trajectory in a classroom, but the outfield catcher cannot.

情境认知的一个简单例子就是学习接高飞棒球。棒球的精确轨迹难以计算，这需要理解微分方程，而这些方程要考虑重力、风力，甚至球自身的旋转。精确计算球的落点对大多数人来说都是一项超出其认知能力的壮举。那么我们是如何打棒球的呢？答案是我们可以走捷径。通过追球并保持自身与飞行物体之间的恒定角度，你无需掌握微积分就能预测球的落点。这项技能需要你与环境之间持续的反馈循环才能成功接球。未来的物理学家可以在教室里练习计算球的轨迹，但外野捕手却无法做到。

Supporters of situated cognition argue that these interactive crossovers, where thinking requires constant feedback from the outside world, are not just limited to catching balls and piloting planes. The car mechanic who runs the engine to listen to a strange sound, the entrepreneur who builds a test product before ramping up production, and the chef who tastes the sauce before deciding whether to add more spices are all engaged in a process of improvisation. According to this view, we cannot understand what the mechanic, entrepreneur, or chef knows without considering the environment they practice in. The knowledge in their head may be less like the physicist’s trajectory and more like the outfielder’s trick—leaning on the world rather than an explicit theory.

情境认知论的支持者认为，这种需要不断从外部世界获得反馈的互动式跨界思考并非仅限于接球和驾驶飞机。汽车修理工启动引擎聆听异响，企业家在扩大生产规模前先制造测试产品，厨师在决定是否添加更多香料前先品尝酱汁，他们都在进行即兴发挥。根据这种观点，如果不考虑修理工、企业家或厨师所处的环境，我们就无法理解他们所掌握的知识。他们头脑中的知识或许不像物理学家那样遵循既定的理论轨迹，而更像是外野手的技巧——依靠的是现实世界，而非明确的理论。

The process of improvisation extends to our interaction with other people. When an insurance claims processor has to decide whether a tricky case deserves coverage, she consults her peers. Over time, these conversations become a collective interpretation of how to apply the protocols. When a new processor joins the team, she must adapt not only to the standard operating procedures, but to the interpretation of those procedures by her more senior colleagues. This process occurs in all professions, from scientists who must submit to the judgment of their peers before their findings are declared a fact, to the lawyers who negotiate the meaning of ambiguous terms such as what standard of behavior accords with a “ reasonable person.” The embedded nature of this knowledge often makes it hard to extract from the contexts in which it was generated.

即兴发挥的过程也延伸到了我们与他人的互动中。当保险理赔员需要决定一个棘手的案件是否应该获得赔偿时，她会咨询同事。随着时间的推移，这些讨论逐渐演变成对如何应用相关流程的集体解读。当一位新的理赔员加入团队时，她不仅要适应标准操作程序，还要适应资深同事对这些程序的解读。这种过程存在于各行各业，从科学家必须接受同行的评判才能将他们的发现公之于众，到律师需要协商诸如“理性人”的行为标准等模糊术语的含义。这种知识的内在性往往使得我们难以将其从其产生的语境中剥离出来。

Legitimate, Peripheral Participation

合法、边缘化的参与

Anthropologist Jean Lave, in collaboration with her student Etienne Wenger, proposed a theory of legitimate, peripheral participation for the process by which people become encultured in a community of practice. Drawing upon her fieldwork with West African tailors, Lave found that apprentices rarely learned through explicit instructions given by a master. Instead, the gradual introduction to the real work of the craft allowed them to become, “with remarkably few exceptions, skilled and respected master tailors.”

人类学家让·拉维与她的学生艾蒂安·温格合作，提出了合法边缘参与理论，用以解释人们如何在实践社群中获得文化熏陶的过程。拉维基于对西非裁缝的田野调查发现，学徒很少通过师傅的明确指导来学习。相反，他们通过逐步接触实际操作，最终“几乎无一例外地成为技艺精湛、受人尊敬的裁缝大师”。

Legitimacy and transparency are central to this process. Legitimacy refers to the acceptance, by members of the community, of the path taken to full participation. An uncredentialed research assistant and a doctoral student may perform similar work in a laboratory, but only the latter is on a legitimate path to becoming a scientist. Similarly, no amount of legal knowledge can make up for lacking a law degree in the eyes of a court. Credentials, however, are only a particularly visible manifestation of legitimacy. The company that has an informal policy of only promoting from within is making an implicit claim about the legitimacy of alternative paths to management.

合法性和透明度是这一过程的核心。合法性指的是社群成员对实现全面参与途径的认可。一个没有资质的研究助理和一个博士生可能在实验室里做着类似的工作，但只有后者才是走在成为科学家的合法道路上。同样，在法庭眼中，再多的法律知识也无法弥补没有法学学位这一缺陷。然而，资质只是合法性的一种特别明显的体现。一家公司如果奉行只从内部提拔人才的非正式政策，实际上是在暗示其他通往管理层的途径也是合法的。

Transparency refers to the ability to observe and understand the cultural practices present in the community. In an illustrative case, Lave and Wenger document how meat cutters in a grocery store were positioned at a wrapping station, while the more experienced butchers worked in a separate part of the facility. One apprentice butcher remarked, “I’m scared to go in the back room. I feel so out of place there. I haven’t gone back there in a long time because I just don’t know what to do when I’m there.” Without a window onto actual practice, the apprentices only had access to their formal instruction, which often emphasized skills that were seldom used on the job.

透明度指的是观察和理解社区中存在的文化习俗的能力。拉夫和温格在一个案例中记录了杂货店的肉类切割员如何被安排在包装台，而经验丰富的屠夫则在店内的另一个区域工作。一位学徒屠夫说道：“我不敢去后面的房间。我感觉在那里格格不入。我已经很久没回去了，因为我不知道到了那里该做什么。” 由于无法接触到实际操作，这些学徒只能接受正规的培训，而这些培训往往强调一些在工作中很少用到的技能。

Lave and Wenger argue that the process of learning can’t be seen as something that takes place entirely inside our heads. Instead, learning is a communal activity, encompassing both the enculturation of new members and the evolution of practices sustained by interactions both within the group and the outside world. Following this line of reasoning, they argue that apprenticeship makes more sense as a path to practice than extensive schooling.

拉维和温格认为，学习过程不能仅仅被视为发生在我们头脑内部的事情。相反，学习是一种群体活动，它既包括新成员的文化融入，也包括实践的演进，而这种演进又依赖于群体内部和外部世界的互动。基于这种逻辑，他们认为，与接受大量的学校教育相比，学徒制更适合作为实践途径。

Pitfalls in Informal Learning

非正式学习中的陷阱

It’s easy to romanticize learning by doing. But learning in practice has just as many drawbacks as detached classroom exercises. As we’ve seen before, experts often make lousy teachers, as they are often unable to articulate the basis for the skills they perform. Even when they can explain themselves, they often don’t have time to teach. Interns at big companies are often exploited for a cheap source of labor, rather than provided an opportunity to slowly work their way into a profession. Existing members of a high-status group may erect barriers to new entrants. These barriers work to limit competition and sustain the prestige of the existing members. They also tend to raise prices and restrict access to essential services the profession provides. Economists Morris Kleiner and Evgeny Vorotnikov estimate that the burden of professional licensing costs the United States economy between $183 billion and $197 billion per year. As George Bernard Shaw observed wryly in his 1906 play The Doctor’s Dilemma , “ All professions are conspiracies against the laity.”

人们很容易将边做边学浪漫化。但实践学习的弊端与脱离实际的课堂练习一样多。正如我们之前所见，专家往往不是好的老师，因为他们通常无法清晰阐述自身技能的基础。即使他们能够解释清楚，也常常没有时间进行教学。大公司的实习生往往被当作廉价劳动力来利用，而不是有机会逐步晋升到专业领域。高地位群体中的现有成员可能会设置障碍，阻碍新成员进入。这些障碍旨在限制竞争，维护现有成员的声望。它们往往还会推高价格，并限制人们获得该行业提供的基本服务。经济学家莫里斯·克莱纳和叶夫根尼·沃罗特尼科夫估计，职业资格认证的负担每年给美国经济造成1830亿至1970亿美元的损失。正如萧伯纳在他 1906 年的戏剧《医生的困境》中讽刺地指出的那样，“所有职业都是对普通民众的阴谋”。

The informal culture that emerges from communal interactions is not always benign. Bullying and harassment are just as likely outcomes as mutual teamwork and support. Sloppy communication norms and a hierarchical cockpit culture led to Jacob Veldhuyzen van Zanten’s disastrous decision at Tenerife. Improvements came about as a result of a greater reliance on formal pilot training, not simply a hope that the culture of aviation would fix itself.

群体互动中形成的非正式文化并非总是良性的。欺凌和骚扰与互助合作一样常见。糟糕的沟通规范和等级森严的驾驶舱文化导致了雅各布·维尔德胡伊岑·范赞滕在特内里费岛的灾难性决策。改进的契机在于更加重视正规的飞行员培训，而非仅仅寄希望于航空文化能够自行改善。

Despite these concerns, it seems clear that the social world cannot be ignored, neither for novices who wish to enter a practice, nor for the authorities and educators who want to ensure that those practices serve the common good. As new entrants, we need to pay attention not only to the content of the skills we wish to master but also to the social environment that enables access to practice. As educators and employers, we must also recognize that formal lessons and standard operating procedures will only emerge in practice after a process of negotiation and accommodation by the people who eventually perform the work.

尽管存在这些担忧，但显而易见，社会因素不容忽视，无论是对于希望进入某个领域的初学者，还是对于希望确保这些实践服务于公共利益的管理者和教育者而言，都是如此。作为新入行者，我们不仅需要关注希望掌握的技能内容，还需要关注能够提供实践机会的社会环境。作为教育者和雇主，我们也必须认识到，正式的课程和标准操作程序只有在最终执行工作的人员经过协商和适应后才能在实践中形成。

Lessons for Learning in Real Life

从现实生活中汲取的教训

Situated learning suggests a potent need for real practice. Classroom lessons and simulations may be essential in the beginning, but eventually all skills must be sustained by engagement in the real world. Here are some lessons to consider when navigating the social and physical obstacles to practice.

情境学习强调了实际练习的迫切需求。课堂教学和模拟练习在初期固然重要，但最终所有技能都必须通过参与真实世界的活动来巩固和提升。以下是一些在克服实践中的社会和实际障碍时值得思考的经验教训。

Lesson #1: Study How Entry into Practice Really Works

第一课：了解执业准入的真正流程。

Legitimacy constrains the possible paths to engaging in a practice. In some cases, these restrictions are highly visible—such as the degree required to become a doctor, or the army officer who must become a major before becoming a general. In other cases, the pathway to full participation is obscured. Jason Brennan, a tenured philosopher at Georgetown University, reviewed data on who makes it in academia in his book Good Work If You Can Get It . He finds that academic rank trumps nearly all other considerations in choosing where to study:

合法性限制了参与某种实践的可能途径。在某些情况下，这些限制显而易见——例如成为医生所需的学位，或者军队军官必须先晋升为少校才能成为将军。而在另一些情况下，充分参与的途径则较为隐蔽。乔治城大学终身哲学家杰森·布伦南在其著作《好工作，如果你能得到它》中回顾了学术界成功人士的数据。他发现，在选择就读院校时，学术等级几乎凌驾于所有其他因素之上：

If you want to succeed in academia, go to the best graduate program with the best job placement you can. This trumps almost everything else, including fit, whether you share the same research interests as the faculty there, the size of the graduate stipend or the location of the university.

如果你想在学术界取得成功，那就去你能找到的就业前景最好的研究生项目。这一点几乎比任何其他因素都重要，包括是否适合该项目、你是否与那里的教授有相同的研究兴趣、研究生津贴的多少，以及大学的地理位置。

Brennan advises against focusing too much on teaching: “ The grad students who spend the most time ‘perfecting their teaching’ often fail out of their programs and never get careers as teachers. It may not be fair, but it’s how it is.” He also stresses the importance of a prestigious academic advisor. “A good rule of thumb: You can’t get any job your advisor couldn’t get. If your advisor wouldn’t be competitive for a job at Princeton, then neither will you.”

布伦南建议不要过分专注于教学：“那些花最多时间‘完善教学技巧’的研究生往往会被淘汰，最终也找不到教师这份工作。这或许不公平，但事实就是如此。”他还强调了拥有一位声名卓著的学术导师的重要性。“一条很好的经验法则是：你的导师能帮你找到工作，你也找不到。如果你的导师在普林斯顿大学都找不到工作，那你也肯定找不到。”

Brennan’s advice applies to academia, but similar stories could be told about entry into almost any elite profession. Acting, entrepreneurship, journalism, music, and executive management all have surprisingly narrow paths to success. If you want to be one of the few who make it, you need to do your homework and figure out how the field actually works. You may not always like what you hear, but you can’t work around an obstacle you can’t even see.

布伦南的建议不仅适用于学术界，也适用于几乎所有精英行业的入门之路。演艺、创业、新闻、音乐和高管管理等领域，通往成功的道路都出人意料地狭窄。如果你想成为少数成功者之一，就必须做好功课，弄清楚这个领域究竟是如何运作的。你可能并不总是喜欢听到的内容，但你无法绕过一个你甚至都看不到的障碍。

Lesson #2: Separate Skills from Signals

第二课：区分技能和信号

Since opportunities for genuine practice are often scarce, it’s natural to want to restrict them to the best possible applicants. This creates a tension, however, when the skills needed to get the job aren’t the skills needed to perform the job. The signaling theory of education argues that a lot of our extensive and expensive schooling is not to build useful workplace skills or build more conscientious citizenry, but to act as a filter so that limited slots for good positions and on-the-job training go to the best applicants.

由于真正的实践机会往往稀缺，人们自然希望将这些机会限定在最优秀的申请者身上。然而，当获得工作所需的技能与实际工作所需的技能不符时，就会产生矛盾。教育信号理论认为，我们大量且昂贵的教育并非旨在培养实用的职场技能或培养更有责任感的公民，而是为了起到筛选作用，确保有限的优质职位和在职培训机会只提供给最优秀的申请者。

Bryan Caplan wrote a spirited defense of signaling theory in his book The Case Against Education . Caplan argues that economic data better fit the theory of signaling than the alternative theories of human capital (the idea that school teaches useful skills and knowledge, and thus make us more productive) and ability bias (the idea that smart people go to school, and so they would be high earners even if they were college dropouts). One source he draws upon is sheepskin effects, where the return to an extra year of college goes up dramatically for students in their graduating year. If we believed the human capital story, we should expect students to get gradually more productive (and thus earning higher wages) with each added year of schooling. Instead, if we believe that schooling is mostly about showing off smarts, work ethic, or social conformity, then most of the value of a college education is obtained with the degree. Another source of evidence comes from General Education Development diplomas. Students with those credentials ought to have the same academic skills as high school graduates, yet the premium for having a GED is much weaker than a high school diploma.

布莱恩·卡普兰在其著作《反对教育》中对信号理论进行了有力辩护。卡普兰认为，经济数据比人力资本理论（认为学校教授实用技能和知识，从而提高生产力）和能力偏见理论（认为聪明人会接受教育，因此即使大学辍学也能获得高收入）更符合信号理论。他引用的一个证据是“羊皮纸效应”，即对于即将毕业的学生来说，多读一年大学所带来的回报会显著增加。如果我们相信人力资本理论，那么随着受教育年限的增加，学生的生产力（以及收入）应该会逐步提高。然而，如果我们认为教育的主要目的是展示聪明才智、职业道德或社会适应性，那么大学教育的大部分价值就体现在学位本身。另一个证据来源是普通教育发展证书（GED）。拥有这些证书的学生应该具备与高中毕业生相同的学术技能，然而，获得 GED 证书所带来的优势远不如高中毕业文凭。

Completely useless activities that have a value in signaling generic abilities are an extreme. In practice, most opportunities for improvement are a mixture of enhancing proficiency as well as credibly communicating talent. The programmer who gets a certificate for a new technology may learn the same amount as the person who studies informally, but only the former can put it on her resume. Similarly, the manager who leads his team to success on a major project may have acquired some useful ideas about leadership, but the visibility of his success matters more for eventual promotion. The theory of signaling means that it’s not enough to get good: you need to find a way to show it.

完全无用的活动如果仅仅是为了展现通用能力，那就属于极端情况了。实际上，大多数提升机会都是提高技能和有效展示才能的结合。获得新技术证书的程序员可能和非正式学习者学到了相同的东西，但只有前者才能把证书写进简历。同样，带领团队成功完成一个重要项目的经理可能积累了一些有用的领导经验，但最终能否晋升，更重要的是他所取得的成就是否引人注目。信号理论表明，仅仅能力强是不够的，你还需要找到展现自身能力的方式。

Lesson #3: Learn the Lore of the Tribe

第三课：学习部落传说

In chapter 4 , we discussed how lore, or informal knowledge held in communities, is often needed for performing a skill. Lore also serves a different function, providing signals of membership to particular groups. Bernard Brodie, the father of pharmacology, discussed the heuristic he used when deciding what research to pay attention to in the emerging field of neurotransmitters. “ When the experiments were good, we called it sero tonin ,” Brodie recalled. “When I heard it pronounced se rot onin, I knew the experiments were bad and I stayed home.”

在第四章中，我们讨论了社群中流传下来的非正式知识（即民间传说）对于掌握一项技能往往至关重要。民间传说还具有另一种功能，即作为特定群体成员身份的标志。药理学之父伯纳德·布罗迪（Bernard Brodie）曾谈到，在神经递质这一新兴领域，他如何运用启发式方法来决定关注哪些研究。“当实验结果良好时，我们称之为血清素，”布罗迪回忆道，“当我听到‘血清素’这个词时，我就知道实验结果很糟糕，所以我就待在家里了。”

Educational theorist E. D. Hirsch argued that acquiring the lore of educated society is a major function of schools. Educated publications like the New York Times or the Atlantic presume a minimum degree of cultural knowledge. This background knowledge smooths communications among educated people, since they can assume that readers will know what the Emancipation Proclamation is or why the Magna Carta mattered. Lacking this lore, the informal discussions that take place are often impenetrable. Lore, however, is not simply a property of general education as every specialization develops a unique argot for facilitating conversations.

教育理论家E. D. 赫希认为，获取受过教育社会的知识是学校的一项重要职能。《纽约时报》或《大西洋月刊》等教育出版物假定读者具备一定的文化知识。这种背景知识有助于受过教育的人们之间的交流，因为他们可以假定读者了解《解放奴隶宣言》的内容或《大宪章》的重要性。如果缺乏这些知识，非正式的讨论往往会变得晦涩难懂。然而，知识并非仅仅是通识教育的专属，因为每个专业领域都会发展出独特的行话来促进交流。

With written texts, one solution for dealing with novel jargon is simply to read slowly and look up every word or phrase you’re unsure of. This approach may be painstaking at first, but eventually you’ll acquire enough of the basic concepts that you can read new material fluently. In interpersonal settings, being the person who asks silly questions about what words mean might be embarrassing at first, but it is often a short-term cost that needs to be paid so you can understand the work.

对于书面文本，应对新出现的术语的一个方法就是放慢阅读速度，查阅每一个不确定的单词或短语。这种方法起初可能比较费力，但最终你会掌握足够的基本概念，从而能够流畅地阅读新材料。在人际交往中，一开始问一些关于词语含义的“傻问题”可能会让人尴尬，但这通常是为了理解对方的工作而必须付出的短期代价。

Integration with real-life practice is necessary, but it’s rarely sufficient for mastery. Improvement requires correcting our mistakes and misconceptions. In the next chapter, we’ll look at the importance of feedback not just in learning new things, but in unlearning bad habits and faulty ideas.

将理论与实际应用相结合固然必要，但这往往不足以让我们精通。进步需要纠正错误和误解。下一章，我们将探讨反馈的重要性，它不仅有助于学习新知识，还能帮助我们摒弃坏习惯和错误观念。

# ↩

Chapter 11

第十一章

Improvement Is Not a Straight Line

进步并非一条直线

Wisdom doesn’t consist in knowing more that is new, but less that is false.

智慧不在于知道更多的新知识，而在于知道更少错误的知识。

—Henry Wheeler Shaw

——亨利·惠勒·肖

  • When do we first need to get worse, before getting better?
    我们什么时候需要先经历一段糟糕的时期，然后才能好转？
  • What are the risks of unlearning?
    摒弃旧知会带来哪些风险？
  • Why does progress eventually stall without corrective feedback?
    为什么如果没有纠正性反馈，进步最终会停滞不前？

F ew athletes have dominated their sport as Tiger Woods has dominated golf. At ten months old, Woods climbed down from his high chair to imitate his father’s golf swing with a plastic club. At age two, he made his national television debut, lobbing balls for the incredulous audience of The Mike Douglas Show . At fifteen, he was the youngest-ever US Junior Amateur champion. He then went on to win it three times in a row. After dropping out of Stanford to turn pro, he won the Masters tournament by a record-breaking twelve strokes. Following this meteoric rise, Woods did something few could have expected: he decided to completely change the way he swung a golf club.

很少有运动员能像泰格·伍兹那样在各自领域占据统治地位，尤其是在高尔夫领域。十个月大的时候，伍兹就从高脚椅上爬下来，用塑料球杆模仿父亲的挥杆动作。两岁时，他首次亮相全国电视荧屏，在迈克·道格拉斯秀上向难以置信的观众抛球。十五岁时，他成为美国青少年业余锦标赛历史上最年轻的冠军，并连续三次夺冠。从斯坦福大学辍学转为职业球员后，他以创纪录的十二杆优势赢得了美国大师赛冠军。在经历了如此惊人的崛起之后，伍兹做了一件几乎无人预料的事情：他决定彻底改变自己的挥杆方式。

Known for his long, powerful drives, Woods had relied on a whiplike action to make the ball reach speeds of up to two hundred miles per hour at impact. To produce the force, his hips rotated so fast that his arms couldn’t always keep up. This delayed action meant Woods’s clubface was pointed outward. Uncorrected, this would fire the ball out to the right, far off the fairway. Woods’s kinesthetic intuition allowed him to correct this discrepancy in the middle of the swing—twisting his hands slightly to turn the clubface and hit the ball squarely whenever his arms got “stuck.” Yet this improvisation depended on luck and precision. “ I won with perfect timing,” Woods remarked when analyzing his record win at the Masters. “[I]f I don’t have that, I’ve got no chance.” In theory at least, by changing his golf swing Woods could add consistent execution on top of athletic genius.

伍兹以其远距离、强劲的开球而闻名，他依靠鞭子般的挥杆动作，使球在击球瞬间达到高达每小时200英里的速度。为了产生如此强大的力量，他的髋部旋转速度极快，以至于手臂有时无法跟上。这种延迟导致伍兹的杆面朝外。如果不加以纠正，球就会飞向右侧，远远偏离球道。伍兹凭借其运动直觉，能够在挥杆过程中纠正这一偏差——当手臂“卡住”时，他会略微扭转双手来转动杆面，从而击中球。然而，这种即兴发挥依赖于运气和精准度。“我靠完美的时机赢得了比赛，”伍兹在分析他创纪录的美国大师赛胜利时说道，“如果我没有这一点，我就没有机会。”至少在理论上，通过改变他的高尔夫挥杆动作，伍兹可以在其运动天赋的基础上，增加稳定性。

Yet the decision to rebuild wasn’t without risks. Other golfers had their professional ambitions shattered after attempts to alter their swing. David Gossett was seen as a golf prodigy, winning the US Amateur at nineteen. After reaching the pros, he decided his swing wasn’t good enough. The botched change scuttled his career. “Chasing the almighty, great swing is not real,” he later told reporters. Chip Beck won four PGA Tour events, but felt he needed a new movement to hit the ball higher. A few years later, he quit golf to become an insurance salesman. David Duval, Ian Baker-Finch, and Seve Ballesteros all decided they needed to redesign their swings. None ever played competitively again. “Long grooved into the frontal lobes of golf’s conventional wisdom is the notion that every person has a ‘born,’ or ‘natural,’ swing,” writes sports journalist Scott Eden, and “to meddle with your natural swing is to meddle with your soul.” For Woods to contemplate such a radical move, not in the face of stiffened competition but after record-breaking success, was seen as bordering on insanity. One commentator argued it was as if Michael Jordan decided to switch to shooting jump shots left-handed, just for fun.

然而，重塑挥杆的决定并非没有风险。其他一些高尔夫球手在尝试改变挥杆动作后，职业生涯的梦想就此破灭。大卫·戈塞特曾被视为高尔夫神童，19岁就赢得了美国业余锦标赛冠军。进入职业赛场后，他觉得自己的挥杆不够好。这次失败的改变毁了他的职业生涯。“追求完美挥杆是不现实的，”他后来告诉记者。奇普·贝克赢得了四场PGA巡回赛冠军，但他觉得自己需要新的动作才能把球打得更高。几年后，他放弃了高尔夫，成为了一名保险推销员。大卫·杜瓦尔、伊恩·贝克-芬奇和塞维·巴列斯特罗斯都决定重新设计自己的挥杆动作。但他们再也没有参加过任何比赛。“长期以来，高尔夫界的传统观念根深蒂固，认为每个人都有一个‘天生的’或‘自然的’挥杆动作，”体育记者斯科特·伊登写道，“改变你天生的挥杆动作就如同改变你的灵魂。”伍兹在打破纪录的成功之后，而非面临日益激烈的竞争，却考虑做出如此激进的举动，这被视为近乎疯狂。一位评论员打趣说，这就像迈克尔·乔丹为了好玩，突然决定改用左手跳投一样。

Despite the risks, Woods wanted no half measures. Instead of gradually introducing the modifications suggested by his swing coach, Butch Harmon, he wanted to implement all of them at once. “ It’s not going to be easy for you to make this change and still play through it,” cautioned Harmon. “I don’t care,” was Woods’s reply. He wanted to be the best golf player of all time. If that meant rebuilding from scratch, so be it. After eighteen months of grinding practice and a tournament season where he underperformed due to the unfamiliar swing, Woods found his groove with the new motion. The year after, he posted eight tournament wins, a feat that hadn’t been accomplished since 1974. In the following years, he became the youngest golfer to complete a Career Grand Slam, winning all of the major golf tournaments and firmly securing his number one position in golf.

尽管风险重重，伍兹却不愿采取任何妥协。他没有像挥杆教练布奇·哈蒙建议的那样循序渐进地进行调整，而是想一次性全部实施。“你要做到这些改变并继续比赛并不容易，”哈蒙告诫道。“我不在乎，”伍兹回答。他想成为史上最伟大的高尔夫球手。如果这意味着要从头开始重建，那就这样吧。经过18个月的艰苦训练，以及一个赛季因不熟悉挥杆动作而表现不佳之后，伍兹终于找到了新动作的节奏。第二年，他赢得了八项锦标赛冠军，这是自1974年以来无人能及的壮举。在接下来的几年里，他成为最年轻的职业生涯大满贯得主，赢得了所有高尔夫大满贯赛事，并牢牢占据了高尔夫世界第一的宝座。

Since his golden years working with Harmon, Woods has made major changes to his swing at least three times. Some critics argue that these frequent transformations robbed Woods of years during his athletic prime, keeping him from overtaking Jack Nicklaus’s untouched career record of eighteen major tournament wins (Woods has fifteen). An alternative view is that Woods’s ability to change his game preserved his longevity in the sport. The lithe, corkscrew motion of his teenage swing wouldn’t have worked as a well-muscled thirty-year-old, and progressively worsening knee and back injuries made significant adjustments unavoidable. Whether you view Woods’s changes as a help or a hindrance—a sign of unhealthy perfectionism or the confidence to take risks—none can question Woods’s track record as one of the greatest golfers of all time.

自从与哈蒙合作的黄金时期以来，伍兹至少三次对他的挥杆动作进行了重大调整。一些评论家认为，这些频繁的改变让伍兹错失了运动生涯的巅峰时期，使他无法超越杰克·尼克劳斯保持的18个大满贯冠军的纪录（伍兹目前拥有15个）。另一种观点则认为，伍兹改变球技的能力正是他保持职业生涯长久的原因。他青少年时期那种轻盈灵动的螺旋式挥杆动作，对于一个肌肉发达的三十岁球员来说显然行不通，而日益严重的膝盖和背部伤病也使得他不得不做出重大调整。无论你认为伍兹的改变是助力还是阻碍——是过度追求完美还是勇于冒险的自信——都无法否认伍兹是史上最伟大的高尔夫球手之一。

Unlearning: Getting Worse to Get Better

摒弃旧知：从恶化到好转
