While few of us will face the level of public scrutiny and performance pressure as Tiger Woods, life often confronts us with situations that require us first to get worse, before getting better. The career change that promises financial stability, but comes at the cost of working up from the bottom in a new industry. The search for a satisfying relationship that means breaking up the one that has hit a dead end. The strategy to ward off an upstart rival that requires winding down your old business. In each case, reaching a new peak requires descending from our spot on the current hill, and creates the risk that we may never rise up from the valley below.

虽然我们当中很少有人会像泰格·伍兹那样面临公众的审视和巨大的压力，但生活常常会让我们经历一段低谷期，然后才能迎来转机。比如，为了获得经济稳定而转换职业，却要付出在新行业从底层做起的代价；又比如，为了寻找一段令人满意的感情，不得不结束一段已经走到尽头的感情；再比如，为了抵御新兴竞争对手，不得不逐步关闭原有的生意。在每一种情况下，想要攀登新的高峰，就必须从当前的山峰跌落，而这也带来了我们可能永远无法从谷底重新站起来的风险。

The difficulty of unlearning is easy to see with motor skills. In 1967, psychologists Paul Fitts and Michael Posner proposed an influential theory for how we develop movement proficiency. They argued that learning occurs in three phases:

运动技能的学习过程很容易体现出遗忘的难度。1967年，心理学家保罗·菲茨和迈克尔·波斯纳提出了一个影响深远的理论，阐述了我们如何发展运动技能。他们认为学习分为三个阶段：

  1. The Cognitive Phase. In this phase, the performer tries to understand the task, what is required, and how to perform the skill. Conscious, deliberate control of movements is often used as the learner tries to figure out the correct technique.
    认知阶段。在此阶段，表演者试图理解任务、要求以及如何完成技能。学习者在摸索正确技巧的过程中，通常会有意识地、刻意地控制动作。
  2. The Associative Phase. After a basic understanding of the skill has been reached, the performer tries different things out. It’s in this phase that major errors are gradually eliminated and performance becomes smoother.
    联想阶段。在对技能有了基本的了解之后，表演者会尝试不同的方法。在这个阶段，主要的错误会逐渐被消除，表演也会变得更加流畅。
  3. The Autonomous Phase. Finally, when errors have been weeded out, skill becomes increasingly effortless. By this stage, the explicit instructions used in the first phase may even be forgotten. The skill may become almost reflex-like, not relying on conscious control.
    自主阶段。最终，当错误被彻底清除后，技能会变得越来越轻松自如。到了这个阶段，第一阶段使用的明确指令甚至可能被遗忘。技能几乎会变成一种反射，不再依赖于意识控制。

For a new golfer, her swing is still in the cognitive phase. A good coach can guide her to the approximate movement she needs to create. At this stage, she’s likely to be thinking about explicit rules guiding her performance, trying to remember to avoid looking up too soon after hitting the ball or making sure to rotate her body enough in the backswing. As she practices in varying conditions, she enters the associative phase. Movements get calibrated to different conditions, so she knows how to swing both woods and irons and adjusts her force to shoot accurately from both the fairway and the rough. Finally, as the movement becomes repeatedly practiced, the details recede from conscious awareness. Once this occurs, internally focused thoughts on the nature of bodily movements can interfere with the autonomous skill. Instead, best performance is achieved by having an external focus on the goal of the movement, not the mechanics for executing it.

对于一位新手高尔夫球手来说，她的挥杆动作仍处于认知阶段。一位优秀的教练可以引导她掌握大致的动作要领。在这个阶段，她可能会思考一些指导动作的明确规则，比如击球后不要过早抬头，或者确保在后挥杆时身体有足够的旋转。随着她在不同的环境下练习，她进入了联想阶段。动作会根据不同的环境进行调整，因此她知道如何挥动木杆和铁杆，并能调整力度，从而在球道和长草区都能精准击球。最终，随着动作的反复练习，细节会逐渐淡出意识。一旦达到这个阶段，专注于身体动作本质的内在思考就会干扰自主技能的发挥。相反，最佳表现的实现方式是将注意力集中在动作的目标上，而不是执行动作的机制上。

Fitts and Posner’s theory helps make sense of the risks involved in Woods’s major swing change. By making significant adjustments, he was regressing to the cognitive phase of skill acquisition. To be successful, he would need to move the skill back through the associative phase, weeding out errors in varied playing conditions, and repeating it enough so that the new movement would be sufficiently automatic that his old swing wouldn’t spontaneously emerge, especially under the added pressure of a tournament.

菲茨和波斯纳的理论有助于理解伍兹大幅改变挥杆动作所带来的风险。通过做出重大调整，他实际上是在技能习得的认知阶段进行退步。为了取得成功，他需要让这项技能重新进入联想阶段，在各种不同的比赛条件下不断纠正错误，并反复练习，直到新的动作足够自动化，以至于他旧的挥杆动作不会自发地出现，尤其是在比赛的额外压力下。

Yet the phases of skill acquisition also point out why major changes can often be necessary. No skilled movement is repeated with machinelike precision. Were that the case, athletic performance would be impossible. A change in wind, grass, or the firmness of the ground would change a golfer’s movements so much that hitting a ball consistently would be impossible. All skills involve a certain degree of flexibility, which enables the performer to adapt to changing conditions. However, this flexibility isn’t unlimited. A person can go from hunting and pecking on a large keyboard to a smaller one, but no amount of practice with that motion will eventually transform that person into a touch typist. Finding a new way to perform a skill requires more than just tweaking an existing motor program, but building a new one from scratch.

然而，技能习得的各个阶段也揭示了为何重大变革往往是必要的。任何熟练的动作都不可能像机器一样精准地重复。如果真是如此，运动表现将无从谈起。风向、草地或地面硬度的变化都会极大地改变高尔夫球手的动作，以至于无法稳定击球。所有技能都包含一定程度的灵活性，使操作者能够适应不断变化的环境。然而，这种灵活性并非无限的。一个人可以从在大型键盘上“一指禅”式地敲击过渡到在小型键盘上敲击，但无论练习多少次，最终也无法使他成为盲打高手。找到一种新的技能执行方式，需要的不仅仅是对现有动作程序的微调，而是从零开始构建一个全新的程序。

Einstellung and Functional Fixedness: Does Old Knowledge Interfere with New Ideas?

定势与功能固着：旧知识会妨碍新思想吗？

Motor skills aren’t the only aspects of learning where previous abilities can interfere with new performances. Abraham Luchins studied the problem of how past successes in problem solving could inhibit future results. In one puzzle, he asked subjects how to fill a bucket of water using only jars of specific volumes. For example, a puzzle might ask a subject to obtain twenty liters of water, using only a twenty-nine-liter jar and a three-liter jar. The answer is to pour in twenty-nine liters, and then remove three liters, three times. For these puzzles, Luchins presented a sequence of problems that could all be solved by repeating a pattern of adding the second jar, and removing the first jar and two times the third jar. Following multiple repetitions of this pattern, he then gave subjects a puzzle that could be solved with the more complicated pattern they had learned (that is, B − A − 2C) or with a simpler solution (A − C). In their initial experiment, none of the subjects noticed the simpler solution. Luchins called this perseveration of a habitual mode of problem-solving Einstellung , or the mindset “which predisposes an organism to one type of motor or conscious act.”

运动技能并非学习中唯一会受到先前能力干扰的方面。亚伯拉罕·卢钦斯研究了过去解决问题的成功如何阻碍未来结果的问题。在一个谜题中，他要求受试者仅使用特定容量的罐子装满一桶水。例如，一个谜题可能要求受试者仅使用一个29升的罐子和一个3升的罐子来获得20升水。答案是倒入29升水，然后取出3升水，重复三次。对于这些谜题，卢钦斯呈现了一系列问题，所有问题都可以通过重复添加第二个罐子、取出第一个罐子以及两次取出第三个罐子的模式来解决。在多次重复这种模式之后，他给受试者一个谜题，该谜题可以用他们已经学到的更复杂的模式（即B-A-2C）或更简单的解决方案（A-C）来解决。在最初的实验中，没有一个受试者注意到更简单的解决方案。卢钦斯将这种习惯性问题解决方式的持续性称为 Einstellung，或者说是“使有机体倾向于某种类型的运动或意识行为”的心态。

Nor is the perseveration of old habits of thinking limited to problem-solving steps. Gestalt psychologist Karl Duncker coined the term functional fixedness to describe how perceiving an object in one role can make it hard to think of alternative uses. In a famous experiment, he gave subjects the problem of affixing candles to the side of a wall. In one condition, the subjects were given boxes, candles, and tacks. In another condition, the materials were the same, but the boxes were filled with the tacks. In the first condition, all of the subjects managed to figure out the solution, which was to use the tacks to fix the boxes to the walls, which, acting like little platforms, could support the candles. In contrast, less than half of the subjects figured this out when the boxes were initially filled. Seeing the box as a container, rather than as a potential platform, strongly influenced how subjects perceived the problem.

思维习惯的固着并非仅限于解决问题的步骤。格式塔心理学家卡尔·邓克尔创造了“功能固着”一词，用来描述人们如何因为习惯于将物体视为某种角色而难以想到其他用途。在一个著名的实验中，他让受试者将蜡烛固定在墙边。在一种情况下，受试者拿到盒子、蜡烛和图钉。在另一种情况下，材料相同，但盒子里装满了图钉。在第一种情况下，所有受试者都找到了解决方案：用图钉将盒子固定在墙上，盒子就像小平台一样，可以支撑蜡烛。相比之下，当盒子一开始就装满图钉时，只有不到一半的受试者想到了这一点。将盒子视为容器而非潜在的平台，极大地影响了受试者对问题的理解。

Figure 11

图 11

Subjects were given a box of tacks and a candle with the aim of affixing the candle to a wall. When tacks were put inside the box, fewer subjects considered the solution of using the box as a platform.

受试者被给予一盒图钉和一支蜡烛，目的是将蜡烛固定在墙上。当盒子里放的是图钉时，较少的受试者想到将盒子用作平台。

The need to unlearn faulty ways of thinking about a problem is a major issue in education. Subjects like economics, physics, and psychology confront students with radically different ways of thinking about everyday subjects. Research shows, however, that many students do not successfully export the reasoning they learn in classrooms to problems from everyday life. Physics students learn to calculate force and momentum like Newton, but continue to think like Aristotle outside the classroom. Economics students learn theories of welfare-enhancing trade, but continue to think like mercantilists when evaluating public policy. And as we saw in chapter 6 , the folk psychological idea that the mind is like a muscle is widely believed, even though considerable evidence weighs against it.

在教育领域，纠正错误的思维方式至关重要。经济学、物理学和心理学等学科会引导学生以截然不同的方式思考日常问题。然而，研究表明，许多学生无法成功地将课堂上学到的推理方法运用到日常生活中。物理系学生学习像牛顿那样计算力和动量，但在课堂外却仍然沿用亚里士多德的思维方式。经济学学生学习增进社会福利的贸易理论，但在评估公共政策时却仍然沿用重商主义的思维方式。正如我们在第六章中看到的，尽管大量证据与“大脑如同肌肉”这一民间心理学观点相悖，但这种观点仍然广为流传。

In some cases, what has to be unlearned may be a popular misconception. The idea that people have different learning styles (for example, visual, auditory, or kinesthetic) and that they will learn best when instruction matches their preferred style doesn’t have much evidence to support it, yet the idea continues to float around in popular culture. In such cases, it’s unlikely that someone spontaneously arrived at the learning styles theory. Instead, it’s probably just an idea that persists because it seems intuitively plausible and few people are familiar with the research against it.

在某些情况下，需要摒弃的可能是一种流行的误解。例如，认为人们有不同的学习风格（例如视觉型、听觉型或动觉型），并且当教学方式与他们偏好的风格相匹配时，学习效果最佳的观点，并没有多少证据支持，但这种观点仍然在流行文化中流传。在这种情况下，学习风格理论不太可能是某人自发产生的。相反，它很可能只是一个经久不衰的观点，因为它似乎符合直觉，而且很少有人了解与之相悖的研究。

In other cases, however, misconceptions are likely deeper. They may reflect a more basic, intuitive module for dealing with the world that develops outside of instruction and may be harder to overcome. Impetus theories of motion don’t make for very good physics. But they may be useful approximations in our high-friction environment for everyday purposes. Would-be physicists don’t replace their original folk intuition with the formal system derived from science, but learn the more rigorous system in parallel. Eventually, if their expertise deepens enough, they can successfully suppress naive intuitions when encountering problems that require physics knowledge. Yet the road to expertise is a twisting one. In one experiment, researchers showed a simulated “race” of two balls going down different tracks. The two tracks began and ended at the same heights as each other, but had different shapes of dips and hills. In one simulation, one of the two balls sped up as it climbed a hill, catching up to the other ball. Few physics-naive students picked this motion as realistic. Distressingly, however, those who had taken the college class frequently said this unusual motion was realistic! They erroneously justified it by invoking conservation of mechanical energy, which, although it requires that the two balls have the same speed when they reach the final height, does not require that the balls arrive there at the same time. Physics novices can apply ideas they’ve learned in class, but they sometimes have difficulty knowing exactly when they apply. Like a well-ingrained golf swing, it takes considerable effort to supplant the intuitions nature has encouraged us to cultivate all our lives.

然而，在其他情况下，误解可能更为根深蒂固。它们可能反映了一种更基础、更直觉的认知模式，这种模式在教学之外形成，并且可能更难克服。基于冲量的运动理论并非严谨的物理学理论，但在我们充满摩擦的日常生活中，它们或许可以作为有用的近似解释。未来的物理学家不会用源自科学的正式体系取代他们最初的民间直觉，而是并行学习更为严谨的体系。最终，如果他们的专业知识足够深入，他们就能在遇到需要物理知识的问题时，成功地抑制住幼稚的直觉。然而，通往专业知识的道路并非坦途。在一项实验中，研究人员模拟了两个小球在两条不同轨道上的“比赛”。两条轨道的起点和终点高度相同，但坡度和起伏的形状不同。在一次模拟中，其中一个小球在爬坡时速度加快，追上了另一个小球。很少有物理基础薄弱的学生会认为这种运动是合理的。然而，令人沮丧的是，那些上过大学物理课的人常常说这种不寻常的运动是符合实际的！他们错误地援引机械能守恒定律来解释这种现象。机械能守恒定律虽然要求两个球到达最终高度时速度相同，但并不要求它们同时到达该高度。物理初学者可以运用课堂上学到的知识，但他们有时很难准确地判断这些知识何时适用。就像根深蒂固的高尔夫挥杆动作一样，要取代我们一生中自然而然培养起来的直觉，需要付出相当大的努力。

Nip Bad Habits in the Bud

防患于未然，扼杀不良习惯

The easiest way to deal with the problem of unlearning is to not need it in the first place. Learning the correct technique, from the start, prevents the need to go back and make changes later. Access to a good coach or tutor early on can prevent bad habits forming that may become entrenched. And, in many cases, once the best method has been learned, no retraining is required.

解决“忘记旧方法”问题的最简单方法就是从一开始就避免需要它。从一开始就学习正确的技巧，可以避免日后需要重新调整。尽早接触优秀的教练或导师可以防止不良习惯的养成，避免这些习惯根深蒂固。而且，在很多情况下，一旦掌握了最佳方法，就无需再进行任何培训。

The importance of learning the best method can be seen in the process of children learning math procedures, like multi-digit subtraction. Cognitive scientists John Seely Brown and Kurt VanLehn found that many of the mistakes children make when learning this algorithm work like buggy computer code—children don’t fully understand how the algorithm works, so they use a procedure that’s different from the correct one. For instance, a common buggy algorithm in subtraction problems is to always subtract the larger number from the smaller one. Consider a student using this buggy algorithm on the question, “22-14 = ?” Instead of following the proper procedure of borrowing one from the tens column to solve “12-4 = 8,” the student would simply swap the digits and put the answer “4-2 = 2” in the ones column. Extra practice may not be helpful for students with buggy algorithms, as they may further ingrain the incorrect procedure. A more successful approach would be for a teacher to stop the student, explain the mistake, and ensure that the technique proceeds on the best footing. Corrective feedback can be essential to avoid falling into bad habits early on.

学习最佳方法的重要性在儿童学习数学运算过程（例如多位数减法）中可见一斑。认知科学家约翰·西利·布朗和库尔特·范莱恩发现，儿童在学习这种算法时犯的许多错误就像计算机代码中的错误一样——儿童没有完全理解算法的运作方式，因此他们使用的步骤与正确步骤不同。例如，减法问题中常见的错误算法是总是用较小的数减去较大的数。假设一个学生在计算“22-14 = ？”时使用了这种错误算法。他没有按照正确的步骤从十位借一位来计算“12-4 = 8”，而是简单地交换了十位和个位上的数字，并将答案“4-2 = 2”填入个位。对于使用错误算法的学生来说，额外的练习可能并无帮助，反而会加深他们对错误步骤的理解。更有效的做法是，教师及时制止学生，解释错误所在，并确保学生以正确的方式继续学习。及时纠正性的反馈对于避免过早养成不良习惯至关重要。

For many skills, there is no “correct” procedure, but there are better ones. Experienced teachers can guide their students to more successful ways to write code, swing a baseball bat, or structure an essay. If those methods get more practice, they’ll eventually become automatic. If alternative methods that don’t work as well take root, they may require more significant unlearning later. Given the heroic efforts that are often required, it’s better to begin with the right approach.

对于许多技能而言，并没有“正确”的方法，但有更好的方法。经验丰富的教师可以引导学生找到更有效的编程、挥棒或文章结构构建方式。如果这些方法得到更多练习，最终会成为一种习惯。如果一些效果不佳的替代方法根深蒂固，日后可能需要花费更多精力去纠正。考虑到这些技能往往需要付出巨大的努力，最好从一开始就采用正确的方法。

But completely avoiding unlearning is often impossible. While using the correct technique in subtraction problems is simply a matter of following instructions, many other skills don’t emerge from a flawless foundation. English-speaking children go through a regular sequence when learning to use the past tense. Initially, they begin using the irregular verbs they hear from adults (for example, “I went there,” “I did it”). With some exposure, they start to learn the rule that they can attach -ed to many verbs to make them past tense. This leads to a period of overregularization—where the rule applies even though that particular case is an exception (for example, “I goed there”). Finally, children learn which words are irregular (for example, go/went, do/did ) and correctly use both the irregular forms and regular past-tense endings. This kind of transition is non-monotonic, as children actually become less grammatical in their speaking at first, before getting better. Young children are also frequently impervious to correction, as many parents have witnessed when trying to adjust a toddler’s pronunciation.

但完全避免遗忘往往是不可能的。虽然在减法题中使用正确的技巧只需遵循步骤即可，但许多其他技能并非天生完美。以英语为母语的孩子在学习过去时会经历一个规律性的学习过程。起初，他们会使用从大人那里听到的不规则动词（例如，“I went there”、“I did it”）。随着接触的增多，他们开始学习在许多动词后加“-ed”构成过去时的规则。这导致了一个过度规则化的阶段——即使特定情况属于例外，他们也会应用该规则（例如，“I goed there”）。最终，孩子们会学习哪些词是不规则的（例如，go/went，do/did），并能正确使用不规则形式和规则过去时词尾。这种过渡并非单调，因为孩子们最初的语法水平实际上会下降，之后才会逐渐提高。幼儿往往难以纠正，许多父母在试图纠正幼儿的发音时都亲眼目睹了这一点。

Children learn grammar automatically, and don’t require instruction to speak properly except in unusual circumstances. All that’s needed is exposure and opportunities to interact. However non-monotonicity has been observed in other domains of learning. Vimla Patel, a psychologist specializing in medical cognition, notes that medical students’ reasoning frequently goes through similar changes in quality. For instance, both early medical students and medical experts tend to make few elaborations when thinking about patient problems. In contrast, intermediate students tend to draw far more inferences and dredge up more medical information than either beginners or seasoned clinicians. This so-called intermediate effect occurs because novice students have little knowledge to recall, and so they fail to elaborate much when they get stuck on problems. Experts, in contrast, don’t elaborate for a different reason: they know the likely answer and so they focus on only critical information pertinent to the problem, ignoring irrelevant aspects of the problem. In a similar vein, developmental psychologist Robert Siegler argues for a “ moderate experience hypothesis” that says people have the greatest variety of strategies (good and bad) with intermediate levels of experience in a field. At this stage, we know enough to have multiple ways to tackle a problem, but not so much that the optimal method has suppressed all alternatives. Non-monotonicity means that the path to mastery is not always a straight line. It invariably has dips and detours along the way.

儿童能够自动学习语法，除了特殊情况外，他们无需指导就能正确说话。他们只需要接触和互动机会。然而，非单调性在其他学习领域也已被观察到。专门研究医学认知的心理学家维姆拉·帕特尔指出，医学生的推理能力经常经历类似的质量变化。例如，无论是初级医学生还是医学专家，在思考患者问题时往往很少进行详细阐述。相比之下，中级医学生往往会进行更多的推断，并挖掘出比初学者或经验丰富的临床医生更多的医学信息。这种所谓的“中级效应”的出现是因为新手学生缺乏足够的知识储备，因此在遇到难题时往往不会进行过多的详细阐述。而专家不进行详细阐述的原因则不同：他们知道可能的答案，因此只关注与问题相关的关键信息，而忽略无关的方面。类似地，发展心理学家罗伯特·西格勒提出了“中等经验假说”，认为人们在某个领域拥有中等经验水平时，会掌握最丰富的策略（包括好的和坏的）。在这个阶段，我们掌握的知识足以让我们拥有多种解决问题的方法，但又不至于因为掌握了最佳方法而忽略了其他可能性。非单调性意味着通往精通的道路并非总是笔直的，而是必然会经历起伏和曲折。

In other cases, unlearning is necessary because the best method simply isn’t available when we’re starting out. The new crop of doctoral students may be more likely to lead a revolution in a scientific field, because they’re not as burdened by calcified ways of thinking about old problems. Max Planck, one of the physicists who led the quantum revolution, noted astutely that “ science proceeds one funeral at a time.” Often, the old guard who spent a lifetime growing accustomed to a particular paradigm find it difficult to switch to a new perspective, even after the evidence has become overwhelming. Albert Einstein fought bitterly against the nondeterministic aspects of quantum mechanics, despite winning his Nobel Prize for discoveries that led to it. Keeping up with new developments in our professional lives often requires uncomfortable adjustments.

在其他情况下，摒弃旧观念是必要的，因为当我们起步时，最佳方法根本无法获得。新一代博士生更有可能引领科学领域的革命，因为他们没有被根深蒂固的旧问题思维模式所束缚。引领量子革命的物理学家之一马克斯·普朗克曾精辟地指出，“科学的发展是一场接一场的葬礼”。通常，那些毕生习惯于特定范式的老派人士，即使证据确凿，也很难转变视角。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦曾强烈反对量子力学的非决定论，尽管他因促成量子力学的发现而荣获诺贝尔奖。在职业生涯中，跟上新的发展往往需要做出一些令人不适的调整。

Confronting Faulty Ways of Thinking

直面错误的思维方式

How do we avoid getting stuck in our ways? One method for unlearning involves confronting the flaws in our thinking with direct feedback. Anders Ericsson argued that a key to deliberate practice, his model for how elite experts get so good, was the presence of immediate feedback and guided practice sessions with the help of a coach. In his theory, the problem of stagnation in our skills results from the transition to Fitts and Posner’s autonomous mode of processing. The “deliberate” part of deliberate practice refers to the need for the performer to shift back to the cognitive phase, where aspects of the skill are under direct, conscious supervision. By combining this effortful mode of processing with immediate feedback from the environment, the performer can make conscious efforts to adjust. In this case, Woods fits the model of deliberate practice perfectly. Not only was he famous for his work ethic to practice relentlessly, but he approached many aspects of his swing from a deliberate perspective—thinking through and consciously adopting adjustments based on feedback.

我们如何避免固步自封？一种打破固有思维模式的方法是利用直接反馈来正视我们思维中的缺陷。安德斯·埃里克森认为，刻意练习的关键——他提出的精英专家如何变得如此优秀的模型——在于教练的指导和即时反馈。在他的理论中，技能停滞不前的问题源于我们向菲茨和波斯纳提出的自主处理模式的转变。刻意练习中的“刻意”指的是练习者需要回到认知阶段，在这个阶段，技能的各个方面都处于直接的、有意识的监督之下。通过将这种需要付出努力的处理模式与来自环境的即时反馈相结合，练习者可以有意识地进行调整。伍兹完美地诠释了刻意练习的模式。他不仅以孜孜不倦的训练精神而闻名，而且在挥杆的许多方面都秉持着刻意练习的理念——认真思考并根据反馈有意识地做出调整。

Feedback can also be used to confront misconceptions in academic subjects, such as physics. Traditional instruction often focuses on mastery of equations in well-defined problem types. While this kind of training is certainly necessary for mastering the subject, it may fail to directly confront a student with the inadequacy of her intuitive conceptions. Physics Nobelist Carl Wieman argues that we should introduce more hands-on physics simulations. These would allow students to make predictions about the movement of objects in idealized experiments and make the correct mental model of the physical process more salient. Other researchers have found that interactive simulations can improve conceptual knowledge over traditional instruction alone. Pure play with simulators is unlikely to produce a scientific level of understanding of a subject. But combined with more traditional exercises working with equations, an expanded set of activities may help to counteract the disconnect many students have between the physics they learn in the classroom and how they reason about objects moving in everyday life.

反馈也可以用来纠正学生在物理学等学科中的误解。传统的教学方法通常侧重于掌握特定题型中的公式。虽然这种训练对于掌握学科知识固然必要，但它可能无法直接让学生意识到自身直觉概念的不足。诺贝尔物理学奖得主卡尔·维曼认为，我们应该引入更多动手实践的物理模拟。这些模拟可以让学生在理想化的实验中预测物体的运动，并使他们更清晰地认识到物理过程的正确心理模型。其他研究人员也发现，交互式模拟比单纯的传统教学更能提升学生的概念知识。单纯地玩模拟器不太可能使学生对学科产生科学的理解。但是，如果将模拟活动与更多传统的公式练习相结合，就能帮助学生弥合课堂上学习的物理知识与日常生活中物体运动的理解之间的脱节。

Unfortunately, direct feedback about mistakes with a familiar strategy may not be enough to fix it. One reason for this is that unless the replacement strategy is sufficiently practiced, it may still be too effortful to compete with the old pattern. This is one reason golfers have so much difficulty switching to a new swing, and they often regress to old habits under pressure. Even if they may know, at some level, that they have mistakes in their performance, the new way of doing things may not work much better! Similarly, many physics novices may continue to use their intuitive mode of reasoning outside the classroom, because reasoning with physics is effortful and error-prone. In contrast, their intuitive system is fast and easy, even if it doesn’t always lead to the correct answer. Experts are far more likely to lean on their training, not simply because they are aware that everyday intuitions can’t be trusted, but also because the training is so well practiced that it doesn’t take nearly as much effort to execute. To unlearn lousy strategies we need to not only confront our mistakes, but also ensure that we can fluently apply a viable alternative.

不幸的是，即使直接反馈了熟悉策略中的错误，也可能不足以纠正错误。原因之一是，除非替代策略经过充分练习，否则可能仍然难以与旧模式抗衡。这就是为什么高尔夫球手很难适应新的挥杆动作，并且经常在压力下退回到旧习惯的原因之一。即使他们在某种程度上意识到自己的表现存在错误，新的方法也未必能带来多大的改善！同样，许多物理初学者在课堂外可能仍然会继续使用直觉推理模式，因为物理推理既费力又容易出错。相比之下，他们的直觉系统快速便捷，即使它并非总能得出正确答案。专家们则更倾向于依赖训练，这不仅是因为他们意识到日常直觉不可靠，还因为他们的训练非常熟练，执行起来毫不费力。要摒弃糟糕的策略，我们不仅需要正视自己的错误，还要确保能够流畅地运用可行的替代方案。

Strategies for Unlearning

重新学习的策略

Unlearning isn’t easy. It requires not only the investment to practice new strategies until they can compete with old habits, but also the emotional punch of accepting a decline in your temporary performance. Despite these difficulties, we often face situations where unlearning is necessary. Bad habits may have taken root early in practice that require correcting; a change in the environment, industry, or our own bodies may require doing things differently than we’re used to and sometimes the path to proficiency itself takes non-monotonic detours in performance, as we stumble through the awkward transition between naivety and mastery. Here are a few tactics to make unlearning more successful.

摒弃旧习并非易事。这不仅需要投入时间练习新策略，直至其足以与旧习惯抗衡，还需要承受暂时表现下滑带来的情绪冲击。尽管困难重重，我们常常会遇到必须摒弃旧习的情况。坏习惯可能在早期实践中就已经根深蒂固，需要加以纠正；环境、行业或自身身体的变化可能要求我们改变以往的做事方式；有时，通往精通的道路本身也并非一帆风顺，我们会在从懵懂到精通的过渡阶段磕磕绊绊。以下是一些有助于更有效地摒弃旧习的策略。

Tactic #1: Introduce New Constraints

策略一：引入新的限制条件

Old habits of thinking can exert a gravity on your performance. You fall back into routines, even if you’re trying to do something original. You can prevent that backsliding by changing the task constraints so performing the skill in the old way is impossible. Sometimes these constraints can take the form of prohibitions against certain kinds of actions—writing an essay without using any adverbs or trying to paint a picture without using color. In other cases, the constraints can be requirements for action. Hitting a tennis shot using an undersize racquet face forces you to hit balls in the center. Constraints are a hallmark of good design practices, in part because the space of possible useful solutions is so large that absent any restrictions, stale ideas may overwhelm the search for original options.

旧有的思维习惯会拖累你的表现。即使你想做一些原创的事情，也会不自觉地回到老路。你可以通过改变任务限制来防止这种退步，使你无法用旧的方式完成任务。有时，这些限制可以表现为禁止某些类型的行为——比如写文章时不使用任何副词，或者尝试画一幅画时不使用颜色。在其他情况下，这些限制可以是对行为的要求。例如，使用尺寸偏小的球拍击球会迫使你击中球的中心。限制是优秀设计实践的标志，部分原因是，可能的有效解决方案空间非常庞大，如果没有限制，陈旧的想法可能会淹没对创新方案的探索。

Designed by a coach, constraints can be chosen to counteract an unwanted tendency in your performance. Deliberate instruction on how to move your body, by moving you back to the cognitive phase of learning, can have unwanted side effects in the fluency of your performance. In golf, the “yips” are a common phenomenon where excessive attention on one’s own movements can ruin a golf swing. Good constraints, in contrast, can push a performer away from their bad habits without focusing attention on them.

教练设计的约束条件可以用来抵消你表现中的不良倾向。刻意指导如何移动身体，让你回到学习的认知阶段，可能会对你动作的流畅性产生意想不到的负面影响。在高尔夫球运动中，“易普症”（yips）是一种常见现象，过度关注自身动作反而会毁掉一次挥杆。相反，有效的约束条件可以帮助运动员摆脱不良习惯，而无需刻意关注这些习惯本身。

Tactic #2: Find a Coach

策略二：寻找教练

A weakness of self-directed efforts at improvement is that it’s often impossible to simultaneously monitor your own performance and actually use the skill. “Feel is not real” is a piece of golf-improvement lore that points to the fact that performers frequently have misconceptions about how their own body is moving during a swing. A putter may think he’s barely holding on to the grip, but he’s actually strangling the club. A golfer teeing off may imagine he’s rotating all the way through, but instead is only bringing the club halfway to where it needs to be. Our distorted self-image makes improvement difficult.

自我提升的一个弱点在于，往往无法同时监控自身表现并实际运用所学技能。“感觉并不真实”是高尔夫球技提升界的一句名言，它指出，球员们常常对挥杆时身体的运动方式存在误解。推杆者可能认为自己只是轻轻握住杆柄，但实际上却紧紧地勒住了球杆。开球者可能以为自己已经完成了完整的旋转，但实际上却只挥杆了一半。这种扭曲的自我认知使得提升变得困难重重。

Coaching and tutoring can make a major difference, even if the person you’re hiring isn’t better than you are. Tiger Woods worked extensively with coaches who were much worse golfers than he was. Because they can observe what you’re doing, without actually needing to devote the mental bandwidth to perform the skill themselves, they can offer insights into your performance.

教练和辅导能带来显著的改变，即使你聘请的教练水平不如你。泰格·伍兹就曾与许多球技远逊于他的教练合作。因为他们无需亲自练习，就能观察你的动作，从而为你提供宝贵的见解。

Tactic #3: Renovate Rather Than Rebuild

策略三：翻新而非重建

Ultimately, complete overhauls of a well-learned skill are probably the exception, rather than the rule. Few golfers could have performed at elite levels had they made such frequent revisions to their basic movements. It’s a testament both to Woods’s athletic skill and his work ethic that he was able to overcome those odds. In most cases, we’re probably better off augmenting or modifying the foundation we’ve built upon, rather than tearing things down and starting from scratch. Whether it’s a golf swing or a scientific worldview, the safest option is usually to make changes smoothly—seek the ridge between mountains rather than recklessly climb down to the valley below. Like the ship of Theseus, whose wooden planks were replaced one by one until none of the original ship remained, radical shifts in perspective are easier to make by adjusting one piece at a time, rather than threatening to demolish the entire foundation.

归根结底，彻底改变一项熟练的技能或许是例外，而非普遍现象。如果高尔夫球手频繁地修改基本动作，恐怕很少有人还能保持顶尖水平。伍兹能够克服这些困难，既体现了他卓越的运动天赋，也证明了他勤奋刻苦的职业精神。在大多数情况下，我们最好是在已有的基础上进行改进或调整，而不是推倒重来。无论是高尔夫挥杆还是科学世界观，最稳妥的做法通常是循序渐进地进行改变——寻找山脊而非鲁莽地坠入谷底。就像忒修斯的船一样，木板一块一块地被替换，直到船身完全消失；观点上的根本性转变，与其威胁要摧毁整个根基，不如一次调整一个部分，这样更容易实现。

The need for unlearning isn’t limited to intellectual ideas or athletic abilities. Ultimately, our emotions often provide the biggest barriers to making improvements. Fears and anxieties hold us back from learning. Feedback matters not just for correcting misconceptions, but for testing out our own apprehensions.

需要摒弃旧观念的领域不仅限于知识层面或运动技能。归根结底，我们的情绪往往是进步的最大障碍。恐惧和焦虑会阻碍我们学习。反馈不仅有助于纠正错误观念，还能帮助我们检验自身的担忧。

# ↩

Chapter 12

第十二章

Fears Fade with Exposure

恐惧会随着接触而消退

One of the major weaknesses of all psychological theories is the assumption that people are highly vulnerable to threats and stress. The theories are designed for creatures more timorous than human beings.

所有心理学理论的一个主要缺陷在于，它们都假设人类极易受到威胁和压力的影响。这些理论是为比人类更胆怯的生物设计的。

—Stanley Rachman, psychologist

——斯坦利·拉赫曼，心理学家

  • Why do many of the steps we take to avoid anxieties make them worse?
    为什么我们为避免焦虑而采取的许多措施反而会加剧焦虑？
  • How do we get outside our comfort zone?
    我们如何才能走出舒适区？
  • Is courage the same as fearlessness?
    勇气和无畏是一回事吗？

I n the years before the Second World War, as conflict with Germany came to be seen as inevitable, leaders began to confront the possibility of a new kind of danger: planes were likely to drop bombs over major populated centers. Air raids during the First World War had been limited. Only three hundred tons of bombs had dropped on London in the entirety of the conflict. In the interwar decades, technology advanced, bringing with it a new scale of destruction. Planners anticipated Germany might begin with a sudden blitzkrieg, dropping 3,500 tons in the first twenty-four hours of an assault, with hundreds more dropped daily for weeks. Casualties were predicted to be in the hundreds of thousands. Whole cities might be destroyed after only a few weeks.

在第二次世界大战爆发前的几年里，随着与德国的冲突被视为不可避免，各国领导人开始正视一种新型危险的可能性：飞机很可能会对人口稠密的主要城市投掷炸弹。第一次世界大战期间的空袭规模有限。整个战争期间，伦敦仅遭受了300吨炸弹的袭击。而在两次世界大战之间的几十年里，科技飞速发展，带来了前所未有的破坏规模。策划者们预料到，德国可能会发动闪电战，在进攻的最初24小时内投下3500吨炸弹，并在接下来的几周内每天投下数百吨。预计伤亡人数将达数十万。短短几周内，整座城市就可能被夷为平地。

Beyond the physical devastation, politicians, leaders, and psychologists all agreed that massive panic was inevitable. Addressing the House of Commons, former British prime minister Stanley Baldwin articulated these fears: “I think it is well also for the man in the street to realize that there is no power on earth that can protect him from being bombed. Whatever people may tell him, the bomber will always get through.” In a public speech, Winston Churchill projected that three to four million people might flee major metropolitan centers in the aftermath of an attack. Tens of thousands of police officers were requested to prevent surging crowds from trampling each other in the inevitable exodus. A group of esteemed psychiatrists in London prepared a report arguing that psychological casualties were likely to exceed physical casualties three to one. The expert consensus was expressed best when the well-known director of a London medical clinic said it was “ clear to everyone that there must be an immediate inundation with cases of neurosis on the declaration of war—and certainly after the first air raid.”

除了物质上的破坏之外，政界人士、领导人和心理学家一致认为，大规模恐慌不可避免。英国前首相斯坦利·鲍德温在下议院发表讲话时，表达了这种担忧：“我认为，普通民众也应该意识到，世界上没有任何力量能够保护他们免受轰炸。无论人们如何劝说，炸弹袭击者总能得逞。”温斯顿·丘吉尔在一次公开演讲中预测，袭击过后，可能有三四百万人逃离主要都市中心。数万名警察被要求部署警力，以防止在不可避免的逃亡过程中，拥挤的人群互相践踏。伦敦一群受人尊敬的精神病学家撰写了一份报告，指出心理创伤很可能是身体创伤的三倍。伦敦一家知名医疗诊所的主任对专家们的共识表达得最为透彻，他说：“每个人都清楚，宣战后，尤其是在第一次空袭之后，必然会立即出现大量神经症病例。”

Yet as war began and bombs fell, no mass panic actually occurred. “ To the considerable surprise of almost everyone, the psychological casualties were few, despite the death and destruction caused by the attacks,” writes psychologist Stanley Rachman. In one report, of the 578 casualties hospitalized after a period of heavy bombing, only two were suffering primarily from psychological symptoms. In another, only fifteen of 1,100 patients in a medical clinic showed obvious psychological disorders. Far from being inundated with traumatized neurotics, the number of patients admitted to mental hospitals in 1940 was actually less than in 1938, with a further decrease in 1941. “ One point emerges very clearly,” writes psychologist Irving Janis: “there was a definite decline in overt fear reactions as the air blitz continued, even though raids became heavier and more destructive.”

然而，随着战争爆发和炸弹落下，并未出现大规模恐慌。“几乎所有人都感到惊讶，尽管空袭造成了大量人员伤亡和财产损失，但心理创伤却很少，”心理学家斯坦利·拉赫曼写道。一份报告显示，在一段猛烈轰炸后入院的578名伤员中，只有两人主要患有心理症状。另一份报告显示，在一家诊所的1100名患者中，只有15人表现出明显的心理障碍。1940年精神病院的收治人数远未达到1938年的水平，反而比1938年有所下降，1941年更是进一步减少。“有一点非常明显，”心理学家欧文·贾尼斯写道：“随着空袭的持续，尽管空袭的强度和破坏性不断增加，但人们的公开恐惧反应却明显下降。”

Witnesses to daily life during the Blitz lends further support to the resiliency of ordinary people. Philip Vernon, who surveyed dozens of doctors and psychologists working during the war, observed that “[n]ear the beginning of the war the mere sounding of the sirens was enough to send large numbers to shelters.” However, as the bombings intensified, “Londoners were generally taking no notice of sirens at all, unless accompanied by the noise of planes, gunfire, or bombs, and in some areas it is a social faux pas to mention the fact that they have sounded.” Another observer at the time noted, “The calm behavior of the average individual continues to be amazing. Commuting suburbanites, who up to yesterday had experienced worse bombardments than people living in Central London, placidly bragged to fellow passengers on the morning trains about the size of bomb craters in their neighborhoods, as in a more peaceful summer they would have bragged about their roses and squash.”

亲历闪电战期间日常生活的人们进一步印证了普通民众的韧性。菲利普·弗农曾调查过数十位在战时工作的医生和心理学家，他观察到，“战争初期，仅仅是警报声就足以让大量民众躲进防空洞。”然而，随着轰炸加剧，“伦敦人通常对警报声置若罔闻，除非伴随着飞机、枪炮或炸弹的轰鸣声；在某些地区，提及警报声甚至是一种社交禁忌。”另一位当时的观察者写道，“普通民众的冷静表现令人惊叹。那些直到昨天还遭受着比伦敦市中心居民更严重轰炸的郊区通勤者，却平静地在早班火车上向其他乘客炫耀着自家街区的弹坑大小，就像在更平静的夏天，他们会炫耀自己的玫瑰和南瓜一样。”

Britain’s stoic reactions were hardly unique. Survivors of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki also experienced surprisingly low rates of mental disturbance. Similar reports came from bombed German cities, where a plurality of respondents to one survey indicated they felt less afraid after successive bombings. In a more recent example, Philip Saigh happened to be conducting a study on anxiety in Beirut, Lebanon, shortly before the ten-week siege by Israeli forces in 1982. Following up with the study participants, he found no difference in anxiety levels before and after the invasion. In addition, those who had not been evacuated showed a marked decline in fear reactions to war-related stimuli. Hysterical panic during disasters is more common in popular imagination than in reality. As Lee Clark reviews in his article “Panic: Myth or Reality?” the Hollywood image of people stampeding over each other in an emergency isn’t based in fact. “ After five decades of studying scores of disasters such as floods, earthquakes, and tornadoes, one of the strongest findings is that people rarely lose control.”

英国人的冷静应对并非个例。广岛和长崎原子弹爆炸的幸存者也表现出令人惊讶的低精神障碍发生率。德国遭受轰炸的城市也出现了类似的报告，一项调查显示，大多数受访者表示，在连续遭受轰炸后，他们的恐惧感反而降低了。最近的一个例子是，菲利普·赛格（Philip Saigh）在1982年以色列军队对黎巴嫩贝鲁特进行为期十周的围困前不久，恰好在那里进行一项关于焦虑的研究。在对研究参与者进行后续调查后，他发现入侵前后他们的焦虑水平并无差异。此外，那些没有被疏散的人对与战争相关的刺激表现出明显的恐惧反应下降。灾难中的歇斯底里恐慌更多地存在于大众的想象中，而非现实。正如李·克拉克（Lee Clark）在其文章《恐慌：神话还是现实？》中所评论的那样，好莱坞电影中人们在紧急情况下互相践踏的画面并非基于事实。 “经过五十年对洪水、地震和龙卷风等数十起灾害的研究，最有力的发现之一是，人们很少会失去控制。”

The experience of Britons during the Blitz illustrates an important psychological principle: fears tend to diminish with exposure. Experiencing fear, without suffering direct harm, reduces fear in similar future situations. Even faced with the terror of nightly bombing raids, the typical response was not escalating anxiety, but adaptation.

英国人在闪电战期间的经历揭示了一个重要的心理学原理：恐惧往往会随着接触次数的增加而减轻。即使没有遭受直接伤害，体验恐惧也能降低未来类似情境下的恐惧感。即使面对夜间轰炸的恐怖，人们的典型反应也不是焦虑加剧，而是适应。

Learning Fear and Safety

学习恐惧与安全

Fear often looms larger than any intellectual difficulty in our efforts at improvement: The person who spends years studying French but doesn’t feel comfortable conversing during a trip to Paris. The student with test anxiety who feels his stomach churn before opening the practice exams. The job candidate who turns down a work opportunity she doesn’t feel “ready” for—even when she’s completely qualified. How many of us completely avoid entire skills or subjects because the thought of practicing them fills us with dread? Despite these difficulties, we often fail to understand our fears. More importantly, we fail to see how the strategies we use to reduce anxiety frequently make it worse.

恐惧往往在我们提升自我的过程中，比任何智力上的困难都更加强大：有人花了数年时间学习法语，却在巴黎旅行时不敢开口交谈；有的学生在打开模拟试题之前就感到焦虑不安；有的求职者即使完全胜任，也会因为觉得自己“还没准备好”而拒绝工作机会。我们当中有多少人因为害怕练习某些技能或科目而彻底放弃？尽管存在这些困难，我们却常常无法理解自己的恐惧。更重要的是，我们看不到那些用来缓解焦虑的策略往往会加剧焦虑。

The origin of our anxieties has long been a popular source of speculation within psychology. Sigmund Freud famously claimed anxieties were infantile impulses, repressed in the subconscious. William James believed fears were innate, ripening with appropriate experience. The father of behaviorism, John Watson, argued that fears came from a simple process of conditioning. In his infamous experiment with Little Albert, he repeatedly showed the eleven-month-old a white rat while striking a steel bar behind the boy to produce a loud sound. As the fright of the noise became associated with the rat, the child came to fear not only mice, but all sorts of white, furry things. The conditioning theory of fear helps explain a divergence in reactions to bombings during the Blitz. Those who experienced a “near miss”—being inside a building that was bombed or witnessing a fatal injury—often had their fears resurge temporarily. In contrast, those who experienced a “remote miss”—hearing the distant rumble of explosions but facing no personal harm—were more likely to have their fears diminish. Whether fears worsened or alleviated with exposure depended, in part, on how direct the danger was.

焦虑的起源一直是心理学领域热议的话题。西格蒙德·弗洛伊德曾提出，焦虑是婴儿时期被压抑在潜意识中的冲动。威廉·詹姆斯则认为恐惧是与生俱来的，会随着适当的经验而逐渐成熟。行为主义之父约翰·华生认为，恐惧源于简单的条件反射过程。在他著名的“小艾伯特”实验中，他反复向11个月大的艾伯特展示一只白鼠，同时敲击他身后的一根钢条发出巨响。随着这种巨响带来的恐惧与老鼠联系起来，孩子不仅害怕老鼠，还害怕各种白色毛茸茸的东西。恐惧的条件反射理论有助于解释二战期间人们对轰炸反应的差异。那些“侥幸逃脱”的人——例如身处被炸毁的建筑物内或目睹致命伤亡——往往会经历短暂的恐惧复发。相比之下，那些经历过“远距离爆炸”（听到远处爆炸的隆隆声但未受到人身伤害）的人，其恐惧感更有可能减轻。恐惧感是加剧还是减轻，部分取决于危险的直接程度。

The conditioning theory of fear, however, isn’t without difficulties. Echoing William James, psychologist Martin Seligman argued we are predisposed to acquire some fears, but not others. Far more people have phobias of snakes than electrical outlets, even though more people have had a shock than a snakebite. Similarly, fears can arrive without an obvious episode of conditioning. Fears of air raids were highest in Britain before the war—when no one had yet experienced an attack. While some phobias and anxieties can be linked to a particularly traumatic experience, others seem to develop without provocation. Fears can be acquired vicariously, through watching someone else’s fearful reaction, and through verbalization, such as when we fear being mugged in a particular part of town after being warned it is dangerous. Avoiding danger is an evolutionary imperative. It makes sense that we would have multiple pathways to fear, beyond those that require direct experience. An animal that could only learn about a danger after a brush with death wouldn’t stick around long enough to have many offspring. Modern theories of anxiety place the blame on a mixture of factors, including specific experiences, general stressors, and innate predispositions.

然而，恐惧的条件反射理论并非完美无缺。心理学家马丁·塞利格曼呼应威廉·詹姆斯的观点，认为我们天生容易习得某些恐惧，但并非总是如此。患有蛇恐惧症的人远多于患有电源插座恐惧症的人，尽管被电击过的人比被蛇咬过的人多得多。同样，恐惧的产生可能并非源于明显的条件反射事件。二战前，英国人对空袭的恐惧程度最高——而当时还没有人经历过空袭。虽然有些恐惧症和焦虑症可能与某种创伤性经历有关，但另一些似乎会在没有任何诱因的情况下发展。恐惧可以通过间接方式习得，例如通过观察他人的恐惧反应，或者通过言语表达，比如当我们被告知某个地方很危险后，就会害怕在那里被抢劫。规避危险是进化的必然要求。因此，除了需要直接经验的途径之外，我们拥有多种产生恐惧的途径也就不足为奇了。如果一种动物只有在死里逃生后才能意识到危险，那么它就无法存活足够长的时间繁衍后代。现代焦虑理论将焦虑归咎于多种因素的综合作用，包括特定经历、一般压力源和先天倾向。

While the conditioning theory of fears doesn’t offer a tidy explanation for how fear originates, it does provide a useful starting point in considering what sustains our anxieties. According to Orval Mowrer’s influential two-factor theory, irrational anxieties persist because we try to avoid them. When we encounter a perceived threat, the natural response is to find a way to neutralize it. The person who feels anxious about giving speeches finds an excuse to get out of presenting at work. The student who feels queasy around equations avoids taking classes with mathematics. The anxious introvert stays home from parties. Escaping from fear, however, has two side effects that make anxiety harder to eradicate. The first difficulty is that by avoiding the potentially dangerous stimuli, we can’t get any new information about whether the imagined threat is significant in reality. By avoiding feedback, the conditioned association between a feared stimulus and danger cannot be extinguished. Like an insect trapped in amber, our fears are preserved because we don’t allow ourselves to encounter disconfirming evidence about them. The second difficulty is that avoidance becomes self-reinforcing. Imagine a situation that makes you anxious (for example, an exam, speech, or job interview). In worrying about it, you take some action to reduce the perceived threat (for example, drop the class, find someone else to present your work, or pass up the job opportunity). The anxiety is now gone and you feel relieved. Yet that relief can act as a psychological reward, strengthening avoidance behavior in the future. This type of conditioning is known as negative reinforcement, as it’s the removal of a potential pain that acts as a positive signal to your central nervous system. Avoidance perpetuates anxiety.

虽然恐惧的条件反射理论无法对恐惧的起源给出简洁的解释，但它确实为我们思考焦虑的根源提供了一个有用的起点。根据奥瓦尔·莫勒颇具影响力的双因素理论，非理性焦虑之所以持续存在，是因为我们试图逃避它们。当我们遇到感知到的威胁时，自然的反应是找到方法来消除它。例如，害怕演讲的人会找借口逃避工作中的汇报；害怕方程式的学生会避免选修数学课；焦虑的内向者会选择待在家里不去参加聚会。然而，逃避恐惧会产生两个副作用，使焦虑更难根除。首先，通过逃避潜在的危险刺激，我们无法获得任何关于想象中的威胁在现实中是否真的严重的新信息。通过避免反馈，恐惧刺激与危险之间的条件反射联系就无法消除。就像琥珀里的昆虫一样，我们的恐惧之所以被保存下来，是因为我们不让自己接触到与之相悖的证据。第二个难题在于，回避行为会自我强化。想象一下，某种情境让你感到焦虑（例如考试、演讲或面试）。在担忧的过程中，你采取了一些措施来降低这种感知到的威胁（例如退课、找别人代你展示作品，或者放弃工作机会）。焦虑消失了，你感到轻松。然而，这种轻松感本身就是一种心理奖励，会在未来强化你的回避行为。这种条件反射被称为负强化，因为消除潜在的痛苦会向你的中枢神经系统发出积极的信号。回避只会加剧焦虑。

Avoidance doesn’t only include a literal escape. Obsessive-compulsive disorder is characterized by engaging in complex rituals to avoid feared consequences. Washing your hands when they get dirty is good, but washing them every fifteen minutes is excessive. In this case, the ritualized handwashing acts like an avoidance behavior: the person feels anxiety about being unclean, immediately washes their hands multiple times, and the perceived threat subsides. The handwashing behavior is reinforced in the future and the person is prevented from experiencing feedback that would show it was unnecessary. Of course, not all avoidance behaviors are unhelpful. The same process is at work when we feel anxious about a big exam and respond by studying harder. A person who avoids standing too close to the edge of a cliff may be entirely reasonable, rather than suffering from acrophobia. Anxiety and avoidance aren’t defects of our design, but profoundly useful features. Avoidance behaviors only become a problem when they interfere with our lives. When you take steps that do little to neutralize the danger, or when the cost of taking preventative measures is completely out of proportion with the actual risks, anxiety is disruptive rather than adaptive.

回避行为并非仅仅指字面意义上的逃避。强迫症的特征之一是进行复杂的仪式性行为来避免恐惧的后果。手脏了就洗手是好事，但每隔十五分钟就洗一次就过头了。在这种情况下，仪式化的洗手行为就如同回避行为：患者会因为担心自己不干净而感到焦虑，于是立即多次洗手，这种焦虑感便会消退。洗手行为在未来会得到强化，患者也因此避免了体验到这种行为其实没有必要的反馈。当然，并非所有的回避行为都是无益的。当我们为即将到来的重要考试感到焦虑时，我们会更加努力地学习，这其中也运用了同样的原理。一个人避免站在悬崖边太近，这可能完全合情合理，而非患有恐高症。焦虑和回避并非我们自身设计的缺陷，而是极其有用的功能。只有当回避行为干扰到我们的生活时，它们才会成为问题。当你采取的措施对消除危险作用甚微，或者采取预防措施的成本与实际风险完全不成比例时，焦虑就具有破坏性而不是适应性。

Exposure diminishes anxiety through processes of extinction and habituation. The term extinction comes from animal learning research. Ring a bell with food and a dog will learn to salivate from the bell alone. However, if you ring the bell enough times without bringing food, eventually the original learned response extinguishes. Similarly, according to the conditioning theory of fear, our anxieties are learned associations between signals and danger. By exposing ourselves to the signal, without experiencing danger, we revise our expectations. As a result, the original fear learning is suppressed. The second mechanism for exposure is through habituation. This occurs when a stimulus that naturally evokes a particular response has a diminishing impact as you experience it more often. A loud sound may cause you to jump instinctively, but as you hear the same loud sound over and over, your jumpiness fades. To understand the distinction between extinction and habituation, consider overcoming a fear of doing stand-up comedy by going to an open-mic night. Extinction would mean going onstage and realizing that, contrary to expectations, being humiliated wasn’t actually so likely. Habituation would mean that after being booed offstage a dozen times, you aren’t so bothered by bombing during your comedy routine.

暴露疗法通过消退和习惯化过程来减轻焦虑。消退一词源于动物学习研究。例如，摇铃时铃铛旁边放着食物，狗就会学会仅凭铃铛声就流口水。然而，如果你反复摇铃而不提供食物，最终最初的习得反应就会消失。类似地，根据恐惧的条件反射理论，我们的焦虑是信号与危险之间习得的关联。通过让自己暴露于信号中，而不经历危险，我们会修正自己的预期。结果，最初的恐惧习得就被抑制了。暴露疗法的第二个机制是通过习惯化。当一个自然引发特定反应的刺激随着你经历的次数增加而减弱时，就会发生习惯化。一声巨响可能会让你本能地跳起来，但当你反复听到同样的声音时，你的惊吓感就会消失。为了理解消退和习惯化之间的区别，不妨想想如何通过参加开放麦之夜来克服对脱口秀的恐惧。灭绝意味着你走上舞台后才意识到，与预期相反，被羞辱的可能性其实并没有那么大。习惯化则意味着，在被嘘下台十几次之后，你对喜剧表演失败已经习以为常了。

Exposure to fear without actual danger results in learning safety. A tempting assumption would be that the learned safety works by erasing the original fear conditioning. In this way, just as learning to fear a neutral stimulus can be seen as a conditioning process, extinguishing that fear might be seen as a gradual “forgetting” of the original association. Unfortunately, this doesn’t appear to be the case. Instead, learning safety appears to be a process of building a new memory, using distinct neural circuitry, that inhibits the original fear response. Evidence for the two-memory view comes from research showing that, while exposure does indeed reduce fears, acquired fears appear to be more general and durable than learned safety. The result is that fears that have been extinguished can return, either when we face the fear in a new context, as time elapses between the episodes of exposure, or even just from general stressors that have nothing to do with the original fear. Consistent with this theory, Vernon observed that fear of air raids tended to return after a prolonged reprieve from bombings, as if the inoculation against anxiety had partly worn off. Exposure works better when it is provided in a broad variety of contexts and refreshed periodically. Some research even suggests that occasional reinforcement—where feared consequences sometimes do occur during exposure— results in more durable benefits than exposure where danger is always absent, as this makes the learning of safety more robust to an unlucky, aversive experience.

在没有实际危险的情况下接触恐惧会导致习得安全感。一个容易让人产生误解的假设是，习得的安全感是通过消除最初的恐惧条件反射来实现的。这样看来，就像学习恐惧中性刺激可以被视为一种条件反射过程一样，消除这种恐惧也可以被视为逐渐“遗忘”最初的关联。然而，事实并非如此。相反，习得安全感似乎是一个利用不同的神经回路构建新记忆的过程，这种新记忆会抑制最初的恐惧反应。支持“双重记忆”观点的证据来自一项研究，该研究表明，虽然接触恐惧确实可以减少恐惧，但习得的恐惧似乎比习得的安全感更普遍、更持久。因此，已经消除的恐惧可能会复发，无论是在新的情境中面对恐惧，还是在两次接触恐惧之间的时间间隔过长，甚至仅仅是来自与最初恐惧无关的一般压力源。与此理论相符，弗农观察到，在长时间没有空袭之后，人们对空袭的恐惧往往会再次出现，仿佛对焦虑的免疫力部分消退了。暴露疗法在多种情境下进行并定期强化效果更佳。一些研究甚至表明，偶尔强化——即在暴露过程中有时会出现令人恐惧的后果——比始终没有危险的暴露疗法带来更持久的益处，因为这能使安全感的习得更能抵御不幸的、令人不快的经历。

Is Exposure Enough to Overcome Fears?

接触恐惧是否足以克服恐惧？

The therapeutic benefits of exposure have long been appreciated, even if they haven’t always been understood. The English philosopher John Locke prescribed a regimen of gradually escalating encounters to deal with an animal phobia in his treatise Some Thoughts Concerning Education . Likewise, the German poet Johann Wolfgang von Goethe overcame a youthful fear of heights by repeatedly standing atop a small ledge in a local cathedral. After completing these exercises, he was able to enjoy mountain climbing and ascend tall buildings without trepidation. Yet it wasn’t until Joseph Wolpe introduced his protocol of systematic desensitization in the 1950s that exposure became a regular part of the clinical treatment for anxiety.

暴露疗法的治疗益处早已为人所知，尽管人们并非一直都理解其原理。英国哲学家约翰·洛克在其著作《教育论》中，就曾提出一套循序渐进的暴露疗法来克服动物恐惧症。同样，德国诗人约翰·沃尔夫冈·冯·歌德也曾克服了年轻时的恐高症，他反复站在当地一座大教堂的狭窄窗台上。完成这些练习后，他便能享受登山的乐趣，并能毫无畏惧地攀登高楼。然而，直到20世纪50年代约瑟夫·沃尔普提出系统脱敏疗法后，暴露疗法才成为焦虑症临床治疗的常规手段。

Wolpe worked with patients to help develop a fear hierarchy. This was an ordered list of situations starting with those that caused mild discomfort, progressing all the way to those provoking extreme terror. By gradually experiencing these situations, along with relaxation techniques, patients’ fears diminished. Wolpe’s theory was that relaxation and anxiety inhibited each other, so by using breathing techniques to relax the patient while they faced stressful stimuli, this would counteract the stressful association. Despite the usefulness of the protocol, the theory of reciprocal inhibition wasn’t borne out. Subsequent research found that relaxation, while potentially helpful, was not necessary to get the required effect. Exposure still worked even if stress levels remained high throughout.

沃尔普帮助患者建立恐惧等级。这是一个按顺序排列的情境清单，从引起轻微不适的情境开始，逐步过渡到引发极度恐惧的情境。通过逐步体验这些情境，并结合放松技巧，患者的恐惧感逐渐减轻。沃尔普的理论是，放松和焦虑相互抑制，因此，在患者面对压力刺激时，通过呼吸技巧帮助他们放松，可以抵消压力带来的联想。尽管该方案有效，但交互抑制理论并未得到证实。后续研究发现，放松虽然可能有所帮助，但并非达到预期效果的必要条件。即使压力水平始终很高，暴露疗法仍然有效。

Around the same time as Wolpe’s development of systematic desensitization, flooding and implosive therapies also applied exposure for treating fear. Instead of gradually ramping up the exposure, flooding presented a patient with their most-feared situation from the outset and prevented them from escaping. A person with a phobia of dogs might be locked in a room with a barking dog, unable to leave until their fear subsided. Implosive therapy was similar to flooding, although usually done with highly vivid fantasy scenarios, guided by a therapist, rather than real-life exposure. Both theories operated under the assumption that fully activating a fear was necessary to refute it, and that milder forms of exposure might fail to have the full therapeutic effect. Once again, scrutinizing research upheld the general value of exposure within these treatments, but extreme fear reactions were not necessary. Exposure came to be seen as the active ingredient, with the debate between diving or wading into fear shifting to the periphery.

在沃尔普发展出系统脱敏疗法的同时，暴露疗法和内爆疗法也开始运用暴露疗法治疗恐惧症。与逐步增加暴露强度不同，暴露疗法从一开始就将患者置于他们最恐惧的情境中，并阻止他们逃脱。例如，一个患有狗恐惧症的人可能会被锁在一个房间里，房间里有一只吠叫的狗，直到恐惧消退才能离开。内爆疗法与暴露疗法类似，但通常是在治疗师的引导下，使用高度生动的幻想场景，而不是现实生活中的暴露。这两种理论都基于这样的假设：必须充分激活恐惧才能克服它，而较温和的暴露方式可能无法达到完整的治疗效果。然而，严谨的研究再次证实了暴露疗法在这些治疗中的普遍价值，但并非必须出现极端的恐惧反应。暴露逐渐被视为有效成分，而关于应该深入恐惧还是浅尝辄止的争论则逐渐淡出人们的视野。

As cognitive approaches came to overtake behaviorism in psychology departments, therapies based on examining thoughts and beliefs eclipsed purely behavioral techniques. Cognitive therapy emphasized not just the behaviors of patients using the language of stimulus and response, but the contents of patients’ thinking. A social phobic’s aversion to parties, for instance, is not just habitual avoidance, but also depends on a distorted worldview, such as the belief that social rejection is likely. Despite its theoretical foundation and appeal to common sense, evidence for the additional efficacy of cognitive therapy beyond exposure has often been weak. Cognitive-behavioral therapies, which usually include both exposure as well as talk therapy, tend not to outperform therapies based on exposure alone. More recently, mindfulness-based approaches to anxiety have gained in popularity, but it remains to be seen whether they can outperform simple exposure.

随着认知疗法在心理学领域逐渐取代行为主义，基于对思维和信念的探究的疗法也超越了纯粹的行为疗法。认知疗法不仅强调患者的行为（运用刺激与反应的语言），更关注患者的思维内容。例如，社交恐惧症患者对聚会的厌恶并非仅仅是习惯性的回避，还源于一种扭曲的世界观，例如认为社交排斥是必然的。尽管认知疗法拥有理论基础并符合常识，但其在暴露疗法之外的额外疗效证据往往不足。认知行为疗法通常包含暴露疗法和谈话疗法，但其疗效往往不优于单纯的暴露疗法。近年来，基于正念的焦虑症疗法越来越受欢迎，但其疗效是否优于简单的暴露疗法仍有待观察。

An explanation for the surprising lack of effectiveness of therapies that seek to change beliefs, induce relaxation, or alter thinking patterns without exposure is that threats are processed by different neural circuitry than those that underlie our consciously accessible memories and beliefs. “Talk therapy requires conscious retrieval of memories and thinking about their origins and/or implications and thus depends on working memory circuits of the lateral prefrontal cortex. By contrast, therapies involving exposure depend on medial prefrontal areas that contribute to extinction, the process on which exposure is modeled,” explains neuroscientist Joseph LeDoux. “[T]he fact that medial frontal areas connect with the amygdala, whereas the latter areas do not, might account for why it is easier and faster to treat fears, phobias and anxiety with exposure-based approaches.” Dissecting your beliefs, in other words, may not be helpful if anxiety is being sustained by neural circuitry in a different part of your brain. Despite this neuroanatomical distinction, LeDoux notes that the relationship between exposure as practiced in therapeutic contexts and the extinction studies done with animals is a complicated one. Encouraging someone to expose themselves to a feared situation generally requires talking. It may turn out that the explanation for the efficacy of exposure does depend on consciously accessible beliefs and expectations, but that the best way to change those is through direct experience rather than discussing them. Adjusting consciously held beliefs may also be useful for sustaining the therapeutic benefits of exposure, helping to protect against relapse. Nonetheless, in keeping with the view that fear is driven in part by unconscious neural circuitry, researchers have found that subliminal exposure, when the feared stimulus is masked so it cannot be perceived consciously, can result in reduced avoidance behaviors. Simply talking about your anxieties is rarely sufficient to overcome them.

那些试图改变信念、诱导放松或改变思维模式而不进行暴露疗法的疗法效果不佳，其原因在于，威胁是由与我们意识中可提取的记忆和信念不同的神经回路处理的。“谈话疗法需要有意识地提取记忆，并思考其起源和/或影响，因此依赖于外侧前额叶皮层的工作记忆回路。相比之下，暴露疗法依赖于内侧前额叶区域，这些区域负责消退过程，而暴露疗法正是以此为模型，”神经科学家约瑟夫·勒杜解释道。“内侧前额叶区域与杏仁核相连，而后者则没有，这或许可以解释为什么基于暴露疗法的治疗方法更容易、更快速地治疗恐惧、恐惧症和焦虑。”换句话说，如果焦虑是由大脑其他区域的神经回路维持的，那么剖析你的信念可能并无帮助。尽管存在这种神经解剖学上的区别，勒杜克斯指出，治疗情境中实践的暴露疗法与动物消退研究之间的关系十分复杂。鼓励一个人暴露于恐惧情境通常需要谈话。暴露疗法的有效性可能确实取决于意识层面可及的信念和预期，但改变这些信念和预期的最佳方法是通过直接体验，而不是讨论它们。调整意识层面持有的信念也可能有助于维持暴露疗法的治疗效果，从而有助于防止复发。然而，与恐惧部分由无意识神经回路驱动的观点一致，研究人员发现，当恐惧刺激被掩盖，使其无法被意识感知时，阈下暴露可以减少回避行为。仅仅谈论你的焦虑很少足以克服它们。

Despite the difficulties in finding consistent enhancements to exposure, the basic protocol remains remarkably successful. A meta-analysis looking at the use of exposure treatment for specific phobias found large effect sizes compared to both placebo and no-treatment conditions. In addition, the authors found that therapies incorporating exposure outperformed alternative therapies that did not. Other meta-analyses draw similar conclusions with social phobias, generalized anxiety, panic, and obsessive-compulsive disorder—with effect sizes roughly equal to those seen from pharmacological interventions. Exposure has even been successfully used to treat post-traumatic stress disorder, which is notable in light of the widespread belief that exposure makes trauma worse. Patients aren’t more likely to drop out of therapies involving exposure and many patients find them to be credible and effective. Despite the strong experimental evidence for the benefits of exposure, researchers Jonathan Abramowitz, Brett Deacon, and Stephen Whiteside report that “the majority of patients with any anxiety disorder do not receive evidence-based psychotherapy; indeed, psychodynamic therapy is received as often as [cognitive-behavioral therapies].” Exposure works, even if it remains underused.

尽管在寻找持续增强暴露疗法效果的方法方面存在诸多困难，但其基本方案仍然取得了显著的成功。一项针对特定恐惧症暴露疗法的荟萃分析发现，与安慰剂组和无治疗组相比，暴露疗法具有显著的疗效。此外，研究人员还发现，包含暴露疗法的治疗方案优于不包含暴露疗法的其他疗法。其他荟萃分析也得出了类似的结论，这些结论适用于社交恐惧症、广泛性焦虑症、惊恐障碍和强迫症——其疗效与药物干预的效果大致相当。暴露疗法甚至已被成功用于治疗创伤后应激障碍，考虑到人们普遍认为暴露会加剧创伤，这一点尤为值得关注。患者在接受包含暴露疗法的治疗时，其退出率并不高，而且许多患者认为这些疗法可信且有效。尽管有强有力的实验证据表明暴露疗法有益，但研究人员乔纳森·阿布拉莫维茨、布雷特·迪肯和斯蒂芬·怀特塞德指出，“大多数焦虑症患者并未接受循证心理治疗；事实上，精神动力疗法与认知行为疗法一样常见。” 暴露疗法确实有效，尽管它仍未得到充分利用。

Fear and Mastery

恐惧与掌控

Fear deals a double blow to the learning process. First, because the natural impulse to anxiety is avoidance, we often fail to practice skills that scare us. The timid driver, unsure presenter, or math-phobic often go out of their way to avoid situations that might use those abilities. But failing to get enough practice also ensures that these skills remain disfluent and effortful—compounding the rationale for avoiding using them. Worse, anxiety crowds out space in our mind for thinking about a problem. Complex skills are harder to learn when we’re highly agitated because distracting worries fill up our limited working memory capacity.

恐惧对学习过程造成双重打击。首先，由于焦虑的自然反应是逃避，我们常常会因为害怕而不敢练习那些令我们恐惧的技能。胆怯的司机、不自信的演讲者或数学恐惧症患者往往会刻意回避可能需要运用这些技能的场合。然而，缺乏足够的练习也会导致这些技能始终不够流畅且费力——这更加深了我们逃避使用这些技能的理由。更糟糕的是，焦虑会占据我们思考问题的空间。当我们极度焦虑时，学习复杂的技能会更加困难，因为各种分散注意力的担忧会占据我们有限的工作记忆容量。

Overcoming anxiety isn’t easy, but exposure at least suggests an escape route. If we can expose ourselves to our apprehensions, in situations where the risks are modest, the fear reaction will eventually subside. Reducing fear, we find practice easier. Practice improves our performance and reduces the effort needed, further expanding the range of situations where it makes sense to use the skill. What was previously a self-reinforcing pattern of anxiety and avoidance can be replaced with increased confidence and enthusiasm.

克服焦虑并非易事，但暴露疗法至少提供了一条出路。如果我们能在风险适中的情境中直面恐惧，恐惧反应最终会消退。恐惧感降低后，练习也变得更加容易。练习能提升我们的表现，减少所需付出，从而进一步拓展运用这项技能的适用范围。原本自我强化的焦虑和回避模式，可以被增强的自信和热情所取代。

The difficulty, of course, is in switching from the pattern of avoidance toward the enthusiastic mindset of the person willing to face their fears. While the process of exposure can be daunting, I think fully accepting and understanding its theoretical rationale can help shift the decision to engage in it. Fears seem totally objective when we’re caught in their grasp. Public speaking simply is scary, rather than being a subjective response to an ambiguous situation. From such a position, it’s hard to fully appreciate how easy and natural it would be if we simply got onstage enough times.

当然，难点在于如何从回避的模式转变为积极面对恐惧的心态。虽然暴露疗法的过程可能令人畏惧，但我认为，充分接受并理解其理论依据有助于我们下定决心参与其中。当我们被恐惧所困扰时，恐惧似乎完全客观存在。公开演讲本身就令人恐惧，而不是对某种模糊情境的主观反应。从这个角度来看，我们很难真正体会到，如果我们多上几次台，公开演讲将会多么轻松自然。

Accepting the logic of exposure doesn’t remove the need for bravery. As we’ve seen, talking through fears doesn’t usually eliminate them. However, if we appreciate how even objectively terrifying situations, like the wartime bombing of the Blitz, could become normal through repeated exposure, perhaps we can have the courage to take steps in confronting the far milder fears that hold us back.

接受“暴露疗法”的逻辑并不意味着我们就不需要勇气。正如我们所见，倾诉恐惧通常并不能消除恐惧。然而，如果我们能够理解，即使是像二战时期伦敦大轰炸那样客观上令人恐惧的情境，也会因为反复经历而变得习以为常，或许我们就能鼓起勇气，去面对那些阻碍我们前进的、远没有那么严重的恐惧。

Strategies for Surmounting Fear

克服恐惧的策略

Courage isn’t just the province of combat survivors. Life challenges us with countless mundane fears and anxieties. In those situations, we have a choice about how we can respond to them—seeking out experiences to test the reality of our fears, or shying away and leaving them forever in the dark. Overcoming fear requires feedback. Not just an intellectual understanding that your worries are overblown, but the visceral feedback from direct experience.

勇气并非只有战斗幸存者才具备。生活中，我们常常会面临无数平凡的恐惧和焦虑。面对这些挑战，我们可以选择如何应对——是主动寻求体验来检验恐惧的真实性，还是选择逃避，让恐惧永远笼罩在阴影之中。克服恐惧需要反馈。这不仅仅是理性地认识到自己的担忧是夸大其词，更是来自直接体验的切身感受。

Let’s look at some strategies for applying exposure to test our fears.

让我们来看看一些运用暴露疗法来检验我们恐惧的策略。

Strategy #1: Construct Your Fear Hierarchy

策略一：构建你的恐惧层级

Wolpe’s practice of having patients construct a fear hierarchy is still used in cognitive-behavioral treatments of anxiety today. While the debate over flooding versus gradual exposure was rendered theoretically irrelevant, there may still be practical reasons to prefer going step-by-step. One reason is simply that if a fear is too strong, you might not be able to go through with exposure to it! This may be truer with self-guided exposure, when the authoritative voice of a therapist isn’t there to push you forward.

沃尔普让患者构建恐惧等级的做法，至今仍被应用于焦虑症的认知行为疗法中。虽然关于“暴露疗法”和“渐进疗法”孰优孰劣的争论在理论上已不再重要，但循序渐进的方法或许仍有其实际优势。其中一个原因很简单：如果恐惧过于强烈，你可能无法坚持完成暴露疗法！在自我引导的暴露疗法中，由于缺乏治疗师的权威指导，这种情况可能更为突出。

Abramowitz stresses the need to mirror the situational, cognitive, and physiological aspects of the fear as closely as possible. “ The importance of closely matching hierarchy items to the patient’s fear cannot be overemphasized: a person afraid of dogs must confront the types of dog he or she is frightened of. Someone afraid of germs from hospitals must confront items in a hospital . Someone afraid of starting a fire because she has left a light on in her house must turn many lights on and leave the house, and so on.” Matching the situational aspects of exposure means identifying exactly which scenarios the person anticipates feeling afraid of. Exposure to situations that are superficially similar but don’t elicit fear won’t work.

阿布拉莫维茨强调，必须尽可能地还原恐惧的情境、认知和生理层面。“将恐惧等级与患者的恐惧紧密匹配至关重要：害怕狗的人必须面对他/她所害怕的那种狗；害怕医院细菌的人必须面对医院里的物品；害怕因为忘记关灯而引发火灾的人必须打开很多灯并离开家，等等。” 匹配暴露疗法的情境层面意味着准确识别患者预期会感到恐惧的场景。暴露于表面上相似但无法引发恐惧的情境是无效的。

Creating a fear hierarchy can also be a first step in questioning the reasonableness of some of the assumptions they are built upon. Just as even the most terrifying nightmare can often feel silly when we say it out loud, the basis of our fears may seem less plausible when we write down what we fear and what we expect to happen. While we’ve already seen that belief change alone is probably insufficient to overcome our unconscious threat-detection circuitry, it can help encourage exposure. The moderate efficacy of cognitive therapy without exposure may partly be due to people engaging in self-exposure after being confronted about the validity of their beliefs about threats.

建立恐惧层级也可以是质疑某些恐惧假设合理性的第一步。正如即使是最恐怖的噩梦，当我们把它说出来时也会觉得荒谬可笑一样，当我们把恐惧的内容和预期发生的事情写下来时，恐惧的根源可能也会显得不那么可信。虽然我们已经看到，仅仅改变信念可能不足以克服我们无意识的威胁检测机制，但它可以帮助鼓励人们进行暴露疗法。认知疗法在没有暴露疗法的情况下疗效有限，部分原因可能在于，人们在被质疑其关于威胁的信念的合理性之后，会主动进行自我暴露。

Strategy #2: Don’t Say “Everything Will Be Okay”

策略二：不要说“一切都会好起来的”

Faced with worry, it’s natural to seek reassurance. Unfortunately, this can have exactly the same problem as the avoidance behaviors we discussed earlier. “ It is important to note that the purpose of exposure therapy is not to persuade or reassure the patient that he or she is absolutely safe or that the feared consequences are out of the question whatsoever,” writes Abramowitz, later adding, “ Under no circumstances should the therapist reassure the patient that ‘everything will be okay.’” The presence of a therapist can, paradoxically, make exposure less effective if the person learns that they are safe, so long as they have their therapist with them.

面对焦虑，寻求安慰是人之常情。然而，这恰恰会引发与我们之前讨论的逃避行为相同的问题。阿布拉莫维茨写道：“需要注意的是，暴露疗法的目的并非说服或安抚患者，让他们相信自己绝对安全，或者让他们相信所恐惧的后果完全不可能发生。”他随后补充道：“在任何情况下，治疗师都不应该向患者保证‘一切都会好起来的’。”矛盾的是，如果患者认为只要有治疗师在身边就安全无虞，那么治疗师的存在反而会降低暴露疗法的效果。

Just as making a list of fears can be helpful, so can making a list of common avoidance behaviors. These can involve actual avoidance, such as the person who excuses himself from speaking at meetings because of social anxiety, or they can involve crutches that increase the feeling of safety. A person who worries about embarrassment from sweating too much might obsessively use strong antiperspirants. Although this behavior “works” to reduce the anxiety, it can make the person reliant on the safety behavior, even when it is impractical. Going to a party with the intention of sweating as much as possible would work better to disconfirm the belief that visible sweating will lead to strong negative social judgments.

就像列出恐惧清单会有帮助一样，列出常见的逃避行为清单也很有帮助。这些行为可能包括实际的逃避行为，例如有人因为社交焦虑而在会议上找借口不发言；也可能包括一些能增强安全感的“拐杖”。例如，担心出汗过多而尴尬的人可能会过度使用强效止汗剂。虽然这种行为确实能减轻焦虑，但它会让这个人依赖这种安全行为，即使这种行为并不实际。如果抱着尽可能多出汗的心态去参加聚会，或许更能打破“出汗过多会导致严重的负面社交评价”这种想法。

Ultimately, the process of exposure is about testing our fearful expectations. We can’t do that if we undermine the experiment by finding ways to neutralize any potential threat. A person who is afraid of speaking in public might get embarrassed onstage. The aim of exposure isn’t to prove that humiliation is impossible, but to recognize that it is probably less likely than we think it is, and even if it does occur, we will be better able to cope than we imagine. Testing fears requires engaging in acceptable risks, rather than the extremes of both recklessness and vainly trying to eliminate all possible danger.

归根结底，暴露疗法的目的是检验我们恐惧的预期。如果我们试图通过消除任何潜在威胁来破坏实验，就无法做到这一点。一个害怕公开演讲的人可能会在台上出丑。暴露疗法的目的不是证明羞辱不可能发生，而是要认识到它发生的可能性可能比我们想象的要小，即使真的发生了，我们也能比想象中更好地应对。检验恐惧需要承担可接受的风险，而不是走向极端，既鲁莽行事，又徒劳地试图消除所有可能的危险。

Strategy #3: Face Fears Together

策略三：共同面对恐惧

Courage is more likely in communities than in individuals. “There is consistent evidence that membership in a small, cohesive group can play an important part in controlling fear,” writes psychologist Stanley Rachman; “most people appear to be more susceptible to fear when they are alone.” Having a social purpose served to inoculate firefighters, rescue workers, and nurses from some of the worst psychological effects of the Blitz. Vernon argues that it was the people who lived alone who were more likely to worsen after repeated bombings. Part of the explanation for the remarkable resilience of people seen during disasters might be that they did not face their fears in isolation.

勇气在群体中比在个体中更容易显现。“有大量证据表明，加入一个小型、凝聚力强的群体在控制恐惧方面发挥着重要作用，”心理学家斯坦利·拉赫曼写道，“大多数人在独处时似乎更容易感到恐惧。” 拥有社会使命感有助于消防员、救援人员和护士免受闪电战带来的最严重的心理创伤。弗农认为，独居者在经历反复轰炸后更容易出现心理恶化。人们在灾难中展现出的惊人韧性，部分原因可能在于他们并非独自面对恐惧。

Fear of public speaking likely matters more than rhetorical skill for the presenting ability of most people. Yet most of us get few opportunities to practice. With limited, infrequent exposure, stage fright usually remains high. Organizations like Toastmasters can help, since in addition to providing ample exposure to public speaking opportunities, they do so within a supportive, communal atmosphere. Joining studying groups for mathematics or conversation clubs for practicing a language can have a similar benefit: providing exposure to the anxiety-provoking situation in the presence of other people.

对于大多数人来说，公开演讲的恐惧可能比修辞技巧更能影响他们的演讲能力。然而，我们大多数人却鲜有机会练习。由于练习机会有限且频率不高，怯场的情绪往往难以缓解。像Toastmasters这样的组织可以提供帮助，因为它们不仅提供大量的公开演讲机会，而且还营造了一种支持性的社群氛围。参加数学学习小组或语言会话俱乐部也能带来类似的益处：在其他人的陪伴下，体验这种令人焦虑的情境。

Strategy #4: Distinguish Courage from Fearlessness

策略四：区分勇气与无畏

Courage is not the same thing as acting without fear. “ Fear is not a lump,” explains Rachman. Instead, he argues that fear can best be seen as at least three different interacting components: a physiological component of arousal (for example, a higher heart rate, sweating palms), a subjective component of beliefs and feelings, and a behavioral component of avoidance and safety seeking. While these three systems generally point in the same direction, they are not identical. People regularly find themselves in situations where physiological and subjective states of fear are quite high, yet they manage to persist in their tasks. Courage is not action without fear, but action in spite of fear.

勇气并非无所畏惧地行动。“恐惧并非一个整体，”拉赫曼解释道。他认为，恐惧最好被理解为至少三个相互作用的组成部分：生理唤醒成分（例如，心跳加速、手心出汗）、主观信念和感受成分，以及回避和寻求安全的行为成分。虽然这三个系统总体上指向同一方向，但它们并不完全相同。人们经常会发现自己身处生理和主观恐惧感都很强的环境中，但他们仍然能够坚持完成任务。勇气并非无所畏惧地行动，而是在恐惧中依然行动。

Exposure itself is unlikely to generalize broadly to many different fears. As we’ve discussed, the learning of safety tends to be more specific than learning fear, and so exposure is needed in multiple contexts with regular refreshers to be sustained. However, seeing courage as an attitude and philosophy of life may be more defensible. “ Fearful people have a strong tendency to overestimate how frightened they will be when they encounter a fear-provoking object or situation,” Rachman explains. He reviews evidence from multiple domains showing that people overpredict their fearful reactions to events, and underestimate their ability to maintain composure. Ultimately, the information we gain from facing our fears isn’t just about the reality of danger, but the reality of ourselves.

仅仅依靠暴露疗法不太可能广泛适用于所有不同的恐惧。正如我们之前讨论过的，学习安全感往往比学习恐惧感更具针对性，因此需要在多种情境下进行暴露疗法，并定期进行巩固练习才能维持效果。然而，将勇气视为一种态度和人生哲学或许更有道理。“恐惧的人往往会高估自己在遇到恐惧对象或情境时的恐惧程度，”拉赫曼解释道。他回顾了来自多个领域的证据表明，人们会高估自己对事件的恐惧反应，而低估自己保持冷静的能力。最终，我们从直面恐惧中获得的信息不仅关乎危险的现实，也关乎我们自身的现实。

The Path to Improvement

改进之路

Seeing examples, doing practice, and getting feedback are key to getting better at anything. But learning is more than just an intellectual process. Emotions, from fear to enthusiasm, play at least as large a role in determining which skills we end up improving. In the conclusion, we’ll synthesize the various perspectives discussed so far in the book, and end with some practical wisdom for charting the path to improvement.

学习任何技能的关键在于观察实例、练习和获得反馈。但学习不仅仅是一个智力过程。从恐惧到热情，各种情绪在决定我们最终提升哪些技能方面都起着至关重要的作用。在结论部分，我们将综合本书迄今为止讨论的各种观点，并总结一些有助于我们规划提升之路的实用建议。

# ↩

Conclusion

结论

Practice Made Perfect

熟能生巧

T here’s an old tale about a woodcutter who was given an axe and three hours to chop down a large tree. The woodcutter decided to spend the first two and a half hours sharpening the axe. In a similar way, we spend countless hours of our lives on things we want to do well. We want to be better parents, professionals, artists, and athletes. In comparison to all this chopping, we often spend only a small fraction of the time actively trying to sharpen our axe. I began writing this book with a particular reader in mind: You’re someone who cares about how learning works. You want to improve at something yourself, whether that is getting an A on your exams, becoming an expert at your work, or feeling confident in a sport or hobby. Or perhaps you’re more interested in helping others get better. You’re a coach, teacher, employer, or parent looking to see how you can help those around you acquire valuable skills. While it’s a professional hazard to make blanket statements about one’s audience as an author, I feel fairly confident that if you’ve made it this far, you care about sharpening the axe.

有个古老的故事讲的是一个樵夫，他被给予一把斧头和三个小时的时间砍倒一棵大树。樵夫决定用前两个半小时磨斧头。同样，我们一生中花费无数时间去做我们想做好的事情。我们想成为更好的父母、专业人士、艺术家和运动员。与所有这些努力相比，我们往往只花极少的时间去磨砺自己的斧头。我写这本书时，心中想着一个特定的读者：你是一个关心学习方式的人。你想提升自己，无论是考试得A、成为工作专家，还是在运动或爱好中充满自信。或许你更感兴趣的是帮助他人进步。你是一位教练、教师、雇主或家长，正在寻找帮助身边的人获得宝贵技能的方法。虽然作为一名作者，对自己的读者群体做出笼统的陈述是一种职业风险，但我相当确信，如果你已经读到这里，你一定很关心如何精益求精。

Throughout this book, I’ve shared stories and research about how learning works. We’ve seen the importance of examples and how our problem-solving efforts build on the knowledge of others, examined the mind’s bottleneck and how it constrains the path to mastery, considered the importance of building skills from a successful foundation, and seen how to extract knowledge from experts who often forget what it was like to be a beginner. We’ve dug into the power of practice: the importance of progressive problem solving and fine-tuning the difficulty in our training, why the mind is not like a muscle and how we should be more precise in our attempts at improvement, the value of variability in creating flexible skills, and why accomplishments at the frontier of creativity correlate so closely with overall productivity. Finally, we’ve examined the critical role of feedback: why many expert estimations are overconfident in environments of uncertainty, how the physical and social environment shapes the skills we need to master, the role of unlearning in eventual mastery, and how we can overcome our fears and anxieties when leaving our comfort zones to learn something new. In each of these chapters, I tried to synthesize a prominent perspective given by the research and suggest a few practical takeaways. The science of learning is diverse and often contentious. While I’m certain that not everyone will agree with all of my conclusions, I hope the citations listed in the endnotes can be a jumping-off point for serious readers to engage with some of the ideas for themselves.

在本书中，我分享了许多关于学习机制的故事和研究。我们看到了例子的重要性，以及我们如何借助他人的知识来解决问题；我们探讨了思维瓶颈及其如何限制我们走向精通的道路；我们思考了从成功的基础中构建技能的重要性；我们还了解了如何从那些常常忘记自己也曾是初学者的专家身上汲取知识。我们深入探讨了练习的力量：循序渐进地解决问题和微调训练难度的重要性；为什么思维不像肌肉，以及我们应该如何在提升的过程中更加精准；变化在培养灵活技能中的价值；以及为什么在创造力前沿取得的成就与整体生产力密切相关。最后，我们探讨了反馈的关键作用：为什么许多专家的评估在不确定的环境中会过于自信；物理和社会环境如何塑造我们需要掌握的技能；“遗忘”在最终精通中的作用；以及我们如何在离开舒适区学习新事物时克服恐惧和焦虑。在每一章中，我都试图综合研究中提出的一个重要观点，并提出一些实用建议。学习科学博大精深，且常常充满争议。虽然我确信并非所有人都会认同我的所有结论，但我希望文末注释中列出的参考文献能够为认真研读相关观点的读者提供一个起点。

In this chapter, I’d like to step back from the research to try to pull all these diverse perspectives together and offer some general advice. My main focus will be on you as the learner. How can you get better at the things you care about? As a secondary consideration I’ll also try to reflect on what this research says about how we can be better teachers, coaches, and mentors to those who depend on us.

在本章中，我想暂时抛开研究本身，尝试将各种不同的观点整合起来，并提出一些总体建议。我的主要关注点将放在你作为学习者身上。你如何才能在自己关心的事情上做得更好？其次，我也会尝试反思这项研究对我们如何成为更好的老师、教练和导师有何启示，从而更好地帮助那些依赖我们的人。

Three Questions for Mastery

掌握这三个问题

The economist and author Tyler Cowen likes to ask people, “ What is it you do to train that is comparable to a pianist practicing scales?” Those without a good answer to this question, he argues, are perhaps not so serious about improving at their craft. The world is changing rapidly. Skills that could have sustained a profession for a lifetime may become obsolete as new technologies can do them automatically. Lifelong learning isn’t just a feel-good slogan, but a necessity. Given its importance, I think it’s useful to ask yourself three questions about the pursuits you care about.

经济学家兼作家泰勒·科恩喜欢问人们：“你做了哪些训练，能与钢琴家练习音阶相媲美？”他认为，如果无法给出令人满意的答案，或许说明你对提升自身技艺并非真心实意。世界瞬息万变，曾经足以支撑终身职业的技能，随着新技术的出现，可能会被淘汰。终身学习并非一句空洞的口号，而是一种必然。鉴于其重要性，我认为，对于你所热衷的事业，不妨问问自己以下三个问题。

Question One: How Can I Improve the Way I Learn from Others?

问题一：我如何才能更好地向他人学习？

Examples, as we’ve seen, play a critical role in learning complex skills. The ability to learn from others is a distinguishing characteristic of our species. We see further by standing upon the hard-won problem-solving insights of those who came before us. When seeking out learning materials:

正如我们所见，例子在学习复杂技能中起着至关重要的作用。向他人学习的能力是我们人类的显著特征。我们能够借鉴前人来之不易的解决问题的洞见，从而看得更远。在寻找学习资料时：

  1. Find examples that include all of the steps needed to solve the problem. While we can easily observe the physical actions of another person performing a skill, mental actions are invisible. Indeed, the danger of learning from experts is that their fluency with a skill causes them to skip over intervening steps. A good worked example should break down the problem-solving steps to a level so that each action is comprehensible to the person who is studying it.
    寻找包含解决问题所有步骤的示例。虽然我们可以轻易观察到他人执行某项技能的实际动作，但心理活动却是不可见的。事实上，向专家学习的风险在于，他们对技能的熟练掌握会导致他们忽略中间步骤。一个好的示例应该将解决问题的步骤分解到学习者能够理解的程度。
  2. Make sure you’ve learned enough background knowledge so the examples make sense. Understanding is not an all-or-nothing property, so we must use judgment. Too little explanation and the problem is a memorized answer without any generality. Too much and we can fall down a rabbit hole of endless elaboration.
    确保你掌握了足够的背景知识，这样才能理解例子。理解并非非此即彼，所以我们需要运用判断力。解释太少，问题就变成了死记硬背的答案，缺乏普遍适用性；解释太多，我们又容易陷入无休止的阐述之中。
  3. Seek out varied examples to generalize the problem-solving patterns. The ability to form abstract concepts and analogies from concrete instances is central to our flexibility as thinkers. Yet novices to a field tend to perceive problems more in terms of superficial features than deep principles. Offering multiple examples that exhibit a broader range of variation makes it easier to extract what they have in common. It’s also often helpful to present counterexamples: similar-seeming situations that don’t work for a subtle reason to prevent overgeneralization.
    寻找各种不同的例子来概括解决问题的模式。从具体事例中提炼抽象概念和类比的能力，是我们思维灵活性的核心。然而，初学者往往更关注问题的表面特征，而非深层原理。提供多个展现更广泛变化的例子，有助于我们提取它们的共同点。此外，提出反例也很有帮助：看似相似但因某些微妙原因而行不通的情况，可以防止过度概括。

The obvious first place to start looking for examples is in well-structured courses. These have the advantage of sequencing examples, making sure background knowledge is made available and in revealing otherwise invisible mental steps performed by experts. As we’ve seen in chapter 3 , beginning with a successful foundation can make a big difference for mastery and motivation. In-person classes, massive open online courses, textbooks, and even YouTube videos can provide a good starting place for many skills. If you can afford it and help is available, getting one-on-one tutoring is also particularly helpful—especially if off-the-shelf materials are lacking.

寻找范例的首要途径显然是结构完善的课程。这类课程的优势在于能够循序渐进地呈现范例，确保背景知识到位，并揭示专家们那些不易察觉的思维步骤。正如我们在第三章中所看到的，打好基础对于掌握技能和保持学习动力至关重要。面授课程、大型开放式网络课程、教科书，甚至YouTube视频，都能为许多技能的学习提供良好的起点。如果经济条件允许且有资源，一对一辅导也特别有益——尤其是在缺乏现成学习资料的情况下。

As we gain experience in a domain, classes replete with worked examples tend to be less common. This is partly a matter of economics. Most people are beginners to a skill, so the largest market exists to serve those just starting out. Additionally, knowledge tends to branch and specialize as skill progresses. This makes it much harder to reliably cover everything that matters as you make more progress. Being more advanced does not imply learning from examples is pointless, however. Recall from chapter 1 that Andrew Wiles, despite being a PhD-holding specialist in the area of mathematics needed to solve Fermat’s Last Theorem, nonetheless spent two years reading everything he could in preparation for the proof. Instead, it is simply the case that as we move beyond the examples neatly laid out in courses we must lean on more informal resources.

随着我们在某个领域经验的积累，提供大量例题的课程往往越来越少见。这部分是经济因素造成的。大多数人都是初学者，因此最大的市场是服务于这些新手。此外，随着技能的提升，知识往往会分支和细分。这使得随着学习的深入，要全面掌握所有重要知识变得更加困难。然而，更高级的技能并不意味着从例题中学习就毫无意义。回想一下第一章的内容，安德鲁·怀尔斯虽然拥有博士学位，是解决费马大定理所需数学领域的专家，但他仍然花了两年时间阅读所有相关资料来准备证明。事实上，当我们不再依赖课程中精心设计的例题时，我们就必须依靠更多非正式的学习资源。
